Headline summary

Shallow migration of The Mind's MindCardRenderer to use core-engine SvgHelpers for lazy SVG rasterisation and texture management; preserve public API or provide compatibility adapters, update tests, and document rasterisation policy.


Problem statement

The Mind currently uses scene.load.svg to load and rasterise card SVGs. This duplicates rasterisation logic and diverges from the engine-wide SvgHelpers approach. We need a shallow migration so MindCardRenderer uses src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts (getOrCreateTexture, rasteriseSvgToTexture, fetchSvgText) with lazy rasterisation on first use, preserving runtime behaviour and tests.


Users

- Engine maintainers: benefit from a single shared SVG rasterisation path for correctness and maintenance.
- Game authors (The Mind): want no visual or functional regressions in card rendering and texture keys.
- QA/CI: deterministic tests and headless integration checks that verify textures are available when needed.

Example user stories

- As an engine maintainer, I want The Mind's card rendering to use SvgHelpers so that bug fixes to rasterisation apply to all games.
- As a game author, I want card textures to be created on first use and exposed at the same texture keys so scenes do not break.
- As QA, I want unit tests and a small headless integration check that confirms a sample card texture is available via the public API.


Success criteria

- Public API preserved: functions used by scenes (e.g., preloadMindCardAssets, getMindCardTexture, ensureMindCardTexture) remain available or are replaced with compatibility shims.
- Lazy rasterisation: textures are created on first use via SvgHelpers.getOrCreateTexture (no eager rasterisation of all 100 cards during preload).
- Tests: Unit tests for MindCardRenderer updated as necessary and pass; at least one integration check (headless) confirms card textures render without missing-texture errors.
- Documentation: docs/DEVELOPER.md and code comments updated to document the rasterisation policy (lazy on first use) and migration notes.
- Full project test suite passes locally (npm test) and build succeeds (npm run build).


Constraints

- Keep changes minimal and localized to example-games/the-mind and SvgHelpers; avoid unrelated refactors.
- Maintain compatibility with both browser and headless test environments.
- Avoid eager rasterisation that increases memory usage; prefer lazy getOrCreateTexture semantics.
- Preserve existing texture key names where possible to avoid widespread caller churn.


Existing state

- example-games/the-mind/MindCardRenderer.ts currently uses scene.load.svg and contains helpers referenced by scenes: getMindCardTexture, ensureMindCardTexture, preloadMindCardAssets (file exists in repo).
- Core helpers exist: src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts with fetchSvgText, rasteriseSvgToTexture and getOrCreateTexture; tests exist for SvgHelpers (tests/core-engine/SvgHelpers.*).
- Tests referencing MindCardRenderer exist at tests/the-mind/mind-card-renderer.test.ts and tests/the-mind/mind-renderer.test.ts.
- Parent migration epic: CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV documents the migration policy and scope.


Desired change

- Replace direct scene.load.svg usage in MindCardRenderer.ts with SvgHelpers calls:
  - Provide compatibility functions that expose the same public API (getMindCardTexture, ensureMindCardTexture, preloadMindCardAssets).
  - Implement ensureMindCardTexture to call SvgHelpers.getOrCreateTexture(scene, textureKey, svgPath) and return a promise/void consistent with existing callers.
  - Implement preloadMindCardAssets as a light-weight registration that does not eagerly rasterise all 100 SVGs but ensures keys will be resolvable (e.g., by pre-registering fetch sources or creating lightweight placeholders).
- Update unit and integration tests to reflect the new behaviour; where tests relied on loader semantics update them to mock SvgHelpers or assert texture availability after ensureMindCardTexture.
- Update docs/DEVELOPER.md with the chosen rasterisation policy (lazy rasterisation via SvgHelpers.getOrCreateTexture) and a short migration note.


Related work

Potentially related docs (file paths)
- src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts — shared SVG rasterisation helpers (implementation and tests).
- docs/DEVELOPER.md — contains notes about SvgHelpers and rasterisation policy.
- example-games/the-mind/MindCardRenderer.ts — current implementation to be migrated.
- example-games/the-mind/scenes/MindRenderer.ts, MindAnimator.ts, MindReplayController.ts — callers that rely on MindCardRenderer public helpers.

Potentially related work items
- CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV — Migrate the-mind SVG usage to core-engine SvgHelpers (parent epic).
- CG-0MOZMT7G80090Y6S — Extract SVG & card rendering into shared engine helpers and migrate Sushi Go (related migration pattern).
- CG-0MOZNY9O0008NEKT — Scan & Create Migrations (scan results show other scenes using load.svg).


Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope — should the migration be limited to example-games/the-mind/MindCardRenderer.ts only, or should callers (scenes such as MindRenderer/MindAnimator) also be updated if necessary?" — Answer (user): "B" (update callers when required). Source: interactive reply in parent epic CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV. Final: yes.
- Q: "Rasterisation strategy — prefer (A) pre-rasterise all Mind SVGs during scene preload, (B) lazy rasterise on first use, or (C) a hybrid (pre-rasterise a small set and lazy for the rest)?" — Answer (user): "B" (lazy rasterisation). Source: interactive reply in parent epic CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV. Final: yes.
- Q: "Testing expectations — should existing tests be adapted to the new implementation if they rely on loader semantics, or should we keep the public behaviour unchanged (texture keys and API), updating tests only to reflect implementation details when unavoidable?" — Answer (user): "API changes OK" (user). Source: interactive reply in parent epic CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV. Final: yes — tests and callers may be updated to reflect intentional API changes.

This draft reuses the existing work item CG-0MP12H40Q003Y7OU. Re-running intake will update the same work item and will not duplicate Appendix entries; existing Appendix items were incorporated from the parent epic and the item's description.

Headline summary

Bring The Mind scenes and tests in line with SvgHelpers-based texture generation: update callers (MindRenderer, MindAnimator, MindReplayController), adjust unit and integration tests, and add compatibility shims where needed to preserve runtime behaviour.


Problem statement

After migrating MindCardRenderer to use src/core-engine/SvgHelpers for SVG rasterisation, several scenes and tests may rely on previous loader semantics (scene.load.svg and eager texture availability). This task updates scenes and tests to consume the SvgHelpers-based textures correctly, adding compatibility shims where necessary to avoid runtime regressions.


Users

- Game authors (The Mind): need scenes to display card textures correctly without visual regressions.
- Engine maintainers: get consistent SVG rasterisation across games and simpler maintenance.
- QA: require deterministic unit and headless integration tests to validate rendering and avoid flaky loader-dependent tests.

Example user stories

- As a game author, I want MindRenderer and related scenes to request or ensure textures via the MindCardRenderer public API and display cards reliably in both browser and headless tests.
- As QA, I want tests updated to assert texture availability using SvgHelpers semantics so CI/headless runs are deterministic.


Success criteria

- Scene compatibility: MindRenderer, MindAnimator, MindReplayController and related callers use MindCardRenderer's SvgHelpers-backed API (getMindCardTexture/ensureMindCardTexture) and render cards without missing-texture errors in browser and headless runs.
- Tests updated: unit tests that previously depended on scene.load.svg semantics are updated to mock or await ensureMindCardTexture; all updated tests pass locally (npm test) and in headless browser runs used by the suite.
- Compatibility shims: if public API names changed, provide lightweight shims so callers do not require large refactors; shims are documented in the migration note.
- Documentation: docs/DEVELOPER.md updated with migration notes and recommended patterns for consuming SvgHelpers-backed textures in scenes (example code snippet included).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; build succeeds (npm run build).


Constraints

- Keep changes focused to example-games/the-mind callers and tests; avoid wide refactors.
- Preserve behaviour in headless test environment; do not rely on browser-only DOM fetch patterns.
- Prefer lazy rasterisation (SvgHelpers.getOrCreateTexture) over eager pre-rasterisation to avoid increased memory usage.
- Maintain existing texture key names where feasible; if renaming is necessary, update caller references and document migration.


Existing state

- MindCardRenderer migration is in-flight (parent epic CG-0MOZN33SQ0057ESV). The MindCardRenderer now (or will) use SvgHelpers.getOrCreateTexture and related helpers.
- Callers: example-games/the-mind/scenes/MindRenderer.ts, MindAnimator.ts, MindReplayController.ts import and call MindCardRenderer helpers (getMindCardTexture, preloadMindCardAssets, ensureMindCardTexture).
- Tests: tests/the-mind/mind-card-renderer.test.ts and tests/the-mind/mind-renderer.test.ts reference MindCardRenderer behaviour and may assume loader semantics.
- Core helpers: src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts provides fetchSvgText, rasteriseSvgToTexture, getOrCreateTexture; tests for SvgHelpers exist (tests/core-engine/SvgHelpers.*).


Desired change

- Update scene callers to use the SvgHelpers-backed MindCardRenderer API:
  - Replace any direct assumptions about eager texture availability with await ensureMindCardTexture(scene, key) or getMindCardTexture that triggers lazy generation via SvgHelpers.getOrCreateTexture.
  - Where scenes previously called preloadMindCardAssets to trigger loader-based preloads, change to a lightweight registration or await-first-use pattern; if necessary provide a shallow shim preloadMindCardAssets that registers sources without rasterising all assets.
- Update unit tests to either mock SvgHelpers or to call ensureMindCardTexture as part of test setup; prefer small focused changes that test public behaviour rather than internal loader semantics.
- Add one headless integration test that boots a minimal The Mind scene, requests a sample card texture, and asserts no missing-texture errors and that the texture key exists.
- Add a short migration note to docs/DEVELOPER.md with example code for scenes to ensure textures via SvgHelpers-backed API and show the compatibility shim usage.


Related work

- example-games/the-mind/scenes/MindRenderer.ts, MindAnimator.ts, MindReplayController.ts — callers to update.

Headline summary

Design and implement a shared src/ui/Renderer API (moderate scope) and migrate Main Street + The Mind to use it; include a moderate API (container/HUD/card rendering helpers + SVG adapter wiring), adapters, tests, and migration docs.


Problem statement

Multiple game scenes implement ad-hoc rendering helpers (container creation, HUD refresh, SVG card wiring), leading to duplication and "god-class" scene files. We need a shared renderer module that exposes a stable, moderate API and per-game adapters to simplify scene code and enable consistent rendering patterns across games.


Users

- Engine maintainers: easier maintenance and single place to fix rendering bugs.
- Game authors (Main Street, The Mind): smaller scene files, consistent helpers, and easier onboarding to engine patterns.
- QA: reliable integration tests and fewer rendering regressions across games.

Example user stories

- As an engine maintainer, I want a shared renderer API so fixes and improvements benefit multiple example games.
- As a Main Street dev, I want to replace duplicated HUD/container helpers with shared functions and keep scene behaviour identical.
- As a QA engineer, I want integration tests that verify Main Street and The Mind render equivalently after migration.


Success criteria

- API design: src/ui/Renderer exports a moderate API including container creation, HUD helpers, refresh patterns, and card rendering adapter hooks; public function signatures documented.
- Migration: Main Street and The Mind use the shared renderer via per-game adapters; scene tests for those games remain green.
- Tests: Unit tests for shared helpers added and passing; browser-level integration smoke tests for Main Street and The Mind demonstrate equivalent rendering (no missing elements, no test regressions).
- Docs: Migration guide in docs/ (usage examples, adapter pattern, and list of moved helpers) added.
- Build & tests: Full project test suite passes locally and CI (npm test; npm run build).


Constraints

- Moderate scope: implement a focused API (not a full facade). Avoid introducing multiple runtime strategies (DOM vs Canvas) in this first PR; prefer a single SVG/texture adapter using existing SvgHelpers.
- Keep migration changes minimal per-scene: replace 1–3 helpers per scene and provide adapters that re-export old names where feasible to reduce caller churn.
- Maintain browser and headless test compatibility.
- Do not change game mechanics or visual assets; this is a refactor/migration only.

- Scenes contain duplicated rendering helpers; several work items note "god class" scenes (e.g., Decompose TheMindScene, Decompose MainStreetScene).

- example-games/the-mind/MindRenderer.ts and current MindCardRenderer
- src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts — raster helpers

## Summary
In The Mind example game, when a player plays a higher card while another player still holds a lower card, the lower card should be auto-discarded (burned) as part of out-of-order resolution. Currently that lower card remains in the other player's hand, causing game state divergence from expected rules.

## User story
As a player of The Mind, when someone plays a card out of turn, all lower-valued cards that should have been played first are immediately removed from players' hands so the round state remains valid and consistent.

## Expected behavior
- When card N is played, any cards with value < N still in any player hand are removed from those hands and moved to the appropriate discard/played history state used by the game.
- No skipped lower card remains in any hand after resolution.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Add/extend automated tests that reproduce the bug: a higher card played before another player's lower card no longer leaves that lower card in hand.
2. Implement fix so skipped lower cards are removed from hands during out-of-order play resolution.
3. Existing tests continue to pass and new tests pass.
4. Document assumptions in work item comments if rule interpretation requires it.

# Tooltip on Played Cards in Sushi Go — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

In Sushi Go!, tooltips with scoring information appear when hovering over cards in the player's hand, but not on cards that have already been played to the tableau. Players must look at small score labels above each group (e.g., "Tmp(5)", "Ssh(10)") to understand current scoring, which is less discoverable and provides no per-card context.

## Users

- **New players** who need to understand how a played card contributes to their current score without memorizing scoring rules.
- **Experienced players** who want quick visual confirmation of the current score a tableau card is earning.

### User Stories

- As a player, I want to hover over any card in my tableau (or the AI's tableau) and see both the scoring rule and the current score contribution, so I can quickly understand my round standing.
- As a player, I want the tableau card tooltip to feel consistent with hand card tooltips, so the interface is predictable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tableau card tooltip** — Hovering over any card in the player's tableau displays a tooltip containing both the scoring rule text (from `SCORING_TOOLTIPS`) and the current score contribution for that card's group (the same numeric value shown in the group label, e.g., "Tmp(5)", "Ssh(10)", "Nig(8)").
2. **AI tableau tooltip** — Hovering over any card in the AI's tableau also displays the tooltip with scoring rule text and current score contribution.
3. **Maki/Pudding tooltip** — For maki and pudding cards in the tableau, the tooltip shows only the scoring rule text (from `SCORING_TOOLTIPS`) without a numeric score contribution, since maki depends on cross-player comparison and pudding is game-end only.
4. **Hover highlight** — Tableau cards highlight on hover with the same visual treatment as hand cards (stroke color change and slight scale-up).
5. **Settings toggle respected** — The tooltip must respect the `showTooltips` toggle in the Settings panel. When tooltips are disabled, no tooltip appears on tableau card hover.
6. **Canvas boundary clamping** — Tooltips must not overflow outside the 1280x720 canvas boundaries (same clamping as hand card tooltips).
7. **No functional gameplay changes** — No gameplay mechanics, scoring, or AI behavior are altered.
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No changes to the generic scoring rules text in `SCORING_TOOLTIPS`.
- No changes to the scoring logic (`SushiGoScoring.ts`) or gameplay mechanics.
- Must work with the existing `TooltipManager` from `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (Phaser render mode).
- Must work in both normal play and replay (`?mode=replay`) modes.

## Existing State

- Hand cards are created via `SushiGoScene.createCardRect()` which passes `onShowTooltip`/`onHideTooltip` callbacks to `SushiGoCardFactory.createCardRect()`.
- Tableau cards are created via `SushiGoTableauRenderer.renderGroupCards()` which calls `SushiGoCardFactory.createCardRect()` **without** tooltip callbacks and with `interactive=false` (default).
- The `SushiGoCardFactory.createCardRect()` only wires `pointerover`/`pointerout` events for highlighting and tooltips when `interactive=true` and tooltip callbacks are provided.
- Score labels above each tableau group are rendered by `SushiGoTableauRenderer.buildTypeLabel()` using `scoreTableauBreakdown()` values (e.g., `Tmp(5)`, `Ssh(10)`, `Dmp(6)`, `Nig(8)`, `Maki(+6)`).

## Desired Change

1. Pass tooltip callbacks (`onShowTooltip`/`onHideTooltip`) from `SushiGoTableauRenderer` into `SushiGoCardFactory.createCardRect()` for tableau cards.
2. Make tableau cards interactive so `pointerover`/`pointerout` events fire highlighting and tooltip display.
3. In the tooltip callback for tableau cards, build tooltip content that combines:
   - The generic scoring rule text from `SCORING_TOOLTIPS[card.type]`
   - The current score contribution for that card's group (from `scoreTableauBreakdown()`), **except** for maki and pudding which show rule text only.
4. Ensure tooltips respect the `SettingsPanel.showTooltips` toggle (already handled by `TooltipManager`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: The work could expand to include refactoring tableau card rendering architecture or adding new scoring display features. **Mitigation**: Opportunities for additional features or refactoring should be recorded as new work items linked to this item, rather than expanding the scope of the current item.
- **Replay mode compatibility**: Tableau card tooltips must not break replay mode. The existing loading of board state should continue to work unchanged.
- **No AI behavior change assumption**: The changes are purely visual/UI — no AI strategy or decision-making is affected.
- **Performance assumption**: Adding interactivity to tableau cards (up to ~20 cards) should have negligible performance impact.

## Related Work

- **Add scoring-rule tooltips on card hover in Sushi Go!** (CG-0MLVZNSIO1QWM4HQ) — Completed. Parent epic that added generic scoring rule tooltips on hover. This work extends that feature to tableau cards and adds score contribution display.
- **Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover** (CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7) — Completed. Child task of the above; its AC explicitly included "Tooltip appears on pointerover for tableau cards". The current code has a gap: tableau cards do not receive tooltip callbacks, suggesting a possible regression from subsequent refactoring.
- **Standardize TooltipManager across all games + create gym scene** (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44) — Completed. Moved TooltipManager to shared `src/ui/`. This work may have refactored tooltip wiring and could be the source of the tableau tooltip regression.
- **Port sushi-go to use shared HandView & PileView components** (CG-0MPDWZGZF008E8BF) — Open. May affect how cards are rendered; coordinate if both are worked on concurrently to avoid merge conflicts.

## Related work (automated report)

- **Add scoring-rule tooltips on card hover in Sushi Go!** (CG-0MLVZNSIO1QWM4HQ): Parent epic that established the tooltip infrastructure for Sushi Go using `TooltipManager` with Phaser render mode. The current work extends this to tableau cards and adds per-card score contribution display.
- **Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover** (CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7): Child task of the epic above. Its AC explicitly required tooltips on tableau cards, which appears to have been lost during subsequent refactoring (likely the TooltipManager standardization or SLL migration). This work effectively re-achieves that AC with enhanced content (score contributions).
- **Standardize TooltipManager across all games + create gym scene** (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44): Standardized the TooltipManager in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`. May have introduced the regression that removed tableau card tooltip wiring.
- **Migrate Sushi Go scenes to SLL and core-engine layout helpers** (CG-0MPKEPV100064IUZ): Refactored Sushi Go scene layout, potentially affecting how tableau cards are rendered and where tooltip callbacks are wired.
- **Port sushi-go to use shared HandView & PileView components** (CG-0MPDWZGZF008E8BF): Open work item that restructures hand/pile rendering in Sushi Go. If worked on concurrently, will need careful merge coordination with this item since both modify card rendering code.
- **Add HUD status-bar tooltips for Coins, Reputation, and Score in Main Street** (CG-0MP2A0X0K007JRU4): Completed example of wiring tooltips with score/computed values using the shared TooltipManager, demonstrating the same pattern this work will apply.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the tableau card tooltip show only the current score contribution, or should it also include the general scoring rule text (from SCORING_TOOLTIPS)?" — Answer (user): "Both". The tooltip should show both the scoring rule text and the current score contribution.

- Q: "How to handle maki and pudding cards, whose scores depend on cross-player comparison or game-end scoring?" — Answer (user): "Rule only". For maki and pudding, show only the generic scoring rule text, not a numeric current score.

- Q: "Should tableau cards get the same hover highlight effect (stroke color change + slight scale-up) as hand cards, or remain static?" — Answer (user): "Same". Tableau cards should have the same interactive hover highlight as hand cards.

Problem statement

Sushi Go's round-end and game-over overlays display incorrect AI scores: the end-of-game pudding bonus/penalty is not being applied to the AI's displayed totals.

Users

- Players (human testers and QA): need overlays to show accurate final scores and breakdowns so they can trust game results and debugging information.
- Developers/Maintainers: need a reproducible bug report, tests, and a minimal, well-scoped fix to ensure scoring logic and presentation remain correct.

User stories

- As a player, when the game ends I want the final totals shown in the overlay to equal the actual computed final scores so I can see an accurate winner.
- As a QA engineer, I want unit tests that assert pudding scoring and score aggregation so regressions are prevented.
- As a developer, I want the overlay to display canonical computed values (not duplicated ad-hoc sums) so presentation bugs are avoided.

Success criteria

1. Pudding bonus/penalty is correctly applied to player.totalScore at game end for all players (measurable by unit tests asserting final totalScore changes when puddingBonuses are non-zero).
2. The round-end and game-over overlays display totals and breakdowns that exactly match the canonical computed values (result and session state) in all observed cases (verified by tests or deterministic reproduction steps).
3. Add unit tests that cover scorePudding and scoreRound behavior for representative cases including tie-splitting and fewest/most pudding scenarios; tests must pass in CI.
4. All related documentation and code comments that describe pudding scoring and overlay display behavior are updated accordingly.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Keep changes localized to Sushi Go example game code (example-games/sushi-go) unless evidence shows a core engine contract is broken.
- Changes must preserve existing public APIs and data structures used by tests and other example games.
- Avoid UI-only workarounds that duplicate scoring logic in the overlay; overlay display should read canonical computed values.

Existing state

- scorePudding(puddingCounts) exists and returns per-player bonuses (example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.ts).
- scoreRound(session) accumulates puddingCount per player and, at final round, computes puddingBonuses and adds them to players[i].totalScore.
- SushiGoOverlayManager.showRoundScoreOverlay and showGameOverOverlay assemble displayed lines from result.* fields and session.player totals. The overlay references result.puddingBonuses only in game-over overlay when present, but the reported bug indicates the AI's displayed total does not include the pudding bonus/penalty.
- Tests exist for scoring logic (tests/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.test.ts) and overlay browser tests (tests/sushi-go/SushiGoOverlay.browser.test.ts).

Likely root causes (inference)

- Overlay code may be reading stale/uncalculated values (e.g., using result.roundScores or session.totalScore before puddingBonuses are applied), or a mismatch between when scoreRound updates session.totalScore and when overlay is rendered.
- Possible off-by-one where puddingBonuses are applied after overlay construction, or overlay displays result.roundScores rather than session.totalScore for final totals.

Desired change

- Audit scoreRound and game flow to confirm puddingBonuses are computed and applied to players[].totalScore before overlays render.
- Ensure overlay rendering uses the canonical session.players[i].totalScore (after puddingBonuses are applied) and, where appropriate, also shows the per-player pudding bonus value from result.puddingBonuses to make the change explicit in the UI.
- Add unit tests that prove pudding bonuses are computed and applied, and that overlays display totals matching session state.
- If a timing/order bug is discovered, fix the order so scoring updates happen before overlays are constructed.

Related work (manual discovery)

- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.ts — Scoring helpers and functions: scoreTableau, scoreTableauBreakdown, countPudding, scorePudding, scoreMaki. Primary reference for scoring logic.
- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoGame.ts — Game orchestration and scoreRound() which invokes scoring functions and updates player.totalScore including pudding bonuses at game end.
- example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoOverlayManager.ts — Overlay rendering for round end and game over; reads RoundResult and session player totals to display scores. Primary suspect for presentation mismatch.
- example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoTableauRenderer.ts — Uses scoreTableauBreakdown for tableau display (may affect breakdown numbers shown in UI).
- tests/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.test.ts — Unit tests validating scoring functions, including scorePudding behavior.
- tests/sushi-go/SushiGoOverlay.browser.test.ts — Browser overlay test that exercises the game-over overlay; useful to extend to assert displayed totals match computed values.

Related work (automated report)

- CG-0MP1MVHB3000X9I0 — This work item (Scores are incorrect in the Sushi Go round end overlay). It reports pudding bonus likely missing from display.
- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.ts — Contains scorePudding implementation (most/fewest split, tie handling) used by game logic.
  Relevance: scoring logic already implemented and tested; any fix should reuse these functions.
- example-games/sushi-go/SushiGoGame.ts (scoreRound) — Calls scorePudding at game end and adds bonuses to players[i].totalScore.
  Relevance: this is the canonical place where pudding is applied; verify ordering relative to overlay rendering.
- example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoOverlayManager.ts — Builds overlay lines using result and session state; likely location where displayed totals diverge from session total.
  Relevance: fix may be in ensuring overlay reads session.players[i].totalScore after pudding application and/or uses result.puddingBonuses for clarity.
- tests/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.test.ts — Contains tests covering scorePudding expectations; useful to extend for failing cases if found.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope: Where have you observed the incorrect scores?" — Answer (user): "A - confirmed it is the pudding bonus/penalty that is missing". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Fix target: Should this work strictly correct a presentation bug in SushiGoOverlayManager (i.e., display wrong value), or should it include verifying and, if necessary, fixing the underlying scoring flow and adding tests?" — Answer (user): "C - Both presentation + scoring audit + tests". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Tests to add: Which tests do you require?" — Answer (user): "A - Unit tests (extend tests/sushi-go/SushiGoScoring.test.ts and add unit test for scoreRound behavior)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Open questions

- None remain; user confirmed scope and requirements.

CHANGELOG: planned code changes

- Audit and, if required, fix ordering in scoreRound/session update so puddingBonuses are applied prior to overlay rendering.
- Update SushiGoOverlayManager to display canonical totals and explicit pudding bonus lines in game-over overlay.
- Add unit tests verifying scorePudding and scoreRound final total application.
- Update any relevant docs or comments describing scoring and overlay behavior.

# Clearer token counts in Feudalism

## Problem statement

In the Feudalism game, resource token count numbers (showing how many oats, flax, wheat, barley, turnip, and mead tokens a player or the supply has) are rendered in black text (`#000000`) on top of colored token circles. On many resource colors, black text is difficult to read against the game's dark-themed background, reducing usability for players.

## Users

Players of the Feudalism game, particularly those who find the current black token count text hard to distinguish against colored token circles and the dark UI background.

### User stories

- As a player, when I look at the token supply or my hand, I want the token count numbers to be clearly readable so I can quickly assess available resources.
- As a player, I want the visual distinction between token count text, crop icons, and resource labels to be maintained so the UI remains clear and uncluttered.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Resource token count text (in the supply area, player token row, AI token row, and discard dialog) is rendered in white (`#ffffff`) instead of black (`#000000`).
2. Crop icon overlays on tokens remain rendered in their current color (black `#000000`), using a new dedicated constant (`RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR`).
3. Resource abbreviation and label text (bonus abbreviations on market cards, cost chip counts, bonus slot labels, patron requirement counts, action button token abbreviations) remains rendered in their current color (black `#000000`), using a new dedicated constant (`RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR`).
4. The `FeudalismAnimator.ts` card bonus abbreviation text is updated to use the new `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` constant.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- No new constant should be created for token count text color. The existing `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` constant is repurposed by changing its values to white.
- New constants should follow logical groupings (icon color vs. label/abbreviation color) to provide flexibility for future styling changes.
- Only the numeric count text color changes; all other UI text and icon colors remain unchanged.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** There may be a desire to rename the repurposed `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` constant or to adjust icon/label colors beyond the current change. *Mitigation:* Record any additional styling or refactoring opportunities as separate work items linked to this item, rather than expanding scope.
- **Visual readability of white text on light token colors:** White text on barley (yellow `#F0E442`) tokens may be less readable than black text. *Mitigation:* Manual visual verification should be performed after implementation; if white-on-yellow is problematic, consider a per-color approach for the token count text.
- **Assumption — constant name stability:** The `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` name remains unchanged (no rename needed per user guidance).
- **Assumption — icon appearance unchanged:** Crop icons rendered at 34% opacity with `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR` (`#000000`) will appear identical to the current rendering, since the color value is unchanged.

## Existing state

The `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` constant in `example-games/feudalism/scenes/FeudalismConstants.ts` maps each resource (`oats`, `flax`, `wheat`, `barley`, `turnip`, `mead`) to `#000000` (black). This single constant is used across three distinct visual purposes:

1. **Token count text** — numeric counts on supply tokens, player/AI token bubbles, and discard dialog (3 usage sites in `FeudalismRenderer.ts`)
2. **Crop icon color** — overlay icons drawn on token circles via `addCropIcon()` using `cssColorToNumber()` (4 usage sites in `FeudalismRenderer.ts`)
3. **Resource abbreviation/label text** — bonus abbreviations on cards, cost chip counts, bonus slot labels, patron requirement chips, action button abbreviations, and animator card labels (7 usage sites across `FeudalismRenderer.ts` and `FeudalismAnimator.ts`)

## Desired change

1. In `FeudalismConstants.ts`:
   - Change `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` values from `#000000` to `#ffffff` for all six resources (this makes token count text white).
   - Add a new `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR: Record<ResourceOrWild, string>` with all values `#000000`.
   - Add a new `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR: Record<ResourceOrWild, string>` with all values `#000000`.
2. In `FeudalismRenderer.ts`:
   - Import `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR` and `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` from `FeudalismConstants`.
   - Replace `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` with `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR` in the 4 `cssColorToNumber(RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR[...])` calls (crop icon color).
   - Replace `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` with `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` in the 6 label/abbreviation text references (bonus abbrev, cost chip count, patron chip count, bonus slot abbrev, action button abbrev, discard dialog bonus abbrev).
3. In `FeudalismAnimator.ts`:
   - Import `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` from `FeudalismConstants`.
   - Replace `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` with `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` for the card bonus abbreviation text.
4. In `CropIconRenderer.ts`:
   - Update the doc comment to reference `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR` instead of `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR`.

## Related work

- `example-games/feudalism/scenes/FeudalismConstants.ts` — Contains `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` and will host the new `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR` and `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` constants.
- `example-games/feudalism/scenes/FeudalismRenderer.ts` — All token rendering code consuming the color constants.
- `example-games/feudalism/scenes/FeudalismAnimator.ts` — Animation rendering with one usage of `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` for card bonus abbreviations.
- `example-games/feudalism/scenes/CropIconRenderer.ts` — Crop icon drawing logic with a doc comment referencing `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR`.
- "Add crop icons to resource tokens in Feudalism" (CG-0MM5KDA9E0QG6OKY) — Prior work that introduced crop icons using `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR`.
- "Replace gem materials with medieval Irish crops in Feudalism" (CG-0MM5KBHTD0Y5Q5JV) — Prior theming work that established the resource-to-crop mapping.

### Related work (automated report)

Worklog and repository search for "RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR", "token count", "readability", and "Feudalism display" found no additional related work items beyond those listed above. The work item has no existing dependencies (no inbound or outbound deps). The most closely related prior work is the crop icon introduction (CG-0MM5KDA9E0QG6OKY), which established the `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` usage pattern for crop icons — the current work item disentangles that pattern by separating count text, icon, and label colors.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should I change ALL elements that use `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` to white, or only the token count numeric text?"
  — Answer (user): "I only want the text colour to change. But I do not want to create a new constant for the text colour. Instead create a new constant for the other items. This need not be a single constant, if there are logical groupings go ahead and create multiple to add flexibility."
  — Final approach: Change `RESOURCE_TEXT_COLOR` to `#ffffff` (token count text), create `RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR` (crop icons, `#000000`) and `RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR` (labels/abbreviations, `#000000`).
  - Q: "Does the grouping into RESOURCE_ICON_COLOR (icons) and RESOURCE_LABEL_COLOR (labels/abbreviations) look correct?"
  — Answer (user): "yes"

# Intake Brief: Cards not updated when upgraded

## Headline Summary

When an upgrade is applied to a Business card in Main Street, the game state updates correctly but the card's visual display remains unchanged (no level badge, no income update, no appearance change). The rendering pipeline must be extended to display upgrade state (level, income bonus, visual distinction) on the street grid.

---

## Problem Statement

When a player uses an upgrade card on a business in Main Street, the game state updates correctly (level increases, income bonus applies, upgrade is tracked), but the card's visual display is frozen. The card continues to show the base card appearance with no indication of the upgrade — specifically, no level badge, no updated income/name display, and no visual changes. This creates a disconnect between what the game state reflects and what the player sees on screen.

## Users

- **Main Street players**: Expect to see visual confirmation when they apply an upgrade, including the new level, updated income calculations, and any visual distinctions from the base card state.
- **Developers**: Need a clear contract between the game engine (state) and the UI renderer (display) so that card upgrades are reflected in real time.

**User Story Example**: 
"As a player, when I upgrade a Bookshop to Level 2, I expect the card on the street grid to show a level badge ('Lvl 2'), an updated name (e.g., 'Library'), and the new income amount (+8 instead of +3). Currently, the card looks unchanged, making it unclear whether the upgrade actually took effect."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Level badge is displayed**: Upgraded cards display a visible level indicator (e.g., "Lvl 2", "Lvl 3") as an overlay or built into the rendered card.
2. **Income details are updated**: The card shows the combined base income + income bonus from all applied upgrades (e.g., "Income: +8" for a card with baseIncome=3 and incomeBonus=5).
3. **Card title/name reflects upgrade**: Upgraded cards display the upgraded card name or a visual indication that the card has been upgraded (e.g., badge, color change, border highlight).
4. **Visual distinction from base card**: An upgraded card is visually distinguishable from its base (non-upgraded) state through styling, badges, or other UI elements.
5. **Refresh triggers re-render**: After an upgrade is applied, `refreshStreetGrid()` re-renders the card with all updated display information. Tooltip/hover info also reflects the current level and combined income (baseIncome + incomeBonus).
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **SVG-based rendering**: Main Street uses SVG templates for card rendering, which are rasterized to textures. The rendering pipeline must support displaying level and income state without requiring separate SVG files for each level variant.
- **State-aware rendering**: The renderer must receive or access the full `BusinessCard` state (not just the base template ID) to display level and income information accurately.
- **Performance**: Card rendering must remain performant; avoid expensive re-rasterization for every render frame.
- **Backward compatibility**: Changes to the rendering system should not break existing upgrade logic or other card types (Event, Upgrade cards in market display).

## Existing State

**What works:**
- Upgrade purchase and application logic in `MainStreetEngine.ts` and `MainStreetMarket.ts` correctly updates game state (level, incomeBonus, appliedUpgrades).
- `refreshAll()` is called after each upgrade, which invokes `refreshStreetGrid()`.
- SVG card rendering system exists and uses cached textures for performance.

**What is broken:**
- The SVG rendering system (`mainStreetRenderCardSvg()`, `templateKeyForCard()`) does not have access to the full `BusinessCard` state; it only receives `cardId`.
- Card SVG sources are loaded from static files (`assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/${templateId}.svg`) and do not include dynamic level/income overlays.
- When `refreshStreetGrid()` renders a card, it passes only `biz.id` to the renderer, not the full card state (level, incomeBonus, appliedUpgrades).
- As a result, all instances of a card (base and upgraded) render the same way.

## Desired Change

Update the Main Street card rendering pipeline to **display upgrade state information** (level badge, updated income, visual distinction) when rendering `BusinessCard` objects on the street grid.

**Implementation approach:**
1. **Extend the renderer interface**: Modify `mainStreetRenderCardSvg()` or `refreshStreetGrid()` to pass the full `BusinessCard` state (not just the ID) to the rendering function.
2. **Add overlay rendering**: Either:
   - (Approach A) Generate a composite texture/overlay that includes the level badge and income details rendered on top of the base card SVG, or
   - (Approach B) Use code-based overlays (Phaser text/graphics objects) to render the level badge, income amount, and upgraded name on top of the card image.
3. **Update the template key logic**: Ensure that the texture cache key is distinct for different card states (base vs. upgraded) so that base and upgraded versions don't share the same cached texture.
4. **Test coverage**: Add unit tests to verify that card state changes (level, incomeBonus) are reflected in the rendered output.

**Related systems:**
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — already correctly updates card state
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts:refreshStreetGrid()` — entry point for card rendering
- `src/ui/Renderer/adapters/MainStreetAdapter.ts:mainStreetRenderCardSvg()` — renders individual cards
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — manages SVG-to-texture pipeline

## Related Work

- **CG-0MMJCMULS1SWMQZC** "Upgrade Cards: matching" — Completed; added 14 upgrade templates to MainStreetCards.ts. This work defined the upgrade system but did not address UI display.
- **CG-0MM4REC2Z0GS2YKT** "Main Street: PRD Milestone 2 -- Full Content and Crafting/Building System" — Completed; includes branching/multi-level upgrades specification.
- **CG-0MOJ5EWOI0080FQS** "Differentiate Main Street transfer SFX by card type and action" — Completed; added audio feedback for card actions including upgrades.
- **CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79** "Add visible game activity log to Main Street UI" — Completed; logs card actions (placements, upgrades, events) but does not address card display refresh.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

### Q1: What specific visual elements are not updating after an upgrade is applied?
**Answer** (user, interactive response): "All of them: (a) the card doesn't show a level badge, (b) the card doesn't show the increased income value, (c) the card appearance doesn't change visually, (d) the tooltip/hover info doesn't show updated stats."
**Evidence**: Playtesting observation — player applied an upgrade (e.g., Bookshop to Library) and the on-screen card did not change.
**Status**: Confirmed and actionable.

---

### Q2: When did you first notice this bug?
**Answer** (user, interactive response): "During playtesting the Main Street game."
**Evidence**: Discovered in live gameplay, not via automated tests or code review.
**Status**: Confirmed.

---

### Q3: Are there any reproduction steps or test cases that demonstrate this issue?
**Answer** (user, interactive response): "No existing test cases."
**Implication**: This is a new discovery; no regression tests exist yet. Any fix should include new tests to prevent recurrence.
**Status**: Test coverage needed as part of this work.

---

### Q4: Does the game state actually update correctly (e.g., do level, incomeBonus, appliedUpgrades increase)?
**Answer** (user, interactive response): "Yes, at least with respect to income."
**Evidence**: Inspection of game state confirms level increments and incomeBonus updates.
**Status**: Confirmed root cause is rendering, not game logic.

---

### Q5: Which card component needs updating?
**Answer** (user): "Unsure."
**Agent research summary**: Investigated the rendering pipeline:
- `refreshStreetGrid()` in MainStreetRenderer.ts calls `mainStreetRenderCardSvg(scene, container, biz.id, width, height)` — passes only the card ID.
- `mainStreetRenderCardSvg()` in MainStreetAdapter.ts delegates to `renderCardSvg()`, which checks for a cached texture based on template ID.
- `templateKeyForCard()` in MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts strips numeric suffixes and returns a key based only on the base card ID (e.g., "ms_card_bookshop").
- Card SVG sources are static files loaded once (`public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/{templateId}.svg`) and do not include level/income overlays.
- **Finding**: The rendering system needs to be extended to either (A) pass full card state to the renderer, or (B) generate state-aware keys/textures.
**Status**: Root cause identified; fix is in the rendering pipeline.

---

### Q6: What visual changes should an upgraded card display (badge, title/name, income details)?
**Answer** (user, interactive response): "All three: a level badge (e.g., 'Lvl 2'), an updated title/name (e.g., 'Library' instead of 'Bookshop'), and updated income details (e.g., '+8' instead of '+3')."
**Status**: Clear acceptance criteria established.

---

### Open Questions / Assumptions

**Assumption 1: One SVG template per card, state-driven rendering**
- The fix assumes the system should use one base SVG template per card and render level/income overlays dynamically (Approach A or B above), rather than creating separate SVG files for each level variant (e.g., bookshop.svg, bookshop-level2.svg, bookshop-level3.svg).
- **Rationale**: Reduces asset duplication and simplifies maintenance.
- **If this is incorrect**: Please clarify the preferred approach, and the implementation may need to pivot to asset-based level variants.

**Assumption 2: Tooltip/hover info is in scope**
- The acceptance criteria mention that tooltip/hover info should show updated stats. This implies the tooltip builder needs access to the current card state (level, incomeBonus, appliedUpgrades).
- **Current state**: Tooltips are built from `biz.name`, `biz.baseIncome`, and `biz.synergyTypes` in MainStreetRenderer.ts.
- **Required change**: Tooltip should show combined income (baseIncome + incomeBonus) and level.

**Assumption 3: Event and Upgrade cards in the market row do not need level badges**
- The upgrade system currently applies only to Business cards on the street grid, not to Event or Upgrade cards in the market. This fix focuses on Business cards in `refreshStreetGrid()`.
- **If incorrect**: The scope may expand to include upgrades/events in the market display.

---

## Risks & Mitigations

1. **Risk: Over-scoping to include all card types at once**
   - *Mitigation*: This work focuses on Business cards on the street grid only. If upgrades to Event or Upgrade card displays are needed, create separate child work items to track them independently.

2. **Risk: Performance regression from re-rasterizing upgraded card textures**
   - *Mitigation*: Cache textures keyed by card state (base + level). Avoid re-rasterizing on every frame; only update when state changes. Use code-based overlays (text/graphics) instead of SVG re-generation if performance testing shows concerns.

3. **Risk: Breaking existing card rendering for non-upgraded cards or other games**
   - *Mitigation*: All changes must remain backward-compatible. Ensure Event and Upgrade cards in the market continue to render correctly. Run full test suite before submitting.

4. **Risk: Unclear implementation approach (A vs. B)**
   - *Mitigation*: The implementation should document the chosen approach (composite texture vs. code-based overlay) in a comment or commit message. If the chosen approach proves inadequate, a follow-up work item can pivot to the alternative.

Headline

Extract a shared HUD layer abstraction into core engine and migrate all example games to use it for help, settings, game-over, and end-round overlays.

## Problem statement
HUD/sidebar/overlay layering is implemented inconsistently across games, with Main Street currently driving a targeted HUD-layer fix. Without a shared core abstraction, layering behavior and maintenance costs diverge across scenes.

## Users
- Players: need overlay/sidebar UI (help, settings, game-over, end-round) to consistently render above gameplay content.
- QA: need deterministic and reusable layering behavior across all games for regression verification.
- Developers: need one core-engine HUD-layer pattern to avoid per-game ad hoc depth/container logic.

## Success criteria
- A reusable HUD layer abstraction exists in core engine and is exposed via shared APIs used by game scenes.
- All games under `example-games/` are migrated to use the shared HUD layer for help, settings, game-over, and end-round overlays where present.
- No migrated game has overlay/sidebar UI rendering behind gameplay/card layers in normal play and end-state flows.
- Automated tests are added or updated to validate overlay/sidebar layering behavior on representative game scenes, including end-round overlays where applicable.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- This work item is dependent on Main Street: move overlay and sidebar UI to shared HUD layer (CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY).
- Migration scope is all games in `example-games/`.
- Required migration depth includes help, settings, game-over, and end-round overlays when a game provides them.
- Do not keep a temporary backward-compatibility path in `@ui`; update call sites directly to the new shared abstraction.
- Do not change game rules, scoring, or non-layering gameplay behavior.

## Existing state
- `CardGameScene` currently initializes HelpPanel and SettingsPanel directly (`src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`).
- Overlay primitives exist (`src/ui/Overlay.ts`, `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts`), but there is no single shared HUD layer contract adopted by all games.
- Main Street has an in-flight dependency focused on consolidating overlay/sidebar surfaces into a HUD layer (CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY).
- Multiple games still manage overlays independently in game-specific managers under `example-games/*/scenes/*OverlayManager.ts`.

## Desired change
- Extract and document a core-engine HUD-layer abstraction that provides a consistent top-layer container/ownership model for overlay/sidebar UI.
- Integrate the abstraction into shared scene foundations (`@ui` / `CardGameScene`) so help and settings attach consistently.
- Migrate all example games to use the shared HUD layer for modal and sidebar surfaces, including end-round overlays when those exist.
- Update/add tests and docs to validate and explain the new cross-game HUD-layer contract.

## Related work
- Main Street: move overlay and sidebar UI to shared HUD layer (CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY) — prerequisite dependency and source implementation intent.
- Extract MainStreetOverlayManager (CG-0MP0B51RK002C0EV) — prior modularization of Main Street overlays.
- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` — common scene entry point for HelpPanel/SettingsPanel initialization.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` and `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — reusable sidebar components that must adopt shared HUD layer semantics.
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` and `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` — existing shared overlay utilities to align with the extracted HUD layer.

## Related work (automated report)
- `CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY` defines game-level HUD-layer consolidation in Main Street and is the direct precursor for promoting the pattern into shared engine modules.
- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` is the highest-leverage integration point because it already centralizes help/settings initialization for many games.
- Existing overlay helpers (`src/ui/Overlay.ts`, `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts`) suggest the codebase already favors reusable UI primitives; this item extends that approach to container/layer ownership.
- Game-specific overlay managers across `example-games/*/scenes` indicate migration breadth and justify explicit acceptance criteria covering all games.

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: broad migration across all games can introduce regressions in input order, focus behavior, and overlay dismissal flow. Mitigation: require representative automated coverage and full-suite validation.
- Risk: some games may have scene-specific overlay timing/depth assumptions that conflict with a single abstraction. Mitigation: document game-specific deviations as linked follow-up work items instead of expanding this item’s scope.
- Risk: scope creep into non-layering refactors while touching many scenes. Mitigation: record additional opportunities as linked work items and keep this item focused on HUD-layer extraction/adoption.
- Assumption: CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY will provide a usable reference implementation pattern.
- Assumption: all target games can be migrated without introducing a temporary compatibility layer.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Scope of 'all games use it': A) all games currently under example-games/, B) only actively maintained games, C) other?" — Answer (user): "A". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Required migration depth: A) Help + Settings + end-game/modal overlays, B) Help + Settings only, C) overlay primitives only?" — Answer (user): "A + end round overlays if they exist". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Backward compatibility for game scenes: A) no compatibility layer; update call sites now, B) temporary compatibility path, C) no preference" — Answer (user): "A". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Main Street should support ending the turn with the Enter key through a configurable keybind, while preserving existing turn legality and preventing accidental triggers when overlays are open.

## Problem statement
Main Street currently requires mouse interaction with the End Turn button, which slows keyboard-first play. The game needs a keyboard shortcut so players can end turns faster without breaking existing phase/overlay safety.

## Users
- Players who prefer keyboard-driven interaction and faster turn pacing.
- Accessibility-minded players who benefit from reduced pointer reliance.
- QA/developers validating deterministic turn-flow behavior and shortcut configuration.

Example user stories:
- As a player, I want to press Enter to end my turn so I can play faster.
- As a player, I want Enter ignored when modal overlays are open so I do not accidentally end turns.
- As a player, I want this keybind configurable in global settings so it matches my preferred controls.

## Success criteria
- Pressing Enter ends the turn only when End Turn is currently legal (market phase / normal legality checks), matching existing button behavior.
- Enter is ignored while overlays/panels are open (including Help/Settings/game-over style blocking overlays).
- A global settings option exists to configure the End Turn keybind; default is Enter.
- Browser/integration tests verify keyboard end-turn path and non-trigger behavior with overlays open.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must preserve existing Main Street turn legality and phase checks; no forced end-turn from illegal phases.
- Must integrate with the existing settings/input architecture (global settings scope, not Main Street-only settings).
- Must not regress existing keyboard shortcuts used by Help/Settings panels.
- Scope control risk: any additional shortcut expansions (other actions, per-game custom mappings, key chord system) must be captured as follow-up work items rather than added to this item.

## Existing state
- End Turn is currently exposed as a clickable action button in Main Street renderer.
- Turn resolution and legality are centralized in Main Street turn controller/engine.
- Keyboard shortcut patterns exist in UI components (HelpPanel, SettingsPanel), but Main Street does not currently expose Enter-to-end-turn.
- No existing Worklog item appears to directly implement this exact shortcut.

## Desired change
- Add an End Turn keyboard shortcut handler in Main Street input flow.
- Gate shortcut execution behind the same legality checks as the End Turn button.
- Prevent shortcut activation when overlays/panels are active.
- Add global configurable setting for End Turn keybind with Enter as the default.
- Add regression tests for positive (turn ends) and negative (overlay open / illegal phase) cases.

## Related work
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — End Turn button behavior and action-row composition.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — canonical end-turn execution path and phase transitions.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — existing configurable keyboard shortcut patterns and panel keyboard handling.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — keyboard shortcut listener pattern and cleanup approach.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — browser-level interaction coverage suitable for keyboard shortcut regression tests.
- Buy investment opportunities (CG-0MMJN0E0F0N1HGH0) — related Main Street turn/market UX changes; useful prior context but not duplicate scope.

## Related work (automated report)

Headline

Rebalance Main Street tier progression by changing reputation-based unlock thresholds to an exponential curve starting at 8, while keeping challenge-based unlock paths unchanged.

## Problem statement
Main Street tier progression currently allows advancing through too many tiers in a single strong run. This makes campaign progression feel too fast and reduces long-term progression pacing.

## Users
- Players: need campaign progression to feel earned across multiple runs instead of being completed too quickly.
- Designers/Producers: need tunable progression pacing aligned with intended milestone difficulty.
- QA: need deterministic, testable tier-unlock behavior under updated thresholds.

## Success criteria
- Reputation thresholds are updated to exponential values: Tier 2 = 8, Tier 3 = 16, Tier 4 = 32, Tier 5 = 64.
- Challenge-based unlock conditions remain unchanged.
- End-of-run tier evaluation uses the new thresholds for future run evaluations without migration changes to existing saved campaigns.
- Automated tests are updated/added to validate new threshold behavior, including updates to any test-game fixtures/scenarios that assume old values.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- No migration of existing saved campaign data is required.
- Saved games should not be rewritten; only unlock evaluation behavior changes going forward.
- Existing challenge-based tier unlock logic must remain as-is.

## Existing state
- Current tier reputation thresholds in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTiers.ts` are: Tier 2 = 6, Tier 3 = 8, Tier 4 = 10, Tier 5 = 12.
- End-of-run unlock checks compare run reputation against `tierDef.reputationThreshold` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`.
- PRD references in `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` currently document the lower thresholds and expected unlock rates.

## Desired change
- Update `TIER_DEFINITIONS` reputation thresholds to 8/16/32/64 for tiers 2-5.
- Keep challenge unlock paths unchanged.
- Update tests and test fixtures/scenarios that rely on previous thresholds.
- Update Main Street milestone/progression docs to match the new thresholds and pacing intent.

## Related work
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTiers.ts` — authoritative tier threshold registry.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — tier unlock evaluation after each run.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — documented tier threshold behavior and progression targets.
- Main Street: include full expanded catalog in tier progression with ~10% available at Tier 1 (CG-0MP1VO5FM008LB5Z) — prior progression rebalance context.

## Related work (automated report)
- `MainStreetTiers.ts` is the direct source of truth for threshold numbers, so changing values there provides a narrow and auditable implementation point.
- `MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` evaluates unlocks using tier definitions, meaning threshold changes should take effect in run-end evaluation without save-data schema changes.
- `prd-milestone-2.md` includes threshold tables and expected unlock percentages that will become inaccurate unless updated in this same work item.

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: 32/64 thresholds may make reputation-path unlocks rare, shifting progression heavily toward challenge-path unlocks. Mitigation: document observed balancing concerns as follow-up work items rather than broadening this item.
- Risk: Existing tests/fixtures may fail due to hardcoded old thresholds. Mitigation: update tests/fixtures in-scope and keep changes focused on threshold expectations.
- Risk: Scope creep into broader economy/card rebalance. Mitigation: record additional balancing opportunities as linked work items instead of expanding this item.
- Assumption: challenge-path unlocks remain viable with unchanged conditions.
- Assumption: no save migration is required because thresholds are evaluated per completed run.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Should double required reputation apply exactly as Tier 2: 6→12, Tier 3: 8→16, Tier 4: 10→20, Tier 5: 12→24?" — Answer (user): "Make it exponential, starting at 8." Source: interactive reply. Final: superseded by follow-up clarification.
- Q: "Should challenge-based unlock paths remain unchanged?" — Answer (user): "A" (keep as-is). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should existing saved campaigns be migrated/reinterpreted?" — Answer (user): "No need to migrate saved games, but if we have test games these need to be updated." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "For exponential starting at 8, do you want Tier 2=8, Tier 3=16, Tier 4=32, Tier 5=64?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

data.description:
Main Street should automatically reshuffle discard piles into their corresponding decks when a draw/refill needs cards and the deck is exhausted, so gameplay continues without starvation.

## Problem statement
In Main Street, deck exhaustion can leave market or incident flows unable to refill from available discard history. The game should recycle discards by shuffling them back into the relevant deck when needed.

## Users
- Players: expect uninterrupted runs even after long sessions that deplete decks.
- Designers/balance testers: need realistic long-run card cycling behavior.
- QA/developers: need deterministic, testable refill behavior for exhausted decks.

Example user stories:
- As a player, when the Upcoming events source runs out, I want discards reshuffled so new incidents continue appearing.
- As a player, I want all Main Street decks to recycle discards so market rows can keep refilling.
- As a tester, I want empty deck + empty discard handled safely without crashes.

## Success criteria
- For all Main Street deck families (business, event, upgrade), when a draw/refill operation encounters an empty deck and non-empty matching discard pile, the discard pile is shuffled and reused as the new deck.
- Reshuffle occurs immediately at draw/refill time (not deferred to a later phase).
- If both deck and matching discard are empty, the game continues safely and leaves slots/queue entries empty as applicable (no crash/hang).
- Unit/integration tests cover each deck family exhaustion path and the empty+empty edge case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Scope includes Main Street only.
- Behavior must remain deterministic with seeded RNG.
- Must preserve existing turn-flow/phase semantics; only refill source behavior changes.
- Scope creep risk: additional balancing rules (e.g., weighted reshuffle, anti-repeat heuristics) must be tracked as separate follow-up work items, not added here.

## Existing state
- Main Street tracks per-family discard piles in game state.
- Refill functions currently draw from active decks and can leave rows/queues partially empty when decks are exhausted.
- Existing tests include no-starvation assertions in Monte Carlo and market tests, but intent now explicitly requires discard-to-deck recycling for all families.

## Desired change
- Add a shared reshuffle helper (or equivalent) used by market/incident refill paths.
- On draw/refill, if deck empty and discard non-empty, shuffle discard into deck using seeded RNG and continue drawing.
- Keep empty-safe behavior when both sources are empty.
- Expand tests to verify reshuffle invocation and resulting refill outcomes across business/event/upgrade and incident queue paths.

## Related work
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — refill logic for business/investments/incident queue and discard handling.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — deck/discard state model.
- `tests/main-street/market.test.ts` — refill behavior and empty-deck tests.
- `tests/main-street/market.integration.test.ts` — no-starvation Monte Carlo invariants.
- `tests/main-street/refresh-investments.test.ts` — discard pile population from market refresh flow.
- Monte-Carlo balance harness & CI assertions (CG-0MP1QZKGM0024T57) — related starvation guardrail context.

## Related work (automated report)
- `MainStreetMarket.ts` is the core implementation locus because it already centralizes refill behavior and is where deck-empty decisions occur for business, investments, and incident queue sourcing.
- `MainStreetState.ts` confirms discard piles are already first-class state, reducing migration risk and suggesting this is a behavior update rather than a data-model change.
- `tests/main-street/market.test.ts` and `market.integration.test.ts` already exercise refill/starvation paths and should be extended to make reshuffle behavior explicit and measurable per deck family.
- Work item CG-0MP1QZKGM0024T57 establishes starvation-related expectations in Monte Carlo, providing traceability for validating this bug fix against existing guardrails.

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: incorrect discard-family mapping could cross-contaminate decks. Mitigation: per-family tests and explicit mapping checks.
- Risk: RNG usage changes may affect deterministic test expectations. Mitigation: use existing seeded RNG pathways and update deterministic tests conservatively.
- Risk: scope creep into balancing/design changes. Mitigation: record any such ideas as linked follow-up work items.
- Assumption: current UI can tolerate temporarily empty slots/queue when both deck and discard are empty.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Which decks should auto-reshuffle from discard when empty?" — Answer (user): "A) All Main Street decks (business, event, upgrade)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "When should reshuffle happen?" — Answer (user): "A) Immediately when a draw/refill sees empty deck". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "If both deck and discard are empty, expected behavior?" — Answer (user): "A) Leave slot/queue empty and continue safely". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Headline

Add contextual tooltips to the top status bar (Coins, Reputation, Score) in Main Street to show expected income this turn, reputation influence on income, and next tier threshold.

## Problem statement
The status bar currently displays numeric Coins, Reputation and Score values but provides no contextual explanation. Players and QA need quick access to calculated projections (expected income this turn), reputation effects (coin multiplier), and progression context (next tier threshold) without navigating to overlays.

## Users
- Players: get immediate, contextual information to inform decisions (e.g., whether buying a business increases next-turn income enough to justify cost).
- QA and Designers: can verify projected income and progression cues visually during playtests.
- Developers: implement tooltip wiring using existing TooltipManager and HUD layout helpers.

## Success criteria
- Hovering (desktop) over Coins, Reputation, and Score in the HUD shows a tooltip with the following content (numeric values where applicable):
  - Coins: expected income this turn (pre- and post-reputation multiplier) and a brief note on how it was calculated (sum of business incomes + synergy).
  - Reputation: current reputation value and the active reputation coin multiplier (numeric, formula: 1 + rep / divisor capped at max), and a short explanation of its effect on income.
  - Score: current final-score estimate and the next locked tier ID and reputation threshold (e.g., "Next tier: tier-3 (requires Rep >= 16)").
- Desktop: tooltips appear on hover; Mobile: tapping the HUD value toggles the tooltip (tap again or elsewhere dismisses).
- Tooltips respect the global tooltips toggle in SettingsPanel (use TooltipManager / SettingsPanel.showTooltips).
- Tooltip strings are added to the i18n keyset (so they are localizable) and ARIA labels are added to each interactive HUD element for screen-readers.
- Tests: Add/adjust browser tests to assert tooltip appears on pointerover and displays expected content (unit tests may stub TooltipManager). Update any test fixtures referring to HUD layout if required.
- All related documentation and code comments updated. Full project test suite must pass.

## Constraints
- Use existing TooltipManager (`src/ui/Tooltip.ts`) and HUD creation points in `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` to attach interactive zones — do not implement a separate tooltip system.
- Keep content generation logic in scene-level helpers (avoid duplicating adjacency/income logic); reuse `computeIncome()` and `applyReputationMultiplier()` from `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`.
- Add i18n keys and ARIA `aria-label` strings; do not ship hardcoded English-only strings.

## Existing state
- HUD elements for Coins, Reputation, and Score are created in `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` (refreshHud()).
- TooltipManager is available and used in the scene (`s.tooltipManager`) and respects SettingsPanel.showTooltips.
- Income computation helpers exist in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`computeIncome`, `computeBusinessIncome`) and reputation multiplier in `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`.
- Tier definitions and thresholds are available in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTiers.ts`.

## Desired change
- In `MainStreetRenderer.refreshHud()` attach interactive zones to the coinText, repText, and scoreText objects. On pointerover/pointerout (desktop) and tap (mobile), call `s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()` with computed content.
- Compose tooltip content using: `computeIncome(s.state.streetGrid)`, `applyReputationMultiplier(...)`, and `TIER_DEFINITIONS` + `s.campaign?.unlockedTiers` to identify next locked tier.
- Register new i18n keys for each tooltip string and wire ARIA attributes to the interactive zones.
- Add browser tests in `tests/main-street/` to assert tooltipManager.show/hide is called with expected content and update any failing HUD layout tests.

## Related work
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — HUD creation and existing tooltip attachments.
- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — tooltip manager and DOM-based tooltip node.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — computeIncome(), computeBusinessIncome().
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — reputationCoinMultiplier, applyReputationMultiplier.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTiers.ts` — tier definitions and thresholds.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — initialises TooltipManager for the scene.

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Tooltip DOM placement may overlap or be clipped on small screens; mitigation: position tooltips relative to HUD and clamp to canvas bounds using TooltipManager.
- Risk: Additional DOM elements and i18n entries need review for localization; mitigation: add keys and request localization review in PR.
- Assumption: TooltipManager is available in all runtime environments (node tests guarded) and SettingsPanel expose `showTooltips` flag.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Which computed values should the tooltip show for each field?" — Answer (user): A) Coins: expected income this turn (numeric); Reputation: current rep and income multiplier effect (numeric); Score: current final-score estimate and next-tier threshold (numeric). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Interaction model (desktop vs mobile)?" — Answer (user): A) Desktop: hover shows tooltip; Mobile: tap toggles tooltip / second tap dismisses. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Accessibility / localization requirements?" — Answer (user): A) Add ARIA labels/readouts and include tooltip strings in existing i18n keys. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
