Headline

Create a standard, reusable HUD component library (help/settings sidebars, overlays, on-screen buttons, status bar) and extract it into the core engine. Implement components under src/ui and export them via the core-engine public API. Migrate all example-games to adopt the shared HUD components.

Problem statement

HUD, sidebar, and overlay UI is implemented inconsistently across example games. This leads to duplicated layering and depth code, inconsistent user experiences (dialogs rendered behind gameplay layers), and higher maintenance costs. A standardized, themeable HUD component library in the core engine will reduce duplication and ensure consistent layering and behavior across games.

Users

- Players: receive a consistent and reliable overlay and HUD experience (help, settings, round/game-over overlays, on-screen environment buttons).
- Developers: gain reusable, documented components to attach overlays into a single HUD container, reducing per-game ad hoc layering code.
- QA: can rely on consistent layering behavior across example games for regression tests.

User stories

- As a player, when I open Help or Settings during gameplay, the panel must render above gameplay content and block input to underlying elements until dismissed.
- As a developer, I can import HUD components from src/ui (exposed via the core-engine public API) and parent panels/buttons into the shared HUD container without per-game depth hacks.
- As QA, I can run automated scene tests that assert overlay z-order and input blocking works consistently across games.

Success criteria

- A reusable HUD component library is implemented under src/ui and exported via the core-engine public API (e.g. src/ui/index.ts and root barrel exports).
- HelpPanel, SettingsPanel, Overlay primitives, and on-screen UI buttons (Help/Settings/Menu) are available as reusable components with documented APIs.
- All games under example-games/ are migrated to use the new HUD components for Help, Settings, round overlays, and game-over overlays where present.
- Representative automated tests are added/updated to verify layering (z-order), input blocking, and overlay dismissal for at least three representative games (Main Street, Beleaguered Castle, and one other).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, README, relevant docs pages).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Implementation location: src/ui with public exports from the core-engine API (per user selection).
- Migration scope: all games under example-games/ (per user selection).
- Visuals: basic, themeable, production-ready visuals consistent with existing UI styles (buttons, spacing, colors).
- Do not change game rules, scoring, or non-layering gameplay behavior.
- This work item is a child of CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM and depends on the parent’s effort to finalize HUD-layer behavior (as a prerequisite reference): CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY is a direct precursor with in-progress implementation patterns.

Existing state

- Reusable UI primitives exist in src/ui (HelpPanel.ts, SettingsPanel.ts, Overlay.ts, OverlayManager.ts, HelpButton.ts, SettingsButton.ts).
- Several games (Main Street, Beleaguered Castle, etc.) create HUD surfaces on their own renderers (see example-games/*/scenes/*Renderer.ts).
- There is no single exported HUD component library in the core-engine that standardizes container ownership and layering semantics across games.

Desired change

- Implement a collection of HUD components under src/ui and expose them via core-engine public exports.
- Provide a lightweight, documented HUD container/ownership contract that CardGameScene and other shared scene foundations can use to parent overlays and buttons.
- Migrate all example-games to use the new components for Help, Settings, round overlays, and game-over overlays.
- Add/adjust tests that verify overlay z-order, input-blocking behavior, and dismissal flows.

Related work

- Parent work: Extract shared HUD layer into core engine and adopt across games (CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM) — overarching consolidation effort.
- Precursor: Main Street: move overlay and sidebar UI to shared HUD layer (CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY) — provides a reference implementation and in-progress migration for Main Street.
- Related feature: Add HUD status-bar tooltips for Coins, Reputation, and Score in Main Street (CG-0MP2A0X0K007JRU4).
- Code refs: src/ui/HelpPanel.ts, src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts, src/ui/Overlay.ts, src/ui/OverlayManager.ts, src/ui/HelpButton.ts, src/ui/SettingsButton.ts, src/ui/index.ts (expected new export barrel).
- Example usage: example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts, example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Migration may introduce regressions in input order, focus behavior, and overlay dismissal flows. Mitigation: add representative automated tests and smoke test manually for migrated games.
- Risk: Some games may expect scene-specific overlay timing/depth behavior that conflicts with a single abstraction. Mitigation: create follow-up work items for game-specific deviations rather than expanding scope here.
- Risk: Scope creep while touching many scenes. Mitigation: capture additional opportunities as linked work items and keep this item focused on component extraction and mechanical migrations.
- Assumption: The parent HUD extraction (CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM) and the Main Street precursor (CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY) provide usable patterns and/or reference code.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Implementation location and export model?" — Answer (user): "A". "Implement components as reusable UI modules under src/ui and export them via the core-engine public API." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Initial migration scope (which games to target first)?" — Answer (user): "A". "Migrate all example-games to use the new HUD components (full migration)." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Visual fidelity and theming preference?" — Answer (user): "A". "Provide basic, themeable, production-ready visuals consistent with existing UI components (buttons, spacing, colors)." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Appendix notes

- All three clarifying items were recorded during the intake interview. The user provided direct answers for all three questions; the third answer was confirmed as "A" (basic, themeable, production-ready visuals). The Appendix records the user's choices and can be updated if the user later changes preference.

Related-work (automated report)

- Search for HUD-related work items and code finds the parent item CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM and the Main Street precursor CG-0MP1TAZU5008OTJY; several UI modules under src/ui already exist and will be the primary extraction surface.

Stabilize the Vitest browser test harness by identifying and fixing the root cause of intermittent WebSocket disconnect errors that currently cause false-negative test failures in CI and local runs.

## Problem statement
`npm test` intermittently fails in the browser test project with a Vitest browser/WebSocket disconnect error despite assertions passing, creating non-deterministic red builds and blocking merges.

## Users
- Contributors and maintainers running local test suites before commits.
- CI/release maintainers who rely on deterministic browser-test outcomes for merge confidence.

User stories:
- As a contributor, I want browser tests to fail only for real regressions so I can trust local validation.
- As a maintainer, I want CI runs to be stable so that PRs are not blocked by infrastructure flakes.

## Success criteria
- Root cause is identified and documented with evidence pointing to the failing layer (Vitest harness, Playwright/browser lifecycle, test configuration, or project-side teardown/leak).
- A root-cause fix (not only a workaround) is implemented in repository code/configuration.
- `vitest run --project browser` passes in CI for 5 consecutive runs without the WebSocket disconnect error signature.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints
- Scope is this specific intermittent browser harness disconnect failure; avoid bundling unrelated browser-test refactors.
- The accepted outcome is root-cause remediation (user specified root-cause fix only).
- Respect existing Phaser/Vitest/Playwright stack and repository conventions.

## Existing state
- The work item currently captures failure excerpts and broad investigation ideas.
- Browser tests are configured in `vite.config.ts` with Playwright Chromium, `fileParallelism: false`, and a 30s timeout.
- Previous browser-flake incidents were addressed in completed work items, but this failure is treated as a new regression, not a duplicate.

## Desired change
- Add focused diagnostics and/or reproducibility tooling as needed to confirm root cause.
- Implement the minimal code/config changes that eliminate the disconnect failure mechanism.
- Keep acceptance evidence in this item (error signature eliminated in 5 consecutive CI runs plus passing full suite).

## Related work
- Intermittent browser test unhandled Phaser resolution null error (CG-0MOZQNA6T008GNW9) — prior intermittent browser-test incident; user confirmed current issue is a new regression, not duplicate.
- [test-failure] tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts :: only materializes purchased cards at destination after transfer animation completes desktop and narrow viewports — failing test (CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3) — historical CI test-failure tracking context.

## Risks & assumptions

Headline

Create an example "Gym" project containing multiple demo scenes that comprehensively showcase core-engine features, UI configuration options, and automated demo/playtest harnesses.

Problem statement

Engine features are proven within example-games, but there is no single, curated "Gym" that demonstrates every major core-engine capability in isolated, configurable scenes suitable for developer onboarding, QA playtests, and automated visual/functional smoke tests.

Users

- Engine developers: want easily runnable examples to validate APIs and to use as references when implementing new features.
- QA/test engineers: want deterministic demo scripts and headless replay for smoke testing and regression detection.
- Designers/Producers: want interactive scenes to validate UX, audio/feedback options and to produce demo recordings.

Example user stories

- As an engine developer, I can open the Gym and run a scene that demonstrates deck shuffling and seeded RNG, so I can verify deterministic behavior across runs.
- As a QA engineer, I can run an automated headless demo script that replays a short scenario and validates no errors are thrown.
- As a designer, I can toggle sound and feedback "juice" settings in a configuration scene and observe changes live.

Success criteria

1. A playable Gym application is delivered containing a scene for each major core-engine feature (deck management, card play, hand/pile management, overlays, seeded RNG/demo, undo/redo, transcript recording, save/load, SoundManager integration and visual/feedback configuration).
2. Each scene exposes a minimal UI that demonstrates configuration options (audio mapping, feedback intensity, seed input) and documents expected behavior.
3. Automated demo scripts exist for at least three representative scenes and can be run headless as Vitest smoke tests and pass deterministically with a fixed seed.
4. The existing HelloWorld example is removed or migrated: example-games/hello-world is replaced by the Gym scenes (HelloWorld assets/code migrated into appropriate Gym scenes or removed) and the repository contains no redundant HelloWorld scene after completion.
5. Comprehensive documentation is provided for the Gym: every scene must include a short per-scene README/usage snippet and in-code comments for public APIs, and a centralized Gym index page (docs or README) must link and summarise all scenes and how to run them.
6. A README and developer guide are added/updated explaining how to run the Gym, run headless demos, and how to add new scenes.
7. Full project test suite must pass locally and in CI with the Gym changes; any new tests are added to the tests/ tree.
8. All related documentation (code comments, README, docs site sections) is updated to reflect the new Gym.

Constraints

- Must reuse existing core-engine APIs; avoid duplicating engine code in example-games.
- Keep runtime dependencies and asset sizes modest so demo scenes run fast in CI (prefer lightweight SVG textures rasterised by existing helpers rather than large raster assets).
- Follow repository path aliasing and build conventions; examples should build with existing Vite + TypeScript config and not require special tooling.
- Compatibility: target modern browsers supported by the project and run headless in the existing Vitest environment.

Existing state

- Multiple example-games already demonstrate subsets of engine features (main-street, the-mind, sushi-go, golf, feudalism, lost-cities, beleaguered-castle, etc.).
- Core engine modules (SeededRng, SoundManager, TranscriptRecorder, UndoRedoManager, SaveLoad, SpatialRules) are available in src/core-engine and are used by existing example-games.
- There are existing PRDs and docs (docs/main-street/*, docs/core-engine/*) and previous demo/playtest scripts and visual smoke tests that can inform Gym content.

Desired change

Deliver a new example app (example-games/gym or example-games/gym-<name>) that includes:
- One scene per major engine feature with minimal but clear UI for demonstration and configuration.
- A configuration scene exposing sound mapping and feedback intensity.
- Headless/demo scripts and Vitest smoke tests for representative scenes.
- README and developer guide for running and extending the Gym.

Related work (automated report)

- CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO - Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (open): Main Street contains demo scripts, game-state code, and tests used as a precedent for deterministic demo scripts and playtest scenarios.
- CG-0MM4RD5I00L2QV7W - Main Street: PRD -- Playable Core Loop (completed): Shows integration patterns between example-games and core-engine; useful for scene structure and testing approaches.
- CG-0MO4LWXI00036V3T - Visual smoke tests & CI integration (completed): Provides guidance and examples for adding visual/functional smoke tests that are CI-friendly.
- docs/core-engine/spatial-rules.md (file): Documents SpatialRules in the core-engine; relevant for any scene demonstrating adjacency/pathfinding.
- docs/the-build/engine-capabilities-audit.md (file): High-level capability mapping showing which engine features should be demonstrated.
- example-games/* (directories): Existing example games (main-street, the-mind, sushi-go, golf, feudalism, lost-cities, beleaguered-castle) contain reusable scene patterns, demo scripts, and usage of core-engine APIs; they should be consulted and reused where appropriate.

Why related: These items contain concrete examples of scene structure, seeded RNG usage, transcript recording, demo scripts, and existing smoke-test patterns; they reduce duplication and provide a WBS seed for Gym scenes and tests.

Desired deliverables

- example-games/gym/* with per-feature scenes and a configuration scene.
- Headless demo scripts and at least three Vitest smoke tests.
- README and docs updates describing how to run, test, and extend the Gym.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Issue type: should this be an epic (coordinating multiple scenes / child tasks) or a single feature/task?" — Answer (user): "Epic". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Minimum viable scope (A: Minimal MVP, B: Medium, C: Full gym) — which do you want?" — Answer (user): "C" (Full gym). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Acceptance criteria & priority confirmations: include measurable acceptance criteria (playable scenes, automated smoke tests, docs updated) and confirm priority is high?" — Answer (user): "correct" (priority high and criteria accepted). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "One of the acceptance criteria should be the removal of the hello world scene. It should be replaced with these gym scenes." — Answer (user): "Yes". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Do the acceptance criteria include compreshensive documentation for all the gym scenes?" — Answer (user): "A" (Require comprehensive per-scene documentation: each scene gets a short README/usage + code comments and a centralized Gym index page linking them). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Scope creep (adding every possible feature may delay delivery). Mitigation: Treat extra features as separate child work items; prioritize a minimal per-feature scene set for MVP.
- Risk: Cross-game API changes may require refactors in multiple example scenes. Mitigation: Prefer adapters and reuse of @core-engine public APIs; include smoke tests to catch regressions early.
- Risk: Large assets or heavy rasterisation could slow CI and headless tests. Mitigation: Use lightweight SVGs and shared SvgHelpers; add test mocks where appropriate.
- Risk: Headless/demo tests may be flaky due to timing or browser differences. Mitigation: Use deterministic seeds, reduce reliance on frame-timing, add retries and clear assertions of state rather than visual pixel checks.

Assumptions

- Core-engine APIs used by the Gym (SeededRng, SoundManager, TranscriptRecorder, UndoRedoManager) are stable for the duration of this work. (If not, a spike/refactor child task will be created.)
- Existing example-games contain reusable patterns and demo scripts that can be adapted rather than rewritten.

Notes

- OPEN QUESTIONS: None at this time.

data.description:
Headline

Adopt a reusable, JSON-schema-backed "Screen Layout Language" (SLL) with TypeScript types and a runtime mapping layer so all games can define named screen zones and coordinates in a single, portable format. Port Main Street as the first canonical example and provide tests, docs, and a migration guide.

---

Problem statement

Current scene layouts are implemented ad-hoc across example games (per-scene computeLayout functions and per-game constants). This causes duplicated layout math, inconsistent coordinates across viewports and DPRs, brittle visual-regression tests, and friction when building reusable HUDs and overlays. We need a single, testable layout language and runtime that: (a) expresses named zones and coordinate anchors, (b) is serialisable (JSON Schema) and typed (TypeScript), and (c) maps to pixel coordinates at runtime respecting viewport size and DPR.

Users

- Game developers who author Phaser scenes and need consistent zone coordinates and helpers (e.g., Main Street, Golf, Lost Cities).
  - Example user story: "As a developer, I want to declare the Activity Log, Market and Street zones in a JSON layout file so I can reuse the same coordinates across scenes and tests."
- UI/UX designers and content authors who want to declare wireframes separate from code.
  - Example user story: "As a designer, I want a human-editable JSON layout that documents where UI chrome and the play area live at 1280×720 so I can propose visual changes without editing scene code." 
- Test/QA engineers who need stable anchors for visual-regression and browser tests.
  - Example user story: "As a QA engineer, I want normalized anchors so tests can assert overlay positions at multiple resolutions reproducibly."

Success criteria (measurable)

- SC-1: JSON Schema + TypeScript types committed under src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts and src/ui/screen-layout.ts, with at least 5 unit tests validating sample layout files.
- SC-2: Runtime mapping functions implemented (normalizedToPixels(layout, viewport, dpr) and pixelToNormalized) with unit tests that assert expected outputs for 1280×720 @ DPR=1 and 720×1280 @ DPR=2.
- SC-3: Main Street scene ported to consume SLL (layout file: example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json) and updated scene adapter implemented. All Main Street layout regression tests (tests/main-street/**) must pass.
- SC-4: A migration guide and developer docs are added: docs/DEVELOPER.md (Screen layout language section) and example-games/main-street/README.md updated to reference the new layout file.
- SC-5: At least one integration/browser test validates overlay and HUD alignment using the new layout system (e.g., a test that asserts Activity Log and End Turn button lie within expected bounds). All new/changed tests pass locally.
- SC-6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki/docs pages.
- SC-7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (npm test and npm run build succeed).

Constraints

- The SLL must be serialisable as JSON and accompanied by a JSON Schema for validation (per Q1=A). TypeScript types must be generated or hand-authored to match the schema.
- Coordinate model must be hybrid: primary representation in normalized units (0..1) with optional absolute pixel overrides for a zone or anchor (per Q3=C). The runtime must support DPR-aware scaling.
- Phaser-based rendering and existing helpers (layoutCardPositions, CardGameScene, PhaseManager) must remain compatible; provide adapters rather than forcing sweeping API changes.
- Backwards compatibility: scenes must be able to fall back to existing computeLayout() behaviour during migration to avoid breaking the whole test-suite at once.
- Scope per user decision: core library + port 1 representative scene (Main Street) as canonical example (per Q2=B). Do not port all example games in this work item.

Existing state

- Many scenes already implement per-scene computeLayout() functions and use constants in files like example-games/*/scenes/*Constants.ts (e.g., MainStreetConstants.ts).
- There are reusable helpers (src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts) and UI components (src/ui/*) that assume callers provide pixel sizes.
- Tests reference layout-dependent positions (browser and unit tests under tests/ and tests/*/**.browser.test.ts) and there are existing visual-replay tools that capture screenshots at 1280×720.
- The work item "Screen layout language" (CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ) already exists with a short description and is at stage=idea.

Desired change (high-level)

- Add a Screen Layout Language (SLL):
  - JSON Schema + example layout files stored under example-games/<game>/layouts/*.layout.json.
  - TypeScript types mirroring the schema (src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts or similar).
  - Runtime library (src/ui/screen-layout.ts) to parse, validate, and map normalized anchors to pixel coordinates using viewport and DPR. Provide utilities: getZoneRect(zoneName, viewport, dpr), anchorPoint(zoneName, anchor, viewport, dpr), and helper to migrate from existing computeLayout outputs.
- Provide an adapter for Main Street that reads example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json and replaces the ad‑hoc computeLayout in the scene with calls to the runtime mappings. Ensure a gentle migration path: if no layout file is found, fallback to existing computeLayout behavior.
- Add unit tests and an integration/browser test validating mapping and Main Street visuals.
- Add developer docs and a migration guide with examples.

Related work (automated report)

- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-1.md — Main Street PRD: contains explicit "Screen Layout and Zones" guidance, 1280×720 desktop + mobile stacking notes, and references to 2×5 street grid. Relevance: authoritative design doc for Main Street layout and the canonical sizes the SLL must support.

- docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md — Card canonical sizes and rendering rules (140×80 canonical market/street slot). Relevance: SLL must respect canonical card sizes and provide anchors suitable for these slots.

- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts and MainStreetConstants.ts — Current computeLayout implementation and SceneLayout interface. Relevance: shows where scene code consumes layout values and demonstrates required runtime APIs (get container positions, slotW/slotH, marketTop etc.). Primary port target.

- src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts — Existing reusable layout helper for horizontal card rows; SLL runtime should interoperate with or call this helper for row layouts.

- example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesMockScene.ts — Static layout mock used for validation and pre-render checks. Relevance: a prior example of a static layout file / mock which SLL can standardise.

- Worklog items:
  - CG-0MP2A64K8007B7EE — "Standard HUD components" (open): reusable HUD components and layout concerns that will benefit directly from SLL (can consume SLL-defined anchors).
  - CG-0MP0B51RK002C0EV — "Extract MainStreetOverlayManager" (completed): precedent for extracting overlay/layout logic as reusable modules; can guide adapter structure.
  - CG-0MLVOT2VY0DG9VLF — "Migrate canvas from 800x600 to 1280x720" (completed): lessons learned on coordinate migration and DPR handling.
  - CG-0MLVIWHC71H56V81 — "Splendor: Responsive full-screen layout" (completed): example of responsive layout considerations across games.

See also: developer docs (docs/DEVELOPER.md) and replay/screenshot tooling (scripts/replay.ts) which rely on stable layout/anchors for screenshot capture and thumbnail generation.

Risks & mitigations

- Risk: Porting scenes may introduce visual regressions and break browser tests. Mitigation: Port Main Street only as the canonical example, provide a runtime fallback to existing computeLayout, and run the full test suite (unit + browser) as a blockade to merging.
- Risk: Tests or scene code rely on absolute pixel values baked into logic. Mitigation: Provide a hybrid model with optional pixel overrides; include migration notes for updating tests to assert anchor-relative bounds instead of exact pixels where appropriate.

# Adapt tutorial system to use layout description

**Headline:** Refactor the Main Street tutorial highlight system to resolve zone bounding boxes directly from the Screen Layout Language (SLL), extending SLL with optional dimension support and a dedicated tutorial layout file, replacing hardcoded pixel-math.

## Problem statement

The Main Street tutorial system (`MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`) uses hardcoded pixel-math in a `zoneToAnchor()` method that manually computes highlight bounding boxes from `scene.layout` fields. This duplicates layout logic and prevents the tutorial from directly leveraging the Screen Layout Language (SLL) that Main Street's primary scene already uses. Several tutorial-specific screen zones (HUD strip, help button, investments row) have no SLL equivalents, making them unreachable from the layout system.

## Users

- **Game/scene developers** who need to maintain or modify tutorial highlight positions without editing pixel-math code.
  > *Example:* "As a developer, I want to adjust the HUD highlight area for the tutorial by editing an SLL layout file rather than tweaking pixel offsets in `zoneToAnchor()`."
- **Tutorial content authors** who want to adjust which screen areas are highlighted for each step.
  > *Example:* "As a content author, I want to change the highlighted zone for T3 from the full market area to just the business row by updating layout JSON."
- **QA/test engineers** who need stable, SLL-validated zone definitions for tutorial regression tests.
  > *Example:* "As a QA engineer, I want tutorial highlight zones resolved through the same SLL pipeline so tests can assert consistent bounds across viewport sizes."
- **Players** who get consistent highlight box positions aligned with actual scene layout across viewport sizes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A separate tutorial-specific layout file is created at `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` defining zones for all tutorial highlight areas, including those not in the base SLL layout (HUD strip, help button, investments row).
2. The SLL `NormalizedRect` type and JSON Schema are extended with optional `w` (width) and `h` (height) dimension fields to support bounding-box zones (backward-compatible, optional fields).
3. `MainStreetTutorialHints.zoneToAnchor()` is refactored to use direct SLL `getZoneRect()` / `anchorPoint()` calls, removing hardcoded pixel-math. Zone resolution uses `composeResolvedLayouts` to merge the base Main Street layout with the tutorial layout.
4. The `TutorialHighlightZone` type in `TutorialFlow.ts` is updated to align with new SLL zone names.
5. All existing tutorial behavior remains unchanged: same T1-T10 steps, same controls, same visual appearance and positioning (verified via existing tests).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test` and `npm run build` succeed).

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility:** Existing tutorial steps (T1-T10), their order, controls, and visual appearance must remain unchanged.
- **SLL schema evolution:** Adding w/h to `NormalizedRect` must be backward-compatible via optional fields. Existing SLL consumers must not break.
- **Phaser compatibility:** The SLL runtime and rendering pipeline must remain compatible with existing Phaser scene setup and existing `SceneLayout` consumers.
- **No gameplay changes:** Do not modify game mechanics, card economy, or turn logic.
- **Existing compose infrastructure:** Use the existing `composeResolvedLayouts` utility for merging base and tutorial zones, rather than inventing a new composition strategy.
- **No scope expansion:** This item is limited to tutorial highlight zone migration. Tutorial i18n/localization (CG-0MP415DUV0032SKK) is independent and out of scope.

## Existing state

- SLL is fully implemented with:
  - `src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts` — JSON Schema + TypeScript types (`NormalizedRect` is position-only x,y)
  - `src/ui/screen-layout.ts` — runtime mapping (`getZoneRect`, `anchorPoint`, `normalizedToPixels`, `adaptLayoutWithFallback`)
  - `src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts` — `composeResolvedLayouts` for merging base + scene layouts with three policies
  - `src/ui/index.ts` — public API exports
  - `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — canonical Main Street layout with 8 zones (position-only)
- Main Street scene uses SLL via `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, populating `SceneLayout` from SLL anchor points
- Tutorial (`MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`) accesses layout through `scene.layout` fields and `zoneToAnchor()` uses hardcoded pixel-math per zone:
  - `hud` — `{ x: 0, y: l.hudY - 14, w: l.gameW, h: 28 }`
  - `market-business-row` — computed from `l.marketTop`, `MARKET_BUSINESS_SLOTS`, `l.marketCardW`, etc.
  - `street-grid` — computed from `l.streetTop`, `l.slotH`, `STREET_COLS`, etc.
  - `end-turn-button` — computed from `l.actionY`, `l.actionButtonW`, etc.
  - `incident-queue` — computed from `l.queueTop`, `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE`, `l.queueCardW`, etc.
  - `investments-row` — computed from `l.marketTop + l.marketRowH + l.marketRowGap`, etc.
  - `help-button` — hardcoded `{ x: l.gameW - 120, y: l.actionY - 4, w: 100, h: l.actionButtonH + 8 }`
  - `center-modal`, `completion-modal` — return null (centered, no highlight rect needed)
- Only zones `market`, `incidentQueue`, `street`, `endTurnButton` exist in SLL with partial overlap to tutorial zones. No SLL zones for `hud`, `help-button`, `investments-row`.

## Desired change

1. **Extend SLL schema** (`NormalizedRect` / `ScreenLayoutZone` / JSON Schema) with optional `w` and `h` fields for zone dimensions.
2. **Create tutorial layout file** `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` with bounding-box zones: `hud`, `marketBusinessRow`, `streetGrid`, `endTurnButton`, `incidentQueue`, `investmentsRow`, `helpButton`.
3. **Refactor `MainStreetTutorialHints.zoneToAnchor()`** to resolve the highlight zone's rect and anchor via `composeResolvedLayouts(baseLayout, tutorialLayout, viewport)` instead of manual pixel-math.
4. **Update `TutorialHighlightZone` type** to align zone names with new SLL tutorial zone IDs.
5. **Update tests** — existing tutorial tests must pass; add tests for new SLL zone resolution path.
6. **Update documentation** — note the tutorial layout file, schema extension, and usage pattern.
7. **No changes to** `TutorialFlow.ts` step definitions, `TutorialState.ts`, or tutorial persistence logic.

## Related work

- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** — "Screen layout language" (completed, parent work item that created SLL). Explicitly recorded the tutorial migration as a follow-up.
- **CG-0MPENWRBO0051ZQT** — "Port Main Street to SLL" (completed, dependency). Main Street scene now uses SLL; this item depends on that being complete.
- **CG-0MP415DUV0032SKK** — "Main Street tutorial localization and i18n externalization" (open, independent). Moves tutorial text to i18n resources. Independent scope from this item.
- **CG-0MPLR9CW0009G7IN** — "Main Street Milestone 5: action-gated tutorial flow" (completed). Implemented the T1-T10 action-gated tutorial controller and step definitions.
- **`src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts`** — Existing `composeResolvedLayouts` utility that can merge base + tutorial layout zones.
- **`example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json`** — The base Main Street SLL layout that the tutorial layout will complement.

## Assumptions

- The existing `composeResolvedLayouts` utility can be reused without significant modification to support dimensioned zones.
- Tutorial highlight position deltas (compared to current zoneToAnchor math) within 1-2px at 1280x720 @1x are acceptable.
- The existing Main Street tutorial tests in `tests/main-street/` are sufficient to detect regressions in tutorial behavior.
- No changes to the `ScreenLayoutDocument` version number (v1) are required; the optional w/h fields maintain backward compatibility.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Risk: Schema extension could break existing SLL consumers.** Mitigation: Add `w`/`h` as optional fields. Existing consumers continue to see only `x`/`y`. Add tests for backward compatibility.
- **Risk: Tutorial highlight box positions may shift compared to current pixel-math values.** Mitigation: Compare new SLL-resolved bounding boxes against current zoneToAnchor outputs during development. Add a regression test that captures expected bounds for at least the primary viewport.
- **Risk: composeResolvedLayouts may not handle dimensioned zones correctly.** Mitigation: Review composeResolvedLayouts and normalizedToPixels to ensure they respect optional w/h fields; add test coverage.
- **Risk: Scope creep — adding unrelated tutorial improvements.** Mitigation: Record any discovered improvements (e.g., animation polish, zone animation hooks) as separate work items linked to this item rather than expanding scope.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** — "Screen layout language" (completed). Parent work item that created the SLL schema, runtime, and composition utilities. Explicitly scoped tutorial migration as a follow-up item, making this the canonical next step.
- **CG-0MPENWRBO0051ZQT** — "Port Main Street to SLL" (completed). Direct dependency: Main Street scene now uses SLL via `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, which this item extends with tutorial-specific zones.
- **CG-0MPLR9CW0009G7IN** — "Main Street Milestone 5: action-gated tutorial flow" (completed). Implemented the T1-T10 tutorial step definitions, `TutorialHighlightZone` type, and `zoneToAnchor()` pixel-math that this item refactors.
- **CG-0MP415DUV0032SKK** — "Main Street tutorial localization and i18n externalization" (open, independent). Touches the same tutorial system but targets text/copy externalization, not layout resolution. Must remain non-overlapping scope.
- **CG-0MPENWQFT008YV9I** — "Implement SLL schema and typing" (completed). Created the `NormalizedRect` and `ScreenLayoutZone` types that this item will extend with optional w/h dimensions.
- **CG-0MPENWQVC0046ORZ** — "Implement layout mapping runtime" (completed). Created `normalizedToPixels`, `getZoneRect`, `anchorPoint` — the APIs this item will use for direct SLL zone resolution.
- **CG-0MPZU9T8C005AO4U** — "Fix tutorial highlight overlay bounding boxes for HUD and market rows" (completed). Previous fix for the same `zoneToAnchor()` code, confirming the pixel-math fragility this item addresses.
- **CG-0MPXX1S2W006JNB4** — "Main Street tutorial overlay missing text and unresponsive" (completed). Bug fix in tutorial overlay rendering, demonstrating the operational risk of the current hardcoded approach.
- **CG-0MPKEQBOM001NJIQ** — "Clean up Main Street layout adapter to remove fallback pattern" (open). Potential follow-up after SLL tutorial integration is complete.
- **CG-0MOY5TOJK008JFJM** — "Main Street Milestone 5" (completed). Parent milestone that delivered the tutorial state, persistence, and flow this item builds upon.

### Related docs & source files

- **`src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts`** — SLL type definitions (`NormalizedRect`, `ScreenLayoutZone`, `ScreenLayoutDocument`) and JSON Schema. Target of the dimension-extension change.
- **`src/ui/screen-layout.ts`** — SLL runtime mapping functions (`getZoneRect`, `anchorPoint`, `normalizedToPixels`, `adaptLayoutWithFallback`). APIs the tutorial will use directly.
- **`src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts`** — `composeResolvedLayouts` utility for merging base + scene layouts. Will compose the Main Street base layout with the tutorial layout.
- **`src/ui/index.ts`** — Public API exports for SLL types and functions. Must be updated if new exports are needed.
- **`example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json`** — Canonical Main Street SLL layout (8 position-only zones). The tutorial layout will complement this file.
- **`example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`** — Tutorial overlay manager with `zoneToAnchor()` pixel-math. Primary target of refactoring.
- **`example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts`** — Tutorial step definitions and `TutorialHighlightZone` type. Will need type alignment with new SLL zone names.
- **`example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`** — Existing SLL adapter for Main Street. Reference implementation for SLL API usage pattern.

### Dependencies

Options: A) Leave adapter-mediated, B) Make tutorial call SLL APIs for existing zones, C) Both B + add missing tutorial zones to SLL layout" — Answer (user): "C". Source: interactive reply. Final: accepted.

Summary:
When the Main Street TF runtime synth module (build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs) is not present the browser console shows a 404 and noisy errors. This should be handled gracefully so the game works without generated TF modules and emits a clear, debuggable log message.

User story:
As an operator, I want the game to continue working if the TF synth module cannot be loaded (404), and for the code to log a clear non-fatal warning, so missing generated assets do not produce noisy failures or leave the player without an explanation.

Expected behaviour:
- If the TF module fetch fails with 404 or any network error, the loader should catch the error, log a single informative warning, and continue without TF synth support.
- No exceptions should bubble to the console other than the single warning.
- Any code that attempts to use the missing synth should detect absence (null) and continue gracefully.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Add a robust fetch/catch path in example-games/main-street/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts that returns null on any load failure and logs a clear message.
2. Update callers (MainStreetLifecycleManager) to handle a null module without logging stack traces or triggering repeated console errors.
3. Add unit tests for the loader: simulate 404 and network failure and assert loader returns null and no uncaught errors are thrown.
4. Add an integration test that runs Main Street with missing TF module and asserts scene boots and tutorial overlay logic unaffected.
5. Add a short note in docs/DEVELOPER.md explaining how to generate TF synths and that missing synths are non-fatal.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the dev server without generating TF synths (or remove build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs).
2. Open Main Street in browser devtools and observe 404 and WebGL errors.

Suggested implementation approach:
- Modify loadMainStreetTfModule() to catch import errors and return null; emit console.warn once (include URL and error). Optionally use a central logger abstraction.
- Ensure getMainStreetTfModule() returns null by default and callers check for null before use.
- Add tests mocking dynamic import failure (or reject the promise) and verify null return.

Issue type: chore
Priority: critical

# Headline
Implement Phaser-native SVG card rendering for Main Street so card visuals remain visible and correctly occluded by Help/Settings overlays without relying on `svgDom` hide/show workarounds.

## Problem statement
Main Street still uses DOM/SVG card rendering (`scene.svgDom`) for several card paths, which sits above the Phaser canvas and forces Help/Settings panels to hide DOM cards while open. This creates visual disappearance behavior and inconsistent layering compared with canvas-native UI overlays.

## Users
- Players opening Help/Settings during gameplay who expect cards to remain visible behind overlays.
  - User story: As a player, I want card visuals to remain present while overlays open so UI behavior feels stable and predictable.
- Developers maintaining Main Street and shared UI overlays.
  - User story: As a developer, I want card rendering to follow Phaser depth/layer rules so overlay behavior does not depend on DOM-specific visibility toggles.

## Success criteria
- Help and Settings overlays visually occlude card visuals while cards remain present in-scene (not hidden/removed), verified in browser tests.
- Manual `svgDom.setVisible(false/true)` calls are not required for normal production overlay behavior.
- Rasterization uses keyed texture reuse (per card variant/size/DPR) and avoids unnecessary regeneration during steady-state rendering.
- Main Street card rendering keeps acceptable fidelity versus current visuals at default resolutions and on resize/device DPR changes.
- Validation and safety gates: `npm test` and `npm run build` both pass after changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the rendering-path changes, including developer docs and relevant in-code comments.

## Constraints
- Must preserve existing gameplay and interaction behavior (card selection/hit areas remain functional).
- Must support fallback behavior in environments where rasterization is unavailable or constrained (tests/SSR/headless cases).
- Must respect canonical Main Street card dimensions/aspect guidance (`140x80`, fit-inside rendering expectations).
- Must keep scope bounded to rendering/layering behavior; additional unrelated UI refactors should be tracked as separate work items.

## Existing state
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` explicitly hide/show `scene.svgDom` when side panels open/close.
- Main Street already has SVG texture helpers and a scene texture manager (`SvgTextureHelpers`, `MainStreetSvgTextureManager`) that rasterize SVG into Phaser textures for some display paths.
- DOM renderer (`SvgDomRenderer`) remains in use for some card flows (notably hand-held event path coverage in existing browser tests).
- Browser tests currently include expectations tied to DOM image visibility changes when overlays open.

## Desired change
Unify Main Street card display on Phaser-native textures/GameObjects for production rendering paths so overlay depth ordering works naturally through Phaser containers/depth. Keep a controlled fallback path for unsupported environments, migrate or update tests that currently encode DOM hide/show behavior, and document the final rendering strategy and cache behavior.

## Related work
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Contains current `svgDom` hide/show behavior that causes card disappearance during panel open.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — Mirrors SettingsPanel hide/show behavior and must align with final layering strategy.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — Existing rasterization/cache orchestration that can be extended rather than replaced.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/SvgDomRenderer.ts` — Current DOM rendering implementation and likely fallback path boundary.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/SvgTextureHelpers.ts` — Core helper for data-URI rasterization and texture keying (`ms_card_*`).
- `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts` — Encodes current DOM visibility expectations; needs revision to validate native layering outcomes.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetSvgSmoke.browser.test.ts` — Confirms rasterized SVG texture generation; useful guardrail for migration.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-4.md` — Documents intended SVG-to-texture runtime path and visual polish expectations.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — Defines canonical dimensions and rendering constraints relevant to fidelity checks.
- Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY) — Historical context for the SVG texture strategy and visual acceptance intent.
- Main Street: PRD Milestone 6 -- Engine Component Extraction and Refactoring (CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC) — Relevant precedent for extracting stable rendering helpers into shared engine modules.

## Risks and assumptions
- Risk: Browser/headless differences in image decode/raster APIs can cause flaky tests.
  - Mitigation note: keep fallback path and prefer assertions against rendered output/state rather than implementation-only internals.
- Risk: Scope creep into broader UI/animation polish while touching overlays.
  - Mitigation note: record non-essential enhancements as linked follow-up work items instead of expanding this item.
- Risk: Texture cache invalidation on resize/DPR changes may cause stale or blurry assets.
  - Mitigation note: explicitly define cache key strategy and regeneration triggers in implementation/docs.
- Assumption: Existing `ms_card_*` texture key conventions and helper APIs are stable enough to reuse.
- Assumption: Critical user pain is layering/visibility correctness, not pixel-perfect art parity.

## Related work (automated report)
- Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY): establishes the intended SVG->texture runtime path and acceptance context for visual layering polish.
- Main Street: PRD Milestone 6 -- Engine Component Extraction and Refactoring (CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC): provides precedent for extracting reusable rendering support from Main Street into shared engine modules.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`: direct source of current `svgDom` visibility toggles; these files are primary change points for removing DOM-dependent overlay behavior.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` and `example-games/main-street/scenes/SvgTextureHelpers.ts`: existing rasterization and texture keying foundation that reduces implementation risk by reusing proven helpers.
- `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`: current behavior-based tests that will need migration from DOM visibility assertions to canvas layering assertions.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`: canonical rendering constraints (aspect ratio, fit-inside rules, derived sizes) that must remain true after migration.

- npm test and npm run build pass.

Implementation notes:
- Review Main Street SVG handling patterns for fallback and async texture lifecycle.
- Ensure setTexture calls only occur when texture is ready (await promise if needed) and always re-apply setDisplaySize after texture swaps.

Minimal implementation notes

- Add a small wrapper in GymRouterScene.createSceneCard() to call runSceneTransition({scene: currentScene, mode:'exit', type:'slide'|'fade', reducedMotion: <from SettingsStore>}) before calling scene.start(target).
- Add a simple hook to GymSceneBase (e.g., protected runEnterTransition(type?:..., duration?:...)) so scenes can call runSceneTransition on their own entry.
- Tests: headless test toggles reduced-motion and asserts router -> scene navigation completes without throwing.

Deliverables

- Edits to GymRouterScene.ts and GymSceneBase.ts
- Tests under tests/gym/ for router navigation with/without transitions
- README snippet documenting transition options and how to disable them for deterministic headless runs

Notes

- Keep the default behavior conservative (no transition) or only run transitions when a new "Animate transitions" setting is enabled so default smoke tests are unaffected.

Summary

Provide a canonical set of standard playing-card SVG assets (52 face cards + 1 back design) and wire them into the Gym graphics scenes so that:
- Face-down cards render the card back.
- Flips swap between face and back textures.
- Scenes load assets reliably in browser builds and have a headless-safe fallback for tests.

Acceptance criteria

1. Assets: 52 face SVGs + 1 back SVG are present under public/assets/cards/svg/ with permissive license (CC0/MIT) and documented in example-games/gym/README.md.
2. Texture keys: scenes can load cards with keys such as "cards/AS", "cards/10H", and a back key such as "cards/back".
3. Face-down card rendering: animations and helpers (flipCard, dealCard, placeCard, discardCard) use the back texture for face-down cards and swap to face textures when revealed.
4. Headless tests: a lightweight runtime fallback is used in headless/test environments so tests do not fail due to SVG/canvas rasterization issues.
5. Tests: add unit/browser tests that verify deck loads, face vs back rendering, flip shows correct face/back, and Save/Load snapshots remain functional.
6. Docs: README and GYM_INDEX.md updated to reference assets and attribution.

Implementation plan

- Create a small generation script (scripts/generate-card-svgs.js) that emits 52 face SVGs and a back.svg using a simple, classic layout (French suits, corner pips, 2:3 aspect ratio). The script will be deterministic and configurable (size/viewBox).
- Run the generator and place committed SVGs at public/assets/cards/svg/. Include a short credit/license file public/assets/cards/CREDITS.md (CC0/MIT).
- Update Gym scenes bootstrap (GymSceneBase or a new helper) to register/load card SVGs as Phaser textures at scene preload/start (texture keys prefixed with "cards/").
- Ensure flipCard/deal/place/discard use card texture keys and show "cards/back" for face-down.
- Implement a headless/test fallback: Option A (preferred) — a lightweight runtime placeholder texture when running in headless/test env (no native deps). Option B (optional) — pre-rasterize PNG fallbacks at build time using puppeteer/sharp (heavier, not preferred unless requested).
- Add tests and update docs.

Estimate & preference

- I will proceed with Option A (runtime placeholder for headless) unless you request pre-rasterized PNGs (Option B).
- Estimated effort: Small — ~2-6 hours. Risk: Low.

Notes

- If you prefer a specific card art style or back pattern (colour), tell me now; otherwise I'll use a clean classic black/red pip style with a simple patterned back in a neutral colour.

# Refactor Gym Scenes — Standardize Features via `src/ui/` Shared Code

## Problem Statement

Gym demo scenes repeat common rendering patterns (event log rendering, deck grid rendering, slider setup) across multiple files. Extracting these into shared utilities under `src/ui/` reduces duplication, ensures consistent behavior, and simplifies maintenance.

## Users

- **Engine maintainers**: Want Gym scenes to be maintainable and consistent without repeating common rendering patterns.
- **Game developers**: Want reusable utilities to build new scenes quickly using proven patterns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new shared utility module `src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts` is created, exported via `src/ui/index.ts` barrel, and contains extracted helpers: at minimum `createEventLog` and `createDeckGrid`.
2. Each of the 13 Gym scenes imports and uses at least one shared utility from `src/ui/` to replace duplicated logic.
3. No duplicated event-log-rendering or deck-grid-rendering code remains across gym scenes.
4. Unit tests for the new `src/ui/` utility modules exist, are placed in the `tests/` tree, and pass.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes: `npm run build` succeeds and `npm test` passes with no regressions.
6. `example-games/gym/README.md` is updated to document the shared utilities and how to use them in new scenes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Extracted code goes to `src/ui/`, not `src/core-engine`.
- All 13 gym scenes must be targeted: `GymAudioFeedbackScene`, `GymDeckRngScene`, `GymGraphicsLightingSpikeScene`, `GymGraphicsShaderSpikeScene`, `GymHandPileScene`, `GymOverlayUiScene`, `GymRouterScene`, `GymSaveLoadScene`, `GymSllScene`, `GymTooltipScene`, `GymTranscriptScene`, `GymUndoRedoScene`.
- Independent of sibling work item CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I ("Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components").
- Preserve existing behaviour — from a player perspective, scenes remain functionally identical.

## Existing State

- `GymSceneBase` already provides common scaffolding: `initHeader()`, `initReducedMotion()`, `addDivider()`, `addLabel()`, `addButton()`, `addLabelAtAnchor()`, `addButtonAtAnchor()`, `initHelp()`.
- However, **12 of 13 scenes** individually import `createHudText` from `../../../src/ui/Renderer`.
- **8 scenes** repeat the event-log rendering pattern (header "── Event Log ──" + loop rendering log lines at fixed x-offset with 17px line spacing).
- **2 scenes** (DeckRngScene, HandPileScene) repeat deck initialization (`createStandardDeck` + `shuffleArray` + `createSeededRng`) and grid rendering.
- **1 scene** (HandPileScene) has 3 nearly identical slider implementations (arc, spacing, rotation) with the same layout pattern.
- Deck utilities (`createStandardDeck`, `shuffleArray`) live in `src/card-system/Deck.ts`; RNG in `src/core-engine/SeededRng.ts` — these are already well-placed.

## Desired Change

1. Create `src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts` exporting shared helpers extracted from gym scenes:
   - `createEventLog(scene, eventLogLines, baseY?, options?)` — renders "── Event Log ──" header and log lines.
   - `createDeckGrid(scene, deck, options?)` — renders cards in a compact face-up grid.
   - Optionally: slider helper for scenes with interactive value controls.
2. Refactor all 13 gym scenes to use these shared utilities.
3. Add unit tests for the new utilities in `tests/ui/`.
4. Update `example-games/gym/README.md` with migration notes and usage examples.

## Related Work

| Item | Title | ID | Relationship |
|------|-------|----|--------------|
| Parent | Create a Gym | CG-0MP3XQBL4008QK8S | Parent epic; this task refines Gym structure |
| Child | Extract reusable HandView and PileView components | CG-0MPDS1QWN004KKNJ | Completed; precedent for gym → src/ui extraction |
| Sibling | Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView | CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I | Independent; separate porting work |
| Related | Migrate remaining Gym scenes to SLL layout helpers | CG-0MPKEQBDT001PQOZ | Completed; already extracted layout helpers into GymSceneBase |

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Scope creep** — Extracting too aggressively could over-engineer simple scenes. Mitigation: only extract patterns repeated in ≥2 scenes; keep helpers focused; record additional extraction opportunities as child work items linked to this item rather than expanding scope.
- **Risk: Over-extraction** — Creating helpers for one-off patterns would add complexity without benefit. Mitigation: require ≥2 usage sites or clear future use.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Where should new extractions go — `src/core-engine` or `src/ui/`?" — Answer (user): "src/ui". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which gym scenes should be targeted?" — Answer (user): "All gym scenes". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should this scope coordinate with sibling CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I?" — Answer (user): "Independent". Source: interactive reply.

# Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components (CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I)

Summary

Port all example-games to adopt the shared HandView and PileView components so hand/pile rendering, input handling, and animations are consistent, testable, and easier to maintain.

---

## Problem statement

Multiple example-games contain duplicated hand- and pile-rendering code and bespoke input/animation wiring. This increases maintenance cost, causes inconsistent UX (selection, reduced-motion, flip/animation behaviour), and makes cross-game automated tests harder to author and maintain.

## Users

- Engine developers: want consistent, reusable UI components so new games can reuse the same APIs and patterns.
- QA engineers: need deterministic, testable scene behaviour (reduced-motion, headless tests) and consistent smoke tests across games.
- Designers/Producers: want predictable animation/feedback settings and a single place to tune visual/audio feedback for hand/pile interactions.

Example user stories

- As an engine developer I can replace per-scene hand/pile rendering with HandView/PileView so new games need only call setCards/setPile and listen for events.
- As a QA engineer I can run a per-scene smoke test that uses shared HandView/PileView behaviour and assert deterministic outcomes.
- As a designer I can tweak reduced-motion or visual feedback behaviour centrally and have it apply across all example-games.

## Success criteria (measurable)

1. All example-games that render or manipulate hands/piles (all directories under example-games/) have their scenes updated to import and use src/ui/HandView.ts and src/ui/PileView.ts where applicable. (Verify by code review and grep: no remaining bespoke hand/pile sprite-management code in scenes.)
2. For each migrated scene, behaviour is preserved: selection, draw/discard/recall, flip, move, illegal-move feedback, and reduced-motion fallbacks behave identically (or with equivalent UX) as before. (Verify with existing per-scene unit and smoke tests.)
3. Each migrated game has updated tests (unit and/or smoke) exercising the migrated flow; at least one headless smoke test per migrated game must pass. (Verify by running npx vitest run tests/<game> or equivalent.)
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments in migrated files, the game README (if present), and example-games/gym/README.md if Gym-specific notes are necessary.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (npm run build && npm test).

## Constraints

- Do not change game logic or data models (card/pile state). The migration must only replace view-layer code (rendering, input wiring, visual animation hooks).
- Preserve reduced-motion behaviour and headless-test determinism for CI.
- Avoid adding large assets or new runtime dependencies. Prefer existing CardTextureHelpers/getCardTexture and existing animation helpers (dealCard, discardCard, flipCard, moveGameObject, shakeIllegalMove).
- Use direct migration (scenes import HandView/PileView directly) per intake decision — do not introduce a new compatibility shim unless a scene cannot be migrated without significant changes; in that case create a separate follow-up task.

## Existing state

- Shared UI components exist: src/ui/HandView.ts and src/ui/PileView.ts (implemented and unit-tested). See files in repo.
- Reference implementation and migration of `GymHandPileScene` already exists (work item CG-0MPDS1QWN004KKNJ, audit: Ready to close: Yes). The Gym example demonstrates intended APIs and patterns.
- Example games in the repository (directories): beleaguered-castle, feudalism, golf, gym, lost-cities, main-street, sushi-go, the-mind. Some scenes already use core-engine helpers; most still contain bespoke hand/pile rendering.

## Desired change

Directly migrate scenes in each example-game that manage hands/piles to use the shared HandView and PileView components:
- Replace bespoke per-scene sprite/layout/selection code with HandView/PileView usage.
- Wire existing animation helpers (dealCard, discardCard, flipCard, moveGameObject, shakeIllegalMove) to the shared views (use getSprite()/getCountText() or create temporary anim sprites as per the Gym reference).
- Update or add unit and smoke tests for migrated scenes to assert behaviour and reduced-motion fallbacks.
- Update per-game README or inline code comments describing usage and any game-specific differences.

## Related work (seeded)

- CG-0MPDS1QWN004KKNJ — Extract reusable HandView and PileView components and migrate GymHandPileScene (reference implementation; Gym migration demonstrates expected patterns and animations). 
- CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE — Refactor gym scenes to standardize features via core-engine shared code (parent/context)
- CG-0MP3XQBL4008QK8S — Create a Gym (higher-level epic grouping Gym work)
- CG-0MPD5XDVZ000U7GU — Gym Graphics: Deal / Place / Discard Animations (DeckRng + HandPile) — graphics/animation integration with Hand/Deck flows
- CG-0MPD5XHFT000QA4W — Gym Graphics: Positional Movement / Tween Demo (HandPile)
- CG-0MPDQO1PH006222N — Add standard playing-card SVG assets (in-progress) — relevant for texture keys used by HandView/PileView

---

## Related work (automated report)

I ran a conservative search of Worklog and the repository for items and files related to hand/pile UI, animation helpers, and Gym migration patterns. The following items and files are the most relevant seeds for implementers:

- CG-0MPDS1QWN004KKNJ — "Extract reusable HandView and PileView components and migrate GymHandPileScene" — Reference implementation and migration performed for the Gym demo. Use this as the primary implementation example and refer to its code changes and tests.
- CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE — Parent task: "Refactor gym scenes to standardize features via core-engine shared code" — Provides the broader refactor context and acceptance criteria for Gym-related changes.

- CG-0MPD5XHFT000QA4W — "Gym Graphics: Positional Movement / Tween Demo" — Shows expected moveGameObject integration patterns and cancellation behaviour.

- CG-0MPDQO1PH006222N — "Add standard playing-card SVG assets" — in-progress asset work that can affect textures used by HandView/PileView and headless test fallbacks.

Relevant repo files (examples to inspect):

data.description:
# Hand & Pile Gym: hand at bottom rendered as adjustable arc; remove card labels

## Problem statement

The Gym "Hand & Pile Interactions" scene currently renders the player's hand as a horizontal row positioned mid-page. This makes it less representative of typical tableau card game layouts and limits demonstrations of curved/arc layouts. We need to render the hand at the bottom‑centre of the viewport and support an adjustable arc layout (0 = straight line) with a slider control to the right of the hand. Additionally, the per‑card text labels used for debugging should be removable via a HandView option so the gym can present a cleaner visual.

## Users

- Engine developers and example‑game authors who will use Gym scenes to validate UI/UX and animations.
- Playtesters and designers who need a realistic tableau hand layout for screenshots and demos.
- QA engineers who will verify layout behaviour across viewport sizes and reduced‑motion settings.

Example user stories

- As a game UI author, I want the hand rendered at the bottom of the screen with an arc so I can preview how a player's hand will look in a real game.
- As a designer, I want a slider to adjust the curvature of the hand in real time so I can fine‑tune aesthetics without code changes.
- As a QA engineer, I want the debug labels hidden in the gym scene so visual tests and screenshots match production visuals.

## Success criteria

1. Hand placement: The hand is rendered at the bottom‑centre of the viewport (flush to the bottom). Concretely, the HandView instance used by GymHandPileScene must be positioned so card centers are at baseY = GAME_H - CARD_H/2 - 10 (or visually within 12px of the bottom edge) when the scene is loaded.
2. Arc behaviour: HandView exposes an `arcRadius: number` option and runtime setter. When `arcRadius === 0`, all cards align on a straight horizontal line at baseY. When `arcRadius > 0`, cards are positioned on an arc such that changing the radius updates per‑card Y offsets live. The slider control (see SC3) must update the `arcRadius` continuously.
3. Slider control (UI): A slider control placed immediately to the right of the rightmost card adjusts the arc radius in real time. (Agent default: slider range 0..200 and default starting radius 60px — see Appendix OPEN QUESTION to confirm numeric range and persistence policy.) Moving the slider must visually update the hand immediately without requiring a scene reset.
4. Labels: HandView gains a `showLabels: boolean` option; GymHandPileScene must set `showLabels: false`. When false, no per‑card text objects are created or visible.
5. Backwards compatibility & animations: Existing deal/discard/flip/move animations and the reducedMotion behavior must continue to work; the dealCard animation (which uses arcHeight) should remain semantically independent from HandView's arcRadius.
6. Tests & docs: Unit tests are added for HandView layout (straight vs arc), label toggle, and slider integration; all related documentation and README snippets updated. Full project test suite must pass with these changes.

> Required universal acceptance criteria (added):
> - All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
> - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Maintain HandView public API compatibility where possible; other example games using HandView should not break. Prefer additive changes (new options and setters) rather than removing existing options.
- Respect reducedMotion preferences: when reducedMotion is enabled, layout changes still apply but animations must remain suppressed.
- Performance: Hand layout updates (slider interaction) must be performant at interactive rates for up to typical hand sizes (e.g., 12 cards).
- Visual: The slider control should be implemented using existing overlay UI utilities in `src/ui` for consistent styling.

## Existing state

- example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts currently constructs HandView with baseX = 60, baseY = 130 and spacing = 56 and places it near the top/middle of the scene. It also renders per‑card labels in HandView and creates control buttons in rows above the scene content.
- src/ui/HandView.ts: currently computes only X positions (layoutCardPositions) and places a text label per card at baseY + 42. No arcRadius or showLabels options exist.
- src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts: returns X center positions only and supports maxWidth compression. No Y/arc math.
- src/ui/dealCard.ts: supports an `arcHeight` option for the trajectory when dealing a card (relevant reference for arc math, but separate concern from HandView's arc layout).

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk (scope creep): The change can grow beyond the small UI improvement if we add multiple control styles (steppers, presets, persistence). Mitigation: limit this work item to adding HandView arcRadius + showLabels options and a simple slider UI; record additional features (stepper buttons, persistence, presets) as separate child work items.
- Risk (API break): Changing HandView internals could inadvertently break other example games. Mitigation: keep changes additive (new options only) and run `wl next`/test suite and smoke tests for all example-games that use HandView.
- Risk (visual regressions): Bottom anchoring and label removal may affect screenshots and visual tests. Mitigation: update snapshot/integration tests and provide a short screenshot regression test in the gym test harness.
- Risk (performance): Recomputing arc positions frequently while sliding could cause frame drops. Mitigation: ensure layout is O(n) per update and debounce slider events if needed; keep layout math lightweight.

Assumptions

- Hand sizes will remain small (typical <= 12 cards) in the gym and example games; layout performance optimization beyond O(n) is not required.
- dealCard's arcHeight is a separate parameter for animation; we will not conflate its semantics with HandView.arcRadius (layout vs motion).
- The slider can be implemented with existing overlay UI components in `src/ui` and does not require adding new low‑level controls.

## Desired change (implementation summary)

- HandView API changes:
  - Add `arcRadius?: number` to HandViewOptions (default 0).
  - Add `showLabels?: boolean` to HandViewOptions (default true). Gym scene will set false.
  - Add `setArcRadius(radius: number)` method and `getArcRadius()` accessors.
  - Update rebuildDisplay() to compute per‑card Y offsets when arcRadius > 0. Prefer a helper `layoutArcPositions(...)` that uses the existing X positions from layoutCardPositions and returns an array of {x,y} centers.
  - Ensure selection tints, pointer handlers and reducedMotion behavior are preserved.

- Gym scene changes (example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts):
  - Instantiate HandView with new baseY computed for bottom flush (see SC1).
  - Add a slider UI to the right of the hand (using existing overlay UI helpers) that binds to HandView.setArcRadius and updates live.
  - Set `showLabels: false` when creating the HandView for this scene.

- Tests and docs:
  - Add unit tests for HandView: straight line layout (arcRadius=0), arc layout with known radius (validate Y offsets), and label toggling.
  - Update GymHandPileScene snapshot or integration tests to account for bottom‑anchored hand and slider UI.
  - Update code comments and README/docs referencing HandView options.

## Related work (manual & automated findings)

Related files (code):
- example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts — gym scene to update
- src/ui/HandView.ts — primary component to change
- src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts — X layout helper; consider composing arc offsets on top of this
- src/ui/dealCard.ts — demonstrates arc animation parameters (arcHeight) which are conceptually related but not the same as layout arcRadius
- src/ui/CardTextureHelpers.ts — asset helpers; relevant when labels are removed (visual fallbacks)

Related work items (Worklog):
- Extract reusable HandView and PileView components and migrate GymHandPileScene (CG-0MPDS1QWN004KKNJ) — completed. (Historical migration that this change should respect.)
- Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components (CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I) — open. (May contain migration notes and related tests.)
- Verify gym migration to shared HandView & PileView (CG-0MPDWZ39L001GPJ2) — open/low. (Validation tasks that may be relevant.)

Related work (automated report)

- The repository already contains a reusable HandView component (src/ui/HandView.ts) that lays out cards horizontally using layoutCardPositions and creates per-card labels. This is the primary target to extend. (see src/ui/HandView.ts)
- layoutCardPositions.ts already computes center-X positions and supports compression — prefer composing arc Y transforms on top of these positions rather than altering the X layout helper.
- The dealCard helper uses arcHeight for projectile motion and is a useful reference for naming and semantics (e.g., arcHeight: 0 -> straight line); ensure naming consistency but keep the two concepts distinct.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Hand vertical placement — where should the hand be anchored vertically?
   - A) Flush to bottom (hand baseline visually near bottom edge; e.g., baseY = GAME_H - CARD_H/2 - 10px)
   - B) Bottom‑centre with a small margin (recommended default: 10% of screen height above bottom)
   - C) Use a configurable pixel offset (please provide default px)
   Suggested default: B"
  — Answer (user): "1.A". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. (Applied: scene will use flush‑to‑bottom placement: baseY = GAME_H - CARD_H/2 - 10 px.)

- Q: "Arc radius controls (buttons & placement) — what UI and control behaviour do you want?
   - A) Two stepper buttons to the right of the hand (+ / −). Each click changes radius by a fixed step (suggested step = 10px). Clamp radius to [0, 200]. Start radius default: 60px. Buttons anchored just to the right of the hand’s rightmost card + 12px margin.
   - B) Slider control (continuous) placed to the right of the hand.
   - C) Both buttons and a small slider (buttons for coarse, slider for fine).
   Also: should the radius preference persist across scene reset / stored in Settings? (yes/no)
   Suggested default: A, start=60px, step=10px, clamp 0..200, do not persist."
  — Answer (user): "2.B". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. (Applied: slider UI to the right of the hand.)
  — Agent inference / OPEN QUESTION: slider numeric config (min/max/default) and persistence were not provided. Agent applied defaults for drafting: min=0, max=200, default=60, persist=no. Please confirm these values; see OPEN QUESTION below.

- Q: "Card text labels — which labels to remove and how to configure?
   - A) Remove/hide all HandView per‑card text labels (rank+suit). Implement as HandView option showLabels: boolean (default: false for this scene). This is scene‑local (GymHandPileScene passes showLabels:false).
   - B) Only remove debug labels (leave rank/suit visible).
   - C) Remove labels but provide an optional runtime toggle (UI or HandView API) to re‑enable for debugging.
   Suggested default: A (hide rank+suit labels in this scene by default, add HandView option so choice is configurable elsewhere)."
  — Answer (user): "3.A". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. (Applied: HandView will gain showLabels option and Gym scene will set false.)

OPEN QUESTION (needs confirmation):
- Q: For the slider (2.B) should the numeric range and default be the agent default (min=0, max=200, default=60) and should the value persist across scene resets/settings? (Agent default: persist = no). — (Answer: not provided by user; Agent set defaults for the intake draft.)

---
