Headline

Add a rotation slider to the Gym Hand & Pile demo so that cards tilt left/right around the hand centre based on their position; the center card remains unrotated.

Problem statement

The Hand & Pile Gym scene currently exposes arc radius and spacing sliders to control hand layout. There is no UI control or HandView API for applying a per-card rotation based on horizontal position. Developers and designers need a live control to preview per-card rotation (tilt) for visual polish and gameplay feedback.

Users

- Engine developers and designers who use the Gym to validate UI/UX changes.
- QA engineers running deterministic smoke tests for card layout and animation.

User stories

- As a designer, I want a slider that live-updates card tilt so I can preview and tune visual styling.
- As a developer, I want the rotation logic in HandView so other scenes can reuse the behavior without duplicating code.
- As a QA, I want reduced-motion to be respected so accessibility settings do not produce unexpected motion.

Success criteria

1. A new rotation slider is present in example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene and visually matches the arc/spacing sliders (track, fill, handle, value text) and is anchored to the hand like the other sliders.
2. Moving the slider live-updates the per-card rotation in HandView: cards left of the hand centre rotate left up to 30°; cards right of centre rotate right up to 30°; the exact rotation for a card at x is proportional to its normalized offset from hand centre; the centre card (offset 0) has 0° rotation.
3. Reduced-motion behavior: when reducedMotion is active, rotation is applied instantly (no animated transitions) and does not add motion beyond an immediate state change.
4. Automated tests: Unit or scene-level tests are added/updated to assert the presence of the rotation slider creation code in GymHandPileScene and that HandView exposes a rotation API (e.g., setMaxRotationDegrees) and applies rotation to sprites. Tests must be executable via the existing test harness (npm test) and must pass.
5. Documentation: README/docs updated to mention the rotation slider and HandView API change. All related documentation (code comments, example-games/gym/README.md, docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md) is updated to reflect the change.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Respect reduced-motion preferences (browser/media query and SettingsStore) by applying rotation as an instant state change when reduced-motion is enabled.
- Keep the change backward-compatible: HandView default behaviour must remain unchanged unless the new API is explicitly used.
- Minimize visual flicker during existing deal/discard animations; ensure final rotation is applied after any animated deal completes.
- Changes should avoid global side-effects outside HandView and GymHandPileScene.

Existing state

- HandView (src/ui/HandView.ts) currently computes positions and applies x/y layout and selection tints but does not set per-card rotation.
- GymHandPileScene implements two sliders (arc radius and spacing) with a reusable slider pattern (track/fill/handle/hit area) and updates HandView via setArcRadius/setSpacing.
- dealCard and discardCard animation helpers accept and apply rotation during animation; dealCard resets rotation at end and HandView.setCards subsequently applies layout.
- Tests exist asserting presence of spacing slider (tests/gym/GymHandPileSpacing.test.ts) and the Gym registry and smoke tests cover the scene booting.

Desired change

- HandView API: add support for a maximum rotation parameter (suggested API: setMaxRotationDegrees(maxDegrees: number) or setRotationRange(maxDegrees:number)) and apply per-card rotation in computeCardPositions/applyLayout by setting sprite.rotation appropriately (degrees -> radians).
- GymHandPileScene: add a third slider (rotation) following the existing slider pattern; the slider should map a normalized value to [-maxDegrees, +maxDegrees] with 0 at centre. Live changes must call HandView.setMaxRotationDegrees or equivalent and update visuals.
- Tests: add/modify tests to assert slider presence and HandView rotation application.
- Docs: update Gym README and GYM_INDEX entries for the scene.

Related work

- example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts — primary scene to modify; contains existing arc & spacing slider implementations and HandView usage.
- src/ui/HandView.ts — add rotation API/implementation here so behavior is reusable.
- src/ui/dealCard.ts — note: deal animation applies temporary rotation; ensure final rotation from HandView is applied after animations complete.
- src/ui/discardCard.ts — discard animation supports rotation; ensure compatibility.
- tests/gym/GymHandPileSpacing.test.ts — existing test that looks for spacing slider; may be used as a template for a rotation slider test.
- WL items: CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I (Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components) — related migration work; CG-0MPDXM6UC0039TEX (Hand & Pile Gym: hand at bottom rendered as adjustable arc; remove card labels) — prior gym changes.

Related work (automated report)

- Work item CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I — "Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components". Relevance: this item touches the same HandView/PileView refactor and may contain discussion or tests that affect how adding an API to HandView should be done to remain compatible with the porting work.
- Work item CG-0MPDXM6UC0039TEX — "Hand & Pile Gym: hand at bottom rendered as adjustable arc; remove card labels". Relevance: historical changes to this scene control how arc/spacing sliders were introduced and provide precedent for slider UI and test coverage.
- example-games/gym/README.md — Relevance: documents Gym scenes and mentions HandView usage and reduced-motion expectations; should be updated to include rotation slider.
- src/ui/HandView.ts — Relevance: primary implementation target for per-card rotation support; modifications here make the feature reusable across scenes.
- src/ui/dealCard.ts — Relevance: deals animate rotation during flight; ensure the final hand rotation is enforced after deal completes to avoid mismatch.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Slider range — what maximum rotation should the slider control?" — Answer (user): "B — 30° max". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Reduced-motion behavior — should rotation be disabled when reduced-motion is active?" — Answer (user): "B — No; keep rotation but ensure changes are instant (no animated transitions)." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Implementation location — where should per-card rotation logic live?" — Answer (user): "A — HandView (recommended)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Idempotence note

- This draft replaces any prior intake content for this work item and includes the canonical Appendix. Re-running intake will reuse work item CG-0MPE47XQG001KWWH and replace the description rather than appending duplicate Appendix entries.

Summary

Ensure the drawn card animation lands exactly on the final hand position computed by HandView for the current layout (spacing, compression, arc). Centralize the draw animation into HandView (ex: animateAddCard or AddCardOptions.animation) so callers do not duplicate layout math.


Problem statement

When a card is drawn (e.g. GymHandPileScene.drawToHand) the temporary animated sprite is given a destX/destY that is computed outside of HandView. Because the scene and HandView duplicate layout logic (spacing, compression, arc math), the animation destination can differ from the final card sprite position after HandView.setCards runs. This results in visual mismatch/jank when sliders (spacing/arc) or compressed layouts are in use.


Users

- Players: expect smooth, visually-correct card draw animations that land exactly where the card appears in the hand.
- Developers: want a single, well-defined API to animate/insert cards into a HandView without duplicating layout math.

Example user stories

- As a player, when I draw a card, the animation should land exactly on the card's final position in my hand so the UI feels polished.
- As a developer, I can call handView.addCard(card, { animate: true, sourceX, sourceY }) and trust the component to perform the animation and integrate the card without needing to compute layout details myself.


Success criteria (measurable)

- Draw animation destination accuracy: For representative scenarios (straight layout, arc layout, compressed layout), the destX/destY used by the animation must match HandView's final computed center for the new card within 1 pixel.
- Automated unit tests added: Vitest unit tests that assert the destination coordinates passed to dealCard (or used by HandView animation) equal the canonical layout positions for at least three scenarios (straight, arc, compressed).
- Integration behavior: Running the GymHandPileScene interactively with different spacing/arc values shows the animated card landing exactly on the new card sprite (observational QA pass).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


Constraints

- Respect reduced-motion settings: animations must short-circuit to instant placement when reducedMotion is enabled.
- Minimize API churn: prefer a small, backwards-compatible change to HandView (or a single new method) rather than a large refactor that touches many scenes.
- Avoid changing public behavior of HandView in ways that break existing callers; if behaviour changes are required, document them and create follow-up work items.
- Tests must be run locally and pass before committing (build → test → commit order).


Existing state

- example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts: drawToHand() and recallFromDiscard() create a temporary animSprite at pile position, compute a destination using a local getHandPositionForIndex() helper, call dealCard({ destX, destY, ... }), and only after the gameEvents 'card:dealt' handler calls handView.setCards(this.hand). This duplicates layout math and order-of-operations causes the mismatch.
- src/ui/HandView.ts: computeCardPositions()/applyLayout() use layoutCardPositions() + arc math to compute canonical card centers.
- src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts: shared algorithm that handles compression when ideal width exceeds maxWidth.
- src/ui/dealCard.ts: animation helper that animates a sprite to destX/destY; it relies on callers to provide accurate destination coordinates.
- tests/ui/dealCard.test.ts and tests/ui/flipCard.test.ts: existing unit tests that exercise animation helpers (useful as test patterns).


Desired change

Per the chosen approach (user-selected): Centralize the drawing animation in HandView so callers do not duplicate layout math.

Proposed minimal changes (conservative):

1) Extend HandView's public API to support animated insertion, for example:

   - Option A (preferred, minimal): Extend AddCardOptions to accept `animate: true | false` (already exists) and an `animation` sub-object with optional fields: `sourceX`, `sourceY`, `duration?`, `arcHeight?`, `ease?`, `rotation?`, `sfx?`. When `animate:true` HandView will:
     - Create a temporary sprite at `sourceX, sourceY` (or use a supplied sprite), compute the final destination center for the new card index using HandView's computeCardPositions, call dealCard() internally with that destX/destY, and on completion integrate the card into HandView's sprites and labels. Return a Promise that resolves when the animation completes.

   - Option B (alternative): Add a new explicit method `animateAddCard(card, animationOptions): Promise<void>` that performs the same behaviour without changing the existing AddCardOptions shape.

2) Update example callers (GymHandPileScene) to call the new HandView API instead of creating animSprite and calling dealCard directly.

3) Add unit tests covering the coordinate equality and integration tests for GymHandPileScene using the existing testing patterns in tests/ui/*.

Note: Implementation must keep reducedMotion behaviour (instant addition) and preserve event ordering where possible (e.g., emit a `card:dealt`-like event after animation completes if external code needs it).


Related work (manual seeds)

- src/ui/HandView.ts — canonical hand layout and computeCardPositions (authoritative source of truth for card centers).
- src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts — shared layout algorithm (handles compression / maxWidth).
- example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts — current caller that duplicates layout logic and performs animation; primary consumer impacted.
- src/ui/dealCard.ts — animation helper currently used by GymHandPileScene to animate temporary sprites to a destination.
- tests/ui/dealCard.test.ts — unit test patterns for dealCard that can be extended to assert destination coordinates.


Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "1) Scope: where has this been observed?
   - A) Gym Hand & Pile scene only (example-games/gym) — suggested default: A
   - B) Any game using HandView (e.g., Main Street) — broader
   - C) Unknown / please investigate"
  — Answer (user): "A". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Evidence: GymHandPileScene.drawToHand uses duplicated layout helper (see example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts).

- Q: "2) Preferred fix approach? (pick one)
   - A) Update callers (e.g., GymHandPileScene) to compute destination using the shared layout algorithm (layoutCardPositions + arc math) — minimal change.
   - B) Add a HandView API (e.g., getPositionForIndex(index, handCount)) so callers can compute accurate destination from the component — encapsulated / preferred.
   - C) Move dealing animation into HandView (HandView.addCard can optionally animate in) — larger API change but centralizes behavior.
   - Suggested default: B"
  — Answer (user): "C". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- Q: "3) Priority / issue type?
   - A) Bug / high (UX-affecting)
   - B) Bug / medium (non-blocking)
   - C) Task / low
   - Suggested default: B"
  — Answer (user): "task, medium". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.


Research & findings (agent inference)

- The root cause is duplicated layout logic between GymHandPileScene and HandView. Evidence: HandView.computeCardPositions uses layoutCardPositions + arc math (src/ui/HandView.ts, src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts) while GymHandPileScene.getHandPositionForIndex implements very similar math and is used to compute destX/destY before animating.
- Recommended approach based on code structure: centralize animation in HandView (user-selected) to remove duplication and reduce future regressions.


Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Scope creep — centralizing animation may invite further refactoring requests (e.g., moving placement/tween concerns for other components into HandView). Mitigation: limit this change to a small, well-scoped API (animateAddCard or AddCardOptions.animation) and record any larger refactors as separate child work items.
- Risk: Behavioral regressions — changing the order of operations (when setCards is applied vs. when animation completes) could affect callers that rely on the previous sequence. Mitigation: preserve event hooks (e.g., emit a "card:dealt" event) and add regression tests for affected flows.
- Risk: Test friction — animation timing and Phaser tween mocks may make testing visual parity brittle. Mitigation: add deterministic unit tests that assert coordinate equality and use existing tween mocks (see tests/ui/*) rather than relying on end-to-end visual tests for acceptance.
- Assumption: reducedMotion handling remains the authoritative gate for skipping animations and should result in immediate integration of the card into HandView.
- Assumption: Only example-games/gym is currently observed to use the caller-managed animation pattern; if other scenes exist they should be migrated as separate follow-ups.


Open questions (if any)

- OPEN QUESTION: Are there any other scenes (beyond GymHandPileScene) that currently rely on the old caller-managed animation pattern and must be migrated in the same change? (asked to the product owner / implementer)



---

Related work (automated report)

- src/ui/HandView.ts — Primary implementation of hand layout and display. This file contains computeCardPositions()/applyLayout() and is the canonical source of truth for card centers; any animation destination must match the positions computed here.

- src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts — Shared layout algorithm used by HandView to compute center-X positions and compression behavior when `maxWidth` is exceeded. Important to re-use or call directly to avoid subtle compression mismatches.

- example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts — Current Gym scene that computes destinations with a local getHandPositionForIndex() and creates temporary animSprite + dealCard(). This is the primary consumer observed to exhibit the bug and should be migrated to the HandView animation API.

- src/ui/dealCard.ts — Deals a card along an arc to a provided destX/destY. The helper is correct but depends on callers to supply accurate destination coordinates — which is the source of the observed mismatch.

- tests/ui/dealCard.test.ts — Unit test patterns that assert tween target coordinates and timing. Use these tests as models when adding tests that assert destination equality.

- Worklog: "Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components" (CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I) — ongoing work to consolidate HandView usage across examples; this intake should reference and coordinate with that work to avoid merge conflicts.

- Worklog: "Hand & Pile Gym: hand at bottom rendered as adjustable arc; remove card labels" (CG-0MPDXM6UC0039TEX) — completed work that introduced the Gym hand layout behaviour (arc, sliders); explains why Gym has the arc/slider UI that exposes the mismatch.

- Worklog: "Animate drawn card to play position and update discard pile visually" (CG-0MLZH41ZS1Y2UV0D) — prior animation/UX work; may contain useful test/UX notes or patterns to re-use.

Relevance summary: The above code paths and work items form a tight cluster around hand layout and transfer animations. The conservative recommendation is to centralize animation behaviour in HandView (as requested) and coordinate with the ongoing HandView consolidation work (CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I) to avoid duplicated effort.

# Add Gym scene to demonstrate the Screen Layout Language (SLL)

## Summary

Add a self-contained Gym demo scene that demonstrates the Screen Layout Language (SLL) end-to-end: parsing, validation, normalized-to-pixel mapping, anchors, pixelOverride, DPR handling, and interactive overlay visualization. The demo will be accompanied by unit tests and headless Playwright browser tests and must not rely on legacy fallback adapters.

## Problem statement

The Gym demo collection currently uses hard-coded pixel coordinates and local layout logic. There is a new Screen Layout Language (SLL) implementation in src/ui (schema, parsing, and mapping helpers) but no Gym scene demonstrates how to author, validate, and consume SLL documents directly in a scene. This work-item will add a full-featured Gym demo that showcases SLL capabilities and how to use them to position UI elements in a Phaser scene (no legacy fallback integration).

## Users

- Engine developers: want a living example of how to author and consume SLL documents to position UI zones and anchors in-game.
- QA/test engineers: need reproducible headless/browser tests to validate layout mapping across viewports and DPRs.
- Integrators/porters: want a template scene to migrate other scenes to SLL without relying on legacy layout code.

Example user stories:
- As an engine developer, I can load a ScreenLayoutDocument and see zones and anchors rendered and used to position UI controls at runtime.
- As a QA engineer, I can run the scene in headless Chromium and assert that the layout mapping yields expected pixel rects at multiple viewport/DPR combinations.
- As an integrator, I can use the Gym example as a copy-paste template to adopt SLL for an existing scene.

## Success criteria (measurable)

1. A new Gym scene (`example-games/gym/scenes/GymSllScene.ts`) is added and registered in `GymRegistry` so it is reachable from the Gym Router.
2. The scene reads one or more layout JSON documents placed under `example-games/gym/layouts/` and uses `parseScreenLayoutDocument` + `getZoneRect` / `anchorPoint` or `normalizedToPixels` to compute and place UI elements at runtime. All sample layout JSON files must validate against the SLL schema using `validateScreenLayoutDocument` (tests must assert `valid === true`). The scene must NOT use `adaptLayoutWithFallback` or any legacy fallback mapping.
3. The demo visually overlays zone rectangles and anchor markers for inspection, and uses sample anchors to position at least: scene title/header, a menu/help button, one interactive control, and a small demo content area. The overlay must toggle on/off in the scene.
4. Unit tests and browser tests are added: (a) unit tests validating layout parsing and mapping at multiple viewport/DPR values; (b) a headless Playwright browser test that boots the scene, waits for a scene-ready marker, and asserts that at least two anchor-derived elements are positioned within the expected pixel ranges. Tests must be added under `tests/` following existing Gym test conventions (e.g., `tests/gym/`).
5. Documentation added or updated: `example-games/gym/README.md` updated with usage instructions, and a short developer note in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` or `example-games/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` referencing the new demo.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the gym README, and any relevant docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite and build succeed: `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The scene must demonstrate SLL directly; it must not use `adaptLayoutWithFallback`, `MainStreetLayoutAdapter`, or other legacy adapter helpers. (User requirement.)
- The demo must run headless in CI (Playwright/Chromium) without DOM-only dependencies that fail in headless runs. Use existing headless-friendly helpers (see other Gym scenes for patterns).
- Keep the demo lightweight and self-contained: assets should be minimal and reused from existing repos where possible (no large new assets).
- Keep API usage limited to exported SLL helpers in `src/ui` (parseScreenLayoutDocument, validateScreenLayoutDocument, normalizedToPixels, getZoneRect, anchorPoint).

## Existing state

- SLL runtime and schema are implemented in `src/ui/screen-layout.ts` and `src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts` with unit tests in `tests/ui/screen-layout-mapping.test.ts`.
- `example-games/main-street` demonstrates using SLL via `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` and `adaptLayoutWithFallback`. That adapter uses SLL but maps it into an existing legacy SceneLayout.
- Gym scenes currently use explicit coordinates (see `example-games/gym/scenes/*`). Gym headless smoke tests exist (`tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts` and `tests/gym/GymHeadlessDeterminism.test.ts`).

## Desired change

- Add a new scene `GymSllScene` under `example-games/gym/scenes` that:
  - Loads and validates one or more SLL JSON documents from `example-games/gym/layouts/` using `parseScreenLayoutDocument` / `validateScreenLayoutDocument`.
  - Computes pixel rects/anchors with `normalizedToPixels` or `getZoneRect` / `anchorPoint` for the current viewport and DPR.
  - Uses those computed rects/anchors to position and render demonstrative UI elements (title, menu/help button, one interactive control, and a demo content area).
  - Provides an overlay mode that draws zone outlines and anchor points and displays normalized coordinates and pixel coordinates for debugging.
  - Exposes a runtime control to switch between multiple sample SLL documents and to toggle simulated DPR/viewports so developers can observe mapping changes.
  - Includes clear code comments explaining which SLL helpers are used and why.
- Add layout sample files under `example-games/gym/layouts/` demonstrating: anchors, pixelOverride usage, requiredZones, and a baseViewport suitable for 1280x720.
- Add unit tests and a headless browser test:
  - Unit tests: verify parsing, validation, and mapping at 1280x720 @ DPR=1 and 720x1280 @ DPR=2 (reuse patterns from `tests/ui/screen-layout-mapping.test.ts`).
  - Browser test: boot the GymRouter -> GymSllScene in headless Chromium; wait for a `window.__sceneReady` or similar scene-ready signal and assert measured DOM/Canvas element positions derived from anchorPoint calculations.
- Update `example-games/gym/README.md` with a short section "SLL demo" and usage instructions.

## Related work

- src/ui/screen-layout.ts — SLL runtime utilities (normalizedToPixels, getZoneRect, anchorPoint, adaptLayoutWithFallback).
- src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts — SLL JSON schema and parser helpers.
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts — Example adapter showing how Main Street consumes a SLL doc and maps it into legacy SceneLayout (useful reference but DO NOT reuse adaptLayoutWithFallback in this demo).
- tests/ui/screen-layout-mapping.test.ts — Unit tests that exercise SLL mapping utilities.
- example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json — Example SLL document used by Main Street (reference sample).
- example-games/gym/* — Existing Gym scenes and tests (serves as example for headless-friendly patterns).
- Worklog: "Screen layout language" (CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ), "Implement SLL schema and typing" (CG-0MPENWQFT008YV9I), "Define SLL schema test suite" (CG-0MPENWP8Z009AO8V).

## Related work (automated report)

- CG-0MPENWQFT008YV9I — "Implement SLL schema and typing": Implements the SLL JSON schema and TypeScript typings used by runtime code in `src/ui`. This is the canonical implementation of the schema and should be the primary reference when authoring sample layout files.
- CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ — "Screen layout language": High-level work item describing the SLL feature. Useful for historical rationale and design decisions.
- example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json — Concrete SLL sample used by Main Street. Shows a practical, production SLL document and how zones/anchors are defined for a complex scene.
- tests/ui/screen-layout-mapping.test.ts — Unit tests that cover parsing and normalized-to-pixel mapping behaviour; tests here provide validation vectors that the Gym demo should reuse for its unit test cases.
- tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts and tests/gym/GymHeadlessDeterminism.test.ts — Existing Gym test patterns for headless scene boot and determinism; copy these patterns for the new browser-level test to ensure consistent headless behaviour.

(Report generated by automated discovery: conservative selection of high-relevance items referencing SLL, sample layouts, and existing Gym test patterns.)

---

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Headless/browser visual tests may be flaky due to renderer differences or timing/tween inconsistencies. Mitigation: reuse existing headless-friendly Gym test patterns, expose a deterministic scene-ready signal (e.g. `window.__sceneReady`), prefer tolerant assertions (ranges or 'within X px'), and add retries/timeouts as needed. Any persistent flakiness becomes a follow-up work item.
- Risk: DPR/viewport mapping differences across platforms could produce slightly different pixel results. Mitigation: include multiple DPR/viewport test vectors (1280x720@1, 720x1280@2) and assert ranges not absolute pixels; surface any mapping edge-cases as a follow-up bug if needed.
- Risk: SLL schema or APIs may change during implementation. Mitigation: keep the demo code decoupled (single import points) and record API-breaking changes as separate work items; prefer adding adapters if schema evolves.
- Risk: Scope creep (additional features or integration into legacy scenes). Mitigation: treat this work item as a focused demo + tests deliverable; record any additional feature requests or migration tasks as child work items linked to this epic.

Assumptions:

- The SLL schema and runtime in `src/ui` are stable for the purposes of a demo and tests.
- The CI environment supports headless Chromium via Playwright (repository already uses Playwright in tests).
- The new scene will be implemented as a self-contained Gym demo and will not modify Main Street production code.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope: Which demo scope do you want?
   - A: Minimal interactive visualization — show zones/anchors from a SLL JSON overlayed on-screen (visual only).
   - B: Integration demo — scene imports a SLL JSON, uses parseScreenLayoutDocument + adaptLayoutWithFallback/getZoneRect/anchorPoint and demonstrates both the SLL mapping and legacy fallback (like Main Street). (Recommended default: B)"
  — Answer (user): "1. Full demonstration of SLL, includign all features. But no utilization of fallback code." Source: interactive reply (user). Final: yes.

data.title: Migrate Gym scenes to Screen Layout Language (SLL)

data.description:
# SLL: Compose base + scene layouts and optional anchorRef support for modular UI (shell + scene)

## Problem statement

The Screen Layout Language (SLL) currently provides per-document normalized zones and anchors and runtime mapping helpers (normalizedToPixels, getZoneRect, anchorPoint), but it does not provide a first-class, lightweight way to compose a shared application "shell" (header/menu/toolbar/toast areas) with scene-specific layouts. As a result, scenes duplicate placement logic for shared chrome and authors cannot easily rely on stable named anchors exposed by the shell.

## Users

- Engine developers: want a reusable API for composing a per-application shell layout with scene-specific layout fragments so UI chrome placement is consistent across scenes.
- Scene authors / integrators: want a simple pattern to adopt SLL for scene placement without copying header/menu coordinates into each scene.
- QA / test engineers: want deterministic, testable layout mappings across viewports and DPRs for automated browser tests.
- Plugin / extension authors: want stable named anchors (e.g., help, toastArea) they can dock to without per-scene wiring.

Example user stories

- As a scene author, I can load the gym-shell layout and my scene layout and compose them so my scene automatically receives the shared header and help button positions without manual pixel coordinates.
- As a QA engineer, I can run unit tests that assert a merged layout produces expected pixel rects and anchor coordinates at specific viewport/DPR vectors.
- As an integrator, I can attach a debug popover to the shell Help anchor and it will land in the correct pixel position across all scenes and DPRs.

## Success criteria

1. A new helper `composeResolvedLayouts(baseDoc, sceneDoc, viewport, dpr, opts)` is implemented and exported from the UI module (or a suitable helper module). It must:
   - parse and validate both documents (using existing schema helpers),
   - produce resolved (pixel) layouts via normalizedToPixels(),
   - merge resolved zones using a conflict policy (default: scene overrides base),
   - expose an option to namespace merged scene zones or to change the conflict policy,
   - emit a lint/validation warning when name collisions occur (per user choice).
2. A Gym example (small demo or an update to an existing Gym scene) demonstrates the pattern by composing a gym-shell layout + a scene layout at runtime and positioning shared chrome (header/menu/help) from the merged resolved layout. The demo visual overlay shall be able to toggle and show merged zones/anchors.
3. Unit tests and at least one browser integration test are added:
   - Unit tests: validate merging behaviour, conflict-policy semantics, and DPR/viewport mapping (examples: 1280×720 @1, 720×1280 @2).
   - Browser test: boot a Gym scene that composes shell+scene layout, wait for a deterministic scene-ready marker, and assert at least two anchor-derived elements are within expected pixel ranges (within tolerant ranges).
4. Documentation is added/updated: example-games/gym/README.md contains a usage snippet (shell + scene composition), and docs/DEVELOPER.md (or a dedicated doc) summarises the recommended pattern and the example use cases/analysis.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite and build succeed with the new changes ("npm test" and "npm run build").

> NOTE: The conflict policy default is: Scene overrides Base. When a Zone/Anchor name collision occurs the helper will proceed with the scene value but will emit a lint/validation warning (developer-visible) explaining the collision, the chosen policy and pointing to both source docs; this warning should be surfaced during local dev/test runs and unit-lint checks.

## Constraints

- The initial deliverable MUST NOT change the SLL JSON schema (no anchorRef/imports changes) — the composition must be implemented at the resolved (pixel) level.
- Keep the change minimal and backwards-compatible with current SLL helpers. Avoid impacting legacy adapters (adaptLayoutWithFallback) or Main Street integration in this epic.
- The runtime must be headless-friendly (no DOM-only dependencies) and performant for frame-sized batch mapping (mapping 500 loops should remain inexpensive in microbenchmarks).
- Provide a clear opt-in path for future schema extensions (anchorRef / imports), but do not land schema changes in this epic unless requested separately.

## Existing state

- SLL schema + runtime are implemented at `src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts` and `src/ui/screen-layout.ts` (parseScreenLayoutDocument, validateScreenLayoutDocument, normalizedToPixels, getZoneRect, anchorPoint, adaptLayoutWithFallback).
- Example: `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` and MainStreet adapter illustrate production usage of SLL via an adapter.
- A lightweight Gym SLL demo scene was added under `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSllScene.ts` which demonstrates loading/validating layout fixtures and drawing overlays (useful reference and test harness).
- Related work items (existing): see "Related work" below for IDs and short descriptions.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

Minimum viable implementation (deliverable for this epic):

1. Create helper `composeResolvedLayouts(baseDoc, sceneDoc, viewport, dpr, opts)` (e.g., export from `src/ui/screen-layout-helpers.ts` or `src/ui/index.ts`):
   - Validate both docs with `validateScreenLayoutDocument` (emit errors if invalid),
   - Call `normalizedToPixels()` for each document,
   - Merge resolved.zones using policy: default `sceneWins` (scene overrides base), but accept opts = { policy: 'sceneWins' | 'baseWins' | 'namespace', namespacePrefix?: string }
   - When a name collision is detected and policy = 'sceneWins', emit a developer-visible lint/console warning and include both zone origins in the warning.
   - Return merged `ResolvedScreenLayout` suitable for direct use by scenes (no further adapter required).
2. Add unit tests covering merging semantics, scaling with DPR, pixelOverride honoring, and collision-warning emission.
3. Add a small Gym example (or update GymSllScene) to show runtime composition between a `gym-shell.layout.json` and a `scene.layout.json` and toggle overlay visualization of merged zones.
4. Documentation and a short code example showing usage and recommended patterns (namespacing, flip/popover positioning using merged anchors).
5. Create a follow-up epic for schema-level extensions (anchorRef/imports) if demand is signalled; include a short design note and JSON examples in the docs for how anchorRef would look.

## Related work

Potentially related work items

- Add Gym scene to demonstrate the Screen Layout Language (CG-0MPF8CAYI009TVQ5) — existing Gym SLL demo (in-progress). Should be consulted and can be referenced or reused as the example harness.
- Migrate Gym scenes to Screen Layout Language (CG-0MPF8WT920076RQ5) — higher-level migration epic; this helper could be a child task or a dependency for that migration.
- Screen layout language (CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ) — parent epic describing SLL adoption across project (completed/planned items exist there).
- Implement SLL schema and typing (CG-0MPENWQFT008YV9I) — completed earlier and is reference for schema and types.
- Implement layout mapping runtime (CG-0MPENWQVC0046ORZ) — completed; contains runtime examples and patterns that the helper should align with.

Potentially related docs / file paths

- src/ui/screen-layout.ts — runtime mapping utilities (normalizedToPixels, getZoneRect, anchorPoint, adaptLayoutWithFallback)
- src/ui/screen-layout-schema.ts — JSON schema, parser and validation helpers
- example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json — canonical layout example used by Main Street
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts — adapter example showing how SLL maps into legacy scene layout
- example-games/gym/scenes/GymSllScene.ts — existing Gym SLL demo scene (use as test harness)
- tests/ui/screen-layout-mapping.test.ts — existing unit tests for mapping utilities (good reference vectors)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Merge / conflict policy when composing base (shell) + scene layouts — which should be the default rule? (A) Scene overrides base, (B) Base overrides scene, (C) Namespacing required, (D) Custom merge policy" — Answer (user): "A but emit a warning when linting". Source: interactive reply. Final: A with lint warning.

- Q: "Schema extension timing — do you want: (A) implement only the resolved-level composition helper + example + docs now, and create a follow-up epic for schema-level anchorRef/imports; or (B) implement both the helper and a minimal prototype of the schema extension (anchorRef) now?" — Answer (user): "A". Source: interactive reply. Final: A (composition helper only now).

- Q: "Acceptance criteria: use the default list (compose helper, gym example, unit/browser tests, docs, tests + build passing). Accept?" — Answer (user): "agree". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

(End of Appendix)

# Add autosave and load feature for Beleaguered Castle

Add autosave transcript and save/load checkpoint features to the Beleaguered Castle example game, matching the pattern established in Main Street.

## Problem statement

Beleaguered Castle already records game transcripts via `BCTranscriptRecorder` and finalizes them on game end, but it does **not** auto-save those transcripts to browser storage or provide game-state checkpoint save/load. Other games (Main Street, Golf, Sushi Go) already have these features; Beleaguered Castle should be brought to parity.

## Users

- **Players** who want their game transcript saved automatically when a game ends, so they can review or replay it later.
- **Players** who want to save game progress and resume later (e.g., after closing the browser or navigating away).

### User stories

- As a player, I want my game transcript to be saved to browser storage automatically when a game ends so I can review past games or replay them.
- As a player, I want the game state saved automatically after the deal completes and after each move so I can resume from where I left off if I close the browser.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1**: Transcript is auto-saved to browser storage (IndexedDB/localStorage via `TranscriptStore`) when a game ends (win or no-moves loss).
- **AC-2**: Game state is saved via `SaveLoadStore` at two key checkpoints:
  - After the deal completes (game-start checkpoint)
  - After each player move (after-each-move checkpoint)
- **AC-3**: A loaded checkpoint restores the game to the exact state at the time of the save (proven by snapshot comparison).
- **AC-4**: Unit or integration test(s) in `tests/beleaguered-castle/` exercise the transcript autosave and save/load round-trips.
- **AC-5**: Imports use `@core-engine/transcript` and `@core-engine` barrel exports (not legacy shim paths).
- **AC-6**: Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC-7**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.

## Constraints

- Must follow the established Main Street pattern for save/load (`MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`) and autosave (`MainStreetTurnController.ts`).
- Must not introduce runtime regressions: existing Beleaguered Castle integration tests must continue to pass.
- Must not modify or disrupt the existing `BCTranscriptRecorder` interface or the replay feature that depends on it.
- Must use existing shared infrastructure (`SaveLoadStore`, `TranscriptStore`, `autoSaveTranscript`) from `src/core-engine/` — no new storage backends.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Scope creep** — The save/load feature may suggest additional UI affordances (e.g., a "Load Game" button in the overlay, manual save slots). *Mitigation:* Record any such opportunities as separate work items linked to this one rather than expanding the current scope.
- **Risk: Storage performance** — Saving a checkpoint after every player move could cause noticeable lag on slower devices or with IndexedDB write latency. *Mitigation:* Keep saves fire-and-forget (not awaited by the input handler); consider debouncing/throttling if profiling shows issues. The Main Street pattern is proven and should be replicated.
- **Risk: Browser storage unavailability** — IndexedDB/localStorage may be unavailable (private browsing, storage quotas, API errors). *Mitigation:* `SaveLoadStore` and `TranscriptStore` already handle unavailable backends gracefully (warning logs, null returns). The game should continue to function without save/load in such cases.
- **Risk: Existing test regressions** — Changes to the scene and turn controller may affect existing integration/unit tests. *Mitigation:* Run the full Beleaguered Castle test suite (and the full project suite) before committing.
- **Assumption**: A single SaveLoadStore slot reused for both checkpoints (deal-complete and after-move) is acceptable — the latest checkpoint always reflects the most recent save point. If the team needs separate slots for game-start vs. latest-move, this should be raised during planning.
- **Assumption**: The transcript autosave pattern from Main Street (call `autoSaveTranscript` with a `TranscriptStore` on game end) is fully applicable without modification.

## Existing state

- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/GameTranscript.ts` contains `BCTranscriptRecorder` (extends `TranscriptRecorderBase`) and `BCGameTranscript` types. Transcript recording and finalization already works.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts` calls `finalize()` on game end (win/loss) but does **not** hook into `autoSaveTranscript` or `SaveLoadStore`.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleTurnController.ts` handles move execution, undo/redo, and auto-complete but has no save/load integration.
- No `BeleagueredCastleSaveLoad.ts` file exists yet.
- No save/load integration tests exist in `tests/beleaguered-castle/`.
- The Main Street game (`example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` and `scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts`) provides the reference implementation.

## Desired change

- Create `example-games/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleSaveLoad.ts` with:
  - State serialization/deserialization helpers (`serializeBCState` / `deserializeBCState`)
  - A `bcStateSerializer` compatible with `SaveLoadStore`
  - `saveBCSnapshot` / `loadBCSnapshot` wrapper functions
  - Constants for schema version, game type, and slot IDs
- Modify `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts`:
  - Initialize a `SaveLoadStore` instance in `create()`
  - Save a checkpoint after the deal animation completes
  - Save a checkpoint after each move (in the turn controller callback chain)
  - Call `autoSaveTranscript(transcriptStore, 'beleaguered-castle', transcript)` when the game ends
- Write integration test(s) in `tests/beleaguered-castle/` covering:
  - Transcript autosave persistence and retrieval
  - Save/load round-trip with state equality verification
  - Both checkpoint points (deal-complete and after-move)

## Related work

- **CG-0MP12WI75001L9P4**: "Transcript & SaveLoad Consolidation" (parent epic) — Consolidated transcript recording, storage, and autosave into `src/core-engine/transcript`. Provides the shared infrastructure this work item depends on.
- **CG-0MPK8Y0UJ006MPJB**: "Add autosave and load feature for The Mind" — Sister work item with identical AC for The Mind game, following the same Main Street pattern.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — Reference implementation for save/load serializer, checkpoint helpers, and campaign persistence.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Reference showing how to wire autosave and save/load into the turn lifecycle and game-end flow.
- `tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts` — Reference tests for save/load round-trip, version compatibility, and deterministic restore.
- `tests/main-street/transcript-autosave.integration.test.ts` — Reference tests for transcript autosave and persistence verification.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q**: "How should the SaveLoadStore checkpoint work in Beleaguered Castle, since Beleaguered Castle doesn't have discrete turns like Main Street?"
  - **Answer (user)**: Both A and B:
    - A) **Game-start checkpoint** — Save automatically after the deal completes.
    - B) **After-each-move checkpoint** — Save game state after each player move.
  - Source: Interactive reply. Final: yes.

## Problem

The SLL layout zones currently define both positioning AND the area where cards are placed. When we fix positioning issues (like the Golf scores visibility bug), we inadvertently change how cards are sized/positioned relative to the available space.

## Current Architecture

1. Layout zones define: x, y, width, height (the area where content is placed)
2. Per-game constants define: CARD_W, CARD_H (the actual card dimensions)
3. Layout adapters use zone dimensions to calculate center positions
4. Renderers use card dimensions from constants to place cards

## Issue

The zone width/height affects how cards are positioned within the zone, which can make them appear larger or smaller. For example:
- In Beleaguered Castle, changing tableau height from 0.556944 to 0.486111 changed how cards are spaced
- The card dimensions (BC_CARD_W=90, BC_CARD_H=126) didn't change, but their visual appearance did

## Proposed Solution

Layout zones should only define positioning (x, y) and NOT dimensions (width, height). The card dimensions should come entirely from per-game constants.

### Changes needed:
1. Update layout JSON schemas to make width/height optional or remove them
2. Update layout adapters to not use zone width/height for card sizing
3. Ensure card dimensions are always derived from per-game constants
4. Update documentation to clarify this pattern

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Layout zones only define positioning (x, y), not dimensions
- [ ] Card sizes come entirely from per-game constants
- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [ ] Documentation updated to reflect this pattern
data.title: Decouple card sizes from layout zones in SLL adapters

## Bug Report

**Summary:** In The Mind, cards in the player's hand grow erratically on mouse hover and don't return to their correct display size on mouse out.

**Root Cause:** In MindRenderer.ts's renderHumanHand method, the pointerover handler calls sprite.setScale(1.03) and the pointerout handler calls sprite.setScale(1). However:
- setDisplaySize(CARD_W=120, CARD_H=164) is used when creating sprites and after texture loads to size them correctly
- setScale() overrides the carefully computed scale factor from setDisplaySize()
- After setScale(1) on pointerout, the card displays at its original SVG texture dimensions (48x65), not the intended 120x164
- When applyEnsuredTexture later calls setDisplaySize (async), it corrects the size, creating a race-condition visual flicker

**Fix:** Use sprite.setDisplaySize() instead of sprite.setScale() in both hover handlers, which correctly handles display dimensions regardless of the underlying texture.

**User Story:** As a player, when I hover over a card in my hand, it should slightly lift and grow subtly, then return to its normal size when I move the cursor away.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Hovering over a card in the human hand shows a subtle size increase (1.03x) and upward movement (4px)
2. Removing the cursor from a card returns it to its exact original display size (120x164) and Y position
3. No erratic resizing, flickering, or cards stuck at wrong sizes
4. All existing tests continue to pass
data.title: Fix Mind hand card hover effect: cards don't return to normal size

## Context

## Summary

Implement the first-launch Main Street tutorial offer and replay/skip onboarding flow for Main Street Milestone 5 (CG-0MOY5TOJK008JFJM).

## Context

Source of truth: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` US-1, US-3, and section 5. Current code auto-starts an informational tutorial overlay when `tutorialSeen` is false, but the PRD requires a modal prompt with `Start Tutorial` and `Skip for Now`, persistent skip/completion semantics, and replay from menu/settings.

## Expected behaviour

- First launch of Main Street shows a modal before free turn interactions begin.
- `Start Tutorial` starts the scripted tutorial run.
- `Skip for Now` starts normal gameplay and persists skipped state without marking completed.
- Completed tutorial state prevents future auto-offers.
- `Replay Tutorial` remains available from settings/menu and starts the tutorial in a new run context regardless of completion state.
- Replay mode and automated tests can disable tutorial prompts via explicit config/query/scene option.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Tests are written first for first-launch prompt, start path, skip path, completed-state suppression, replay-tutorial path, and explicit disable path.
2. The onboarding modal blocks normal gameplay interactions until the player starts or skips.
3. Skip persists `status: skipped`; tutorial completion persists `status: completed` with a completion timestamp.
4. Replay tutorial restarts into a deterministic tutorial run and does not corrupt the game selector registry or save data.
5. Browser/integration tests cover the modal and replay menu flow without relying on manual clicks where scene APIs can be used.
6. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass for this change.

# Improve Gym Deck & Seeded RNG scene to display entire deck face up

## Problem statement

The GymDeckRngScene shows only one card at a time (the last drawn) alongside abstract counters and a text event log — not the deck contents themselves. This makes it an ineffective visual demo of deck lifecycle and seeded randomness; users cannot see the full deck or quickly verify deterministic shuffle behavior.

## Users

- **Engine developers**: want to visually verify that seeded shuffles produce different arrangements and that the same seed reproduces the identical arrangement.
- **QA/test engineers**: want to confirm deck state at a glance rather than reading event logs.
- **Designers/Producers**: want an immediate visual showcase of the deck + RNG capability for demos and onboarding.

### Example user stories

- As an engine developer, I want all 52 cards face-up in a grid so I can instantly compare shuffled arrangements between different seeds.
- As a QA engineer, I want to see "Shuffle" replace the grid with a new arrangement, visually confirming seeded-deterministic behavior without reading log text.
- As a designer showing the engine to stakeholders, I want a visually rich scene that communicates "here are all the cards, and shuffling rearranges them" rather than hiding cards behind manual draw operations.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On scene load (create), a standard 52-card deck is displayed entirely **face up** in a compact grid layout — no cards are hidden.
2. The existing **Draw**, **Flip Last**, **Deal**, and **Reset** controls are removed.
3. The **Shuffle** button clears all displayed cards, shuffles the deck using the current seed, and redraws all 52 cards face up in the grid.
4. **Seed adjustment** controls (`[ -1 ]`, `[ +1 ]`, `[ Reset Seed ]`) remain functional and affect the shuffle outcome deterministically.
5. The **event log** is removed; card counters ("Deck: X cards", "Drawn: X cards") may be kept or replaced by a simpler status display.
6. Cards in the grid are rendered with face-up textures via `getCardTexture()` / `ensureCardTextureFallbacks()`, consistent with existing card rendering throughout the Gym.
7. Cards are positioned using SLL zone anchors (from `getGymAnchor('cardDisplay', ...)`) rather than hardcoded pixel coordinates, consistent with other Gym scenes.
8. The Gym registry entry description in `GymRegistry.ts` is updated to accurately describe the full-deck display and shuffle behavior.
9. Existing tests in `tests/gym/GymDeckRng.test.ts` are updated to reflect the removed features (no longer testing Draw/Flip/Deal-specific behavior) and new tests are added validating that the full deck is displayed (count of visible card sprites equals 52) and that shuffle produces a different visual arrangement.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
11. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and the Gym scene description in the registry/catalogue.

## Constraints

- Must use existing core-engine/card-system/UI APIs (`createStandardDeck`, `shuffleArray`, `createSeededRng`, `getCardTexture`, `ensureCardTextureFallbacks`, `preloadCardAssets`, `flipCard`).
- Must continue to reuse `GymSceneBase` and its layout helpers (SLL zones/anchors).
- Card assets must remain the standard SVG-based textures used elsewhere in the Gym.
- The grid layout must fit 52 cards on screen within the existing Gym scene viewport (1280×720) and card-display zone; cards may need to be scaled down accordingly.
- All Gym scenes must continue to be switchable from the Gym Router; the scene key (`GYM_DECK_RNG_KEY`) remains unchanged.

## Existing state

- `GymDeckRngScene.ts` creates a standard 52-card deck, provides seed controls, shuffle, draw (one card at a time), flip last drawn card, deal (arc animation), and reset.
- Only one card is visually displayed at a time (the most recently drawn or dealt card).
- An event log scrolls text entries for all actions.
- Card counters show remaining deck count and drawn count.
- The scene's description in `GYM_SCENE_CATALOGUE` reads: "Create, shuffle, and draw from decks using deterministic seeded randomness. Verify reproducible sequences across runs."
- Tests in `tests/gym/GymDeckRng.test.ts` test core functions (deterministic seeding, shuffle, draw) but do not test the visual scene content.

## Desired change

Reimplement the GymDeckRngScene to:

1. **Generate and display a full 52-card deck face up in a grid** on scene `create()`, positioned within the SLL cardDisplay zone.
2. **Keep seed adjustment controls** (the core educational feature of the scene) but **remove Draw, Flip Last, Deal, Reset buttons and the event log**.
3. **Rework the Shuffle button** to: clear all card sprites from the grid, shuffle the deck array using the current seed RNG, then re-render all 52 cards face up in the grid.
4. **Arrange cards in an 8×7 compact grid** (8 columns, up to 7 rows; row 7 may be partially filled for 52 cards) with appropriately scaled card textures.
5. Update the Gym registry entry description to reflect the new scene behavior.
6. Update existing tests to align with the new scene behavior (no longer testing removed features); add tests for full-deck display and shuffle-persistence behavior if feasible in the test harness.

## Related work (automated report)

The following related work items and repository resources are relevant to redesigning the GymDeckRngScene to display the full deck face up:

### Worklog items

- **CG-0MP4187KY007SKQ1 - Deck & Seeded RNG Demos (completed)**: The original work item that created the GymDeckRngScene. Its acceptance criteria defined the current scene behavior (shuffle, draw, flip, deal, reset with event log). This item is a redesign/improvement of that deliverable — the scene already exists but needs to be reworked to show the entire deck face-up with a simplified control set.

# Intake Brief: Fix deck/discard pile highlight orientation in GymHandPileScene

## Problem Statement

The valid-drop highlight rectangles for the deck and discard piles in the Gym's Hand & Pile scene are drawn with landscape dimensions (160×100), but the underlying pile card graphics use a portrait aspect ratio (96×130). This creates a visual mismatch: the highlight zone shape does not align with the card shape it's meant to indicate.

## Users

- **Gym visitor / engine developer (primary):** Uses the Gym scene to understand and test card-system APIs. The mismatch is visually distracting and reduces confidence in the demo.
  - *"As a developer exploring the Gym, I want the highlight zones to match the card aspect ratio so the demo looks polished and the highlight code serves as a correct reference implementation."*
- **UI component consumer (secondary):** Developers who reference the Gym's highlight code as a pattern for their own games.
  - *"As a developer using the highlight pattern, I want the reference implementation to use correct dimensions so I don't copy the wrong aspect ratio into my game."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Highlight rectangles use portrait dimensions `CARD_W + 16 × CARD_H + 16` (112 × 146), matching the card aspect ratio with uniform 8px padding on each side.
2. Highlights remain correctly centered on the deck and discard pile positions (`DECK_X`, `PILE_Y` and `DISCARD_X`, `PILE_Y`).
3. Existing browser test at `tests/gym/__screenshots__/GymHandPileHighlights.browser.test.ts` is updated to use the new dimensions (112 × 146 instead of 160 × 100) and still passes.

7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, test header comments, and the Gym README if applicable.

If that refactor is done first, this dimension fix would need to be applied within the new manager rather than directly in GymHandPileScene. # Fix arc slider position drift in GymHandPileScene

## Problem statement

The original manual slider implementations in `GymHandPileScene.ts` used `this.<slider>Track.x` as the minimum X reference for computing slider ratios. Because `track.x` could drift from the intended positional constant (e.g., `ARC_SLIDER_X`) when slider positions were updated elsewhere, pointer tracking became inaccurate.

## Users

- **Developers/maintainers of GymHandPileScene**: Want sliders that consistently track pointer position regardless of layout updates or resets.
- **Players/operators of the Gym demo**: Expect the arc, spacing, and rotation sliders to respond predictably and accurately to pointer drags.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The slider position drift bug has been eliminated: slider pointer position computation no longer depends on a potentially stale `track.x` value.
- Slider behavior (value range, initial value, visual appearance) is functionally unchanged from the original implementation.
- Full project test suite passes (`npm test`).
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Keep existing slider behavior and appearance unchanged.
- No expansion of scope beyond fixing the drift issue.

## Existing state

The original `GymHandPileScene.ts` (as of late May 2026) contained three inline slider implementations (arc, spacing, rotation), each with methods like `setArcRadiusFromPointer()` that used `this.arcSliderTrack.x` as the minimum X reference for computing the slider ratio. This approach was vulnerable to position drift because `arcSliderTrack.x` could become stale if track positions were modified by layout changes or scene resets.

## Desired change

The fix required removing the dependency on `track.x` for slider ratio computation and using a stable position reference instead.

## Related work

- **Refactor gym scenes to standardize features via core-engine shared code** (CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE) — Parent epic for extracting common Gym rendering patterns into `src/ui/`. Completed. Included the `createSlider` utility extraction and `GymHandPileScene` slider refactoring.
- **Create slider helper utility** (CG-0MPVPSILH0036XAB) — Child of CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE. Extracted the track/fill/handle/value-text drag pattern into `createSlider()` in `src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts`. The utility uses a closure variable `x` (captured at creation time) instead of `track.x`, eliminating the drift issue. Completed.
- **Refactor HandPileScene to use slider helper** (CG-0MPVPU713004ZOJP) — Child of CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE. Replaced the three inline slider implementations in `GymHandPileScene` with `createSlider()` calls. Completed. Commit `2660c23`.
- **`src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts`** — Contains the `createSlider()` function that provides the drifted-position fix via closure-based position tracking.

## Current status

The bug described in this work item has been fixed. All original acceptance criteria have been satisfied. The fix was implemented as part of the broader slider utility refactoring (CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE, completed June 1-2, 2026). Specifically:

- The `setArcRadiusFromPointer()`, `setSpacingFromPointer()`, and `setRotationFromPointer()` methods no longer exist in `GymHandPileScene.ts`.
- All three sliders (arc, spacing, rotation) now use `createSlider()` from `GymSceneUtils.ts`, which captures the reference X position as a closure variable at creation time.
- The track position drift vulnerability has been fully eliminated.
- Documentation updates (code comments, README, docs) were handled as part of the parent refactoring work item (CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE) and its children, which included updating `example-games/gym/README.md` and code comments.
- Verified: `npm test` passes (186 test files, 3322 tests passed), `npm run build` succeeds.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Scope creep** — The work item focused on a specific line-level fix, but the actual resolution involved a broader refactoring of all slider implementations. The refactoring was already scoped under a separate work item (CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE) and completed independently, confirming the risk was avoided for this item.
- **Risk: Regression from refactoring** — Replacing inline slider code with a shared utility could introduce subtle behavioral differences. Mitigation: the parent refactoring item included unit tests and pass/fail verification (`npm test`), and all existing tests pass.
- **Assumption:** The `createSlider()` utility's closure-based position tracking is at least as accurate as the original track-based approach for all pointer positions (verified by passing tests).
- **Assumption:** No other parts of the codebase depend on the removed methods (`setArcRadiusFromPointer`, etc.) — confirmed by code search.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the bug described by this work item still present in the current codebase?" — Answer (agent inference): "No. The bug has been fixed by the slider utility refactoring completed on June 1-2, 2026." Source: Inspection of current `GymHandPileScene.ts` (no `setArcRadiusFromPointer`, no `arcSliderTrack` properties) and commit `2660c23` which refactored the sliders to use `createSlider()`. The `createSlider` utility uses a closure variable `x` rather than `track.x`, eliminating the drift issue. Final: yes, bug is fixed.
- Q: "Was the fix applied via direct modification of the buggy methods, or through a broader refactoring?" — Answer (agent inference): "Through a broader refactoring." Source: The methods described in the work item (`setArcRadiusFromPointer`, etc.) were removed entirely as part of the slider utility refactoring. The fix was achieved by replacing the entire inline slider implementation with the `createSlider()` utility rather than by patching the individual methods. Final: yes, refactoring-based fix.

## Summary

In `GymHandPileScene.ts`, `discardSelected()` splices the card out of the `this.hand[]` array before the discard animation starts. If the animation never fires its completion event (e.g., texture missing, scene destroyed), the card is orphaned — removed from the hand model but never added to the discard pile.

## Location

`example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts`, `discardSelected()` method

## Current Behaviour

```typescript
const card = this.hand.splice(this.selectedIdx, 1)[0];  // removed from hand immediately
// ... animation starts ...
(gameEvents as any).on('card:discarded', () => {
  card.faceUp = false;
  this.discardPile.push(card);  // added to discard only if animation completes
});
```

If the animation is interrupted or the completion event never fires, the card exists in neither `this.hand` nor `this.discardPile`.

## Desired Behaviour

Either:
- Set `card.faceUp = false` before the animation starts and push to discardPile immediately (synchronous model update), or
- Add a safety net (e.g., on `shutdown` or timeout) to recover orphaned cards

## Acceptance Criteria

- Discard animation failure (or interruption) does not result in a lost card
- A unit or integration test is added that verifies the fix (e.g., simulates an interrupted animation and asserts the card is not orphaned)
- Card is either in `this.hand` or `this.discardPile` at all times
- Normal animated discard still works with the same visual effect
- `npm test` passes; `npm run build` succeeds
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

# Intake Brief: Optimize slider pointermove listeners in GymHandPileScene

## Problem Statement

The GymHandPileScene registers a single global `pointermove` listener that forwards every pointer event to all three sliders (arc, spacing, rotation), even when no slider is being dragged. Each slider's `handlePointerMove` checks an internal `isDragging` flag and returns immediately if idle, resulting in unnecessary per-frame function calls during all pointer movement.

## Users

Developer maintainers of the Gym demo scenes and engineers using the `createSlider` utility as a reference pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When no slider is being dragged, zero active `pointermove` handlers are processing per-frame (i.e., listeners are only registered during active drag)
- [ ] When a slider IS being dragged, pointermove events are forwarded to that specific slider's handler (not all three)
- [ ] All three sliders (arc, spacing, rotation) continue to work identically — no regression in appearance, value range, or visual feedback
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test` passes; `npm run build` succeeds)
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries

## Constraints

- Sliders live in the shared `createSlider` utility (`src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts`) and the per-scene wiring in `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts`
- The slider API (SliderResult.handlePointerMove, SliderResult.handlePointerUp) is public and used by GymHandPileScene; any changes must maintain backward compatibility or update all callers
- Existing `pointerdown` handler on each slider's hit area zone is sufficient for drag start detection — only `pointermove` and `pointerup` need global listeners
- Pre-existing build errors in `tests/gym/GymHandPileDiscardConsistency.test.ts` (unrelated to this work item) exist on the `dev` branch; they may need to be resolved or worked around before this item's AC can be fully verified

## Existing State

The `createSlider` utility in `src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts` provides a `SliderResult` with `handlePointerMove` and `handlePointerUp` methods. The slider internally tracks `isDragging`, set to `true` on the hit area's `pointerdown` event. Previously, the GymHandPileScene registered three separate `pointermove` listeners (one per slider). After the slider utility refactoring (commit 2660c23), this was consolidated into a **single** `pointermove` listener that calls all three sliders' `handlePointerMove`:

```typescript
this.input.on('pointermove', (pointer) => {
  this.arcSlider.handlePointerMove(pointer.x);
  this.spacingSlider.handlePointerMove(pointer.x);
  this.rotationSlider.handlePointerMove(pointer.x);
});
this.input.on('pointerup', () => {
  this.arcSlider.handlePointerUp();
  this.spacingSlider.handlePointerUp();
  this.rotationSlider.handlePointerUp();
});
```

Each slider's `handlePointerMove` checks `if (!isDragging) return;` before computing any value, so idle sliders are essentially no-ops. However, all three methods are still invoked on every pointer move across the entire viewport.

## Desired Change

Move listener registration into the slider itself so that each slider self-manages its own pointermove/pointerup listeners only during active drag. This eliminates the need for the GymHandPileScene to register any global pointermove/pointerup handlers at all. Options include:

1. **Self-contained slider drag**: In `createSlider`, register `scene.input.on('pointermove', ...)` inside the hit area's `pointerdown` handler and remove it on `pointerup`. Each slider manages its own lifecycle, so only the currently-dragged slider has an active listener.
2. **Consolidated scene-level approach**: Keep the single scene-level listener but register it lazily (on any slider's `pointerdown`) and remove it on `pointerup`. This reduces overhead to zero when idle.
3. **Use Phaser's built-in drag**: Make the slider handle `setInteractive({ draggable: true })` and use Phaser's `drag` event system, but this would change the interaction model significantly and may not map cleanly to horizontal-only drags.

Option 1 is preferred as it makes the slider fully self-contained and reusable without requiring the scene to wire up pointermove/pointerup forwarding.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MPVPSILH0036XAB** ("Create slider helper utility", **completed**): Created the `createSlider` function in `src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts` with the current pointer-event forwarding pattern.
- **CG-0MPVPU713004ZOJP** ("Refactor HandPileScene to use slider helper", **completed**): Refactored GymHandPileScene to use the `createSlider` utility, consolidating the three separate listeners into one.
- **CG-0MPNWGQJ0003034V** ("Add proper shutdown lifecycle cleanup to GymHandPileScene", **open**): Related cleanup work in the same scene; the slider refactoring is a prerequisite or parallel concern.
- **CG-0MPNWH0X1002OQKN** ("Extract reusable slider component from GymHandPileScene", **open**): A broader extraction that would supersede this optimization by creating a standalone Slider component. This work item represents a smaller, incremental improvement.

## Related work (automated report)

**Work Item Relations**
- **CG-0MPVPSILH0036XAB** — "Create slider helper utility" (completed): Directly relevant because it introduced the `createSlider` utility whose listener forwarding pattern this item aims to optimize. The `createSlider` function's pointer-event architecture is the specific target of this optimization.
- **CG-0MPVPU713004ZOJP** — "Refactor HandPileScene to use slider helper" (completed): Relevant because it was the refactoring that consolidated the three original separate listeners into one. This item seeks to further optimize that consolidated approach.
- **CG-0MPNWGQJ0003034V** — "Add proper shutdown lifecycle cleanup to GymHandPileScene" (open): Relevant as a parallel concern — if listeners become self-contained in `createSlider`, the shutdown cleanup for the scene should be updated accordingly.
- **CG-0MPNWH0X1002OQKN** — "Extract reusable slider component from GymHandPileScene" (open): A broader extraction that would create a standalone Slider component in `src/ui/`. This work item's self-contained listener optimization (Option 1) would be a stepping stone toward that componentization.

**Repository File Matches**
- `src/ui/GymSceneUtils.ts` — Contains the `createSlider` function with the current `isDragging` + `handlePointerMove`/`handlePointerUp` pattern. This is the primary file to modify for Option 1.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Contains the scene-level pointermove/pointerup listener wiring that forwards to all three sliders. This is the secondary file to modify (cleaning up scene wiring once sliders are self-contained).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk of breaking slider behavior**: The drag interaction relies on the pointer being tracked even when it moves outside the hit area. Self-contained listeners must ensure `pointerup` is always caught (e.g., to cancel drag when pointer leaves the scene).
  - **Mitigation**: Use `scene.input.on('pointerup', ...)` which fires regardless of which GameObject is under the pointer. Use `scene.input.on('pointermove', ...)` similarly for global tracking during drag.
- **Scope creep risk**: The optimization could expand into a full reusable Slider component (as described in CG-0MPNWH0X1002OQKN).
  - **Mitigation**: Limit this work item to the listener optimization only. Record the broader extraction as a separate work item (already exists as CG-0MPNWH0X1002OQKN).
- **Risk: Pre-existing build/test failures block verification**: The `dev` branch currently has build errors in `tests/gym/GymHandPileDiscardConsistency.test.ts` (unrelated to this work item). These may need to be resolved before the acceptance criterion "Full project test suite must pass" can be satisfied.
  - **Mitigation**: Flag this as a known pre-existing issue. Consider whether this work item should fix those tests or work around them.
- **Assumption**: The slider's hit area `pointerdown` event is sufficient for drag detection and no additional gesture detection is needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Have the three separate pointermove listeners already been consolidated?" — Answer (agent inference): Yes, the slider refactoring (commit 2660c23, part of CG-0MPDQRNWX00701UE) replaced the three separate listeners with a single consolidated listener that forwards to all three sliders. The current code in GymHandPileScene shows one `pointermove` and one `pointerup` listener.
- Q: "Is the work item description (which references three separate listeners and old method names like `createArcRadiusSlider()`) still accurate?" — Answer (agent inference): No, the description is outdated. The slider utility refactoring removed the old per-slider methods and consolidated the listeners. This intake brief updates the description to reflect current reality.
- Q: "Should the optimization focus on self-contained slider listeners (Option 1) or a lazy scene-level approach (Option 2)?" — Answer (agent inference): Option 1 is preferred because it makes the slider fully self-contained and reusable without requiring the scene to wire up pointermove/pointerup forwarding. It also aligns with the broader extraction goal in CG-0MPNWH0X1002OQKN.

## Summary

`GymHandPileScene.ts` creates various objects (highlightGraphics, slider references, event listeners) that are never explicitly cleaned up when the scene shuts down. This could cause memory leaks or stale references if the scene is restarted.

## Specific Issues

1. **highlightGraphics** - Created lazily in `showValidMoves()` but never destroyed
2. **Slider references** - arcSliderTrack, arcSliderFill, arcSliderHandle, spacingSliderTrack, rotationSliderTrack, etc. are never nulled or destroyed
3. **Event listeners** - Registered via `this.events.once('shutdown', ...)` which is good, but other non-cleaned references remain

## Location

`example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — missing `shutdown()` override

## Current Behaviour

No explicit cleanup — Phaser's GC handles scene destruction but objects with cross-scene references could leak.

## Desired Behaviour

Add a `shutdown()` method that:
- Destroys `highlightGraphics` if it exists
- Nulls out all slider reference properties
- Cleans up any active tweens (`activeMoveTween`)
- Calls `super.shutdown()` (or parent cleanup if available)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GymHandPileScene` has a `shutdown()` method with explicit cleanup for all scene-created GameObjects
- All Phaser GameObjects created by the scene (highlightGraphics, slider components, text labels, UI components) are properly destroyed or nulled on shutdown
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test` passes; `npm run build` succeeds)
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
