# Change upcoming two-card stack to a face-down deck

## Headline

Replace the visible two-card "Upcoming" incident queue with a face-down incident deck (card back + count): each turn the top card is revealed and resolved at end of turn, deck order is constraint-validated at build/reshuffle time, and a new staff "peek" skill (once per turn, as an action) lets the player look at the top card.

## Problem statement

Main Street shows the next two Incident events face-up in an "Upcoming" panel (`incidentQueue`, `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE = 2`). This removes all suspense about upcoming events and makes the early game trivially predictable. The change replaces visible foresight with a face-down deck — the player knows only how many incidents remain, not what they are — while preserving the fairness constraints and adding a staff skill that gives the player controlled, limited foresight.

## Users / user stories

- **Main Street players** — want suspense and uncertainty about what happens next; a face-down deck adds tension to every end of turn.
  - *As a player, I want upcoming incidents hidden until they resolve, so each turn has suspense and I cannot optimise against known future events.*
- **Main Street players** — want agency despite the hidden deck.
  - *As a player who hired a peeking staff member, I want to peek at the top card of the incident deck once per turn as an action, so I can prepare for (or accept) what is coming.*
- **Game designer / balancer** — the difficulty-tuned draw limits (repeat spacing, good/bad streak) must keep working.
  - *As a designer, I want the constrained-draw balance limits applied to the deck order itself so the face-down deck is no more (un)fair than the visible queue.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Face-down deck replaces the visible queue.** The two face-up "Upcoming" cards are removed: `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE` and the 2-card visible refill loop are gone; the incident source is a face-down deck whose remaining count is the only up-front information (a card back + count in the UI panel). No incident content is visible before its turn.
2. **End-of-turn resolution from the deck top.** Each end of turn reveals and resolves the top card of the incident deck through the existing incident reveal presentation (animation + SFX from `animateIncidentReveal`, CG-0MSRGU8M0009F02C; origin changes from the front queue slot to the deck stack). When the deck is exhausted, event discards reshuffle in (existing `reshuffleIfNeeded`/`forceReshuffleFromDiscards` behavior). Seeded determinism is preserved (same seed ⇒ same deck order and sequence).
3. **Constraint-aware deck ordering (option (a)).** Deck order is fixed at build and at every (re)shuffle so the full pre-arranged draw sequence satisfies `incidentRepeatSpacing` (N) and `incidentMaxStreak` (M) from the difficulty preset / runtime config (`state.incidentBalance`); `recordIncidentDraw` history still tracks the resolved sequence. Constraint violation in any deck built from a valid seed is a unit-testable invariant.
4. **Tutorial, docs, and tests updated.** Tutorial T6 "Upcoming Incidents" is reworded to teach the face-down deck + peek (remove "top happens this turn, below next turn"; update `tutorial-en.ts`, `TutorialFlow.ts`, `TutorialScenario.ts` queue setup, and the tutorial-wording contract test, CG-0MSLXI5MT009CDAP). All related documentation (code comments, help text, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`/`AGENTS.md` where the mechanic is described) is updated. Full project test suite passes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Seeded determinism** must be preserved; RNG-consumption order should not change for unrelated subsystems (deck shuffle is the source of deck order).
- **Balance limits stay runtime-configurable** per difficulty preset (`config.incidentRepeatSpacing` / `incidentMaxStreak`) — do not hard-code new values; legacy saves without those fields keep engine defaults (existing `??` fallback in `createIncidentBalanceState`).
- **View/model separation**: the deck stack should be rendered through the core-engine view components (`PileView` or equivalent) rather than bespoke sprite arrays, per AGENTS.md best practice 2; if the existing panel structure is kept, document why.
- **Audio/visual feedback rule (AGENTS.md rule 8)**: deck-top reveal must animate + play SFX via `SoundManager` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS`), respecting reduced-motion and mute/volume settings; the peek action should also give lightweight feedback (`popTextOrIcon` acceptable).
- **SLL layout**: the incident panel keeps SLL anchoring (no new hardcoded pixel positioning).
- **Doc-update policy**: developer-facing changes ship with `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and this file's relevant sections) updated in the same commit; otherwise a doc-update child work item is created and the parent cannot close.
- **Save compatibility**: saved games store `incidentQueue` (`MainStreetState.ts` deserialization path) — the loader must migrate/adapt old saves (e.g. treat saved queue + remaining event deck as the new deck) without crashing mid-game.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts:685` — `export const INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE = 2`.
- `MainStreetState.ts` — `incidentQueue: EventCard[]` populated at setup via `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE` constraint-aware pre-draws (`findConstrainedIncidentIndex`), saved/restored, `createIncidentBalanceFromQueue` derives balance history from it.
- `MainStreetMarket.ts:505` — `refillIncidentQueue()` tops the queue back up to 2 after each resolve, routing every draw through `findConstrainedIncidentIndex`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveIncident()` shifts the front queue card, resolves it, then refills.
- `MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshIncidentQueue()` renders up to 2 face-up cards (+ hover tooltips with full effect text) and "Deck: N".
- `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateIncidentReveal()` flies the resolved card from the front queue slot to the log; `MainStreetTurnController.ts` calls it with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()`.
- Tutorial: `tutorial-en.ts` T6 text ("The event at the top happens at the end of this turn; the ones below happen next turn"), `TutorialFlow.ts` T6 step (confirm gate, `incidentQueue` highlight), `TutorialScenario.ts` builds exactly `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE` queue cards and validates it.
- Staff cards: 7 templates (CSV rows 135–141) providing `handSlotsAdded`, `ongoingCost`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount` — no deck-related ability exists.
- Event deck: ~35 Incident-trigger cards + ~21 Investment-trigger cards; investments are pulled into the market at setup; `MAX_TURNS = 20` — an incident-only deck comfortably covers a game.

## Desired change

- Replace the visible FIFO queue with a face-down incident deck (the incident-only subset of the event deck, as today). Remove `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE`; the deck itself is the incident source.
- At setup and at every reshuffle, arrange the deck order so the entire sequence satisfies repeat/streak limits (constraint-aware ordering, seed-driven). `resolveIncident` pops the top card and records its draw history.
- UI: the "Upcoming" panel becomes a face-down stack (card back + remaining count). Reveal animation originates from the deck position.
- New staff "peek" ability: once per turn, as an action, reveal the top card, then return it face-down.
- Update T6 tutorial, save-load migration, and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — remove `INCIDENT_QUEUE_SIZE`; add a constraint-aware deck-ordering helper (e.g. `orderIncidentDeck()`) built on `findConstrainedIncidentIndex`; `StaffCard` peek field (`peekOncePerTurn?: boolean` or similar).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — setup: build/order the incident deck (no pre-drawn queue, or `incidentQueue` repurposed as the deck); state field + save/load migration for old saves.

# Intake Brief: Implement Community Favour mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET)

## Problem statement

Main Street gives players a single action per turn (buy/move/place) plus a Hint and End Turn. When a player cannot afford any market purchase, the turn offers no meaningful decision — they simply pass. The Community Favour mechanic adds a once-per-turn resource exchange (coins ↔ reputation) available every MarketPhase, giving players a fallback action and creating a "save for a business vs invest in reputation" tension.

## Users

- **New players** (tutorial): learn that reputation is a spendable resource that can be converted to coins when short on cash.
- **Regular players**: use Community Favour to smooth early-game resource imbalance (coin-rich/reputation-poor and vice versa) and to keep turns meaningful when no purchase is affordable.
- **AI players**: gain a legal fallback action so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market.

Example user story: "As a player who can't afford the market card I want, I can spend reputation to gain coins so I don't waste my turn."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Engine action:** A new `PlayerAction` of type `community-favour` with a `direction` (`'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins'`) is implemented in `executeAction`, validated by the EconomyLedger, and legal only during `MarketPhase`, at most **once per turn** (enforced by a `favourUsedThisTurn` flag reset at `DayStart`).
- **AC2 — Exchange rates:** Defaults follow the brainstorming notes and are tunable per-difficulty via `GameConfig`: **2 coins → 1 reputation**; **2 reputation → 3 coins**. Round-trip is lossy (2 coins → 1 rep → 1.5 coins) so no infinite arbitrage is possible. (Producer delegated balancing; rates live in config constants like `reputationCoinDivisor`.)
- **AC3 — UI:** Two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar (one per direction), rendered via SLL zones in `main-street.layout.json`. Buttons are disabled when the player lacks the required resource, when `favourUsedThisTurn` is true, or outside `MarketPhase`. Interaction follows the established animated/sounded action pattern (popTextOrIcon + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX).
- **AC4 — Tutorial:** The tutorial teaches the mechanic with a new action-gated step inserted between T12 and T13 (renumbered T13–T17 → T14–T18), requiring the player to perform the rep→coins direction to afford the Library ($7). Tutorial scenario starting coins reduced from **16 → 12** so the conversion is required (budget: 12 − 4 + 0.625 − 3 + 1.25 = 6.875 < 7 → must convert 2 rep → 3 coins). `TutorialActionType` gains a `community-favour` value wired into `isTutorialActionAllowed` / `isRequiredAction`. (Note: the original description says "T1-T10 action-gated steps" but the current tutorial is T1–T17 with the Library at T13 — the step is inserted there.)
- **AC5 — AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` includes the `community-favour` action when affordable and unused; `scoreAction` assigns a sensible heuristic score; AI turns use the same animated/sounded path as human turns.
- **AC6 — Persistence & transcripts:** `favourUsedThisTurn` is serialized in save/load with a legacy-save backfill (mirroring `actionsRemaining`); the action is recorded as a transcript event (`recordMainStreetEvent`).
- **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: legal exchange, both directions, insufficient funds rejection, once-per-turn enforcement + DayStart reset, MarketPhase gating, legacy save backfill, AI enumeration/scoring. Browser test covers both buttons rendering, disabling, and a full exchange round. All related docs (see Key Files) are updated, and the full project test suite (`npm test`) plus `npm run build` pass.

## Constraints

- Must follow the flat-monorepo conventions (path aliases `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@core-engine`).
- UI must use SLL (no hardcoded pixel positions) per the SLL requirement.
- SFX must use `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` from `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — no game-scoped string literals.
- Reduced-motion and settings-panel mute/volume preferences must be respected.
- Hands/piles and card actions must go through shared engine components (`HandView`, `PileView`, animator helpers); the favour action is a resource exchange (no cards), so it uses the overlay/action-button pattern instead.
- The action is a resource exchange only — it does not consume or create cards, and does not interact with the street grid.

## Existing state

- `PlayerAction` union (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) has no exchange action; `executeAction` decrements `actionsRemaining` for purchase actions.
- Resources are `coins` / `reputation` in `resourceBank`, mirrored by a shared `EconomyLedger` (`syncResourceBankToLedger`); reputation already feeds the income multiplier (`reputationCoinMultiplier`) and final score.
- Tutorial scenario starts at 16 coins / 5 rep with a documented coin budget (T3–T17); the Library purchase at T13 costs $7 and is affordable without conversion.
- Action bar renders End Turn + Hint buttons during `MarketPhase` (`MainStreetRenderer.ts`); SLL zones live in `main-street.layout.json`.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` enumerates legal actions and scores them; `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` drives AI games.

## Desired change

Add the Community Favour exchange to the engine, UI, AI, tutorial, persistence, and transcripts, with per-difficulty configurable rates and a once-per-turn guard. Reduce the tutorial scenario's starting coins so the Library step requires a rep→coins conversion, demonstrating the mechanic's liquidity value.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `CommunityFavourAction` to `PlayerAction`, new `case 'community-favour'` in `executeAction`, validation (MarketPhase, once-per-turn, ledger check), `DayStart` flag reset.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Add `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` to state + setup/save/load with legacy backfill.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — Add exchange-rate constants to `GameConfig` + all presets (e.g. `favourCoinsToRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Render two favour buttons in the market-phase action bar with disabled states.
- `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — Add SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Dispatch the new action through the animated/sounded path; wire `popTextOrIcon` + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add the action to `enumerateLegalActions` and `scoreAction`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Insert the new action-gated step between T12/T13; renumber T13–T17 → T14–T18; extend `TutorialActionType`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Reduce starting coins 16 → 12; update the coin-budget doc table.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Tutorial copy for the new step.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — Ensure the action is captured (existing `'action'` event covers it; add descriptor typing if needed).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Verify AI games remain valid with the new action; regenerate affected baseline fixtures if AI behavior shifts.
- `tests/main-street/` — New unit + browser tests; update tutorial E2E expectations (step count 17 → 18, coin balances).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / Main Street scene `README.md` — Document the mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Baseline churn:** Adding a legal AI action changes AI decision ordering → Monte Carlo CSVs and catalog baselines may shift; baselines must be regenerated via the existing `generate-*-baseline` scripts (verified locally before push).
- **Tutorial budget tightness:** Reducing starting coins to 12 makes the tutorial budget tight by design (the festival at T14 offsets the Library spend); the budget table and T12/T13 copy must be updated consistently. If E2E balance assertions break, they should be updated to the new expected values, not weakened.
- **Renumbering risk:** Inserting a step renumbers T13–T17 → T14–T18; all references (i18n keys, E2E tests, `tutorial-en.ts`, `TutorialFlow.ts` docs) must be updated in the same change.
- **Scope guard:** No changes to card data, street grid, adjacency, or challenge systems; the exchange is purely a resource operation. Any ideas discovered during implementation (e.g. a market "sell card for coins" mechanic) should be filed as new work items, not folded in.
- **Assumption (documented):** The action does **not** consume `actionsRemaining` — it is a free once-per-turn action available during MarketPhase, so it functions as a true fallback when the player cannot afford a purchase. This preserves the description's intent ("meaningful action every turn, even when they cannot afford a market purchase") and avoids competing with the purchase economy. (If the producer prefers it to consume the action, the change is a one-line guard removal plus AC rewording.)

## Related work

- CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 — Tutorial coin-budget "cost-at-play" change (TutorialScenario.ts budget table; this feature modifies that budget).
- CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL — Main Street two-step click-to-place flow (same action-bar/tutorial area; tutorial gating must remain compatible).
- CG-0MRER3RE300418SG — Fractional coins (income multiplier precision; exchange rates must not floor fractional values).
- CG-0MSOKG89N001LDT4 — Festival-hold timing in T11 (tutorial copy adjacent to the insertion point).
- CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO / CG-0MMLR20XP1IPPD03 — Difficulty preset tuning (config constant pattern used for the new rates).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Exchange rates — The description proposes '2 coins → 1 reputation' and '2 reputation → 3 coins'. Are these rates confirmed, or should they be balanced differently (e.g. asymmetric 3:1/4:1)?" — Answer (Producer, interactive reply): "balance them as you see fit". Final decision: keep 2→1 and 2→3 as defaults, exposed as per-difficulty config constants; round-trip is lossy (25% haircut on the rep→coins leg) which prevents arbitrage. Research: reviewed `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` (reputationCoinDivisor/maxReputationCoinMultiplier pattern) and `MainStreetState.ts` (EconomyLedger sync) — rates are purely data-level, no engine changes needed to retune later.
- Q2: "UI interaction model — single toggle button or two separate buttons?" — Answer (Producer): "one for each". Final: two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar, each labelled with its direction, each disabled when its input resource is insufficient.
- Q3: "Per-turn limit — 'Once per turn' means a single exchange per turn?" — Answer (Producer): "correct". Final: `favourUsedThisTurn` flag set on first exchange, reset at DayStart; both directions share the single per-turn budget (one exchange total per turn).
- Prior answers: none changed.

# Intake Brief: Expand player hand to 3 slots and rework marketplace to single row

## Problem statement

Main Street's marketplace is a two-row board (4 business slots + 3 investment slots) with two separate paid refreshes and no player hand capacity to plan ahead with. This rework simplifies the market to a single 3-card line with one re-roll button, grows the base hand to 3 slots, and defers card payment from purchase time to play time so the hand acts as a free planning buffer.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they see one simple market line, hold up to 3+ cards in hand, and can acquire cards for free and pay only when they commit to playing them.
- **TCE developers** — maintainers of the shared engine and Main Street, who need the two-row market logic (rows, per-row refresh costs, buy-to-hand pricing) replaced cleanly with a single-row model, keeping AI, Monte Carlo, tutorial, and save-load in sync.

Example user stories:
- "As a player, I want one simple market line with a single re-roll button so I can read my options at a glance."
- "As a player, I want to move market cards into my hand for free and pay only when I play them, so I can plan my turn and hedge against a bad day's market."
- "As a player, I want a hand that holds up to 3 cards (and more with staff) so I have room to build a buffer."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hand:** base `maxHandSize` is 3 (was 2); staff cards' `handSlotsAdded` still stack above 3 (no hard cap); the hand renders as one horizontal row via `HandView` (no bespoke rendering).
2. **Single-row market:** exactly 3 visible cards each day, always at least 1 business card; the remaining composition is randomly drawn within the bounds "1–2 business, 0–1 upgrade, 0–1 event" (i.e. one of: 2B+1U, 2B+1E, 1B+1U+1E), subject to deck availability and existing reshuffle conventions.
3. **One re-roll button:** replaces both `REFRESH_DEVELOPMENT_COST` and `REFRESH_INVESTMENTS_COST` with a single `REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 5`; the Accountant's `refreshCostDiscount` applies to it. Re-roll discards all currently-visible (unmoved/unpurchased) cards and refills the whole line to full composition; unlimited per turn while affordable (same cadence as today).
4. **Acquisition & payment:** moving a market card to hand is free **of coins** but now **consumes the player's single daily action** per the action economy (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R — updated at that item's intake: move-to-hand and play-from-hand are each one action); direct buy-and-place remains, still pays immediately, and costs **50% more** than the listed cost (surcharge set at CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R intake); playing a card from hand pays its listed cost at play time (business on placement; upgrade/event when played/triggered); discarding from hand is free, allowed any time during the player's turn, and sends the card to its corresponding discard pile.
5. **Consumers & quality gates:** AI strategy, Monte Carlo harness, tutorial flow + scenario validation, save-load migration, and docs are updated for the single-row market; all tests pass (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds, including updated tutorial E2E tests.

## Constraints

- Staff-card market remains a separate board from the single marketplace.
- Community-space cards count as "business" cards for the 1–2 business slots.
- Market is not refilled mid-turn after moves/purchases (refill at day start, as today); end-of-turn market cycling (`cycleMarketCards`) still applies.
- Deferred payment is intentional: the player may hold cards they cannot yet afford to play; no balance change is requested beyond the costs already specified.
- Do NOT implement the action economy (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R) here; this rework is a design prerequisite for it, not part of it. Action semantics per that item's intake: one action per day (two while a General Manager is employed); actions = move market→hand, play hand→street, direct buy-and-place (+50%), hire staff; refresh, sell, hint, discard, end-turn are free.

## Existing state

- `MARKET_BUSINESS_SLOTS = 4`, `MARKET_INVESTMENT_SLOTS = 3` (2 upgrades + 1 event) in `MainStreetCards.ts`; `REFRESH_DEVELOPMENT_COST = 2`, `REFRESH_INVESTMENTS_COST = 2`.
- `MainStreetState.maxHandSize` defaults to 2; staff `handSlotsAdded` grows it (prior decision CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD: "start 2, growable, no hard cap").
- `purchaseBusinessToHand` / `purchaseEvent` deduct coins at purchase time; upgrades apply directly from market.
- Renderer draws two rows with two refresh buttons; AI, Monte Carlo, tutorial scenario validation, and save format all reference `market.development` / `market.investments`.

## Desired change

Replace the two-row market with a single line (3 cards, always ≥1 business, random within bounds), a single €5 re-roll (Accountant discount applies), a base-3 growable hand, and a free-move/deferred-payment economy where direct buy-and-place remains an option. Update all consumers (state, market logic, commands, renderer, AI, Monte Carlo, tutorial, save-load, docs, tests) consistently.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — replace market-slot constants with single-row constants (e.g. `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS = 3`, business min/max, upgrade/event max); `REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 5`; deprecate the two `REFRESH_*` and `MARKET_*_SLOTS` constants.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `maxHandSize` default 3; market state shape (single row); save migration for old two-row saves.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — single-row refill with random composition; free `moveToHand`; `playBusinessFromHand` / `playUpgradeFromHand` / `playEventFromHand` with cost-at-play; `discardFromHand`; single `canRefreshMarket` / `refreshMarket` (€5, Accountant discount); `cycleMarketCards` single-row; remove per-row purchase helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — replace `refreshDevelopmentCommand` / `refreshInvestmentsCommand` with `refreshMarketCommand`; add move/play/discard-from-hand commands.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — single-row market reads; free-move-aware strategy.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — iterate single market row.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — single-row market layout, one re-roll button, cost-at-play affordances.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — market deal-in animation (single row), phase wiring.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — click/drag flows: move-to-hand vs buy-and-place vs play-from-hand.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` / `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — copy updates for the new market/refresh wording.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts`, `TutorialScenario.ts`, `TutorialState.ts` — steps/validation referencing the two-row market ('buy-event', 'buy-and-place', 'select-business').
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — migrate saved two-row market + `maxHandSize=2`.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/refresh-development.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/refresh-investments.test.ts` (→ single refresh-market tests), `tests/main-street/market-extraction-parity.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (Accountant discount), tutorial E2E parts, AI-strategy tests, hand tests.
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `example-games/main-street/README.md`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** — "Limit player actions to one action per turn (action economy)" (open): lists "move market→hand" as an action; this rework is a design prerequisite (free moves + single-row market) — do not implement here.
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** (done) — merged single-row hand; this item raises its base `maxHandSize` 2→3.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** (done) — Group F staff; Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` now applies to the single re-roll.
- **CG-0MSRGU17D0061SGT** (done) — market deal-in animation per row; must be adapted to one row.
- **CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY** (done) — 50+ card design; card costs unchanged (payment timing changes only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Tutorial E2E sensitivity:** scenario-placed market cards + always-3-card composition change T3/T7/T10/T13 expectations; tutorial steps and E2E parts must be updated in the same item or they will fail the quality gate.
- **Save-load compatibility:** old saves hold a two-row market and `maxHandSize=2`; a migration (mirroring the held-event merge in CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD) is required or deserialization fails.
- **AI/Monte Carlo baselines:** free-move vs paid-play changes the AI's evaluation; `monte-carlo-baseline.json`/results may need re-baselining — verify, don't silently break the harness.
- **Deferred-payment overreach:** players may fill the hand with unaffordable cards; intended design, not a bug — no balance change in scope.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the action-economy item (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R) and any balance tuning of the €5 cost are out of scope; record as linked work, do not implement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (re-roll pricing): "How should the single re-roll button be priced, and does the Accountant's refresh discount apply?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "€5 (yes accountant stands)". Research: current `REFRESH_DEVELOPMENT_COST=2` / `REFRESH_INVESTMENTS_COST=2` (MainStreetCards.ts:688-691); Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` from CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 applies via `refreshInvestmentsCost` (MainStreetMarket.ts). Accepted: single `REFRESH_MARKET_COST=5`, discount applies.
- Q2 (acquisition path): "Is the hand the only way to acquire market cards, and how many moves per turn?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "direct buy-and-place is allowed, can move as many as the hand/street/budget allows". Accepted: both paths remain; moves free and unlimited in count.
- Q3 (hand capacity): "Base 3 growable, or hard cap 3?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "can grow". Research: prior decision CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD chose "start 2, growable". Accepted: base 3, growable via staff `handSlotsAdded`.
- Q4 (market composition): "Always exactly 3 with a fixed rule, or random within bounds? Can upgrades and events coexist?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "a (random selection that always includes at least one business)". Accepted: exactly 3 cards, ≥1 business, random within 1–2B/0–1U/0–1E (combos: 2B+1U, 2B+1E, 1B+1U+1E).

# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
- **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
- **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
- **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
- **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

AC2 is therefore delivered; remaining scope = trigger, hire/decline/let-go, employment slots, presentation, tests/docs.

# Intake Brief: Limit player actions to one action per turn (action economy)

## Problem statement

Main Street currently lets the player perform unlimited purchases/plays during the MarketPhase, so each day reduces to "do everything affordable." There is no cost to *choosing* — the tension that should define a day. This item introduces a strict action economy: the player may take exactly **one action per day** (two while a General Manager is employed), forcing a meaningful "what do I do with my one action?" decision each turn.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — each day they weigh one decisive move against free supporting operations (market re-roll, selling, hint, discarding), building a plan over multiple days.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the action budget enforced in the rules engine, commands, turn controller, AI, Monte Carlo, tutorial, and save-load consistently, so the mechanic is testable and the AI behaves sensibly under the limit.

Example user stories:
- "As a player, I want exactly one meaningful action per day so every day feels like a real decision."
- "As a player, I want to move a market card to my hand today and play it tomorrow, so my action economy lets me plan ahead."
- "As a player, I want to hire a General Manager so I get a second action per day while I keep paying their salary."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Action budget:** the player has **1 action per day** during MarketPhase, resetting at day start; spending the action blocks further action-type operations until the next day; refresh/re-roll, sell, hint, discard-from-hand, and end-turn remain free (non-actions) and unlimited.
2. **Action list:** each of the following consumes the single daily action — move a market card to hand (free of coins), play a card from hand to the street (pays the card's listed cost), **direct buy-and-place** (market→street without the hand; pays immediately; **costs 50% more** than the listed cost, per the operator decision at intake), and hire a staff card from the staff market.
3. **General Manager card:** a new `staff-general-manager` StaffCard grants **+1 action per day** while employed (2 actions instead of 1); stats set via the balancing methodology (proposed cost 20, ongoingCost 5, handSlotsAdded 4, new `actionsPerTurn` ability field outside the cost curve, mirroring `refreshCostDiscount`); CSV column + `StaffCard` interface + template loading updated.
4. **Enforcement & consumers:** `executeAction`/commands reject action-type operations when the budget is spent; state carries the remaining-action count; turn controller spends/refills it; AI strategy and Monte Carlo harness respect the 1–2 action limit; save-load round-trips or safely derives the budget; renderer shows the remaining-action indicator and the buy-and-place premium; tutorial updated (new step/copy covering the action economy and the +50% buy-and-place premium, per operator).
5. **Quality gates:** unit tests cover budget enforcement (spend, reset at day start, GM +1), the 50% premium pricing, and AI/Monte Carlo behavior under the limit; tutorial E2E and scenario validation updated; `npm test` passes and `npm run build` succeeds. All related documentation updated (rules engine, card catalog, tutorial copy, README/AGENTS as needed).

## Constraints

- **Free operations** are NOT actions: market re-roll/refresh, selling a business, hint (still 1/day), discarding from hand, and end-turn.
- The **single daily action resets at day start** (MarketPhase), not per-phase.
- The General Manager's extra action applies only **while employed** (staff ongoing-cost model as today).
- This item does **not** implement the staff job-applicant mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX) — hiring from the existing staff market board is the in-scope "hire" action.
- The +50% buy-and-place premium applies to direct market→street placement (business cards under the single-row market); hand-based play pays the listed cost.
- Scope-creep guard: balance tuning of the premium %, rework of the hand-expansion mechanics, and the job-applicant mechanic are recorded as related work, not implemented here.

## Existing state

- No action economy: `executeAction` (MainStreetEngine.ts:167) validates only phase, not an action budget; `PlayerAction` union has buy-business / buy-business-to-hand / buy-upgrade / buy-event / play-event / end-turn (refresh and sell are separate commands).
- Staff cards live in `card-data.csv` (7 cards today: Assistant→Executive, Socialite, Accountant) loaded into `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` (MainStreetCards.ts:192-208); `StaffCard` interface has `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn?`, `refreshCostDiscount?` (MainStreetCards.ts:390-408).
- No "General Manager" card exists (closest: `staff-manager`, +2 hand slots, cost 7).
- Balancing: staff cost curve `ongoingCost * 5 + handSlotsAdded * 5` (docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md; src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts:140-142); ability fields (refreshCostDiscount, reputationPerTurn) are excluded from the curve.
- AI picks one action per `chooseAction` call (MainStreetAiStrategy.ts) and the harness loops it; the action budget must cap the loop.

## Desired change

Add a per-day action budget (base 1, +1 while a General Manager is employed) enforced in state + engine + commands; define the action list (move-to-hand, play-from-hand, direct buy-and-place at +50%, hire staff) with everything else free; add the `staff-general-manager` card with its new `actionsPerTurn` ability; update AI, Monte Carlo, turn controller, renderer, tutorial, save-load, and docs; cover with unit + E2E tests.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — add `staff-general-manager` row (cost 20, ongoing 5, handSlots 4, actionsPerTurn 1) and the new `actionsPerTurn` column header (mirroring `refreshCostDiscount`); keep the balancing tool (`scripts/run-balance-cards.ts`) schema in sync.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `StaffCard.actionsPerTurn?` field + template loading; validate the new CSV column.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `actionsRemaining` (reset to 1 + GM bonus at DayStart); serialize/deserialize handling (derive or round-trip).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `executeAction` budget check + spend; day-start reset (GM bonus lookup from employed staff cards).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `purchaseStaffCard` unchanged; direct buy-and-place helpers gain the +50% premium (`buy-and-place` price = cost × 1.5) and budget awareness.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — action spend on move/play/buy-and-place/hire commands; free ops (refresh, sell, hint, discard) untouched.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `enumerateLegalActions` filtered by the budget (only action-type moves when budget > 0); `end-turn` when the budget is spent.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — loop respects the 1–2 action cap per day.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — spend/refill wiring, action-count gating for input, day-start reset.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetInputManager.ts` / `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` / `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — action-counter UI, +50% premium affordances, updated copy.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` / `TutorialScenario.ts` / `TutorialState.ts` — new/updated steps for the action economy and the buy-and-place premium; E2E parts updated.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — save schema/migration for the action budget.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (new), staff/GM tests (`tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`), AI-strategy tests, Monte Carlo tests, tutorial E2E parts, save-load tests.
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Core Actions + turn structure), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (GM card), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` (new ability field), `example-games/main-street/README.md`, tutorial docs.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2** (in_progress, prerequisite) — hand-to-3-slots + single-row market rework; defines free-of-coins move/play and the market re-roll; description updated at this intake: move-to-hand and play-from-hand are each one action, buy-and-place is one action at +50%.
- **CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX** (open, related) — staff job-applicant mechanic; distinct from this item's "hire from the staff market" action; do not implement here.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** (done) — Group F staff abilities (Accountant `refreshCostDiscount`); precedent for ability fields outside the cost curve and for extending `StaffCard`.
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** (done) — merged single-row hand; base hand size raised to 3 by the rework item above.
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** (done) — no-turn-limit default; relevant to pass-turns-without-acting behavior under the new budget.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Prerequisite ordering:** the action economy assumes the single-row market + hand rework lands first (free-coin move semantics, single re-roll). Verify CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 is merged before/with this item; keep the two AC sets consistent (cross-update already applied).
- **AI/Monte Carlo behavior shift:** with 1–2 actions/day, the greedy strategy's single-action evaluation is a natural fit, but Monte Carlo baselines may shift; re-baseline `monte-carlo-baseline.json` and verify the harness, don't silently break it.
- **Tutorial sensitivity:** existing steps assume unlimited buys/refreshes (e.g. buy-and-place, multiple acquisitions per day); tutorial steps and E2E parts must be updated in the same item or the quality gate fails.
- **50% premium rounding:** define rounding for odd costs (e.g. round up to nearest 0.5? document the rule) to keep pricing deterministic and testable.
- **Assumption — discard stays free:** the rework defines discard-from-hand as free; kept as a non-action (operator confirmed refresh/sell/hint are non-actions; discard not contradicted). Flag if it should cost an action.
- **Scope-creep risk:** balance tuning of the premium/action economy, the job-applicant mechanic, and hand-rework changes are out of scope; record as linked work (CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX, CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2), do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (action list): "What counts as an action — do refresh/re-roll, sell, and hint count?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "refresh/re-roll is not an action. sell it [sell is not an action]. hint is not." Source: interactive reply. Accepted: only move/play/buy-and-place/hire consume the action; refresh, sell, hint are free.
- Q2 (General Manager card): "Does the GM card exist, or must it be created, and what stats?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Not sure, check and act accordingly. If the card needs to be created then use the balancing algorithms to set stats." Research: no `staff-general-manager` in card-data.csv; staff cost curve `ongoingCost*5 + handSlotsAdded*5`, ability fields excluded (docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md, src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts). Accepted: create the card; proposed cost 20, ongoing 5, handSlots 4, +1 action; ability tracked as a new `actionsPerTurn` CSV column/interface field outside the curve.
- Q3 (reset timing): "When does the action counter reset?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "start of the day". Accepted: reset at DayStart/MarketPhase each day.
- Q4 (move-to-hand semantics): "The prerequisite rework defines market→hand moves as free and unlimited — is moving to hand free or an action?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "both moving from marketplace to hand and hand to street is an action, update CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 accordingly". Research: CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 AC4 previously said "free and unlimited"; updated to "free of coins but consumes the single daily action" (wl comment CG-C0MSW6UJ27007KTH6 + description patch). Accepted: move-to-hand is an action (free of coins); play-from-hand is an action.
- Q5 (buy-and-place & hiring): "Is direct buy-and-place one action, and is hiring staff one action?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "buy-and-place is a single action, but costs 50% more (this needs to be added to the tutorial as well as to the rules engine)." Accepted: buy-and-place = 1 action at +50%; hiring a staff card = 1 action; tutorial + rules engine updated.
- Q6 (GM stats): "Confirm General Manager stats: cost 20, ongoingCost 5, handSlotsAdded 4, +1 action/turn?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "OK". Accepted: as proposed; verified against the staff cost-curve band (Executive parity).

# Intake Brief: Fix empty user.email in global git config blocking wl sync (CG-0MSUZASM10035QSG)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

## Problem Statement

The global git config (`~/.gitconfig`) has an empty `user.email` value, which caused `implement.py` commits to be authored with empty emails (`Sorra the Orc <>`). These empty-email commits accumulated on the remote `refs/worklog/data` ref, and the `wl sync` pre-push hook author-identity gate began refusing to merge worklog data, blocking all git pushes. The current workaround (`WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) masks the problem but leaves the root cause unaddressed.

## Users

- **Agent / operator** — needs `wl sync` (via pre-push hook) to work without manual workaround env vars.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Global git config fixed:** `~/.gitconfig` no longer contains an empty `user.email` entry; `git config --global user.email` returns a valid, non-empty email.
2. **No empty-email commits:** Future commits authored by agents (via implement.py) have valid author emails.
3. **Pre-push hook unblocked:** `wl sync` succeeds in the pre-push hook without requiring `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`.
4. **Local override cleaned up:** The local `.git/config` `user.email` override (which was added as a band-aid) is either removed (if global fix is sufficient) or documented as intentional.
5. **Test suite passes:** `npm test` and `npm run build` remain green.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing agent workflows or commit signing.
- Global config change affects all repos on the machine — the email chosen should be the operator's standard agent email.
- The workaround `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` should be documented as deprecated once fixed.

## Existing State

- `~/.gitconfig` has `user.email=` (empty) and `user.name=Sorra the Orc`.
- `.git/config` (local) has `user.email=250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` (override).
- `wl sync` currently works with `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` bypass.
- Remote `refs/worklog/data` contains only commits with valid emails (the offending commits were pushed before the local override was added, then overwritten by clean syncs).

## Desired Change

Remove or replace the empty `user.email` entry in `~/.gitconfig` with a valid email address, and remove the local `.git/config` override if no longer needed.

## Key Files

- `~/.gitconfig` — **modify** — remove empty `user.email`, set valid email
- `.git/config` — **modify or remove** — remove local `user.email` override if no longer needed

## Related Work

- **wl pre-push author-identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB)** — the gate implementation that validates author emails; referenced in the issue description (work item not found in this project).
- **release-windows skill (CG-0MSQ6MV7N0085V9R)** — discovered from the same parent work item; unrelated fix.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Global config scope change:** Setting a global email affects all repos — confirm this is the intended agent identity email.
- **Commit signature impact:** If commits were previously made with empty emails and signed/verified, changing the email won't fix existing bad commits — only prevents future ones.

### Assumptions
- The operator's standard agent email (`250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`) is acceptable as the global `user.email`.
- No existing remote worklog data commits have empty emails (confirmed: all remote commits have valid emails).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. **Q: What email should be set globally — the agent email or the operator's personal email?**
   - A: (not yet answered — defaulting to `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` based on current local override)

# Intake Brief: Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner instead of center-to-center

**Work item:** CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP | **Priority:** medium | **Type:** feature

## Problem statement

In Main Street, the synergy lines (colloquially the "wyndergy" lines) between adjacent synergistic businesses are drawn from slot **center** to slot **center**, so each line runs across the interiors of both cards. The lines should instead connect the two cards at their **facing edges** (orthogonally adjacent slots) or **facing corners** (diagonally adjacent slots), so they read as links *between* the cards rather than strokes *through* them.

## Users

Players of Main Street who rely on synergy lines to read adjacency bonuses at a glance.

- As a player, I want synergy lines to start and end at the edges/corners of the two connected businesses rather than at their centers, so the link visually connects the cards instead of running through them.
- As a player, I want diagonal synergy links to run corner-to-corner so the connection reads cleanly across the diagonal.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Orthogonally adjacent pairs: line endpoints lie on the facing edges of the two cards (not their centers).
2. Diagonally adjacent pairs: line endpoints lie at the facing corners of the two cards.
3. Extended-range pairs (`synergyRangeBonus` ≥ 1, Chebyshev range 2+): endpoints are clipped to the card boundaries in the same edge/corner manner (straight line between facing edges/corners).
4. The animated formation line in `MainStreetAnimator.animateSynergyFormation()` uses the same clipped endpoints as the static lines — no visible discrepancy between the draw-in line and the persistent line.
5. The outer glow stroke (6px, 0.2 alpha) shares the same clipped endpoints as the main 3px stroke.
6. New/extended unit and/or browser tests cover the endpoint geometry (edge vs. corner cases); existing synergy tests still pass.
7. Full project test suite passes; `npm run build` succeeds.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (geometry notes in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetAnimator.ts`), `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Reuse existing layout math (`streetX`, `streetTop`, `slotW`, `slotGap`, `slotH`, `streetCols`, `streetRowGap`); no new layout configuration.
- Keep current depth ordering (lines above the street grid, behind tooltip zones).
- The visual card is inset 2px from the slot rect (`renderW/H = slotW − 4`); endpoint clipping may target the slot rect or the visual card rect — recommend the slot rect for consistency with existing geometry (implementation detail, note in code).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetRenderer.drawSynergyLines()` computes `x1,y1` / `x2,y2` at slot centers and strokes a 3px main line plus a 6px/0.2-alpha glow.
- `MainStreetAnimator.animateSynergyFormation()` duplicates the same slot-center math — its doc comment explicitly says the geometry "mirrors `MainStreetRenderer.drawSynergyLines()` (slot centres from the same layout math)".

## Desired change

Clip the line to the two card rectangles: compute the intersection of the center-to-center segment with each card's rect boundary; draw the main and glow strokes between those two boundary points. This yields edge-to-edge for orthogonal neighbors, corner-to-corner for diagonal neighbors, and generalizes to extended-range pairs.

Preferably extract a shared `synergyLineEndpoints(pair, layout)` helper used by **both** the renderer and the animator, eliminating the duplicated (and now deliberately divergent) geometry.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `drawSynergyLines()`: replace center endpoints with boundary-clipped endpoints (main + glow strokes).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateSynergyFormation()`: use the same clipped endpoints for the draw-in line.
- (optional) shared endpoint helper — in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` or a small new module imported by both.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts` — extend or add endpoint-geometry unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-formation.browser.test.ts` — verify the animated line matches (if geometry is exposed for assertions).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — update line-rendering notes.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR** "Synergy link formation animation" (completed, in_review) — introduced `animateSynergyFormation()`, which mirrors the renderer geometry; this item changes that shared geometry in both places.
- **CG-0MSKS963N000ZSTU** "Library next to Bookshop should trigger synergy bonus (line not drawn)" (done) — synergy line coverage on the grid.
- **CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4** "Dynamic synergy bonus text on business cards" (done) — related synergy visuals.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — current synergy-line rendering documentation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "edge to edge or corner to corner" generalizes to range-2+ pairs as endpoints clipped at the facing card boundaries (the straight line still crosses intermediate cells). If far pairs should instead be routed around intermediate cards, that is a separate decision and out of scope here.
- **Assumption:** the animated formation line should match the static line geometry (it currently mirrors it by design).
- **Risk:** duplicated geometry in renderer + animator drifts — extracting a shared helper avoids regression ("mirrors" comment is a smell).
- **Scope guard:** pure visual change; `computeSynergyPairs()` / `diffNewSynergyPairs()` logic untouched.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed intent ("drawn from edge to edge or corner to corner, not center to center") is unambiguous given the 8-way adjacency model, and assumptions above are recorded. Source: operator intake request (`/intake`, --priority medium), 2026-08-14.

# Intake Brief: Business cards incur ongoing per-turn cost (1/4 purchase price, min 0.25), even in hand

**Headline:** Every business card in Main Street gains an `ongoingCost` field (set per-card in CSV) that is deducted from coins every turn during the income phase — whether the card is placed on the street grid or held in the player's hand.

## Problem statement

Main Street already applies ongoing costs to staff cards and community-space cards (Library) each income phase. Business cards — the core tableau cards players invest in — currently have no running cost, making them pure income generators once placed. Adding an ongoing cost for business cards creates a meaningful trade-off: placing a business card is a capital investment that also commits recurring funds.

## Users

- **Players** building a Main Street tableau: business cards now have a running cost that affects long-term strategy — higher-cost cards are riskier to hold and place.
- **Producer/balance analysts**: the ongoing cost field (CSV) feeds the balance methodology, just like `ongoingCost` on staff and community-space cards.

User stories:
- "As a player, I want to see the per-turn cost of each business card displayed on the card art and in tooltips, so I can factor ongoing expenses into my placement decisions."
- "As a player, I want business cards I hold in hand to still incur their per-turn cost, so that hoarding expensive cards is penalised."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **BusinessCard interface:** The `BusinessCard` interface in `MainStreetCards.ts` gains a `readonly ongoingCost: number` property (defaults to `0` for legacy cards).
2. **CSV parsing:** `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness` reads the existing `ongoingCost` CSV column (column 28) and assigns it to the `BusinessCard` instance. Cards with missing/empty `ongoingCost` default to `0`.
3. **Per-turn deduction:** A new `applyBusinessOngoingCosts(state)` function iterates over **all business cards in `state.hand` AND all business cards on `state.streetGrid`**, sums their `ongoingCost` values, and deducts the total from `coins` during the income phase. Deduction is clamped at 0 coins (no negative coins) and logged to the activity log with the same pattern as `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
4. **Turn integration:** `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` is called in `processEndOfTurn` during the `IncomePhase`, immediately after `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
5. **Visual display:** Business card SVG generation (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) and tooltip formatting (`cardTooltipText`) show the ongoing cost when > 0, using the same `-[value]/turn` format as staff/community-space cards (red/orange text).
6. **Card display:** Cards in hand and on the street grid display the ongoing cost visually (SVG-based card art shows `-0.50/turn` style label).
7. **Testing:** Unit tests validate that: (a) `ongoingCost` is parsed from CSV for business cards; (b) `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` deducts from both hand and street cards; (c) coins are clamped at 0; (d) the cost appears in card SVG and tooltip; (e) `processEndOfTurn` correctly chains the new function.

## Constraints

- The `ongoingCost` CSV column already exists (column 28) — no CSV schema change needed. The column is currently populated only for staff/community-space cards; business cards have an empty trailing value.
- Deduction happens **every turn** during the income phase — no separate "round" concept.
- Only the `business` card family is affected (not `community-space`, `staff`, `event`, or `upgrade`).
- Existing save data with business cards will serialize correctly (the field is `readonly` but set at parse time; legacy deserialised cards get default `0`).
- The min 0.25 is a balance decision for individual card data, not a code-level clamp — the engine deducts whatever value is on the card.

## Existing state

- `BusinessCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~232–310): no `ongoingCost` property.
- `StaffCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~394–400): has `readonly ongoingCost: number`.
- `CommunitySpaceCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~954–961): has `readonly ongoingCost: number`.
- `parseBusinessRow` (`MainStreetCards.ts` line ~99): does NOT read `ongoingCost` from CSV.
- `parseStaffRow` / `parseCommunitySpaceRow`: DO read `ongoingCost`.
- `processEndOfTurn` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` line ~782): calls `applyIncome`, `applyStaffOngoingCosts`, `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
- `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` lines ~1217–1270): deduct costs, clamp at 0, log.
- SVG generation (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` `generateBusinessCardSvg`): does NOT show ongoing cost for business cards (only for staff/community-space in other functions).
- Tooltip formatting (`MainStreetFormatting.ts` `cardTooltipText`): does NOT show `ongoingCost` for business cards.

## Desired change

1. Add `ongoingCost` to the `BusinessCard` interface.
2. Wire `ongoingCost` into `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness` (read from CSV column 28).
3. Create `applyBusinessOngoingCosts(state)` following the `applyStaffOngoingCosts` pattern, iterating over both hand and street.
4. Call `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` in `processEndOfTurn` during income phase.
5. Update `generateBusinessCardSvg` to render ongoing cost label (red text, "-X/turn" below cost circle).
6. Update `cardTooltipText` for `business` family to include ongoing cost info.
7. Add unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Add `ongoingCost` to `BusinessCard` interface; wire into `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()`; call it in `processEndOfTurn`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Update `cardTooltipText` for business family to show ongoing cost.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — Update `generateBusinessCardSvg` to render ongoing cost label.
- `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for the new mechanic.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Populate `ongoingCost` column for business cards (balance: 1/4 purchase price, min 0.25).

## Related work

- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE** "Why would a library bring in money" — Introduced `ongoingCost` for community-space cards; established the pattern for `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
- **CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX** "Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic" — Staff cards already have `ongoingCost`; the pattern for `applyStaffOngoingCosts` is the canonical reference.
- **CG-0MSXUHPGT003ZMU2** "Browser test: assert count-only rendering in game-over overlay" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).
- **CG-0MS7UEUL000610A2** "When buying a card it animates to the wrong position" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).
- **CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39** "Coloretto full rules expansion" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Legacy save data:** Deserialised `BusinessCard` objects from older saves won't have `ongoingCost` (will be `undefined`). Mitigation: `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` uses `card.ongoingCost ?? 0` (nullish coalescing), consistent with existing ongoing-cost functions.
- **CSV data entry:** The seed mentions "1/4 purchase price, min 0.25" — documented as a balance decision for CSV data entry, NOT a code-level clamp. All ~50 business cards need manual CSV population by a producer; engine implementation is independent.
- **Scope creep — other families:** Only the `business` family is affected. `upgrade`, `event`, `staff`, and `community-space` cards are excluded. The per-card field structure already supports future extension.
- **Hand holding:** Players can hold up to 3 business cards in hand (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2). Cumulative hand + street ongoing costs could be significant; this is a balance concern, not an implementation risk.
- **Docs:** `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Ongoing Cost table, income-phase summary) and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` must be updated per the doc-update policy.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Per-card field vs. computed formula: for business cards, should each card have its own `ongoingCost` in CSV, or should it be a computed value `Math.max(0.25, cost / 4)` from the purchase price?" — Answer (producer): "In CSV". Research: the CSV already has an `ongoingCost` column (column 28) used by staff and community-space card rows; business rows currently leave it empty. The seed's "1/4 purchase price, min 0.25" is a balance guideline for populating that CSV column, not engine logic. Source: interactive reply during intake.
- Q2: "'End of the round' vs. Main Street's turn model: Main Street operates on turns, not rounds. Does 'deducted at the end of the round' mean every turn during the income phase?" — Answer (producer): "every turn". Research: `processEndOfTurn` (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) runs an `IncomePhase` each turn and already calls `applyStaffOngoingCosts` and `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` there; the new business cost hooks into the same phase. Source: interactive reply during intake; `MainStreetEngine.ts:782`.
- Q3: "Scope of 'business cards': Main Street has business, community-space, staff, event, and upgrade families. Does 'all business cards' mean only the `business` family?" — Answer (producer): "only business". Research: `BusinessCard` is the core tableau-card family (`MainStreetCards.ts:232`); it currently lacks `ongoingCost`, unlike `StaffCard` and `CommunitySpaceCard`. The mechanic excludes upgrades, events, staff, and community spaces. Source: interactive reply during intake.
data.title: Main Street: business cards incur ongoing per-turn cost (1/4 purchase price, min 0.25), even in hand

## Summary

Write the failing unit-test suite that defines the target single-row market and from-hand behavior for CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2, driving subsequent implementation children via TDD.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Tests define the single-row composition contract: exactly 3 cards, always ≥1 business card, drawn within the bounds "1–2 business, 0–1 upgrade, 0–1 event" (combos: 2B+1U, 2B+1E, 1B+1U+1E), using `createSeededRng` for determinism. Community-space cards count as business.
2. Tests define `refreshMarket`: costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 5` (Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` applied), discards all visible/unmoved cards, refills the whole line to full composition; unlimited per turn while affordable.
3. Tests define free move-to-hand (bounded only by `maxHandSize`) and preserved direct buy-and-place with immediate payment.
4. Tests define cost-at-play: business pays on placement; upgrade/event pays when played/triggered.
5. Tests define free discard-from-hand any time during the player's turn, sending the card to its corresponding discard pile.
6. Tests define `maxHandSize` base of 3, growable via staff `handSlotsAdded` (no hard cap).

## Summary

Implement the single-row market logic (refill with random composition, one €5 re-roll, free move-to-hand, cost-at-play, free discard) and replace the per-row commands with single market/hand commands.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Refill produces exactly 3 cards, always ≥1 business, within "1–2 B / 0–1 U / 0–1 E" bounds; community-space cards count as business; subject to deck availability and existing reshuffle conventions.
2. `refreshMarket` costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 5` (after Accountant `refreshCostDiscount`), discards all currently-visible (unmoved/unpurchased) cards, refills the whole line to full composition; unlimited per turn while affordable.
3. `moveToHand` is free, bounded only by hand capacity, and removes the card from the market; market is not refilled mid-turn after moves/purchases (day-start refill unchanged).
4. `playBusinessFromHand` / `playUpgradeFromHand` / `playEventFromHand` deduct the card's cost at play time (business on placement; upgrade/event when played/triggered); direct buy-and-place still pays immediately.
5. `discardFromHand` is free, allowed any time during the player's turn, and sends the card to its corresponding discard pile.
6. `cycleMarketCards` works on the single row; per-row purchase helpers removed.
7. `refreshMarketCommand` replaces `refreshDevelopmentCommand` / `refreshInvestmentsCommand`; `moveToHandCommand`, `playFromHandCommand`, and `discardFromHandCommand` added — all respecting legality (hand capacity, turn/phase, affordability).

- Rewrite `MainStreetMarket.ts` (refill/composition, `canRefreshMarket`/`refreshMarket`, `moveToHand`, `play*FromHand`, `discardFromHand`, single-row `cycleMarketCards`).

## Summary

Adapt the AI strategy and Monte Carlo harness to the single-row market with free move-to-hand and cost-at-play, and verify or re-baseline Monte Carlo results.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `MainStreetAiStrategy` reads the market as a single row of up to 3 cards and no longer references `market.development` / `market.investments`.
2. The AI strategy is free-move aware: it may move market cards to hand for free and factor cost-at-play into placement decisions (holding cards it cannot yet afford within hand capacity).
3. `MainStreetMonteCarlo` iterates the single market row; harness runs cleanly.
4. `monte-carlo-baseline.json` / `monte-carlo-sample-results.md` verified against the new economy; re-baselined if results shift — never silently broken.
5. AI-strategy tests and Monte Carlo guardrail tests updated and passing.

## Minimal Implementation

- Update `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` market reads + decision logic for free moves / deferred payment.
- Update `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` row iteration.
- Regenerate or verify Monte Carlo baseline outputs (`npm run monte-carlo`), committing updated baseline only if the numbers legitimately changed.

## Dependencies

# Implement: Shared synergyLineEndpoints() helper + renderer/animator + docs

**Parent:** CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP "Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner instead of center-to-center"

## Goal

Extract a shared `synergyLineEndpoints(pair, layout)` helper that clips the center-to-center segment to the two card/slot rect boundaries, and use it in **both** `MainStreetRenderer.drawSynergyLines()` and `MainStreetAnimator.animateSynergyFormation()` so static, animated, and glow strokes all share identical geometry. Update documentation.

## Problem statement

Synergy lines run slot-center to slot-center, stroking through card interiors. Endpoints must be clipped to the facing edges (orthogonal) / corners (diagonal) so lines read as links *between* cards. Geometry is currently duplicated in renderer + animator (a drift risk — the animator's doc comment says it "mirrors" the renderer).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Orthogonally adjacent pairs: line endpoints lie on the facing edges of the two cards/slots (not their centers).
2. Diagonally adjacent pairs: line endpoints lie at the facing corners of the two cards/slots.
3. Extended-range pairs (`synergyRangeBonus` ≥ 1, Chebyshev range 2+): endpoints clipped to the card/slot boundaries in the same edge/corner manner (straight line, still crossing intermediate cells).
4. `MainStreetAnimator.animateSynergyFormation()` uses the same clipped endpoints as the static lines — no visible discrepancy between the draw-in line and the persistent line.
5. The outer glow stroke (6px, 0.2 alpha) shares the same clipped endpoints as the main 3px stroke.
6. A shared `synergyLineEndpoints(pair, layout)` helper exists and is used by both renderer and animator; the "mirrors" duplication is removed.
7. Depth ordering preserved (lines above street grid, behind tooltip zones); `computeSynergyPairs()` / `diffNewSynergyPairs()` logic untouched.
8. Full project test suite passes and `npm run build` succeeds.
9. Documentation updated: geometry code comments in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetAnimator.ts`, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, and any relevant wiki/docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- Reuse existing layout math (`streetX`, `streetTop`, `slotW`, `slotGap`, `slotH`, `streetCols`, `streetRowGap`); no new layout configuration.
- Clip to the slot rect (recommendation in intake brief); note the visual card inset (renderW/H = slotW − 4) in a code comment.
- Pure visual change; no changes to synergy pair computation.

# AI & Monte Carlo Action Budget Awareness

## Summary
Update AI strategy and Monte Carlo harness to respect the 1–2 action budget per day.

## Implementation

1. **AI strategy** (`MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`):
   - `enumerateLegalActions`: filter out action-type moves when `state.actionsRemaining <= 0`; only return `end-turn` when budget is spent.
   - `chooseAction`: when budget > 0, evaluate and pick the best action; when budget = 0, auto-select `end-turn`.
   - AI no longer loops infinitely through actions; each turn, AI takes at most `1 + (employed GM actions)` action-type actions, then end-turn.

2. **Monte Carlo harness** (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`):
   - Loop respects the 1–2 action cap per day (same logic as AI: action-type moves only while `actionsRemaining > 0`).
   - Each simulation run enforces the same budget as the real game.

3. **Re-baseline**: After implementation, run the Monte Carlo harness and update `monte-carlo-baseline.json` to reflect the new action-constrained behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AI strategy's `enumerateLegalActions` filters action-type moves when `actionsRemaining <= 0`.
- [ ] AI auto-selects `end-turn` when budget is spent.
- [ ] Monte Carlo harness loops respect the 1–2 action cap per day.
- [ ] `monte-carlo-baseline.json` updated to reflect new action-constrained baselines.
- [ ] Tests: AI picks action only when budget > 0; Monte Carlo respects cap; no infinite loops.

## Goal (user story)

When a player boots Main Street, the Day Start banner ('Day 1') and its click SFX fire immediately — before the player has had a chance to choose how to begin (run the tutorial, skip, resume a checkpoint, or start fresh). The banner should only play once the game actually starts.

## Root cause

`create()` (and the async campaign-load path in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`) call `s.startDayPhase()` at boot, each firing `MainStreetAnimator.animateDayBanner` (visual + CLICK SFX) before the tutorial-offer modal / resume overlay is shown. Up to two banners play before any player choice.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Booting the scene fires NO Day-N banner (visual or SFX) before the player has chosen how to start: boot-time `startDayPhase` calls are banner-suppressed.
2. The banner plays once the game actually starts: (a) Start Tutorial, (b) Skip for Now (free play), (c) fresh start with no eligible offer modal.
