# Intake Brief: Play illegal move sound/animation when player cannot afford card (CG-0MSXIA61S00686G5)

## Problem statement

In Main Street, when a player attempts to buy (or place) a card they cannot afford via the click UI, the game only updates the instruction text — no illegal-move sound or shake animation is played. The drag-and-drop path already provides this feedback (via `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` `onIllegal` → `shakeIllegalMove`), so the click paths are inconsistent with the game's own conventions (AGENTS.md pattern #8: all player rejections/feedback must be animated and audible).

## Users

- **Main Street player** — tries to place a business card taken into hand (free transfer) when coins run short, or clicks an upgrade/event card they cannot afford, expecting the standard "illegal move" audio + visual shake like the drag path provides.

User stories:

- As a player, when I click an upgrade or event card in the market that I cannot afford, I want the illegal-move sound and a shake on the card, so I immediately understand why the purchase was rejected.
- As a player, when I try to place a business card from my hand onto the street without enough coins, I want the illegal-move sound and shake, so the rejection is obvious without reading the instruction line.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts`, all click-path purchase rejections that are caused by insufficient coins play the illegal-move feedback: the `sfx-illegal-move` sound (via the reusable `shakeIllegalMove` helper or equivalent `SoundManager` path) and a shake animation on the offending card.
   - Paths in scope: `onEventCardClick` (canPurchaseEvent fails), `onUpgradeCardClick` (canPurchaseUpgrade fails), `onSlotClick` placing a business card from hand (`placeFromHand` throws "Not enough coins…"), `onPlayHeldEvent` playing a held event (`playEventCommand` throws "Not enough coins…").
2. The illegal-move feedback respects existing audio settings: it goes through `SoundManager` / `safePlaySound` so mute and volume controls apply, and it must not throw or break the game loop when the audio asset or tween target is unavailable (headless/replay/transcript modes and tests must be unaffected).
3. Non-affordability rejections (hand full, occupied slot, tutorial gating, wrong card, synergy placement) keep their existing instruction-text-only behaviour — no sound/shake added there (scope discipline).
4. Testing: add unit tests (Node project) verifying that each in-scope click path invokes the illegal feedback (e.g. sound played / shake tween created) when coins are insufficient and does not mutate game state; existing engine legality tests (e.g. `tests/main-street/market-extraction-parity.test.ts`, `refresh-market.test.ts`) continue to pass unchanged.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (e.g. `MainStreetTurnController.ts` doc comments, any scene help text) and any relevant wiki/docs-site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test` + `npm run build`).

## Constraints

- **Scope: Main Street only.** It is the only example game with a player click-to-buy market (business/upgrade/event cards). Feudalism purchases are AI-driven (no player click-buy UI); Golf/Blackjack/Lost Cities/Beleaguered Castle/Coloretto have no market purchase mechanic.
- Priority medium (operator-specified). Issue type `bug`: the click paths are inconsistent with the game's own illegal-feedback convention (drag path already does this).
- Follow TCE conventions: reuse `shakeIllegalMove` from `src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts` (plays `sfx-illegal-move` via `safePlaySound`); do not introduce new SFX keys (illegal-move is a `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` entry, already loaded in `MainStreetLifecycleManager` lines 83–88).
- No changes to AI/headless/replay/transcript paths (documented exemption per AGENTS.md pattern #8 — no rendering/audio in those modes).
- Do not weaken existing instruction-text error messages; the sound/shake is additive feedback.
- Market cards are `Phaser.GameObjects.Container` objects (no `setTint`); use a container-safe shake or target the inner rendered card sprite. Hand cards are sprites (`handView.getSpriteAt(index)`).

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — `SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE = COMMON_SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE` (`sfx-illegal-move`) already defined.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts:83-88` — `assets/audio/default/illegal-move.wav` already loaded (namespaced and bare keys).
- `src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts` — reusable helper: plays `sfx-illegal-move` via `safePlaySound`, red-tint + horizontal shake, safe on null target.
- `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` — drag path wires `onIllegal` → `shakeIllegalMove` (or container-safe `shakeContainer`) for pickup veto / rejected drop / snap-back (already covered by `tests/main-street/drag.test.ts`).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — click paths that reject insufficient-coins purchases with text only:
  - `onSlotClick` (business place-from-hand, `placeFromHand` throws "Not enough coins to place…", catch ~line 767)
  - `onEventCardClick` (`canPurchaseEvent` fails, ~line 902)
  - `onUpgradeCardClick` (`canPurchaseUpgrade` fails, ~line 1068)
  - `onPlayHeldEvent` (`playEventCommand` → `playEventFromHand` throws "Not enough coins to play…", catch ~line 346)

## Desired change

Add illegal-move sound + shake to the four above-mentioned click-path rejection branches in `MainStreetTurnController.ts` when the rejection reason is insufficient coins. Centralise if cheap (e.g. a small private helper `playIllegalFeedback(target)` that wraps `shakeIllegalMove` with reduced-motion handling), otherwise inline calls matching the existing style. The instruction text stays as-is.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — add illegal feedback to the four click-path rejection branches (primary change).
- `src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts` — reusable helper to invoke (read-only reference; no change expected unless a container-safe variant is needed).
- `tests/main-street/` — new unit tests for the click-path illegal feedback (e.g. `illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` or additions to an existing controller test file).
- `docs/` — verify DEVELOPER.md / SFX_CONVENTION.md need no update (likely none; SFX key and convention already documented).

## Related work

- CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 "Expand player hand to 3 slots and rework marketplace to single row" (completed) — introduced free move-to-hand + cost-at-play; created the "place from hand, pay at placement" path where the unaffordable-placement case arises.
- CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R "Limit player actions to one action per turn (action economy)" (open) — adjacent action-economy work; not a dependency.
- `tests/main-street/drag.test.ts` — existing drag-path illegal-feedback tests (reference for new test style).
- AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Best Practices" pattern #8 (event-driven audio/visual feedback) — the convention this work makes consistent.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "buy card" is scoped to Main Street click-to-buy paths; refresh-market re-roll cost is NOT a card purchase → out of scope (can be a follow-up if desired).
- **Assumption:** non-affordability reasons keep text-only behaviour (avoid scope creep; the request is specifically about affordability).
- **Risk:** shaking a container that gets re-rendered mid-tween (refreshAll recreates market containers) — mitigate by targeting a stable child sprite or guarding with stale-object checks; keep the shake short.
- **Risk:** sound playing in tutorial flows could confuse — mitigations: sound is momentary; message text unchanged; tests verify tutorial gating still takes precedence.
- **Scope-creep risk:** other feedback gaps (hand-full shake, refresh-cost feedback, Feudalism AI purchases) are recorded here as linked opportunities, not in scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interactive clarifying questions were required — the seed request ("When player attempts to buy card they cannot afford play the illegal move sound/animation", priority medium) suffices to scope the work.
- Research summary: searched work items (`wl search`) and repo for purchase/afford/illegal handlers. Verified Main Street is the only player click-to-buy game; the `sfx-illegal-move` key is defined in `MainStreetConstants.ts` and loaded in `MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts`; `shakeIllegalMove` is the established reusable helper (used by the Main Street drag path via `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` and by Beleaguered Castle). The four click-path gaps were identified by reading `MainStreetTurnController.ts` (onSlotClick/onEventCardClick/onUpgradeCardClick/onPlayHeldEvent). Decisions: scope = Main Street click paths; issue type `bug` (inconsistency with the game's own illegal-feedback convention); priority `medium` (operator-specified).

- **CG-0MR4RP87X004DIZV** – Add culture business purchase to tutorial and update investment card timing guidance (completed) — purchase-flow precedent (tutorial buy-event steps)
- **CG-0MST2LS3E004BTPO** – Main Street: drag-and-drop transfer animation duration should be proportional to distance travelled (completed) — drag animation work adjacent to the reusable drag-drop module

# Intake Brief: Main Street game over screen — show count of unlocked cards instead of listing each card

## Problem statement

The Main Street game-over overlay's "Tier Unlocked!" section lists every newly unlocked card by name (one line per card, per unlocked tier). As the card catalog grows, this makes the game-over panel unwieldy — the user wants the count of unlocked cards shown instead of the full list.

# Intake Brief: Graffiti Art — reputation only (no coins)

## Problem statement

The Graffiti Art good-incident card (`evt-graffiti-art`) in Main Street currently grants **+1 coin to all businesses AND +1 reputation**. It should grant reputation only (+0 coins, +1 reputation), matching the design intent of reputation-focused positive incidents (parallel to the Free Health Screening card change in CG-0MSXIS2QI002WMKR).

## Users / context

- Main Street players encounter incident events that modify resources. Some incidents give coins, some give reputation, and some give both.
- Graffiti Art is a "good" polarity, tier-3, universal ("All") incident. Its theme ("artists transform the street with murals") is a community/cultural initiative — fitting for reputation gains, not coin generation.
- Graffiti Art is the exact mirror of the "Graffiti" bad incident (`evt-graffiti`), which gives -1/-1 to all businesses.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Graffiti Art grants reputation only** — `coinDelta` changed from `1` to `0` in `card-data.csv`; the event resolves to +0 coins and +1 reputation to all businesses.
2. **Card description and effect text updated** — description and effect fields no longer reference "+1 coin"; reflect "+1 reputation" only.
3. **Test contract updated** — `tests/main-street/graffiti-art-incident.test.ts` updated to reflect `coinDelta: '0'` in `GRAFFITI_ART_CONTRACT`.
4. **Documentation updated** — `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` updated to reflect "+1 reputation" only (no coin component).
5. **Full project test suite passes** — all unit tests, browser tests, and E2E tutorials pass with no regressions.

## Constraints

- This is a single-card behavior change — scope is limited to `evt-graffiti-art`.
- Must not affect other incident cards or engine mechanics.
- The `resolveEvent` function logic for `All` targets remains unchanged (it applies coinDelta and reputationDelta uniformly; with coinDelta=0, no coins are granted).

## Existing state

| Field | Current value |
|---|---|
| `coinDelta` | 1 |
| `reputationDelta` | 1 |
| `target` | All |
| `tier` | 3 |
| `trigger` | Incident |
| Polarity (coinDelta + reputationDelta) | +2 (good) |

## Desired change

| Field | Current value | New value |
|---|---|---|
| `coinDelta` | 1 | **0** |
| `reputationDelta` | 1 | 1 (unchanged) |
| `description` | "Artists transform the street with murals. +1 coin to all businesses and +1 reputation." | "Artists transform the street with murals. +1 reputation." |
| `effect` | "+1 coin to all businesses and +1 reputation." | "+1 reputation." |
| Polarity (coinDelta + reputationDelta) | +2 (good) | **+1 (good)** — still classified as "good" |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — change `coinDelta` from `1` to `0`; update description and effect text for `evt-graffiti-art`
- `tests/main-street/graffiti-art-incident.test.ts` — update `GRAFFITI_ART_CONTRACT.coinDelta` from `'1'` to `'0'`; update test expectations for the mirror-reverse relation (Graffiti Art coinDelta=0 means Graffiti's -1 is no longer reversed)
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — update Graffiti Art entry to reflect "+1 reputation" only
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — update table row to reflect "+1 reputation" only

## Risks & assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| The "exact reverse of Graffiti" assertion in `graffiti-art-incident.test.ts` (AC: `expect(Number(art.coinDelta)).toBe(-Number(graffiti.coinDelta))`) will break because Graffiti Art coinDelta=0 is not the negation of Graffiti coinDelta=-1 | Update the test to reflect the new contract: Graffiti Art is a *loose* mirror (reputation reversed, coin not mirrored). Document this design decision. |
| Polarity balance system classifies cards by `coinDelta + reputationDelta` — net delta changes from +2 to +1 | Still > 0 → remains "good" polarity. Balance constraint verified in tests. |
| E2E replay/test data files in `tmp/` reference "Graffiti Art" by name | These are test artifacts (not tracked by git); no code impact. |
| Scope creep: operator might want to adjust other universal incidents (Movie Premiere, Farmers Market) | Out of scope. Each requires a separate work item. |

## Related work

- **CG-0MSXIS2QI002WMKR** — "Main Street: Free Health Screening grants reputation only (no coins)" — parallel change, completed, same pattern (coinDelta 1→0).
- **CG-0MSRC9UR9006FBXC** — "Main Street: add Graffiti Art good-incident card" — original creation of evt-graffiti-art with coinDelta=1.
- **CG-0MSQJ7QLM0076FTD** — "Group D: Incident events — polarity-balanced (10 cards)" — created evt-graffiti with coinDelta=-1.
- **CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA** — "Main Street: reputation score multiplier (x5) should become a simple count" — reputation sources feed the count.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

- *Q: Should Graffiti Art give +1 reputation total (like evt-library-reading) or scale with business count?* — **Answer:** +1 reputation total, no coins, to all businesses (same target as Graffiti). This is the operator's explicit requirement.
- *Q: Does the net polarity change (+2 → +1) affect the incident-polarity balance constraint?* — **Answer:** Net delta is still > 0, so it remains classified as "good" polarity. The balance constraint (good/bad/neutral count) is preserved.
- *Q: The test asserts Graffiti Art is the "exact reverse" of Graffiti. With coinDelta=0, this relationship no longer holds (0 ≠ -(-1)).* — **Answer:** The test should be updated to reflect the new contract. Graffiti Art is a *partial* mirror (reputation reversed, coin not mirrored). Document this in the test comments.

# Problem Statement

The HUD bar and game-over overlay currently display coins as a rounded integer (e.g. "Coins: 123") and reputation as an unformatted floating-point number (e.g. "Reputation: 2.3000000000000003"). Both should be shown to exactly 2 decimal places for consistency, precision, and readability.

# Users

- **Main Street players** — Need to see their exact coin and reputation values at a glance to make informed purchasing decisions.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **HUD bar** — `Coins:` displays the current coin balance to 2 decimal places (e.g. "Coins: 123.46"), not rounded to an integer.
2. **HUD bar** — `Reputation:` displays the current reputation value to 2 decimal places (e.g. "Reputation: 2.30").
3. **Game-over overlay** — Score breakdown `Coins:` line also shows 2 decimal places, consistent with the HUD bar.
4. **Score display** — `Score:` and `Final Score:` remain rounded to whole numbers (no change).
5. **All existing tests pass** — Updated browser test assertions reflect the new formatting.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** — `npm test` completes with no failures.
7. **All related documentation is updated** — code comments and any relevant docs reflect the 2-decimal display convention.

# Constraints

- Only affects HUD bar (`MainStreetRenderer.refreshHud`) and game-over overlay score breakdown (`MainStreetOverlayContent`).
- `Score:` display must not change — remains `Math.round(score)`.
- Tooltip content is not in scope — tooltips already show detailed breakdowns with 3 decimal places.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — HUD bar formatting (line ~330-337)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Game-over overlay score breakdown (line ~102-103)

# Related work

- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE** — Library card rebalanced as reputation asset (introduced fractional coin costs)

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** 2 decimal places is sufficient precision. Coin values are stored with 3-decimal precision internally (`toFixed(3)` in engine code); rounding to 2 for display is a presentation concern only.

# Intake Brief: Main Street — don't auto-select a card moved to hand from the market for another action

## Problem statement

When a player moves a business card from the market into their hand, Main Street immediately auto-selects the newly added card for placement: the scene switches to the `placing-from-hand` phase with `pendingHandIndex` pointing at the last hand card, so a single street-slot click places the card right away. The player is thus pre-committed to playing the card without an explicit choice, which is surprising when they only wanted to bank the card in their hand (e.g. to plan ahead or free a market slot).

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — after moving a market card to hand, they want the card to rest unselected in the hand; they explicitly click the hand card when they actually want to place it.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the click flow, tutorial gating, and tests updated so the hand acts as a neutral buffer rather than an auto-commit to placement.

Example user stories:
- "As a player, I want a market card I move into my hand to stay unselected, so I can hold it for later instead of being forced into the placement step."
- "As a player, I want to tap the card in my hand when I am ready to place it, so I decide what happens next rather than the game deciding for me."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No auto-selection:** after a business card is moved from the market to the hand (click flow), `pendingHandIndex` stays `null` and `uiPhase` returns to `market` — the card is NOT pre-selected for placement.
2. **Manual selection preserved:** clicking a hand business card still selects it (`onHandBusinessCardClick` sets `pendingHandIndex` and enters `placing-from-hand`); clicking an empty street slot then places the selected card and returns to `market` as today.
3. **Tutorial compatibility:** tutorial steps that require placement (T5 `place-business`, T10/T13 composite `buy-and-place`) still complete with the new flow — hand-card selection must be permitted during those steps (the `select-hand-card` gate currently blocks it), and the tutorial copy/overlay reflects "select the card in your hand, then click a slot".
4. **Unaffected flows:** direct drag-and-drop buy-and-place (market → slot, bypassing the hand), AI turns, and undo/redo of move-to-hand/placement behave exactly as before.
5. **Tests & docs:** existing tests that depend on auto-selection (`click-place.browser.test.ts`, tutorial E2E parts) are updated to click the hand card first; new/updated unit coverage asserts move-to-hand leaves `pendingHandIndex` null and phase `market`; `npm test` passes and `npm run build` succeeds; all related documentation updated (instruction copy, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and tutorial docs if they describe the flow).

## Constraints

- The change applies to the **click buy-to-hand** path in `MainStreetTurnController.onBusinessCardClick` → `afterTransfer`. Drag-and-drop direct placement already bypasses the hand and is untouched.
- The card should still be playable the same turn at its listed cost; only the auto-selection step is removed (playing remains one deliberate click on the hand card + one on a slot).
- Keep the phase/selection state machine consistent: no half-selected states; undo of a move-to-hand must leave the scene in `market` with no pending selection (mirroring the existing reset behaviour in `onSlotClick` / lifecycle).
- Do NOT implement or pre-empt the action-economy item CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R (move-to-hand and play-from-hand each consuming an action) — this request only removes the auto-selection UI behaviour.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetTurnController.ts` `onBusinessCardClick` (click market business card) animates the card to the hand; its `afterTransfer` callback (≈lines 455–481) executes `moveToHandCommand`, then sets `s.pendingHandIndex = hand.length - 1`, `s.uiPhase = 'placing-from-hand'`, and instruction text "Click an empty slot to place …" — this is the auto-selection to remove.
- `onHandBusinessCardClick` (≈lines 1140–1200) already implements manual selection during `market` phase (sets `pendingHandIndex`, switches to `placing-from-hand`, updates the selection highlight), and allows switching selection while already in `placing-from-hand`.
- `onSlotClick` (≈lines 701+) places the card at `pendingHandIndex` when set, then clears it and returns to `market`.
- Tutorial gating: `isTutorialActionAllowed` allows an action only when it matches the current step's `requiredAction` (or `select-business`/`place-business` for composite `buy-and-place`). `select-hand-card` is NOT in the allowed set for T5/T10/T13, so hand-card clicks are currently blocked during those steps — the gate must be widened (e.g. allow `select-hand-card` when the step's required action is `place-business` or `buy-and-place`) or the place steps must accept hand selection as part of `place-business`.
- Tests currently relying on auto-selection: `tests/main-street/click-place.browser.test.ts` (buys to hand → expects `placing-from-hand`, then clicks the slot directly) and `tests/e2e/main-street-tutorial-e2e-part4.browser.test.ts` (T10: `clickRequiredBusinessCard` then `clickStreetSlot` without a hand-card click in between).

## Desired change

1. In `afterTransfer` of the market→hand click flow: stop setting `pendingHandIndex`; set `uiPhase = 'market'`; update the instruction text to say the card is in hand and can be selected/placed or held (cost paid at play).
2. Widen tutorial action gating so hand-card selection is allowed during `place-business` / `buy-and-place` steps (and add any tutorial step/overlay copy so the flow is self-explanatory).
3. Update affected browser/E2E tests to click the hand card before clicking the street slot; add unit coverage for the new no-auto-select behaviour (e.g. via the `hand-business-click.test.ts` harness: after `moveToHandCommand`-style flow, assert `pendingHandIndex` null and `uiPhase` market).
4. Update docs/copy that describe the move-to-hand → auto-place flow.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — remove auto-selection in `afterTransfer` (≈lines 472–474); widen `onHandBusinessCardClick` tutorial gate as needed.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — tutorial action gating (`isTutorialActionAllowed`, `onTutorialActionComplete` composite handling) to permit hand selection during placement steps.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — step/action-type definitions if a new required action or composite gate is needed for hand-selection-then-place.
- `tests/main-street/click-place.browser.test.ts` — insert a hand-card click between buy-to-hand and slot click.
- `tests/e2e/main-street-tutorial-e2e-part4.browser.test.ts` (+ any other tutorial E2E parts using buy-then-place) — same insertion.
- `tests/main-street/hand-business-click.test.ts` — add/keep coverage asserting manual selection works and move-to-hand does not auto-select.
- Docs: `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, tutorial copy (`example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` texts / `TutorialState`), `example-games/main-street/README.md` if they describe the buy-to-hand → place flow.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Tutorial E2E sensitivity:** multiple tutorial E2E parts walk buy-to-hand → slot-click sequences (not only part 4); the implementation must scan all six parts and any `tests/main-street/*.browser.test.ts` for flows that assume the slot is placeable immediately after buy-to-hand, and insert the hand-card click.
- **Hidden behavioural dependencies:** tests or code may assert the instruction text "Click an empty slot to place …", the `placing-from-hand` phase right after buy-to-hand, or drag-drop interplay (e.g. a slot drag while a hand card is pending); grep for `placing-from-hand` / `pendingHandIndex` / instruction-text assertions before finalising.
- **Slightly more interaction for immediate placers:** players who want to place right away now need one extra click (select hand card). Mitigation: keep the instruction-text hint clear; do not add other friction. This is the operator's requested trade-off.
- **Assumption: pendingHandIndex is the right mechanism.** The change keeps the existing `pendingHandIndex` selection model and only stops auto-populating it after move-to-hand — minimal, surgical change.
- **Scope-creep guard:** balance tuning, extra hand UI affordances (e.g. "place" buttons), or the action-economy work (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R) are out of scope; record as linked work, do not implement.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2** (completed, in_review) — single-row market + 3-slot hand rework; introduced the current move-to-hand auto-selection behaviour.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (open, plan_complete) — action economy: move-to-hand and play-from-hand each consume the daily action; this request's no-auto-select behaviour is consistent with (and a UI prerequisite for) that design, but independent — do not implement it here.
- **CG-0MSOKUOUE005LQFZ** (completed) — "Animate card placement from hand in Main Street" (related hand-placement flow).
- **CG-0MS7EPE0I001R6PI / CG-0MS7ML1W7002DZKB** (completed) — hand-card clickability; `onHandBusinessCardClick` origin.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (interpretation): "What is 'the mark' and which game is this about?" — Answer (operator request text): "When a card is placed in the hand from the mark …". Research: no card game mechanic called 'mark' exists in the repo; the only market→hand move flow is Main Street's click buy-to-hand after the single-row market rework (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2), where the moved card is auto-selected for placement. Accepted: "mark" = "market"; scope is Main Street's click move-to-hand flow (drag-and-drop buy-and-place unaffected).
- No further interview questions needed — the seed context and repo state fully determine the change. If the operator intended a different game or flow, this item should be re-scoped before implementation.

# Intake Brief: Free Health Screening — reputation only

## Problem statement

The Free Health Screening incident card (`evt-health-screening`) in Main Street currently grants **+1 coin per Health business AND +1 reputation**. It should grant reputation only (no coins), matching the design intent of reputation-focused positive incidents.

## Users / context

- Main Street players encounter incident events that modify resources. Some incidents give coins, some give reputation, and some give both.
- Free Health Screening is a "good" polarity, tier-2, Health-synergy incident. Its theme ("a free screening day boosts well-being") is a community health initiative — fitting for reputation gains, not coin generation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Free Health Screening grants reputation only** — `coinDelta` changed from 1 to 0 in `card-data.csv`; the event resolves to +0 coins and +1 reputation regardless of Health business count.
2. **Test contract updated** — `tests/main-street/group-d-incident-events-expansion.test.ts` updated to reflect `coinDelta: 0` in the Group D incident contract.
3. **Documentation updated** — `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` updated to reflect "+1 reputation" only (no coin component).
4. **Polarity classification remains valid** — with coinDelta=0, reputationDelta=1, net delta = +1 (good polarity), which is consistent with the intended "good" classification.
5. **Full project test suite passes** — all unit tests, browser tests, and E2E tutorials pass with no regressions.

## Constraints

- This is a single-card behavior change — scope is limited to `evt-health-screening`.
- Must not affect other incident cards or engine mechanics.
- The `resolveEvent` function (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) logic for `SpecificSynergy` targets remains unchanged (it multiplies coinDelta by matchCount; with coinDelta=0, the product is 0).

## Existing state

| Field | Current value |
|---|---|
| `coinDelta` | 1 |
| `reputationDelta` | 1 |
| `target` | SpecificSynergy |
| `targetSynergy` | Health |
| `tier` | 2 |
| `trigger` | Incident |
| Polarity (coinDelta + reputationDelta) | +2 (good) |

## Desired change

| Field | Current value | New value |
|---|---|---|
| `coinDelta` | 1 | **0** |
| `description` | "A free screening day boosts well-being. +1 coin per Health business and +1 reputation." | "A free screening day boosts well-being. +1 reputation." |
| `effect` | "+1 coin per Health business and +1 reputation." | "+1 reputation." |
| Polarity (coinDelta + reputationDelta) | +2 (good) | **+1 (good)** — still classified as "good" |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (line 91) — change `coinDelta` from 1 to 0; update description and effect text
- `tests/main-street/group-d-incident-events-expansion.test.ts` (line 66) — update `coinDelta: 1` to `coinDelta: 0` in `NEW_INCIDENT_CONTRACTS`
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (line 54) — update table row to reflect "+1 reputation" only

## Risks & assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Polarity balance system classifies cards by `coinDelta + reputationDelta` — net delta changes from +2 to +1 | Still > 0 → remains "good" polarity. Balance constraint verified in tests. |
| E2E replay/test data files in `tmp/` reference "Free Health Screening" by name | These are test artifacts (not tracked by git); no code impact. |
| Scope creep: operator might want to adjust other synergy-based incidents (Movie Premiere, Farmers Market) | Out of scope. Each requires a separate work item. |

## Related work

- **CG-0MSXILJHN008CHQY** — "Main Street: Graffiti Art grants reputation only (no coins)" — parallel change for the Graffiti Art card (same pattern, in-progress).
- **CG-0MSQJ7QLM0076FTD** — "Group D: Incident events — polarity-balanced (10 cards)" — created evt-health-screening with coinDelta=1.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

- *Q: Should Free Health Screening give +1 reputation total (like evt-library-reading) or scale with Health business count (like evt-movie-premiere gives +1 coin per Entertainment)?* — **Answer:** +1 reputation total, no coins. This is the operator's explicit requirement.
- *Q: Does the net polarity change (+2 → +1) affect the incident-polarity balance constraint?* — **Answer:** Net delta is still > 0, so it remains classified as "good" polarity. The balance constraint (good/bad/neutral count) is preserved.

**Work item:** CG-0MSXITDJ5009I2FT — Rename 'Library Story Hour' event card to 'Children's Story Hour'
**Priority:** medium (operator-specified) · **Issue type:** chore · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

The Main Street incident event card `evt-library-reading` is displayed as "Library Story Hour". The operator wants the display name changed to "Children's Story Hour" (proper US punctuation with straight apostrophe, matching the existing CSV convention, e.g. "Reader's Café").

## Key Files

# Play illegal move audio/visual when hand is full during buy

## Problem statement

In `MainStreetTurnController.onBusinessCardClick()`, when `canAddToHand()` returns illegal (hand full), the game only sets an instruction text message — no illegal-move sound or shake animation is played. Other illegal move scenarios (e.g. drag-to-buy with insufficient coins, invalid drop zone) play the standard illegal-move feedback via `shakeIllegalMove` + `sfx-illegal-move`. This inconsistency violates AGENTS.md pattern #8.

## User story

As a player, when I try to buy a card and my hand is full, I want to see and hear the illegal-move feedback so I immediately understand the card cannot be added.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts`, the hand-full rejection branch in `onBusinessCardClick()` (around line 445) plays illegal-move feedback: the `sfx-illegal-move` sound and a shake animation on the clicked market card.
2. The feedback respects existing audio settings: sound goes through `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound` (mute/volume apply), and shake has reduced-motion fallback.
3. Non-hand-full rejections keep existing behaviour — no change to tutorial gating, affinity gating, or other rejection paths.
4. Full test suite passes with the new changes.

## Implementation approach

The hand-full check in `onBusinessCardClick()` is at approximately line 445:
\`\`\`typescript
if (!handCheck.legal) {
  s.instructionText.setText(\`Hand full: \${handCheck.reason ?? 'Place or sell a card first.'}\`);
  return;
}
\`\`\`

We need to add illegal feedback before the `return`. The card being clicked is a `BusinessCard` data object. The visual representation is in the market renderer as a Container.

Market cards are rendered as `Phaser.GameObjects.Container` objects (not sprites) in `MainStreetRenderer.drawMarketCard()`. The container's first child is the card `Image` sprite. `shakeIllegalMove()` requires a sprite with `setTint()`/`clearTint()`, so we need to either:
- Extract the first child (card sprite) and pass to `shakeIllegalMove()`, or
- Use a container-safe shake variant (like `shakeContainer` from `src/ui/dragDrop.ts`)

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — primary change
- `src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts` — reusable shake helper (reference)
- `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` — `shakeContainer` for container-safe shake (reference)
- `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — `safePlaySound` + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`

## Effort & Risk

- **Effort:** Extra Small
- **Risk:** Low

## Appendix

- Q: How to shake a Container (market card visual model)? Answer (plan): Market cards are Phaser Containers, not raw sprites. Use `shakeContainer` from `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` as the container-safe shake pattern. This is the approach in `MainStreetRenderer` already.
- Q: How to play the illegal-move sound? Answer (plan): Use `SoundManager.safePlaySound(COMMON_SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE)` which respects mute/volume settings. Pattern #8 in AGENTS.md.
- Q: Are there existing tests for onBusinessCardClick? Answer (plan): Check MainStreetTurnController tests; add a test for the hand-full case if not present.
data.title: Play illegal move audio/visual when hand is full during buy

# Intake Brief: Vite dev server crashes with JS heap OOM (Main Street end-game)

**Work item:** CG-0MSXL0A25009WZVK — bug — critical

## Problem statement

Running `npm run dev` (Vite 6.1.0 under Node v22) and playing Main Street through to the
game-over screen reproducibly crashes the **dev-server process** (not the browser) with
`FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit — JavaScript heap out of memory`
after roughly 4.6 minutes, once the heap reaches the ~4 GB Node default old-space cap
(`Aborted (core dumped)`). The operator observed the crash twice across a restart —
once on the Main Street end-game screen, and suspects an earlier occurrence at another
point too. Impact: the dev server dies mid-session, blocking development and playthroughs.

## Users

- **Developer/operator** playing the game from `localhost:3000` during development:
  wants to finish a play-through (in particular reach the game-over screen) without the
  dev server dying underneath them.
- **Intake/implement agents** running `npm run dev` to test changes or reproduce issues.
- **Transcript pipeline consumers**: on-disk transcripts written by the dev-server plugin
  feed the replay/transcript tooling (`scripts/replay.ts`, `scripts/export-transcripts.ts`).

Example user stories:

> "As a developer, I want to play Main Street to the game-over screen without my dev
> server crashing, so I can validate end-game behaviour."
>
> "As an implementer, I want a clear diagnosis and regression guard, so this class of
> dev-server memory growth does not silently return."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Bounded dev-server memory on full play-through.** Reproducing the reported flow —
   `npm run dev`, play a Main Street game to the game-over screen — the dev server stays
   alive and its memory usage reaches a stable plateau (e.g. RSS stays below 1.5 GB,
   heap well under the Node cap) over 3 consecutive play-throughs including game-over.
   No OOM/abort in the dev-server process.
2. **Root cause identified and documented.** A heap/process-memory profile captured during
   reproduction identifies the growing allocation site (suspects investigated:
   `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` writing transcripts into the Vite-watched
   `data/transcripts/` tree on every `POST /api/transcripts`; module-graph/watcher growth;
   `--host` network exposure). Findings recorded in the work item and in the relevant
   documentation.
3. **Dev transcript persistence preserved.** Transcripts are still POSTed and persisted to
   disk in the same location/format (`data/transcripts/<game>/...`) so `scripts/replay.ts`
   and `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` keep working; any relocation/change to the pipeline
   is mirrored in the tooling in the same change.
4. **Regression guard.** A test (unit and/or browser E2E harness) that would catch
   unbounded dev-server memory growth passes — e.g. asserting the transcript-persist
   middleware cannot write into Vite-watched paths, or a bounded-memory dev-server smoke
   run — and is wired into the test suite.
5. **Docs + suite green.** Any changed scripts/config (npm scripts, `vite.config.ts`,
   plugin) update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` per the doc-update policy; `npm test` passes and
   `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Server/tooling-side defect** — do not change game behaviour or the browser game loop
  to mask the issue.
- Keep dev iteration fast: no blocking, per-request heavy work, or added latencies.
- Minimal, surgical change: do not overhaul the Vite config or move directories
  gratuitously.
- Transcript on-disk format and location must stay compatible with the transcript
  tooling (`scripts/replay.ts`, `scripts/export-transcripts.ts`), or be updated together.
- No direct edits to `.worklog/` or agent infrastructure.

## Existing state

- `npm run dev` = `vite --host` (Vite 6.1.0, Node v22.22.1) on port 3000, exposed on LAN
  (`192.168.68.53`) and Tailscale (`100.106.5.111`).
- The only game→server round-trip is `TranscriptStore.postToDisk()` →
  `POST /api/transcripts` → `transcriptPersistPlugin` middleware
  (`scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts`) which writes each JSON transcript via
  `writeFileSync` into `data/transcripts/<gameType>/` — **inside the Vite-watched
  project root** — with no rate/size limit and unbounded request-body buffering
  (`body += chunk.toString()`).
- Transcripts on disk are tiny (0.7–2 KB; `data/` total ~2 MB), so payload size is not
  the direct cause — the write→watch→re-serve cycle and/or other Vite-internal growth is.
- `animateGameOver` (confetti, 24 rectangles) is bounded and destroys its objects; the
  native stack trace is `libnode.so` — the Node/Vite process, ruling out a browser-tab
  leak as the crash site.
- Node default old-space cap ≈ 4 GB; the crash log shows the heap at ~4.1 GB after
  ~275 s of process uptime, then `Aborted (core dumped)`.
- Working tree contains unrelated uncommitted WIP (day-banner deferral) — not implicated.

## Desired change

Diagnose and fix the dev-server-side memory growth that caps out at the Node heap limit
during a Main Street play-through, prioritising the transcript-persist write-into-watched-
tree path and any Vite module-graph/watcher amplification; keep transcript persistence
working; add a regression guard and documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — middleware writing into the watched tree; prime
  candidate for relocation (write outside watched paths or ignore `data/` in the watcher)
  and/or rate/body limits.
- `src/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.ts` — `postToDisk()`/`save()` fire-and-forget
  POST; candidate for throttle/chunking and error handling review.
- `vite.config.ts` — `server.watch.ignored` / server options; possible memory-related
  config.
- `scripts/replay.ts`, `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` — consumers of persisted
  transcripts (compatibility contract).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — dev-server troubleshooting / transcript-pipeline notes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — game-over path that
  triggers `autoSaveTranscript` (the observed trigger point for the transcript POST).

## Related work

- **CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT** – Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (completed)
- **CG-0MR4RP87X004DIZV** – Add culture business purchase to tutorial and update investment card timing guidance (completed)
- **CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY** – Main Street: design 50+ new cards of varying types (completed)
- **CG-0MSM9PEP1007N55H** – [test-failure] dev server crash resilience > stale lock file from previously crashed server (completed) — prior dev-server crash-resilience work.
- **CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE** – [test-failure] vitest Browser connection closed under memory pressure (completed) — machine memory-pressure context.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which game / flow were you on?** — Answer (operator): "Yes Main Street game-over"
  (i.e. the Main Street game-over overlay). Evidence: interactive reply.
- **Q2: Reproducibility — did the crash recur on a restart?** — Answer (operator): "I
  believe it happened once, I restarted and played through, it happened again."
  Evidence: interactive reply. → Confirmed reproducible (2/2 play-throughs).
- **Q3: Session shape / other clients connected?** — Answer (operator): "Not sure, I
  don't think other instances were connecting." Evidence: interactive reply. → Treat as
  single-browser-client reproduction; `--host` exposure remains a risk factor to note.

Research summary: repo inspection found the only game→server interaction is the
transcript POST handled by `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts`; transcripts are small and
written into the Vite-watched `data/` tree. Browser-side game-over animation is bounded.
No existing work item covers this symptom.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the crash is reproducible on the current `dev` HEAD (operator's repro
  predates any later changes; an implementer should re-verify first with a fresh run).
- **Risk:** root cause may be Vite-internal (module graph/watcher/HMR) rather than the
  transcript plugin; diagnose first (heap profile + `--trace-gc` + RSS sampling) before
  changing code.
- **Risk:** moving transcript writes could break the replay/transcript CLI contract — keep
  the on-disk contract or update tooling in the same change.
- **Risk (scope creep):** don't attempt a general Vite memory-hardening pass; scope is the
  reproducible play-through OOM. Record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Summary

Fix the root cause of the dev-server OOM by addressing the transcript-persist plugin. The primary suspect is `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` writing transcripts into the Vite-watched `data/transcripts/` tree, triggering Vite watcher/HMR churn that accumulates module-graph entries or retained objects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause fix applied.** The fix addresses the identified root cause:
   - If confirmed: either move transcript writes outside the watched tree (e.g., `data/transcripts/` → a non-watched path), or configure Vite to ignore `data/transcripts/` via `server.watch.ignored`, AND add request body size limits and rate limiting to the transcript middleware.
   - If refuted: implement the fix identified by heap profiling (documented in task CG-0MSXNMDZ6004RA6I).
2. **Dev server stays alive.** A full Main Street play-through to game-over completes without OOM crash (RSS stable, no FATAL ERROR).
3. **Transcript persistence preserved.** Transcripts are still POSTed and persisted to disk in the same location/format (`data/transcripts/<game>/...`) so replay tooling works unchanged. If the write path changes, update `scripts/replay.ts` and `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` in the same commit.
4. **No performance regression.** Dev server start time and HMR update latency are unchanged (within noise).

## Implementation

1. Apply the fix based on profiling results from task CG-0MSXNMDZ6004RA6I.
2. Add request body size limits to `vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (e.g., max 10KB).
3. Add rate limiting to prevent burst writes (e.g., max 1 write/second).
4. If moving writes: update the plugin and transcript consumers.
5. Test: run a full Main Street play-through to game-over and verify the server stays alive.

## Key Files

- `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — middleware to fix
- `vite.config.ts` — may need `server.watch.ignored` addition
- `src/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.ts` — POST endpoint used
- `scripts/replay.ts`, `scripts/export-transcripts.ts` — transcript consumers

# Implement: Add illegal-move feedback to click-path rejections

## Summary

Add illegal-move sound + shake animation to the 4 click-path purchase rejection branches in MainStreetTurnController.ts when the rejection reason is insufficient coins. The drag-and-drop path already provides this feedback via shakeIllegalMove; the click paths currently only show instruction text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. onPlayHeldEvent — when playEventCommand throws "Not enough coins...", the catch block plays sfx-illegal-move and shakes the held event card sprite (from handView.getSpriteAt).
2. onSlotClick — when placeFromHand throws "Not enough coins...", the catch block plays sfx-illegal-move and shakes the placed card sprite (from handView.getSpriteAt).
3. onEventCardClick — when canPurchaseEvent returns a legality failure with reason "Not enough coins...", play sfx-illegal-move and shake the event card container (container-safe shake, no tint).
4. onUpgradeCardClick — when canPurchaseUpgrade returns a legality failure with reason "Not enough coins...", play sfx-illegal-move and shake the upgrade card container (container-safe shake, no tint).
5. All feedback goes through SoundManager/safePlaySound so mute and volume controls apply.
6. Feedback is safe in headless/replay/transcript modes (no throws, no broken game loop).
7. Non-affordability reasons (hand full, occupied slot, tutorial gating, wrong card, synergy placement) keep instruction-text-only behavior — NO sound/shake added.
8. Existing instruction text error messages are preserved (sound/shake is additive).
9. Code comments updated to document the illegal feedback behavior.

## Implementation Details

### Private helper: playIllegalFeedback(target, scene)

Create a small private helper in MainStreetTurnController.ts that:
1. Plays sfx-illegal-move via safePlaySound(scene, SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE).
2. Shakes the target:
   - For sprites (hand cards): use shakeIllegalMove from src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts.
   - For containers (market cards): use a container-safe shake (tween x oscillation, no tint).

### 4 locations to modify:

1. onPlayHeldEvent catch — Get hand sprite via s.msRenderer.handView.getSpriteAt(index), call playIllegalFeedback(sprite, s).
2. onSlotClick / afterTransfer catch — Get hand sprite for the placed card, call playIllegalFeedback(sprite, s).
3. onEventCardClick legality check — when legality failure reason includes insufficient coins, shake the event card container.
4. onUpgradeCardClick legality check — same pattern as onEventCardClick.

### Key decision: container-safe shake

Market cards are Phaser.GameObjects.Container objects (no setTint). Two options:
- Option A: Create a public container-safe variant of shakeIllegalMove in src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts (exported for reuse).
- Option B: Inline the container shake logic in MainStreetTurnController.ts (simpler, no API change).

Recommendation: Option B (inline) — the container shake is trivial (just x oscillation tween), keeping the change scoped to Main Street. If other games need this, it can be extracted later.

## Key Files

- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts — primary change (4 rejection branches)
- src/ui/shakeIllegalMove.ts — reference for the sprite-based shake pattern
- src/ui/dragDrop.ts — reference for shakeContainer (container-safe, no tint)
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts — SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE (already defined)

# Fix latent drag.browser.test.ts firstBusinessCard flake

## Problem statement

The single-row market rule (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2) guarantees >=1 business OR community-space card in the development row, but test helpers filter `c.family==='business'` only. When the dev row's sole business slot deals a Park (community-space) card, the find returns undefined and the test fails.

## Current status

**Primary fix already applied:** `firstBusinessCard()` in `tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts` was fixed in commit `8e1a3d0b` to accept both `'business'` and `'community-space'` families.

## Remaining latent flakes

Two additional test files have the same pattern:

1. **`tests/main-street/drag.test.ts`** line 122 — `pickAffordableBusiness()` filters `c.family === 'business'` only. Uses deterministic seed `'ms-drag-test'`.
2. **`tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts`** lines 247, 272 — two instances of `.find(c => c.family === 'business')` in onSlotClick test setup. Uses deterministic seed `'ms-illegal-afford'`.

## Fix

Add `|| c.family === 'community-space'` to each filter. Same pattern as the drag.browser.test.ts fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three test files accept community-space cards in addition to business cards when searching the market row.
2. `npm test` passes (no flaky firstBusinessCard failures).
3. `npm run build` succeeds.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts` — already fixed (commit 8e1a3d0b)
- `tests/main-street/drag.test.ts` — needs fix at line 122
- `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` — needs fix at lines 247, 272

## Related work

- CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 — single-row market (root cause of the flake)
- CG-0MSX40334001L0W0 — applied the drag.browser.test.ts fix (commit 8e1a3d0b)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the fix apply to the already-fixed drag.browser.test.ts, or only the two remaining latent files?" — Answer (Map): "The drag.browser.test.ts fix was already applied in commit 8e1a3d0b; this item covers the two remaining files (drag.test.ts, illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts) with the same pattern." Evidence: git history review of tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts (all branches). Accepted.
- Q2: "What is the accepted family set for the market-row find filters?" — Answer (Map): "business OR community-space, exactly matching the pattern proven in the merged drag.browser.test.ts fix and consistent with the single-row market rule (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2)." Evidence: drag.browser.test.ts:170-177; drag.test.ts:122; illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts:247,272. Accepted.

# Speed up browser tests and create test profiles

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Task**

> Browser tests take ~15 min (92 files). Profile: smoke (30s), dev (3 min), ci (full). Remove low-value tests (27 reduced-motion variants, redundant gym smokes).

## Current State

- 92 browser test files across 14 directories
- Total runtime: ~12-15 minutes (non-tutorial browser tests)
- isolate: true + fileParallelism: false = fresh browser per file, sequential
- Per-game timing: Main Street ~146s (24 files), Golf ~64s, Gym ~42s, Beleaguered Castle ~49s

## Problems

1. Browser launch overhead dominates: fresh Chromium per file + Phaser boot
2. Sequential execution blocks fast tests on slow ones
3. 27 reduced-motion variants across 10 files - duplicate assertions with animation disabled
4. Gym tests (19 files) check rendering/boots, not game play
5. No test profiles - developers wait 15 min for feedback

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Three Test Profiles

- smoke: 1 file/game (8 files) - ~30s - rapid feedback during implementation
- dev: Smoke + key E2E per game (~25 files) - ~3 min - implement/audit workflow
- ci: All 92 files - ~5-6 min - CI (after cleanup)

- income-collection.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants

d) Tutorial E2E tests (7 files) excluded from smoke/dev profiles

(Audited variance accepted: dev omits tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts despite run-dev-tests.sh:28 and DEVELOPMENT.md:374 claiming "all smoke files" - gym coverage is provided via GymDeckRngScene/GymOverlayUiScene, so the fast-smoke-superset + key E2E intent holds.) (`vite.config.ts` smoke/dev projects, `package.json` `test:smoke`/`test:dev` scripts, `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` / `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh`).

# Replace incident deck pre-ordering with runtime balanced card selection

## Problem Statement

The current incident deck uses `orderIncidentDeck()` to pre-order the entire face-down deck at build/reshuffle time using a soft-greedy algorithm. While this strongly favours repeat-spacing and streak constraints across the deck body, it can admit rare tail deviations when the pool is imbalanced, and the pre-arranged order changes the deterministic simulation in ways that are harder to predict and test (monte-carlo median widened from ~39.8 to ~153).

The fix: instead of pre-ordering, select each incident card **at runtime** from the remaining face-down deck pool, constrained by the resolved draw history. The deck remains face-down; only the selection mechanism changes.

## Users

- **Player (Main Street)**: Experiences fair, balanced incidents without visible deck manipulation — no card order visible, only the resolved sequence matters.
- **Developer/Tester**: Can reproduce deterministic game outcomes (same seed → same result) and reason about incident balance without tracking pre-order algorithms.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runtime selection**: `resolveIncident()` selects the next incident card at runtime from the remaining face-down pool using constraint-aware selection (`repeatSpacing` / `maxStreak`), instead of popping from a pre-ordered sequence. The deck is shuffled once at setup/reshuffle; cards are removed by index.
2. **Determinism preserved**: Same game seed produces the same incident draw sequence. The selection is fully deterministic (no RNG consumed during selection — constraints are evaluated against the pool order).
3. **Constraint compliance**: The same repeat-spacing (N) and max-streak (M) constraints from `IncidentBalanceState` are enforced at draw time using the existing tiered constraint relaxation (strict → relax-repeat → invariant-window → invariant-any → fallback).
4. **Reshuffle integration**: `replenishIncidentDeck()` shuffles remaining incident cards from the event deck/discards and then uses runtime selection (not pre-ordering) for subsequent draws.
5. **Full test suite passes**: Existing incident-balance tests are updated to reflect runtime selection; all Monte Carlo guardrails and regression tests pass.
6. **Documentation updated**: Code comments and docs (DEVELOPER.md incident-balance sections) reflect the runtime-selection mechanism, replacing pre-ordering references.

## Constraints

- Must keep seeded determinism — same seed produces the same draw sequence.
- Selection must consume no RNG (constraint evaluation is deterministic against deck order).
- Deck remains face-down and invisible to the player (UI unchanged).
- Backward compatibility with saved games must be maintained (existing saves use pre-ordered decks; deserialization should handle both formats).
- The existing `IncidentBalanceState` and `recordIncidentDraw()` must continue to work unchanged.

## Existing State

- **`MainStreetCards.ts`**: Contains `orderIncidentDeck()` (pre-orders entire pool) and `findConstrainedIncidentIndex()` (runtime selection from a deck). Both use the same constraint tier system.
- **`MainStreetMarket.ts`**: `replenishIncidentDeck()` calls `orderIncidentDeck()` at reshuffle time.
- **`MainStreetState.ts`**: `setupMainStreetGame()` calls `orderIncidentDeck()` at game start.
- **`MainStreetEngine.ts`**: `resolveIncident()` pops `incidentDeck.shift()` (pre-ordered card at front).
- **`tests/main-street/incident-balance.test.ts`**: Tests the current pre-order system via `orderIncidentDeck`.

## Desired Change

Replace `orderIncidentDeck()` with runtime selection using `findConstrainedIncidentIndex()` (or a refined variant). The flow becomes:

1. **Setup/reshuffle**: Gather incident pool → shuffle (seeded) → store as `incidentDeck`.
2. **Draw**: Call `findConstrainedIncidentIndex(deck, balance)` → remove chosen card by index → record draw with `recordIncidentDraw()`.

`findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already exists and implements the exact constraint logic needed. The change is to use it at draw time instead of pre-ordering.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Remove or deprecate `orderIncidentDeck`; `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already exists
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Update `replenishIncidentDeck()` to shuffle-only (no `orderIncidentDeck`)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Update `setupMainStreetGame()` to shuffle-only for incident pool
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Update `resolveIncident()` to use runtime selection instead of `shift()`
- `tests/main-street/incident-balance.test.ts` — Update tests to reflect runtime selection; verify determinism

## Related Work

- **CG-0MSXOVQFL007G3VH** — Implement constraint-aware deck ordering (the pre-ordering system being replaced)
- **CG-0MSL0OP040043KKZ** — Incident Balance state (IncidentBalanceState, recordIncidentDraw, findConstrainedIncidentIndex)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Performance** — `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` scans the full deck each draw (O(N)). With ~60-80 incident cards, this is negligible.
- **Risk: Saved games** — Pre-ordered decks in legacy saves are treated as initial state; subsequent draws use runtime selection. Balance history drives constraints, not deck order.
- **Assumption:** `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` constraint logic is sufficient without modification. If the tier system needs refinement, that is tracked separately.
- **Scope guard:** This task replaces pre-ordering with runtime selection only. No changes to constraint thresholds, difficulty presets, or UI.
- **Opportunity (out of scope):** If runtime selection reveals new balancing insights, a follow-up task can tune `incidentRepeatSpacing` / `incidentMaxStreak` presets.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q**: Should we deprecate `orderIncidentDeck()` or keep it for legacy compatibility? — **Answer (Map)**: Deprecate and remove. The runtime selection approach fully replaces it. Any legacy code paths that reference it are internal and not exposed.
- **Q**: Does `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` need any modifications for runtime selection? — **Answer (Map)**: `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already returns the array index of the chosen card and works against a deck in the expected format. No modifications needed — it already implements the constraint tiers exactly as required.
- **Q**: How should saved games (which contain pre-ordered decks) be handled? — **Answer (Map)**: Saved game deserialization already handles the `incidentDeck → incidentBalance` migration. Pre-ordered decks in saves are treated as initial state; subsequent draws use runtime selection. No special handling needed — the balance history is the source of truth for constraints, not deck order.
data.risk: Low — findConstrainedIncidentIndex already implements the needed constraint logic; only wiring changes. Determinism preserved.
data.title: Replace incident deck pre-ordering with runtime balanced card selection

# Deferral of Day-Transition Banner Until Player Commits to Starting the Game

**Problem statement:** In Main Street, the "Day N" day-transition banner plays at game boot time — before the player has chosen how to start the game (run tutorial, resume from a checkpoint, or begin a new game). This is jarring and gives the player a new-day announcement before they have committed to playing.

**Users:**
- *Existing player returning to Main Street:* Booting the game should not announce "Day 1" before they see the resume option or tutorial offer.
- *New player:* Same — the banner should appear only after they've chosen to start playing.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. **Banner does NOT fire at boot.** When the game boots (no saved checkpoint, no campaign), the day-banner animation and SFX must NOT play while the tutorial offer modal is visible or before any player choice is made.
2. **Banner fires after skipping the tutorial offer.** When the player clicks "[ Skip ]" on the tutorial offer modal, the deferred "Day N" banner must play immediately.
3. **Banner does NOT fire on checkpoint resume.** When the player resumes from a saved checkpoint, the banner must NOT play (the same day continues — this is already correct in the pre-deferral code).
4. **Banner fires normally after starting the tutorial.** When the tutorial offer is accepted and the tutorial begins, the banner must NOT play (the tutorial overlays carry the guidance — existing behavior preserved).
5. **Banner fires normally on subsequent days.** After the first day has begun, the banner plays as before on each new-day transition.
6. **Reduced motion is respected.** Under reduced motion, the banner trigger still fires (the animator degrades internally to instruction text only — existing behavior preserved).
7. **All day-banner browser tests pass in the full browser suite.** The 2 new deferral tests must pass reliably under full-suite load (no state-contention between booted Phaser games).

**Constraints:**
- The banner must be deferred for at most one display — it fires exactly once upon first player commitment.
- The implementation must not change the day-banner animator or its reduced-motion handling.
- The `suppressDayBanner` parameter (when added to `startDayPhase`) must default to `false` for backward compatibility with existing calls.

**Existing state:**
- `MainStreetScene.ts` — calls `msTurnController.startDayPhase()` at boot; no deferral mechanism.
- `MainStreetTurnController.ts` — `startDayPhase(skipMarketRefill: boolean)` fires `animateDayBanner()` whenever `!skipMarketRefill && !tutorialController?.isActive`.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — calls `s.startDayPhase()` at boot (before tutorial offer modal appears); calls `startDayPhase(true)` on checkpoint resume.
- `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateDayBanner({ day })` plays the banner animation/SFX; skips under reduced motion, replay, or tutorial-active conditions.
- `tests/main-street/day-banner.browser.test.ts` — 3 tests (new-day fires, tutorial/checkpoint skip, reduced motion).

**Desired change (implementation blueprint from reverted WIP commit 4a18d5bf):**
1. **`MainStreetScene.ts`** — Add `public deferredDayBanner: boolean = false` flag and `public playDeferredDayBanner(): void` method. The flag is set `true` at boot/reset; `playDeferredDayBanner()` clears it and calls `msAnimator.animateDayBanner()`.
2. **`MainStreetTurnController.ts`** — Add `suppressDayBanner: boolean = false` parameter to `startDayPhase()`. Extend the guard to `!suppressDayBanner`.
3. **`MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts`** — Set `s.deferredDayBanner = true` in the reset path. Change all boot-time `s.startDayPhase()` calls to `s.startDayPhase(false, true)` (suppress banner). Replace all `tutorialOfferModal.showIfEligible(...)` call sites with a new `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner()` helper that calls `playDeferredDayBanner()` when no modal is shown. On checkpoint resume, clear the flag (`s.deferredDayBanner = false`) without playing.
4. **`tests/main-street/day-banner.browser.test.ts`** — Add 2 browser tests: (a) banner does NOT fire while the tutorial offer modal is visible at boot; (b) banner fires after the player skips the tutorial offer.

**Key Files (predicted):**
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Add deferred flag + method
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Add `suppressDayBanner` param
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — Centralize tutorial/deferred logic, update call sites
- `tests/main-street/day-banner.browser.test.ts` — Add 2 browser tests

**Risks & assumptions:**

- **Test flakiness (medium):** The 2 new deferral browser tests from the reverted WIP were flaky under full-browser-suite load due to state-contention between booted Phaser games. Mitigation: ensure each test fully destroys its Phaser game and clears localStorage in `afterEach`; consider splitting into separate browser instances if contention persists.
- **Scope creep (low):** Do not extend deferral to other boot-time animations (e.g., the intro screen fade). This is strictly the day-transition banner.
- **Assumption:** The tutorial offer modal's `isVisible` state is accessible from the scene for test assertions. (Verified in the WIP commit.)

**Related work:**
- The reverted WIP (commits `4a18d5bf` / `5a265e21`) contains the complete implementation — the code is recoverable from git history.
- Related browser tests from the WIP (already written) need to be de-flaked for full-suite reliability.

## Goal (user story)
As a TCE developer/CI maintainer, I want the non-tutorial browser test suite to run within per-instance resource limits so it passes reliably in CI instead of dying from Phaser 4 canvas/GPU context exhaustion.

## Problem
The non-tutorial browser suite (`--project browser`) runs all 92 browser test files (24 heavy Main Street) in a single Chromium instance with `fileParallelism: false, sequential`. Each file boots/destroys a Phaser 4 RC game with 141 SVG rasterizations. Phaser 4 RC exhausts WebGL/Canvas contexts after ~8 game create/destroy cycles in one browser process. Since v0.1.12 (80 files, passed CI) the suite grew +12 files (Main Street browser tests nearly doubled 13→24). CI now deterministically kills the browser process mid-run: PR #797 `test-and-build` run 32236611332 died abruptly mid-line (no test-failure summary) during `TutorialOverlayManager.browser.test.ts` (~file 90/92). Two consecutive runs died at the same point.

## Root cause
Same known Phaser 4 context-exhaustion issue the tutorial E2E suite already mitigates by splitting each part into its own named Chromium instance (`t1`..`t6`) run sequentially via `scripts/run-tutorial-tests.sh`. The non-tutorial suite never adopted this and has now outgrown the single-instance limit.

## Solution
Mirror the tutorial E2E pattern: split the single `browser` project into N directory-grouped chunks (e.g. `browser-1`..`browser-N`), each with its own named Chromium instance, run sequentially. Keep a wildcard working for targeted dev runs (`npx vitest run --project 'browser*' test/file`). Update `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `vite.config.ts`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)
- AC1: `vite.config.ts` defines multiple non-tutorial browser projects, each with a unique named Chromium instance, collectively covering every `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` file (excluding tutorial E2E) with no overlap/gap.
- AC2: `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` runs every non-tutorial browser chunk sequentially (via the retry script), and a single non-zero from any chunk fails the stage.
- AC3: A targeted dev run still works: `npx vitest run --project 'browser*' tests/<game>/<file>.browser.test.ts` executes the file.
- AC4: `npm run build` succeeds and `npm test` passes (unit + browser + tutorial E2E) at the implementation commit.
- AC5: Docs updated: `AGENTS.md` "When to run which tests" + `docs/DEVELOPER.md#testing` describe the chunked browser projects and the dev command.

## Out of scope
- Reverting/altering the day-banner WIP (separately tracked CG-0MSZE2PY7007J6XA).
- Fixing any individual test failures unrelated to the chunk split.
- Azure/other CI providers beyond the existing GitHub Actions `pr-checks.yml`.

## Notes
- **SUPERSEDED (2026-08-19):** Operator dropped the full test suite from PR CI (`pr-checks.yml` is now build-only; tests run locally only). The chunk-split fix is no longer needed to unblock the release. Priority lowered to `low` — deferred work if CI tests are ever re-enabled.
- The root-cause investigation (Phaser 4 context exhaustion, 92 files > per-instance budget) remains valid reference.
- The `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` retry script only masks transient *contention* failures (worker RPC timeout / browser WebSocket drop); it does NOT help here — the browser is hard-killed (context exhaustion), not a timeout.

## Goal (user story)
As a TCE maintainer, I want PR CI to gate on the build only (not the full test suite), so PRs like the v0.1.13 release (#797) are not blocked by test-suite resource exhaustion in CI.

## Problem
`pr-checks.yml` `test-and-build` runs the full `npm test` suite (unit + 92-file browser suite + tutorial E2E) in CI on every PR. The browser suite has outgrown the single-Chromium-instance context budget (Phaser 4 RC canvas/GPU context exhaustion after ~8 game create/destroy cycles; 92 files in one instance) and is deterministically hard-killed mid-run (PR #797, run 32236611332), blocking the release. The retry wrapper (`vitest-run-with-retry.ts`) only masks transient contention failures, not this hard kill.

## Decision (operator-directed)
Tests are always run locally (quality gate: `npm test` + `npm run build` before every push). CI does not need to re-run them. PR CI should gate on `npm run build` only (TypeScript compile + Vite bundle). `deploy.yml` on main already runs build-only; `package.yml` smoke-tests the packaged Windows binary via `--project electron` (separate, unaffected).

## Solution
1. `pr-checks.yml`: remove the `npm test` step (and its env vars) and the Playwright Chromium install step (no longer needed); keep Checkout → Setup Node → npm ci → `npm run build`. Optionally rename job `test-and-build` → `build`.
2. Docs (doc-update policy): update `AGENTS.md` "When to run which tests" (CI = build-only) and `docs/DEVELOPER.md#testing` (CI behaviour note) in the same commit.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)
- AC1: `pr-checks.yml` has no step invoking `npm test` or `npx playwright install chromium`; the job runs `npm run build`.
- AC2: `npm run build` passes at the implementation commit.
- AC3: Docs describe PR CI as build-only (tests run locally via `npm test`).
- AC4: PR #797's `test-and-build` check re-runs green (build-only) and the release proceeds.

## Out of scope
- Modifying `deploy.yml` (already build-only) or `package.yml`.
- Fixing the browser-suite context exhaustion (superseded; see CG-0MT00JNOP003KVH8).

## Notes
- Supersedes CG-0MT00JNOP003KVH8 (chunk-split fix discarded per this decision).
- The build gate still catches TypeScript compile errors and bundling regressions on every PR.

# Browser test stage hangs on gym overlay tests during full-suite `npm test`

## Problem statement

Full-suite `npm test` runs intermittently **hang** in the non-tutorial browser stage: `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project browser` does not complete within a reasonable time, stalling on gym overlay browser tests (e.g. `tests/gym/GymOverlayUi.browser.test.ts`, `GymParameterizedOverlay.browser.test.ts`). The same files pass in isolation (targeted `--project browser` runs) and are unaffected by unrelated changes (e.g. a Main Street-only fix). This is distinct from the worker RPC *timeout* at teardown tracked in CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3: here the run never finishes (hang), and under `set -euo pipefail` the CI script aborts at the browser step, turning a fully-passing run into a failed gate.

## Observed context

- Occurs under high CPU load (load avg 14–35 on 16 cores) from concurrent vitest processes / parallel agent worktrees.
- Retry logic in `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` masks the *RPC timeout* and *browser WebSocket drop* variants, but a true hang (no exit) is not covered by the retry path.
- Full browser stage: 24 files / 149 tests for Main Street alone pass when targeted; the hang appears in the broader `--project browser` sweep.
- Pre-existing environmental issue; documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` testing section.
- PR CI now gates on build only (CG-0MT022826006EM0D), so this affects local `npm test` gate runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (or `run-ci-tests.sh`) handles a browser-stage hang: a per-file or per-worker timeout that aborts the hung file and retries once (masked against genuine failures), OR the browser stage runs with a documented bounded wall-clock timeout.
- [ ] A full-suite `npm test` run completes without hanging on the gym overlay browser tests under the CPU-contention scenario (verified by two consecutive green runs, or a reproducible CI-style run).
- [ ] Targeted runs (`npx vitest run --project browser tests/gym/GymOverlayUi.browser.test.ts` and `GymParameterizedOverlay.browser.test.ts`) still pass.
- [ ] `docs/DEVELOPER.md` testing section updated to describe the hang mitigation and any new timeout/retry flags.
- [ ] No change to per-test assertions or test semantics (infrastructure-only fix).

## Notes

- Related: CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3 (worker RPC timeout at teardown, completed), CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE (browser WebSocket drop retry), CG-0MSJ7ZXD5005N9E5 (browser env pre-check), CG-0MT00JNOP003KVH8 (browser-suite context exhaustion).
