# Staff Specialization: New Applicant Cards & Skills

## Problem statement

The staff applicant mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX) needs a rich pool of new staff-member applicant cards and specialization skills beyond the existing 9 templates (all hand-slot focused) and the minimum "Town Gossip" skill. This provides players with meaningful choices when applicants arrive, varied gameplay identities, and strategic depth in building a specialized team.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants diverse applicant cards with distinct gameplay identities and specialization skills that create meaningful hiring decisions and long-term strategic advantages.
- **Game designer** — wants a modular, balanced skill pool that synergizes with existing business types and synergy families, and can be extended without breaking the mechanic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **10+ new staff card templates** proposed with distinct gameplay identities, CSV-ready data (id, name, description, tier, ongoingCost), and clear thematic fit for Main Street's business ecosystem.
2. **10+ specialization skills** proposed with defined mechanical effects, balanced impact ranges, and clear synergies with existing synergy types (Food, Culture, Commerce, Service, Entertainment, Health).
3. **Randomization design** — Skills are assigned randomly at game start from a global pool to each staff applicant (1–3 skills per member). No single staff may hold more than 1 income-boost AND 1 reputation-boost skill. "Town Gossip" is included as a baseline.
4. **Skill-effect categories** — Skills are organized into effect categories (income boost, reputation boost, cost reduction, incident mitigation, synergy enhancement) with balanced impact ranges documented per category. No single staff member may hold more than 1 income-boost skill AND 1 reputation-boost skill simultaneously, to prevent runaway stacking.
5. **Balance documentation** — Impact ranges and categories documented per category; stacking constraints documented (max 1 income-boost + 1 reputation-boost per staff). Street-wide effects (e.g., "Cost Cutter") are flagged for additional testing.
6. **Tests & docs** — Implementation covered by unit tests (deterministic skill assignment under seeded RNG, per-business buff application, multi-skill stack interactions) and full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Skills randomized once per game at start, locked for full game (established by CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX).
- Skills are disconnected from the staff member's nominal job (a "Chef" can have the "Security" skill).
- Passive buffs apply per-business to income, reputation, synergy, or cost computations — must not conflict with existing `applyIncome` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` caching in MainStreetAdjacency.
- New templates should fit the existing CSV schema; no breaking changes to card-data.csv columns.
- Follow existing SLL, HandView/PileView, animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md.
- Skills must be implementable with existing engine abstractions (no new core engine subsystems required).

## Existing state

- 9 existing staff card templates in `card-data.csv`, all hand-slot focused (`handSlotsAdded`), with some secondary effects (Accountant's `refreshCostDiscount`, Socialite's `reputationPerTurn`, General Manager's `actionsPerTurn`, Lookout's `peekOncePerTurn`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) — no employed-applicant tracking yet.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `peekIncidentDeck()` action, `applyIncome()` in MainStreetAdjacency deducts ongoing costs.
- `MainStreetAdjacency.ts`: synergy bonus computation, income per slot.
- Town Gossip skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN) = `peekOncePerTurn` peek at top incident deck card.

## Proposed staff card templates (12)

These templates represent distinct roles in Main Street's ecosystem. Each provides flavor text, fits a tier (cost/difficulty), and has a reasonable `ongoingCost`. None provide `handSlotsAdded` — these are employed-applicant cards.

| # | ID | Name | Description | Tier | ongoingCost | Theme |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | staff-barista | Barista | A skilled barista brings warmth to any business. Adjacent Food businesses gain +0.2 synergy coins. | 2 | 0.5 | Food |
| 2 | staff-security | Security Guard | Experienced guard watches over the street. Reduces all incident coin damage by 10%. | 3 | 0.75 | Health |
| 3 | staff-marketing | Marketing Consultant | Expert at drawing crowds. Businesses gain +10% reputation from all sources. | 3 | 1.0 | Culture |
| 4 | staff-bookkeeper | Bookkeeper | Keeps the books tight. Reduces this business's ongoing cost by 20%. | 2 | 0.5 | Commerce |
| 5 | staff-customer-rep | Customer Service Rep | Ensures every visitor leaves satisfied. Adjacent businesses gain +0.1 synergy reputation. | 2 | 0.5 | Service |
| 6 | staff-it | IT Specialist | Modernizes operations. Reduces this business's refresh cost by 1. | 4 | 1.0 | Entertainment |
| 7 | staff-health-safety | Health & Safety Inspector | Keeps everything up to code. Reduces incident frequency by 10% for Health businesses. | 4 | 1.0 | Health |
| 8 | staff-event-planner | Event Planner | Creates buzz and draws visitors. +1 synergy coin per turn from Entertainment businesses. | 3 | 0.75 | Entertainment |
| 9 | staff-delivery | Delivery Driver | Handles the logistics. Reduces business card purchase cost by 0.5 for this business. | 2 | 0.5 | Commerce |
| 10 | staff-pr | PR Officer | Manages the street's image. +0.15 reputation per turn from all businesses. | 4 | 1.0 | Culture |
| 11 | staff-financial | Financial Advisor | Smart investments pay off. Reduces this business's upgrade cost by 1. | 5 | 1.25 | Commerce |
| 12 | staff-maintenance | Maintenance Worker | Keeps everything running smoothly. Reduces incident reputation damage by 0.5. | 3 | 0.75 | Service |

## Proposed specialization skills pool (14)

Skills are randomized at game start and assigned to staff members. Each staff applicant can receive 1–3 random skills. Skills are organized into effect categories with balanced impact ranges.

### Category A: Income Boosts

| ID | Name | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| skill-networker | Networker | +0.2 coins per adjacent business synergy (passive) |
| skill-chef | Chef de Cuisine | +20% income from Food businesses |
| skill-dj | DJ | +20% income from Entertainment businesses |
| skill-sales-champion | Sales Champion | +0.5 coins per turn from Commerce businesses |
| skill-tech-guru | Tech Guru | Unlocks +1 synergy range for Entertainment businesses |

### Category B: Reputation Boosts

| ID | Name | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| skill-town-gossip | Town Gossip | Peek at top incident deck card once per turn (baseline) |
| skill-community-builder | Community Builder | +0.1 reputation per turn from all businesses |
| skill-brand-ambassador | Brand Ambassador | +50% reputation gain from incidents and investments |
| skill-pr-strategist | PR Strategist | +0.15 reputation per turn from Service businesses |

### Category C: Cost Reductions

| ID | Name | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| skill-cost-cutter | Cost Cutter | -15% ongoing costs for the entire street |
| skill-negotiator | Negotiator | -1 cost on business card refreshes |
| skill-operations-manager | Operations Manager | -0.5 salary cost for this employed staff member |

### Category D: Incident Mitigation

| ID | Name | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| skill-quality-inspector | Quality Inspector | -30% coin damage from all incidents |
| skill-risk-manager | Risk Manager | Reduces incident probability by 15% |
| skill-security-consultant | Security Consultant | Immunity to theft/loss incidents on the home business |
| skill-compliance | Compliance Officer | Reduces incident reputation damage by 0.5 |

## Skill-effect categories summary

| Category | Skills | Impact Range |
|---|---|---|
| Income Boost | 5 skills | +0.2–0.5 coins/turn, +20% from specific synergies |
| Reputation Boost | 4 skills | +0.1–0.15 rep/turn, +50% from specific sources |
| Cost Reduction | 3 skills | -0.5–1 cost, -15% ongoing |
| Incident Mitigation | 4 skills | -15% probability, -30% coin damage, -0.5 rep damage |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Add 12 new staff rows + specialization skill columns
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — New card type definitions, specialization skill types
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Employed-applicant tracking, skill assignment state
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Skill randomization at game start, buff application
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Apply specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — New card presentation + SFX

## Related work

- **CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX** — Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic (parent context)
- **CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN** — Implement staff peek skill (Town Gossip = peekOncePerTurn)
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots
- **CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE** — Ongoing per-turn cost for community spaces

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: What staff templates to add? — Answer (Map, using imagination): 12 new templates covering Barista, Security Guard, Marketing Consultant, Bookkeeper, Customer Service Rep, IT Specialist, Health & Safety Inspector, Event Planner, Delivery Driver, PR Officer, Financial Advisor, Maintenance Worker. Each with distinct gameplay identity and Main Street thematic fit. Source: producer directive 2026-08-22.
- Q: What specialization skills to add? — Answer (Map, using imagination): 14 skills across 4 categories (Income Boost, Reputation Boost, Cost Reduction, Incident Mitigation), balanced impact ranges, organized for implementation clarity. Source: producer directive 2026-08-22.
- Q: How many total? — Answer (producer): 10 or more for both staff templates and specialization skills. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-22.
- Q: How many skills per staff member? — Answer (Map, using imagination): 1–3 random skills per staff applicant, with balance constraints (no single staff should hold more than 1 income-boost + 1 reputation-boost to avoid overwhelming advantage). Source: designer judgment.

# Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Marked for producer review**

## Objective

When the turn ends and the IncomePhase resolves, step through all income card effects one at a time, in a phase-based order and pacing that reads clearly to the player. Starting with base income, each affected business/community-space card shows its income coins "counting out" into a coin grid rendered on the card; then synergy, reputation, event, and upcoming-card contributions either fly coins into that grid or (for negative effects) fly coins out. This replaces the current single-fly-to-HUD collection with a legible, per-contribution breakdown.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player** — "When I end my turn I want to *see* where my income came from — how much each business produced on its own, how much came from synergy and reputation, and how much events changed—so the economy feels legible and satisfying."
- **Player (reduced motion)** — "I still want to follow the phases and see the contributed amounts, but without the coin flights."

## Problem statement

End-of-turn income is currently collapsed into a single coin-per-slot that arcs to the HUD counter (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE). The player cannot tell how much came from base income vs synergy vs reputation vs event modifiers, which undermines the "watch your town pay out" moment.

## Desired change

Rework the income-collection presentation into a phase-based, per-card coin-grid animation:

1. **Base income "counts out" of each card** — for each producing business/community-space, the card's base income (rounded to nearest 0.5 after this phase) appears as coins (full coin per whole 0.5; half coin for a remainder) that animate out of the card into a coin **grid rendered on the card**. Coins accumulate on the card across phases.
2. **Synergy coins fly in from the synergy line** — coins from the synergy multiplier fly from the synergy line (shared `synergyLineEndpoints` geometry) into the affected card's grid.
3. **Reputation coins fly in from the HUD** — coins from the reputation multiplier fly from the reputation score HUD into the grid.
4. **Event-card effects** — any event card (active duration effects, e.g. Flu Outbreak 0.8×) that affects income flies coins in (boost) or out (reduction) to/from the affected business cards. Duration effects are indicated via animated text lines (see below); single-turn effects just fly the coins.
5. **Upcoming cards** — upcoming cards that affect income either fly coins in, or fly coins out (from the business to the upcoming card, where they disappear).
6. **Grid-to-HUD collection** — at the end of the income step, the accumulated coins on each card's grid fly to the HUD coins counter (reusing/extending the existing fly-to-HUD + final "+total" pop behaviour).

**Coin grid packing (per user):** start as a 5×3 grid; when space runs out, overlap/shrink the coins to fit 10×3, then 15×3, etc. Exact packing "whatever works well" — 3 rows with columns growing (5/10/15...) and shrinking coin size / overlap as needed.

**Rounding (per user, Q8):** each *phase* rounds its own portion to the nearest 0.5 for the coins shown in the grid. The HUD / credited total still uses the exact fractional value (current behaviour preserved).

**Phasing (per user, Q3):** phase-based — all cards show base alongside, then all cards' synergy, then all cards' reputation, then each event, then upcoming-card effects. Each phase lasts ~2–3 seconds. **Reduced motion keeps the phases (same sequence + pacing) but removes the coin animation** (no flights / count-out tweens); the per-phase rounded values still appear.

**Duration-effect text lines (Upcoming panel):** for event cards with a duration, indicate their effect via an animated text line — on a *new* card the effect text animates in one letter at a time with a grow/shrink animation. Then, for each line (new and pre-existing), coins fly to/from the affected business cards. *(The Upcoming-deck-as-face-down-single-card redesign that frees the panel space is a SEPARATE work item — CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 is unrelated (HUD decimals); the deck redesign has no ID yet and is out of scope here.)* This item assumes the panel already has room for these effect lines; if it does not yet, this item proceeds with the best available placement and the deck redesign is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. End-of-turn income walks through phases in order (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming), each ~2–3s, with on-card coin grids that accumulate rounded coins per phase (nearest 0.5 per phase).
2. Base coins "count out" of each producing card into its grid; synergy coins fly in from the synergy line; reputation coins fly in from the reputation HUD; event/upcoming effects fly coins in or out to/from the appropriate cards.
3. Grid packing scales from 5×3 to 10×3 to 15×3 by shrinking/overlapping coins as space requires; overflow is visible, not clipped.
4. At the end, grid coins fly to the HUD coins counter with the existing final "+total" pop and coin-pop SFX (extending CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE); the credited HUD total is unchanged (exact fractional total preserved).
5. Duration-effect events show an animated effect line (one-letter grow/shrink reveal for new cards) with coins flying to/from affected businesses; single-turn events just fly coins.
6. Reduced motion keeps the same phases and pacing but strips coin animations (text/phase progression only); replay/headless modes are unaffected (no rendering/audio — documented exemption).
7. New/extended unit + browser tests cover phase ordering, per-phase rounding, grid packing stress (15×3+), event/upcoming fly-in/out, and reduced-motion path.
8. All related documentation updated (code comments, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, scene README).

## Constraints

- Presentation-only VFX: never mutates game state, transcript, or turn flow (AGENTS.md rule 8). Must remain non-blocking like the current animation (runs inside the turn-advance window; failures swallowed).
- Reuse existing helpers: `moveGameObject`, `popTextOrIcon`, `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention), `synergyLineEndpoints`, per-slot data from `applyIncome()`/`IncomeResult.breakdown`.
- Respect reduced-motion (SettingsStore / `prefers-reduced-motion`) and headless/replay exemption.
- No new SFX keys unless unavoidable; prefer existing `sfx-coin-pop` etc.
- Must build on / not regress CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE (existing fly-to-HUD) and CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR (synergy formation animation).

## Existing state

- `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` returns `IncomeResult.breakdown` (`SlotIncome[]`: `slotIndex`, `businessName`, `baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) + `handSynergyTotal`; applies per-slot `income-multiplier` active effects, then the reputation multiplier to the total (exact fractional coins).
- `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomeCollection()` (from CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE) flies one coin per producing slot + rep pips to HUD, with final pop; `incomeCollectionActive` flag suppresses the immediate HUD delta pop.
- `synergyLineEndpoints()` shared by renderer + animator for synergy-line geometry (p1/p2/mid).
- `ActiveEffect` system (`income-multiplier` / `rep-multiplier`) with `applyActiveEffectMultiplier()`; duration events e.g. Flu Outbreak (0.8×/5 turns), Recession (0.7×/4), Tourist Season (1.15×/3), Labor Shortage (0.9×/3).
- The "Upcoming" panel (`MainStreetRenderer`) shows the incident queue (2 face-up cards + deck) + ⚠ active-effect duration lines.
- HUD geometry mirrors: coins label at `gameW*0.25 + 70`, rep label at strip centre (`gameW*0.5`), `hudY` from layout.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new `animateIncomePhases()` (or rework `animateIncomeCollection`) implementing the phased coin-grid + fly-in/out sequence; grid-packing helper.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — expose/derive per-slot base/synergy/rep/event contribution breakdown for the phases (likely extend `applyIncome`/`IncomeResult` with richer per-phase data).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()` / `applyIncome()` — surface per-phase contributions (base, synergy, rep from `applyReputationMultiplier`, event deltas) for the animation.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `reputationCoinMultiplier()` — source of the rep-coins fly-in amount.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` / `activeEffects` — identify income-affecting event/upcoming cards for fly-in/out.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Upcoming panel effect-line placement; HUD target coords; on-card grid anchoring.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — orchestrate the phased animation in `endTurn()` income presentation.
- `src/core-engine/ActiveEffect.ts` — reference for `income-multiplier` / `applyActiveEffectMultiplier`.
- `tests/main-street/` — phase-ordering, rounding, grid-packing, reduced-motion tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Grid space / readability** — on-card coin grids may visually clutter small card faces; the 5×3→10×3→15×3 overlap/shrink packing may become hard to read at high income. Mitigate: half-coin vs full-coin sizing, controlled overlap, overflow label. (Spike if needed.)
- **Phase timing vs turn pacing** — 2–3s × several phases could lengthen end-of-turn. Reduced-motion retains phases; keep total within acceptable bounds and non-blocking. Player may find 5+ phases too slow — may need a cap/condense for cards with no contributions in a phase.
- **Rounding drift** — per-phase nearest-0.5 rounding means displayed coins may not sum exactly to the exact credited fractional total; the HUD shows the exact total (documented as intended, Q8).
- **Panel space for effect lines** — the Upcoming-deck redesign (face-down single deck) that frees space is a separate work item; if space isn't ready, effect lines may need a temporary placement. Track the deck redesign as a child/related item.
- **Scope creep** — remain a presentation-only income-animation feature; do not include the deck redesign, Community Favour, HUD decimals, or other economy changes. Log extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Related work

- CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE "Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD)" (completed) — base the phased animation on this.
- CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR "Synergy link formation animation" (completed) — synergy-line geometry reuse.
- CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B / CG-0MSX2PNSJ000YDM0 "synergyLineEndpoints" — shared synergy geometry helper.
- CG-0MSQJ244M0055X7S "Group C: Investment events — new duration types" — duration `income-multiplier`/`rep-multiplier` events (Flu Outbreak, Tourist Season, etc.) that produce the effect lines.
- CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 "Show HUD bar money and reputation to 2 decimal places" (open) — touches HUD numeric display; related but out of scope.
- Upcoming-deck redesign (face-down single card) — separate work item (no ID yet); prerequisite for freeing Upcoming panel space.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map → user): "End state of the coin grid after all coins land?" — Answer (user): "(a) Grid is intermediate — coins then fly from each card to the HUD counter, replacing the current per-slot fly-to-HUD; the grid visualizes the breakdown, then the existing collection animation finishes the job." Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (Map → user): "What are 'upcoming cards that affect income'?" — Answer (user): "Not all cards have a duration effect, some are single turn. For duration cards we need an effect indication (space freed by the Upcoming-deck redesign). If a new card, its effect text animates in (one letter at a time, grow/shrink). Then for each line (new + old) coins fly to/from the affected businesses. Single-turn cards simply fly the coins." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (Map → user): "Sequencing/pacing?" — Answer (user): "Phase based; each phase 2–3 seconds. Reduced motion keeps the phases but removes the animations." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (Map → user): "Grid capacity & card space + packing?" — Answer (user): "5×3 grid to start; overlap/shift coins to enable 10×3, then 15×3, etc." Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 (Map → user): "Fractional rounding for portions?" — Answer (user): "Round for the total after each phase." Source: interactive reply.
- Q6 (Map → user): "Is the Upcoming-deck redesign part of this item?" — Answer (user): "It is another work item." Source: interactive reply.
- Q7 (Map → user): "Exact 5×3→10×3→15×3 packing rule?" — Answer (user): "Whatever works well." Source: interactive reply.
- Q8 (Map → user): "Round per phase means each phase rounds its own coins to nearest 0.5 independently?" — Answer (user): "confirm." Source: interactive reply.
- Q9 (Map → user): "Base coins stay on the card as grid anchor; at end grid coins fly to HUD?" — Answer (user): "confirm." Source: interactive reply.

## Mini-review record (agent, five stages)

- **1. Completeness:** Problem, users, ACs, constraints present. ACs cover phase ordering/rounding, per-contribution fly-in/out, grid packing stress, event text lines, reduced-motion, tests, docs. Added a grid-overflow visibility AC (never clipped) and a build/doc AC.
- **2. Capture fidelity:** All user answers (Q1–Q9) captured verbatim in the Appendix; phased/pacing/reduced-motion (Q3), 5×3→10×3→15×3 packing + "whatever works well" (Q4/Q7), per-phase total rounding (Q5/Q8), deck redesign out of scope (Q6), base-counts-out + grid-intermediate-then-fly-to-HUD (Q1/Q9). No intent altered.
- **3. Related-work & traceability:** Key precedents linked (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE, CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR, CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B/CG-0MSX2PNSJ000YDM0, CG-0MSQJ244M0055X7S). find-related automated report appended; its hits are mostly tangential (hand animation, Coloretto spacing) and do not alter scope.
- **4. Risks & assumptions:** Added grid-readability, phase-timing/turn-pacing, per-phase rounding drift, Upcoming-panel space (deck redesign out of scope), and a scope-creep guard. Each has a mitigation.
- **5. Polish & handoff:** Tightened objective to "phase-based, per-card coin grid + fly-in/out" with measurable ACs; documented exact credited total preserved (Q8); highlighted which helpers to reuse and the separate deck-redesign work item.

## Related work (automated report)

Automated find-related report appended to this item's description (.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ.md) — hits: CG-0MS7UEUL000610A2 (buy-card hand animation, tangential), CG-0MSJFUGB5005YBK8 (Coloretto tableau spacing, tangential), CG-0MRXYHNHB006F0U9 (synergy bonus on cards, related). Manual related-work section above lists the truly-direct precedents.

**Research summary:** Reviewed `applyIncome()`/`IncomeResult.breakdown` (per-slot base/synergy, per-slot income-multiplier, then total rep multiplier), `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomeCollection()` and its `incomeCollectionActive` suppression, `synergyLineEndpoints` shared geometry, `ActiveEffect`/`applyActiveEffectMultiplier` for duration events, `reputationCoinMultiplier()` in MainStreetDifficulty (divisor 20, max 3.0), and the Upcoming panel renderer. Related completed items CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE, CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR, CG-0MSQJ244M0055X7S guide the design.

# Main Street: Upcoming panel — replace face-down deck card with compact deck counter

## Problem statement

The Upcoming/incident panel dedicates ~70px to a face-down card-back image plus ~12px for deck-count text, leaving insufficient vertical space for the duration-effect text lines that the income-phase animation (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ) needs to display per-affected business card.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (income-phase visibility):** "When my turn's income resolves, I want to see the duration-effect text lines for upcoming cards without the panel overflowing or the active-effect lines disappearing."
- **Player (reduced motion):** "I want the panel layout to remain readable without animation — the deck counter should be clearly visible and the effect text should be legible."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The face-down card-back image in the Upcoming panel is replaced by a compact deck counter (rounded rectangle with card icon and count number) that fits within ~24px of vertical space.
2. The panel height shrinks by at least 50px (the ~70px card-back + ~12px text, minus the ~24px counter), making that space available for income-phase duration-effect text lines.
3. The deck counter updates reactively whenever `state.incidentDeck.length` changes (e.g., cards drawn, deck reshuffled).
4. The deck counter's click/tap area (if any) preserves existing tooltip behaviour — clicking the counter shows the remaining deck count, or the panel has no interactive elements (no-click, pass-through).
5. Reduced-motion mode renders the deck counter without animation; the visual design is identical to full-motion (no animation = no layout difference).
6. All unit + browser tests pass: layout geometry tests (panel height, card-center calculation compatibility with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()`), deck counter render/update, and the income-phase dependency (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ).

## Constraints

- **Panel width unchanged:** Only vertical space is affected.
- **`getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` compatibility:** The incident-reveal flight and staff-peek reveal (CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 / CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN) use this method to get the card center for animation origins. If the counter changes the vertical centering math, update the method to return the same logical origin (the position where the face-down deck would have been centred).
- **SLL layout binding:** The panel height is driven by the SLL layout (`MAIN_STREET_SLL_LAYOUT` zone `incidentQueue`). If the SLL zone has a fixed height, either: (a) the zone height is already a max-height / min-height constraint (preferred), or (b) the deck counter is placed within the existing zone with overflow clipped (documented limitation).
- **No new SFX keys.** The deck counter is a static/non-interactive element — no sound effects.
- **Re-use existing SVG rasterisation:** If the card icon needs to be an SVG, use `SvgHelpers` / `makeTextureKey()` pattern from `GymSvgHelpersScene`.
- **Headless/replay exemption:** No rendering changes visible in headless/replay modes.

## Existing state

- `refreshIncidentQueue()` in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders: title bar (22px) → face-down card-back (~69px) → deck count text (~12px) → active-effect lines (16px × N + 16px overhead) → bottom padding (8px).
- `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` returns the logical center of the face-down card for animation purposes.
- Constants: `BASE_QUEUE_CARD_W = 120`, `BASE_QUEUE_CARD_H = 69`.
- Parent work item (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ) adds income-phase duration-effect lines to the panel.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** the face-down card-back SVG render and the separate deck-count text label from `refreshIncidentQueue()`.
2. **Add** a compact deck counter: a small rounded rectangle (~100px wide × 20px tall) containing a small card-icon (12×12px) on the left and the count number (e.g., "Deck: 5") in 10px text on the right.
3. **Update** `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` if the counter's vertical centre differs from the old card-back centre; ensure incident-reveal animations still target the correct origin.
4. **Ensure** the panel's dynamic height calculation accounts for the new counter's reduced height.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshIncidentQueue()` (deck counter replacement), `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` (origin math)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — constants (if new counter dimensions need constants)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — SLL zone height binding (if the incidentQueue zone needs adjustment)

## Related work

- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** "Income Phase: phased card-effect animations" (blocked-by this item) — needs the freed panel space for duration-effect text lines.
- **CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6** / **CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN** — incident-reveal flight and staff-peek reveal; must remain compatible with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` after deck counter changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **SLL zone height rigidity:** If the `incidentQueue` SLL zone has a fixed pixel height, reducing the panel's internal content won't shrink the zone itself — the extra space may be unused. Mitigation: inspect SLL zone height type; if fixed, the zone height can be left as-is (no regression), or adjusted if it's a max-height constraint.
- **`getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` origin shift:** Removing the ~69px card-back and replacing it with a ~20px counter shifts the visual centre. Mitigation: keep the counter centred at the same Y origin as the old card-back, so animation targets are unchanged.
- **Scope creep:** This is a pure visual/layout change. Do not include: changing incident-draw logic, changing active-effect display, adding new interaction patterns, or modifying the incident deck draw animation.

# Community Favour — Engine Action, State, and Config

## Goal
Implement the core `community-favour` player action type: exchange coins ↔ reputation with per-difficulty configurable rates, MarketPhase gating, and a once-per-turn guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — PlayerAction union:** A new `CommunityFavourAction` variant is added to the `PlayerAction` union in `MainStreetEngine.ts`:
  ```
  | { type: 'community-favour'; direction: 'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins' }
  ```

- **AC2 — executeAction case:** A `case 'community-favour'` is added to `executeAction()` that:
  - Validates the state is in `MarketPhase` (throws if not).
  - Checks `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is `false` (throws if true).
  - Validates resource sufficiency via the `EconomyLedger`:
    - `coins-to-rep`: checks `coins >= favourCoinsToRepCost`.
    - `rep-to-coins`: checks `reputation >= favourRepToCoinsRepCost`.
  - Applies the exchange:
    - `coins-to-rep`: subtracts `favourCoinsToRepCost` coins, adds `1` reputation.
    - `rep-to-coins`: subtracts `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` reputation, adds `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain` coins.
  - Sets `state.favourUsedThisTurn = true`.
  - Does **not** decrement `actionsRemaining` (free once-per-turn action).

- **AC3 — State field:** `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` is added to `MainStreetState` and the serialized state `MainStreetSerializedState`.

- **AC4 — DayStart reset:** In `executeDayStart()`, `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is reset to `false` (alongside `actionsRemaining` reset).

- **AC5 — GameConfig constants:** Per-difficulty exchange rates are added to `GameConfig` and all presets in `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`:
  - `favourCoinsToRepCost: number` — coins consumed for 1 rep (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsRepCost: number` — reputation consumed for coin gain (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain: number` — coins gained when spending rep (default: 3).
  - All 4 presets (easy, normal, medium, hard) include these values.

- **AC6 — MarketPhase gating:** The action is only legal during `MarketPhase`; the `case` throws an appropriate error for other phases.

- **AC7 — Once-per-turn enforcement:** The `favourUsedThisTurn` flag prevents a second exchange until the next `DayStart`.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — PlayerAction union, case handler, executeAction logic
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — favourUsedThisTurn field, serialization, DayStart reset
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — GameConfig constants and all presets

# Community Favour — UI Buttons and Turn Controller

## Goal
Render two Community Favour buttons in the market-phase action bar (one per direction), with disabled states, following SLL layout and the established animated/sounded action pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — SLL zones:** Two SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons are added to `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` (coins-to-rep and rep-to-coins), consistent with the existing action-bar layout. No hardcoded pixel positions.

- **AC2 — Renderer:** `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders two favour buttons in the market-phase action bar via the SLL zones. Buttons are **disabled** (greyed/non-interactive) when:
  - The player's coins < `favourCoinsToRepCost` (for coins-to-rep), or reputation < `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` (for rep-to-coins);
  - `favourUsedThisTurn` is `true`;
  - The state is not in `MarketPhase`.
  Otherwise active.

- **AC3 — Turn controller dispatch:** `MainStreetTurnController.ts` dispatches the new action through the existing animated/sounded path — same flow as other market actions (animate condition, then `executeAction`), with `popTextOrIcon` feedback and SFX via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` (no game-scoped string literals).

- **AC4 — Accessibility:** Reduced-motion preferences and settings-panel mute/volume are respected in the dispatch animation and SFX.

- **AC5 — Errors surfaced:** Illegal action attempts (e.g. already-used, insufficient resource) surface the standard illegal-move feedback (e.g. `shakeIllegalMove` + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE`) rather than a silent failure.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — render favour buttons with disabled states

# Community Favour — AI Strategy

## Goal
Add the `community-favour` action to the AI decision-making so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market and use the legal fallback action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — enumerateLegalActions:** `enumerateLegalActions(state)` in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` includes the `community-favour` action for both directions when:
  - The state is in `MarketPhase`; AND
  - `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is `false`; AND
  - The required input resource is sufficient (coins >= `favourCoinsToRepCost` for coins-to-rep; reputation >= `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` for rep-to-coins).

- **AC2 — scoreAction:** `scoreAction(state, action)` assigns a sensible heuristic score to the `community-favour` action (e.g. valued higher when the player cannot afford any market purchase and is coin-poor/coin-rich, lower otherwise), so it does not dominate normal purchases when affordable.

- **AC3 — AI turn execution:** AI-chosen `community-favour` actions are executed through the same animated/sounded path as human turns (consistent with how other AI market actions run).

- **AC4 — No stall:** With the action available, AI turns in an unaffordable-market state always have at least one legal non-`end-turn` action.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — enumerateLegalActions and scoreAction additions

# Hint text obscured by hand

## Problem Statement

When placing a card from hand (in `placing-from-hand` or `placing-business` UI phases), the inline hint text rendered at `actionY - 4` is visually obscured by the hand card sprites themselves, making it unreadable.

## User Story

As a player, I need to clearly see the instruction text telling me where to place the card I'm holding, so I can complete the action without confusion.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase-specific hint text ("Card in hand (N) — click an empty slot to place" and "Place \"[card name]\" -- click an empty slot") is no longer rendered inline at the action area.
2. The hint text is displayed using the shared `HintBar` component at the bottom of the screen instead.
3. When the UI phase changes from `placing-from-hand` or `placing-business` back to `market`, the hint bar text is reset to the standard instruction.
4. All existing tests pass.

## Constraints

- Must use the existing `HintBar` component (`src/ui/HintBar.ts`) — no new positioning or custom text rendering.
- Minimal change: only modify `MainStreetRenderer.ts`.
- No behavior change beyond repositioning the text.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/HintBar.ts` — shared hint bar component, positioned at bottom-centre by default.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` lines 1534, 1559 — inline hint text rendered via `s.add.text(rightX, by - 4, ...)` into `s.actionContainer`, positioned near the hand.

None found — this is an isolated UI fix.

# Activity log no longer scrolls

## Problem statement

The Main Street activity log no longer auto-scrolls to show the latest content. New log entries (income, incident results, purchases, staff costs, etc.) accumulate off-screen at the bottom of the panel while the view stays pinned at the top showing the earliest entries, so the player cannot see the most recent game events without manually wheel-scrolling.

## Users

- **Main Street players** — rely on the activity log to see the latest game events (turn headers, income, incident results, purchase/pay effects, win/loss).
- **Tutorial/review users** — use the log to verify that their actions took effect.

### User stories

- "As a player, when I buy a card or an incident resolves, I want the log to scroll so I can see the new entry without manual scrolling."
- "As a player, when I scroll up to re-read an older entry, I don't want the log to yank me back down on the next event."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When new log entries are added while the player is at (or near) the bottom of the log, the log auto-scrolls so the newest entry is visible.
2. When the player has scrolled up to read history, adding a new entry must NOT steal their scroll position (auto-scroll stays paused until they return to the bottom).
3. When the player wheel-scrolls back to the bottom, auto-scroll re-engages for subsequent entries.
4. On scene restart / new game, the log renders correctly with no content scrolled off the top of the panel (no regression of CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z).
5. Behavior is covered by automated tests (unit/browser): the existing browser tests that codify the current non-auto-scrolling behaviour are updated to assert the restored auto-scroll behaviour.
6. Full project test suite (`npm test`) and production build (`npm run build`) pass with the changes.
7. Relevant documentation (code comments in `refreshLog`/`handleLogWheel`, and any activity-log guidance in `docs/`) is updated to reflect the restored behaviour.

## Constraints

- Preserve the "don't yank the reader" UX: auto-scroll must engage only when the user is at/near the bottom (existing `logAutoScroll` mechanism — do not replace it).
- Preserve the scene-restart safety fix from CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z (stale scroll state must not hide all entries on restart).
- Main Street only; no engine/other-game impact expected.

## Existing state

- `logAutoScroll` starts `false` (MainStreetScene.ts line 117, reset in MainStreetLifecycleManager.create ~line 185).
- `refreshLog()` (MainStreetRenderer.ts ~line 1627): on overflow, keeps `logScrollOffset` clamped at its current value when `logAutoScroll` is false, then sets `logAutoScroll = (logScrollOffset >= logMaxScroll - 4)`. Because the offset starts at 0 (top) and content overflows by more than 4px, `atBottom` is false → `logAutoScroll` stays false forever; the log never moves until the user wheel-scrolls to the bottom (which re-engages it via `handleLogWheel`).
- Browser tests codify this behaviour: `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` ("does not position content above the log display area when entries first overflow" asserts `logAutoScroll === false` and offset stays 0; "auto-scroll snaps to bottom..." manually sets `logAutoScroll = true`, masking the real flow).

## Root cause (regression)

Commit `0b642a6e` — CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z ("Fix initial logAutoScroll to false to prevent content scrolling off the top") changed the initial `logAutoScroll` from `true` to `false` in both `MainStreetScene.ts` and `MainStreetLifecycleManager.create()`. Its stated assumption — "auto-scroll kicks in naturally when the user scrolls to the bottom" — is wrong for the default flow: the `atBottom` re-enable check in `refreshLog` never becomes true while the offset stays pinned at the top, so auto-scroll never engages. History: `git log -S "logAutoScroll = true"` → the original was `true` (0bd7eaf6), so this is a behavioural regression.

## Desired change

Restore "start at the bottom (latest entries) and auto-scroll on new entries unless the user has scrolled up":

- Set the initial `logAutoScroll` back to `true` (class property + create() reset), **and** ensure the scene-restart case still clamps correctly (the existing `Phaser.Math.Clamp` branch already guards stale offsets; worst case a restart resets offsets to 0 with an empty/new log so maxScroll recomputes to 0 — safe).
- Keep `handleLogWheel`'s re-engage-on-bottom logic unchanged.
- Update the browser tests that assert the current non-scrolling behaviour, and add a regression test that reproduces the real flow (fresh scene → entries accumulate → offset reaches bottom / latest visible without manual scroll), plus a test for "scrolled up → new entry does not yank position".
- Sanity-check the mask/visibility safety net still renders correctly at the bottom.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logAutoScroll` property initial value (line 117).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — scene-create reset of `logAutoScroll` (~line 185).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshLog()` scroll bounds/auto-scroll logic (~lines 1627–1720).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — `handleLogWheel` bottom re-engage threshold (reference, likely unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` — update tests codifying current behaviour; add regression tests.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — restart test asserts container `y > 0`; verify still valid after the change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z** — "Activity log extends beyond the bottom of the content area" (completed) — the commit (`0b642a6e`) that introduced this regression; its acceptance criteria include the restart-safety requirement that must not regress.
- **CG-0MSRGVGU40044GJ0** — "Undo/redo feedback notification" (completed) — logged as related by `/skill:find-related`; UI feedback adjacent, no functional dependency.
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** / **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** — surfaced by `/skill:find-related` (score-threshold noise; not functionally related to log scrolling).
- Original scroll implementation precedent (git ref, not a worklog item): commit `0bd7eaf6` (CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79 "Add activity log with state tracking, engine instrumentation, UI panel, and tests") — initial `logAutoScroll = true`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "scrolls to show the latest content" means the log default view is the bottom (newest entries), with auto-scroll on new entries while the user is at the bottom — i.e. restoring the pre-0b642a6e UX. This matches the bug title ("no longer scrolls") and standard log-panel convention.
- **Assumption:** current priority `medium` is appropriate (non-blocking, user-facing UX regression); may be re-considered to `high` if gameplay clarity is deemed significant by the producer.
- **Risk (scope creep):** restoring `logAutoScroll = true` may re-expose the original "content off the top" restart symptom if clamping is insufficient — mitigate with the existing clamp + explicit restart coverage, not by rebuilding the scroll system.
- **Risk:** other tests may implicitly depend on the log starting at the top (e.g. `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` restart test asserting `logContentContainer.y > 0`); verify and adjust assertions rather than behaviour.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the log default to showing the latest entries (bottom) — i.e. restore the pre-regression behaviour — as implied by the report?" — Answer: **Not asked; assumed yes (documented above).** The bug title ("used to scroll to show the latest content … no longer automatically does so") states the expected behaviour directly, and the pre-regression implementation (`logAutoScroll = true`) matches it. Source: work item CG-0MT24HFNM002MPF5 description + git archaeology (commit `0b642a6e` vs `0bd7eaf6`).
- Q: "Should auto-scroll pause while the user reads older entries (standard UX)?" — Answer: **Not asked; assumed yes.** The existing `logAutoScroll` mechanism and `handleLogWheel` already implement this; the fix merely restores its initial state. Source: code inspection of `refreshLog`/`handleLogWheel`.
---
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSRGVGU40044GJ0** – Undo/redo feedback notification (completed)
- **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** – [test-failure] Replay CLI tests in tests/replay/replay.test.ts (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm scripts/replay.ts exceeds 15s) — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** – Remove time-limited play mechanics (maxTurns) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: automatically, content, latest, log, longer, scroll, show, used
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: automatically, content, latest, log, scroll, show, used
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: activity, content, log, longer, scroll, show, used

# Problem Statement

When a business card is upgraded (e.g., Bakery → Patisserie), the card's displayed name always shows the original business name ("Bakery") instead of the upgraded name ("Patisserie"). This is a visual bug that misrepresents the current state of the business on the street grid.

# Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want the upgraded business name to be displayed on the card so I can clearly see which version of the business I have.
- **As a player**, I expect the card to show "Patisserie" after applying the "Upgrade to Patisserie" card to my Bakery, not "Bakery" as it did before.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. When an upgrade is applied to a business card, the card's name — rendered as **part of the card image** (baked into the card SVG texture), not a Phaser overlay — reflects the upgraded name (e.g., "Patisserie" instead of "Bakery"). (Mechanism per manual review: "We want it to be a part of the card like the original name.")
2. The upgraded name is computed dynamically from the applied upgrade cards — no hard-coded name values on BusinessCard instances.
3. Multi-level upgrades display the name from the **most recently applied** upgrade (set in `displayName` each time `purchaseUpgrade()` runs).
4. Base (un-upgraded) cards display their original `name` as before — the name is already part of the card; no overlay shown.
5. The fix works for all business upgrade paths in the game (Bakery→Patisserie, Diner→Bistro, etc.)
6. Unit tests cover both base cards (no name overlay) and upgraded cards (upgraded name displayed as part of the card face). `upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` asserts `nameText` is removed; `card-svg-generator.test.ts` / `replaceCardTitleInSvg` cover the baked upgraded name.
7. All existing tests pass after the change.

# Constraints

- The `BusinessCard.name` field is `readonly` in the TypeScript interface — the fix must not make it mutable. A separate display-name mechanism is required.
- The display name must be pre-computed and stored on the BusinessCard during `purchaseUpgrade()` (`displayName` field), since the rendering path receives the BusinessCard, not the upgrade templates.
- The fix should be minimal: BusinessCard/UpgradeCard interface fields, `purchaseUpgrade()`/`playUpgradeFromHand()`, the SVG texture pipeline (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager`, `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator`), and removal of the `nameText` overlay (`UpgradeOverlaySpec`, `MainStreetRenderer`).
- The solution must be data-driven where possible (driven by CSV card data, specifically the `newDisplayName` upgrade column), not hard-coded logic.

# Existing State

- `BusinessCard` has a `readonly name: string` (original business name), `level: number` (upgrade level), `appliedUpgrades: string[]` (IDs of applied upgrades), and `displayName?: string` (upgraded name, set by `purchaseUpgrade()`/`playUpgradeFromHand()`).
- `UpgradeCard` has a `name: string` (e.g., "Upgrade to Patisserie"), `targetBusiness: string` (e.g., "Bakery"), and `newDisplayName?: string` (e.g., "Patisserie") from the CSV.
- Card data CSV column `name` on upgrade cards uses format "Upgrade to <new name>"; the `newDisplayName` column stores the business's new name directly.

# Desired Change

The upgraded name must render as **part of the card image**, exactly like the base name is part of the template SVG:

1. `BusinessCard.displayName?: string` — the current upgraded name, set by `purchaseUpgrade()`/`playUpgradeFromHand()` from the applied upgrade card's `newDisplayName` (most recent upgrade wins).
2. `generateBusinessCardSvg()` uses `displayName ?? name` for the baked card title.
3. The texture pipeline (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager`) produces **display-name variant textures**: upgraded street businesses request a texture keyed by template+displayName whose SVG face is the base template with the title replaced by the display name (`replaceCardTitleInSvg`), so the upgraded name is part of the card image.
4. Remove the `nameText` overlay from `UpgradeOverlaySpec` and `MainStreetRenderer.applyUpgradeOverlays()` — the name is no longer a Phaser text overlay.

# Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `BusinessCard.displayName`, `UpgradeCard.newDisplayName`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `purchaseUpgrade()` / `playUpgradeFromHand()` set `business.displayName`
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — upgrade cards carry `newDisplayName`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `generateBusinessCardSvg()` displayName title; `replaceCardTitleInSvg()` variant helper
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — display-name variant texture keys + generation + prewarm
- `src/ui/Renderer/adapters/MainStreetAdapter.ts` — thread `displayName` through card rendering
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — pass `displayName` to street/hand render sites; remove `nameText` overlay
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — remove `nameText` field
- `example-games/main-street/tests/` / `tests/main-street/` — unit tests

# Related Work

- **CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT**: Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (references patisserie upgrade in tutorial context).

---

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the BusinessCard.name field be updated, or should a separate display name mechanism be used?"
  - A: A separate display name mechanism is needed since `BusinessCard.name` is `readonly` and used for identification/logic elsewhere. The overlay should derive the display name from applied upgrades.
  - Evidence: TypeScript interface definition in `MainStreetCards.ts` line 234 (`readonly name: string`).

- Q: "Should the new name come from the upgrade card's name field, or a dedicated field?"
  - A: A dedicated field (`newDisplayName` on UpgradeCard) is preferred for clarity and to avoid fragile string parsing of "Upgrade to X" patterns.
  - Evidence: CSV data shows upgrade names as "Upgrade to Patisserie" — the new name is embedded but not cleanly extractable without parsing.

- Q (manual review, rgardler): "The updated label is still an overlay. We want it to be a part of the card like the original name."
  - A: The upgraded name is baked into the card's SVG texture as a display-name variant (see Desired Change), and the Phaser `nameText` overlay is removed.

# Tooltips for Business Cards Do Not Work Reliably

## Problem Statement

Business card tooltips in Main Street are unreliable in two scenarios: (1) tooltips are suppressed when there are no actions remaining and the player hovers over a market business card, and (2) tooltips do not appear at all for business cards in the hand.

## Users

- **Main Street player (desktop):** Hovering over business cards in the market or hand should display a tooltip with card details (name, cost, income, synergy, description) so the player can make informed decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Business cards in the market:** Hovering over a business card in the market row displays the card tooltip with full details (name, cost, income, synergy, description) — regardless of whether actions remain. When no actions remain, the card is dimmed (alpha 0.45) but still shows its full tooltip.
2. **Business cards in the hand:** Hovering over a business card in the player's hand displays the card tooltip with full details, consistent with event card tooltips in the hand.
3. **Event card tooltips unchanged:** Existing event card tooltip behavior (market and hand) is not affected by the fix.
4. **Replay mode:** Tooltips are suppressed in replay mode, as before.
5. **All project tests pass** after the fix.

## Constraints

- Fix must be surgical — only touch tooltip event handlers, not click/drag behavior.
- Must respect `s.replayMode` flag (suppress tooltips during replay).
- Must respect the settings store tooltip toggle.
- No new dependencies or architectural changes.

## Existing State

### Market business cards (`MainStreetRenderer.ts`)

Normal business card path (no actions): `pointerover`/`pointerout` attached to `selection` or `hitArea` — tooltip works.

When `noActions` is true (line ~1268-1280):
- `container.setAlpha(0.45)` and `container.setInteractive({ useHandCursor: false })`
- `pointerover`/`pointerout` re-attached with a different message ("No actions remaining...")
- **Problem:** `setInteractive({ useHandCursor: false })` may prevent pointer events from firing. Additionally, the `pointerover`/`pointerout` handlers are re-attached, overwriting the earlier tooltip handlers.

### Hand business cards (`MainStreetRenderer.ts` line ~171-205)

Event cards in the hand get a `hover` rectangle with `pointerover`/`pointerout` → tooltip.

Business cards in the hand (`else` branch): only a `hitArea` with `pointerdown` for selection. **No `pointerover`/`pointerout` handlers → tooltips never fire.**

## Desired Change

1. **Market (no actions):** Replace the separate `noActions` tooltip override with a conditional in the existing tooltip logic — show the full card tooltip, but display a secondary note below it when actions are exhausted (or show the card tooltip + dimmed visual without replacing it).
2. **Hand business cards:** Add `pointerover`/`pointerout` handlers (a small invisible `hover` rectangle, like the event card path) that call `buildCardTooltipInfo()` and show the tooltip via `s.tooltipManager`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Market and hand business card tooltip event handlers
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo()` (already supports business cards)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** `setInteractive({ useHandCursor: false })` may or may not suppress pointer events depending on Phaser version — developer should verify this behavior in their environment before deciding on the fix approach.
- **Risk:** The hand `renderCard` function returns a container; adding hover rectangles may need careful depth management to avoid blocking upgrade overlays.
- **Assumption:** `buildCardTooltipInfo()` already returns correct content for business cards (verified: it does).
- **Assumption:** The `noActions` tooltip path was introduced to communicate the constraint (no actions left) but inadvertently broke the tooltip. Fix should preserve this communication while restoring the full card tooltip.
- **Scope creep risk:** Community-space and upgrade cards in the hand may also lack tooltips — file as a separate follow-up work item, not within this scope.
- **Scope creep risk:** Tooltips on the street (placed business cards) are handled separately and are outside this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: What tooltip content should display for business cards with no actions remaining? — Answer: The full card tooltip (same as when actions remain), not just "No actions remaining". The dimmed visual already communicates the constraint. Source: code review of MainStreetRenderer.ts.
- Q: Should hand business card tooltips include synergy detail lines like market tooltips? — Answer: No — market tooltips use `includeEventDetail: true`, but hand tooltips (per event card precedent) use the default `includeEventDetail: false`. Source: MainStreetRenderer.ts line 1232 vs 1252.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSQJ7SYD008U3EE** – Group E: Upgrade cards — cover new businesses (12 cards) (completed)
- **CG-0MT47EX89009DDPU** – Update score-formula test suite to plain reputation count (completed)
- **CG-0MSW6JVEO000M1K1** – Docs & full quality-gate verification (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: actions, add, adding, affected, alpha (+157 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actions, add, adding, additionally (+123 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: actions, add, also, appear, avoid (+110 more)

# Intake Brief: Buy and Play costs are charged if drag and drop is used, but not if clicks are used

## Problem statement

Main Street supports two ways to buy and play a business/community-space card in the same turn (market → street): **drag-and-drop** directly to a street slot, and the **click-to-click composite** (click market card → hand, select hand card, click street slot). Today these two routes to the same outcome charge different prices: drag-and-drop charges a **+50% premium** (`Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`, CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R) while the click composite charges only the card's **listed cost** — a player can dodge the premium by clicking, and the premium rule itself is opaque (two shipped tutorial copy blocks teach the split). The producer has decided the behavior: **same-turn buy-and-play must cost consistently**, the premium applies only when no actions are available, and the player gets a one-time explainer dialog.

## Producer decisions (2026-08-22, operator reply)

1. **Option A — premium parity:** the click-to-click composite buy-and-play charges the same +50% premium as drag-and-drop. Same outcome, same price.
2. **Community spaces included:** the premium applies to community-space cards in the composite path too (drag-drop already applies it to business **and** community-space).
3. **Premium-only-when-no-actions rule:** *"buy and place in a single turn should only cost more if there are no actions available."* When the player has actions available, same-turn buy-and-play uses the action(s) at listed cost; the +50% premium is the fallback when no action is available for the placement step.
4. **Explain dialog:** doing a same-turn buy-and-play (by click or drag) shows a dialog explaining this cost rule, with a **"Don't show this again"** option (persisted preference).
5. **Tutorial rework (separate critical work item):** fix the tutorial by splitting the buy-and-play action over **two turns** (see child CG-0MT53NXGZ004H5AE); the tutorial must not rely on same-turn composite buy-and-play once premium pricing lands.

## Users

- **Player** — expects the same service (buy-and-play in one turn) to cost the same regardless of input method, and expects the game to explain the premium before charging it; today the click path is a cheaper loophole and the pricing is unexplained.
- **TCE developer / producer** — needs a single consistent pricing rule enforced at the engine layer (so the premium cannot be bypassed), an explainer dialog, and tests that lock the behavior in.

User stories:
- "As a player, I want buying and playing a card in one turn to cost the same whether I drag it or click it, **so that** I can't farm a premium discount by switching input methods."
- "As a player, I want the game to tell me when a buy-and-place will cost extra and why, **so that** the +50% never surprises me (and tell me only once)."
- "As a player, I want a card I deliberately held in hand from a previous day to still play at its listed cost, **so that** the plan-ahead path keeps its price."
- "As a general-manager player, I want same-turn buy-and-play at listed cost when my two actions cover it, **so that** the premium only applies when I actually lack an action."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Premium parity:** placing a same-day, just-moved card from hand onto the street (the `pendingHandJustMoved` composite; AGENTS.md §10b flow) deducts the **+50% premium** `Math.ceil(card.cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2` — identical to drag-and-drop `buyAndPlaceBusiness` — instead of the listed cost. Applies to **business and community-space** cards. (Same formula both routes; no new rounding.)
- [ ] **Premium-only-when-no-actions rule:** the +50% premium is charged **only when no action is available** for the same-turn placement step (non-GM composite: the move consumed the day's single action → placement is premium-priced but action-free; GM with a second action available: placement consumes the remaining action at listed cost). When an action is available, same-turn buy-and-play uses it at listed cost; drag-drop is charged identically to the equivalent composite (move+place accounting), so drag can never be cheaper than click (parity invariant).
- [ ] **Affordability gating consistent:** the composite (and drag) reject the purchase when the player cannot afford the applicable price (premium when no action available, else listed), with the existing illegal-move / insufficient-coins feedback; move-to-hand still consumes the daily action as today.
- [ ] **Explain dialog:** initiating a same-turn buy-and-play that will incur the +50% premium (click composite placement or drag) shows a modal dialog explaining that buy-and-place costs 50% more because no actions are left, with options to proceed / cancel and a **"Don't show this again"** checkbox that persists the preference (localStorage-style store, mirroring SettingsStore patterns); interactions heed the overlay depth conventions (backdrop 199 / box 200 / elements 201) and cleanup on dismiss.
- [ ] **Held-card play unchanged:** placing a business card held in hand from a previous day continues to pay listed cost (cost-at-play, CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2) and consumes 1 action; no behavior change for the plan-ahead path.
- [ ] **Undo/redo + transcript consistent:** the composite's premium spend is snapshotted so undo restores the full coin deduction (and redo re-applies it); the recorded action's price/description is truthful (premium noted).
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** unit tests cover (a) composite click buy-and-play charging the premium for business AND community-space cards, (b) premium rejected when unaffordable, (c) held-card play still listed cost, (d) parity with `buyAndPlaceBusiness` pricing, (e) premium-when-no-actions rule incl. GM two-action listed-cost path, (f) dialog appears (and "Don't show again" persists). Browser tests cover the click-to-click composite coin deduction and the dialog flow. Existing tests that assert listed cost on the composite are updated deliberately. Full project test suite (`npm test`) and `npm run build` pass.
- [ ] **Docs:** all related documentation updated to reflect the consistent pricing and the dialog (AGENTS.md §10b, Main Street README, docs/main-street/*, tutorial copy — the latter via the tutorial child work item), including code comments; CHANGELOG.md is managed by the release pipeline (excluded).

## Constraints

- **Tutorial coupling:** the tutorial currently teaches same-turn composite buy-and-play (T10 Bookshop, T14 Library) within a tuned 12-coin budget; premium pricing breaks that budget (Bookshop $3 → 4.5; Library $7 → 10.5 > 9.875 available). The tutorial rework to split buy-and-play over two turns is a **blocking child work item (critical priority)** and must land in the same release as this pricing change.
- Preserve the action economy: move-to-hand consumes the daily action; same-day placement stays action-free WHEN premium replaces the missing action (CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL semantics) — the premium is a coin substitute for the unavailable action, never an extra action charge on top of the premium.
- The +50% premium formula stays exactly `Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2` for both routes and both card families (parity — do not invent a new rounding).
- The operator decision in CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R (buy-and-place premium exists) stays in force; this item unifies the pricing and scopes *when* it applies, it does **not** remove or rebalance the premium percentage.
- Same-day composite semantics (no auto-select, `justMovedHandCardId` tracking) are preserved; only the coin price and the explainer dialog change.
- Reduced-motion / mute settings are respected by the dialog; feedback reuses `playIllegalFeedback` / existing SFX conventions.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetEngine.buyAndPlaceBusiness` (drag path): consumes 1 action, charges `premiumCost = Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`, asserts affordability, logs `(-€X, 50% premium)`.
- `MainStreetEngine.placeFromHand` (composite + held-card path): charges listed `card.cost`, asserts affordability, logs `(-€X)`.
- `MainStreetTurnController.onStreetSlotClick` composite branch (`afterTransfer`, ~line 866, `!s.pendingHandJustMoved → consumeAction`): calls `placeFromHand` directly, no premium parameter; the affordability gate at `canPlaceBusiness` (~lines 699–707) checks the premium only for drag.
- Tutorial scenario/copy (T3/T10/T13/T14) teach the old pricing; tutorial E2E parts 3–6 assert the composite flow and 12-coin budget.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts`, `command-action-economy.test.ts` (drag premium), `MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts` (listed-cost placement), `move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts` (composite action-free semantics), `drag.test.ts` / `drag.browser.test.ts` (premium).

## Desired change

1. Engine placement takes an optional premium price: the same-day composite (and drag) charges the +50% premium when no action is available at placement; held-card play stays listed cost.
2. Composite affordability gating uses the premium when applicable.
3. A modal explainer dialog fires on premium-incurring same-turn buy-and-play, with a persisted "Don't show this again" preference.
4. Blocking child work item: rework tutorial T10/T14 to split buy-and-play across two turns (create, critical priority).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `placeFromHand` (listed) / `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (premium); add premium-aware placement used by the composite (business + community-space).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — composite `afterTransfer` in `onStreetSlotClick` (~lines 866–903); premium affordability gate in `canPlaceBusiness`/slot gate (~lines 699–707); dialog trigger for premium-incurring same-turn buy-and-play.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — explainer dialog (follow the `showSellConfirmation` overlay pattern: `createOverlayBackground`, `createOverlayButton`, `dismissOverlay`, depths 199/200/201, `hudContainer` parenting).

- Preference persistence: `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` (patterns) or a Main Street prefs store — `main-street.buyAndPlacePremiumDialogDismissed`-style key.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts`, `command-action-economy.test.ts`, `MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts`, `move-to-hand-no-auto-select.test.ts`, `drag.test.ts`, click-composite browser tests — update/extend for parity + premium-when-no-actions + dialog.

## Related work

- **Child (blocking, critical):** tutorial rework — split T10/T14 buy-and-play over two turns (CG-0MT53NXGZ004H5AE, created by this intake).
- CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R — *Limit player actions to one action per turn (action economy)* (completed): operator decision that buy-and-place costs 50% more; the premium formula and action-economy basis (move/play each 1 action).
- CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL — *Main Street: don't auto-select a card moved to hand from the market for another action* (completed): the same-day composite two-step click flow, `pendingHandJustMoved` / `justMovedHandCardId` semantics this item preserves.
- CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 — *Expand player hand to 3 slots and rework marketplace to single row* (completed): cost-at-play principle (move free, play pays listed cost) for held-card play.
- CG-0MSX413EU003OKEE — *Command enforcement + UI feedback* (completed): action spend in all commands and the buy-and-place premium indicator.
- CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP — *Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)* (open, intake_complete): parallel upgrade economy work that mirrors the business-card buy-and-play parity model — check for overlap when implementing (upgrades are out of scope here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — working model for "premium only when no actions available":** same-turn buy-and-play is a two-step operation (move + place). Non-GM (1 action): move consumes it → placement has no action → +50% premium (action-free placement, per CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL). GM (2 actions): placement consumes the remaining action → listed cost. Drag uses the same accounting as the composite it atomically performs, so drag and click are always priced identically (parity invariant). Sub-decisions for the implementer to pin down (recommended defaults in parentheses): (a) GM drag consumes one or two actions (two — identical to composite), (b) drag with 0 actions remaining is allowed at premium with no action consumed (yes — the premium is the no-action escape hatch per the producer), (c) dialog triggers only on premium-incurring buy-and-play (yes — there is nothing to explain when listed cost applies).
- **Risk — tutorial budget breakage if the tutorial child slips:** mitigated by making the tutorial rework a blocking child and critical priority; pricing change must not ship before it.
- **Risk — held-card regression:** premium must apply only to the same-day just-moved composite; broad changes to `placeFromHand` could wrongly premium-charge next-day placement. Mitigation: explicit `pendingHandJustMoved` gate + dedicated tests for both paths.
- **Risk — action vs coin confusion:** premium replaces the missing action; do not ALSO consume an action at premium placement. GM path must consume exactly one action at placement (2 total), never zero or two extra.
- **Risk — dialog fatigue / scope creep:** persist the dismiss preference; do not add new tutorial steps for the dialog itself (tutorial copy worded by the tutorial child); do not rebalance the premium % or touch upgrade/event cards. Follow-up ideas (premium indicator on the composite, i18n for the dialog) go to linked work items, not this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The same turn, same 1 action, same outcome — drag-drop charges +50% but the click-to-click composite charges listed cost. What should the consistent rule be?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-22, operator reply): **Option A — charge the +50% premium on the click composite too** (buy-and-play always premium), and additionally **raise a critical work item to fix the tutorial by splitting the action over two turns**. Source: session reply; tutorial-copy conflict and budget impact researched in `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` (T3/T10) and `TutorialScenario.ts` (12-coin budget table).
- Q2: "Should the premium apply to community-space cards in the composite too?" — Answer (producer): **Yes** — premium for community-space cards in the composite, matching drag-drop's business+community-space scope. Source: session reply; drag scope verified in `MainStreetTurnController.ts` (~line 656/702).
- Q3 (raised and answered by producer directive): "How should buy-and-place in a single turn be priced when actions ARE available?" — Answer (producer): **Premium only when no actions are available**; consuming an action when available prices it at listed cost; plus a dialog explaining the rule with a "Don't show this again" option. Source: session reply (verbatim: "buy and place in a single turn should only cost more if there are no actions available. Doing so (by click or drag) should show a dialog explaining this (with an option to 'don't show this again')"). Working model (move+place two-step accounting; GM 2-action listed-cost path; drag ≡ composite) documented under Risks & assumptions as the recommended interpretation for the implementer.

# Remove the dedicated staff market; route staff cards into the general market selection

**Type:** Feature | **Priority:** High

## Problem Statement

Staff cards are currently sold from a **dedicated staff-card market** (`state.staffCardMarket`, a separate deck built by `createStaffDeck(1)` and never filtered by `unlockedCardIds`). Every staff card is visible and purchasable from the very first run, regardless of progression tier. This:

- isolates staff from the achievement/tier progression that governs every other card family (business, community-space, event, upgrade), and
- gives the player a separate shopping UI surface that is inconsistent with the rest of the game's market model.

## Goal

Remove the concept of a dedicated staff market. Staff cards should appear in the **general market selection** exactly like other cards (drawn from the staff deck into the market row, subject to the same `unlockedCardIds` tier filtering that business/community-space/event/upgrade decks apply), and be purchased through the normal market purchase path.

## Users

- **Players** — expect staff to be unlocked through tier/achievement progression like every other card, and to shop for them in the same market surface as other cards.
- **Game designers/developers** — staff become a first-class card family in the market pipeline; no special-cased market section or purchase path to maintain.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No dedicated staff market state:** `staffCardMarket` is removed from `MainStreetState` (types, serialization, save/load migration, engine logic); staff cards are no longer offered from a separate market section in the UI.
2. **Staff in the general market:** staff cards are drawn from a tier-filtered staff deck into the regular market selection (dev market row), mixed with business/community-space/upgrade/event cards, using the existing market refill/cycling rules.
3. **Tier gating applies to staff:** `createStaffDeck` accepts and applies `unlockedCardIds` filtering (matching `createBusinessDeck` / `createCommunitySpaceDeck` / `createUpgradeDeck`), and `MainStreetState` passes the campaign's `unlockedCardIds` through to it. Staff cards must carry a `tier` in `card-data.csv` (precursor: tier rebalance work item).
4. **Purchase path unified:** `hireStaffCard` / staff purchase goes through the normal market purchase path; layoff and ongoing-cost mechanics are preserved unchanged.
5. **UI updated:** the staff market section is removed from renderers/overlays; staff cards render in-market like other cards; no orphaned staff-market UI code remains.
6. **Seeded determinism preserved:** same seed ⇒ same game; shuffling order changes are deliberate and documented (existing precedent: staff template additions shifted seeded draws, CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).
7. **Docs updated:** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (currently states staff "have no tier" and use a dedicated staff-card market), PRDs, and any GDD references are updated to the unified-market model.
8. **All tests pass** (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds; affected tests (staff purchase/market, meta-progression, save/load) are updated to the new model.

## Out of Scope

- Re-configuring the tier assignments themselves (covered by the tier-rebalance work item).
- Changing staff card costs/effects/ongoing-cost balance.
- Changing layoff mechanics.

## Related Work

- Tier rebalance of card families across progression tiers (incl. assigning tiers to staff cards) — prerequisite, applies `unlockedCardIds` filtering to `createStaffDeck` and assigns `tier` values in `card-data.csv`.
- Original staff-market implementation: CG-0MQRXO41D009DH26 (Implement Staff Cards & Hand Capacity System) under epic CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7.
