# [test-failure] card-schema-validation.test.ts: runtime market/decks contain unregistered template IDs

## Headline

`CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` (the Main Street card template registry) omits the **staff** card family, yet staff cards are drawn into the runtime general market row. The schema-validation test therefore fails whenever a staff card lands in the market/decks at runtime.

## Problem statement

`tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` asserts that every card ID present in the runtime game state (`state.market.cards`, `state.incidentDeck`, `state.decks.business/event/upgrade`) maps — after stripping the `-\d+` instance suffix — to a registered template ID in `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` (from `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts`). The assertion fails (reproduced at HEAD, seed `schema-registry-validation`) because the runtime market contains a staff card (`staff-lookout-0` in the failing deal) and staff templates are never registered: `rebuildTemplateArrays()` adds business, community-space, event, and upgrade templates to `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`, but staff templates are built into `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` only.

Since the staff-in-general-market work (CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55), `refillSingleRowMarket` draws staff cards into the single-row market alongside the other four families — so staff cards are legitimate runtime cards whose template IDs must be registered. This is a registry gap (a bug), not a broken test: the schema registry should cover every family that can appear in the runtime market/decks.

## Users

- **Developers extending the Main Street card pool** — they rely on `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` (via `card-schema-validation.test.ts`) as the guardrail that every runtime card corresponds to a known template. Today the guardrail errors on valid staff cards.
- **Players** — an unregistered template can surface as a missing name/title in animation lookups (`CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.get(templateId) ?? cardId` in `MainStreetAnimator.ts` falls back to the raw card ID, e.g. showing `staff-lookout-0` instead of "Lookout").

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All staff template IDs present in `card-data.csv` (family `staff`) are registered in `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` so that every staff card ID valid at runtime (e.g. `staff-lookout-0`) resolves to a registered template ID.
2. `tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` passes: `runtime market/decks only contain registered template IDs` and `all template IDs are represented in CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` both green against `dev` with the reproduction seed.
3. The validation test covers the full set of runtime card families — the runtime sample includes staff (market/decks) so this regression cannot silently recur; consider also asserting `state.decks.staff` (and `decks.communitySpace`) explicitly rather than only via market draw.
4. Runtime CSV reload (`loadTemplatesFromCsv` / `resetTemplatesToDefault` → `rebuildTemplateArrays`) keeps the registry consistent — staff re-registered/cleared together with the other families.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (regenerating any doc/card-catalog artifacts required by the change).
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should be surgical: register staff templates in `rebuildTemplateArrays()`; do not weaken the validation test.
- Staff cards in the general market row is intended behavior (CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55) — the fix must not remove staff from the market.
- `CARD_TIER_MAP` already includes staff rows (every CSV row with a non-empty `tier`), so the staff tier entries exist; only the name registry is missing them.
- Static staff SVGs exist under `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` (9 files) and `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.loadCardSvgSources()` iterates `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.keys()` — registering staff will also make the SVG loader pick up the existing static staff assets, which is consistent (verify no duplicate/stale texture keys).

## Existing state

- `rebuildTemplateArrays()` (MainStreetCards.ts ~L92–212) registers `bizTemplates`, `csTemplates`, `evtTemplates`, `upgTemplates` into `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` but builds `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` from `staffRows` without touching the name map.
- `createStaffDeck()` builds runtime staff card IDs as `` `${template.id}-${c}` `` — same instance-suffix convention as other families, so `.replace(/-\d+$/, '')` correctly recovers the template ID.
- Reproduced at HEAD (87934225): market contains `staff-lookout-0`, and `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.has('staff-lookout') === false`.
- Sibling test-failure item CG-0MT4ZR4AP006MCUC (`MainStreetIntegration.test.ts` save/load migration old-format saves) also stems from the staff-card migration work but is a separate failing assertion (`restored.decks.staff` vs `staffCardMarket` handling) — related, not a duplicate.

## Desired change

Add staff templates to `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` inside `rebuildTemplateArrays()` (e.g. a loop over the freshly built `_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES` or over `staffRows`), so the name registry covers all five runtime families bidirectionally with load/reset, and optionally extend the test's runtime sample to explicitly include `state.decks.staff` / `decks.communitySpace` for full-family coverage.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `rebuildTemplateArrays()`: register staff templates in `_CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`; `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` export.
- `tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` — failing test; extend runtime coverage to staff (and community-space) decks.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — iterates `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.keys()` for SVG fetch; verify staff asset pickup after registration.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.get(templateId) ?? cardId` title lookup benefits from staff registration.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and any generated card catalog) — update if the doc lists registered families or staff.

## Related work

- CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55 — "State, Serialization & Refill: staff in the general market" (in_progress, parent epic CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53) — the change that introduced staff into the general market row; root-cause precursor.
- CG-0MT4ZR4AP006MCUC — sibling test-failure from the same CI run (MainStreetIntegration save/load migration); related, distinct assertion.
- CG-0MT3KZOBZ005IRYE / CG-0MT3KZOUX007GQ44 / CG-0MT3KZPDR004IEIH — staff purchase/render/test work items under the same "staff in general market" epic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: None asked — the failure signature plus direct repo reproduction (staff card `staff-lookout-0` in the runtime market with `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES.has('staff-lookout') === false`) fully determined the root cause; the obvious fix (register staff templates) was validated against registry usage sites (SVG loader, animator title lookup, tier map) and requires no user decision. Source: repo investigation (runs of the failing test at HEAD, diagnostic vitest run, `wl` lookups for CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55 / CG-0MT4ZR4AP006MCUC).

# Intake Brief: Tutorial — split buy-and-play over two turns (T10 Bookshop, T14 Library)

## Problem statement

The Main Street tutorial currently teaches **same-turn composite buy-and-play** (T10: Bookshop market→hand→street in one day; T14: Library) within a tuned 12-coin budget. Parent CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN (producer decision) makes same-turn buy-and-play charge the +50% premium for a 1-action player (business and community-space), which breaks the tutorial's budget (Bookshop $3 → $4.5; Library $7 → premium $10.5 > $9.875 available after T13). The tutorial must teach **plan-ahead**: move a market card to hand on day 1 (consumes the action), end the turn, place it from hand on day 2 (consumes the action, listed cost). Producer directive (2026-08-22): *"fix the tutorial by splitting the action over two turns"* (critical priority — must ship in the same release as the pricing change).

## Users

- **Players** — learn Main Street by following a working tutorial with a positive coin balance; the tutorial must demonstrate the honest action economy and listed-cost play, not a premium path the budget can't afford.
- **TCE developers / producers** — the tutorial E2E suite and scenario budget must stay green and consistent with the engine's pricing.

User stories:
- "As a tutorial player, I want to buy a card to my hand today and place it tomorrow, **so that** I see how the action economy works and never hit a surprise premium."
- "As a developer, I want the tutorial E2E to pass after the premium-parity pricing change, **so that** the engine pricing and the tutorial tell the same story."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Two-turn buy-and-play taught:** The Bookshop and Library purchases no longer complete as same-turn composite buy-and-play; each becomes two steps across two days — (day N) move-to-hand consumes the daily action; end turn; (day N+1) select the hand card and place on the street at **listed cost**, consuming that day's action. `TutorialScenario` step flow and gating updated accordingly (no same-turn place after move within a tutorial step). Implemented step IDs: Bookshop move T11 / place T15, Library move T17 / place T19 (renumbered from the intake's T10/T14 because the Laundromat is also split — see TutorialFlow.ts UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS, T1-T23).
- [ ] **Scenario budget rebalanced:** `TutorialScenario.ts` budget table/card-cost enumeration recomputed for the two-turn flows; all steps remain affordable (positive balances) under the 12-coin (or newly-tuned) starting wallet; the T13 Community Favour rep→coins step remains coherent with the new cash flow.
- [ ] **Copy updated (i18n):** `tutorial-en.ts` (and any other locale bundles) T3/T11/T15/T17/T19 copy updated to teach move-to-hand-today / place-tomorrow and remove any text implying same-turn composite buy-and-play at listed cost; the drag = "faster but 50% more" framing reconciled with the new premium-only-when-no-actions rule (per parent item); copy uses the `{cardName}`/`{cost}` placeholders, never hardcoded card facts. (T3 Laundromat move, T11 Bookshop move, T15 Bookshop place, T17 Library move, T19 Library place — renumbered from the intake's T10/T14.)
- [ ] **E2E + unit tests updated:** tutorial E2E parts 3–6 walk the new two-turn steps (pickup on day N, end turn, place on day N+1) and assert listed-cost coin deductions; `tutorial-text-updates.test.ts` assertions updated to the new copy; all tutorial tests pass.
- [ ] **Docs:** tutorial documentation (docs/main-street/*, AGENTS.md §10b if it describes tutorial steps, Main Street README) updated to reflect the two-turn teaching; code comments updated.
- [ ] **Quality gates:** full project test suite (`npm test`) and `npm run build` pass; ships in the same release as CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN (blocking child — parent cannot close until this closes).

## Constraints

- Do not change game-economy rules in this item — only the tutorial scenario, copy, gating, and tests (pricing change lives in the parent CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN).
- The tutorial must remain completable by a player following highlighted steps; steps must never require a premium purchase the 12-coin budget can't afford.
- Same-day composite gating hooks (T5 `place-business`, T10/T13-ish `buy-and-place` terminal actions) must be re-pointed to the new two-turn step sequence without breaking step completion.
- Respect i18n copy conventions (`{cardName}`/`{cost}`/`{bonus}` placeholders; keep tutorial text in sync with card-data.csv).
- No new assets; reduced-motion/mute unaffected.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — 16-step scenario; T10 "Buy-and-place Bookshop ($3)", T14 "Buy Library ($7)"; 12-coin budget table; T13 Community Favour rep→coins (+3) required to afford the Library.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — T3 copy ("you pay {cost} when you place it"), T10 copy teaching composite click (listed cost) vs drag (+50%).
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` / `TutorialState.ts` — step gating incl. composite `buy-and-place` terminal-action steps.
- Tests: `tests/e2e/main-street-tutorial-e2e-part{1..6}.browser.test.ts` (parts 3–6 walk the 12-coin budget, composite T10 drop, T13 conversion, T14 Library), `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Rework the tutorial scenario, copy, and E2E so T10/T14 demonstrate move-to-hand on day N and place-from-hand at listed cost on day N+1, keeping the budget positive, and aligned with the parent item's new pricing rule.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — re-enumerate steps/budget for two-turn flows.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — update T3/T10/T13/T14 copy (and other locales if present).
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` / `TutorialState.ts` — gating for the new step sequence.
- `tests/e2e/main-street-tutorial-e2e-part{3,4,5,6}.browser.test.ts` — walk new two-turn steps; update coin assertions.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts` — copy assertions.
- Docs: `docs/main-street/*`, `AGENTS.md` §10b (tutorial mentions), Main Street README.

## Related work

- **Parent (blocks on this):** CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN — *Buy and Play costs are charged if drag and drop is used, but not if clicks are used* — the premium-parity pricing change this tutorial fix supports.
- CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R — action economy / premium operator decision (the rule the tutorial must teach honestly).
- CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL — same-day composite semantics (the no-auto-select flow the tutorial currently walks).
- CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET — 12-coin tutorial budget tuning (part3/part5 comments) — budget re-tuned here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — step-completion regressions:** re-pointing composite `buy-and-place` terminal steps to two-turn sequences can strand tutorial progress if gating mismatches; mitigate with E2E walking each new step and asserting step indices.
- **Risk — budget arithmetic:** recomputing the scenario budget is error-prone; the E2E coin assertions (part3/part5) and the scenario table must agree — keep the starting wallet and per-step deltas in one place.
- **Risk — scope creep:** do NOT add new tutorial steps beyond what's needed to split T10/T14, do not rebalance game economy or premium, do not add the explainer dialog to the tutorial (dialog is in the parent scope).
- **Assumption:** splitting T10/T14 over two turns does not change the parent's pricing ACs; if the GM (2-action) listed-cost path makes same-turn legal in niche cases, the tutorial (non-GM) is unaffected.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What exactly should the tutorial teach instead of same-turn buy-and-play?" — Answer (producer, 2026-08-22, operator reply): "fix the tutorial by splitting the action over two turns" — move to hand day 1 (action), place from hand day 2 (action, listed cost). Source: session reply on CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN intake.
- Prior answers: intake draft (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN) initially assumed the tutorial would keep the composite flow at listed cost; superseded by the producer's option-A decision and tutorial-split directive.

# Main street arcade should not be a service bridge

**Type:** Bug | **Priority:** High | **Assignee:** Map

## Problem Statement

The Arcade (`biz-arcade`) is currently a **Service bridge** — its synergy types are `Entertainment|Service`, so it earns adjacency bonuses from, and grants bonuses to, both Entertainment and Service neighbours. An arcade is purely an entertainment business ("retro fun for all ages"); it should be Entertainment-only and must not function as a Service business. The bridge designation was an artificial balance lever (CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB stretched T3 to two synergy types via this bridge), and it is thematically wrong.

## Users

- **Players** — an arcade alongside a laundromat or hardware store earning Service synergy feels wrong; the game's adjacency bonuses should match the business's real-world identity.
- **Designers/balance** — a correct, defensible per-tier synergy composition documented in `card-data.csv` and the docs; balance regenerated without distorting card identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Arcade becomes Entertainment-only:** `biz-arcade` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` has `synergyTypes = Entertainment` (no `Service`); its `description` no longer claims a Service bridge and matches the Entertainment single-type template used by Cinema/Music Store.
2. **T3 stays balanced — a second card carries the non-Entertainment type:** exactly one additional card is added or retagged into T3 (producer directive: option (b)) so T3 still spans ≥ 2 distinct synergy types and satisfies the ≤2× per-tier balance rule from `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` (e.g. moving Community Shelter `cs-shelter` Service T6→T3 keeps T3 at `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}`, leaving the existing T3 snapshot unchanged; a viable alternative is adding a new Service card at T3).
3. **No other tier regresses:** after the change, every tier 1–12 with synergy-bearing cards still spans ≥ 2 distinct types with no type exceeding 2× any other (the `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` rule must still pass for all tiers; its `retagged/bridged cards carry the expected synergy types` assertion is updated so `biz-arcade` = `['Entertainment']` only).
4. **Tests:** `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` updated (Arcade assertion; T3 snapshot adjusted only if the chosen card changes the composition); any other affected tests (e.g. `group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` if `cs-shelter` is moved) updated; full suite `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
5. **Docs updated in the same commit:** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (Arcade catalog row; Service bridge list drops Arcade — currently 3 bridges listed; Service/Entertainment type-coverage tables) and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (per-tier synergy model notes) reflect the change, per the doc-update policy.

## Constraints

- No `synergyTypes` added to cards that currently have none (standing constraint from CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB).
- Retagging/relocation acceptable where flavour-sensible; a new card is allowed if no retag fits, but additions stay minimal (cost ladder and tier economy apply — T3 new-card cost should sit in the cost-4 band like Arcade/Laundromat).
- Flavour preserved: the Arcade stays Entertainment; Playground remains Entertainment (it is a park-type amenity).
- No dedicated SVG needed if the chosen fix moves an existing card (no pool-size change ⇒ no seeded RNG shift); adding a new card requires the SVG pipeline run and shifts seeded draws (precedent CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).

## Existing state

- `biz-arcade` row (CSV): cost 4, baseIncome 2.9, tier 3, `Entertainment|Service`, rep +0.05/turn, desc "Retro fun for all ages. Bridges Entertainment and Service synergies."
- T3 currently: `biz-arcade` + `cs-playground` (Entertainment) ⇒ synergy counts `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}`; this exact snapshot is asserted in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts`.
- The Arcade bridge was introduced by CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB to stretch T3 (which otherwise had only Playground=Entertainment and was single-type); its rationale is recorded in test comments and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` ("Entertainment→Service bridge so T3 spans two types; an arcade is an entertainment service").
- Service bridges today: Arcade (T3), Day Spa (T11), Physiotherapy (T11).
- Community Shelter `cs-shelter` (Service, tier 6, cost 6, rep +0.15/turn) sits alone as T6's Service card; T6 also has Tailor (Service) and Toy Store (Commerce).

## Desired change

1. Edit `card-data.csv`: `biz-arcade` `synergyTypes` → `Entertainment`; rewrite its description to the Entertainment single template ("Retro fun for all ages. Gains {SYNERGY_RATE} of base income per adjacent Entertainment business.").
2. Rebalance T3 per option (b): move `cs-shelter` T6→T3 (recommended — restores `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}` in T3 with zero pool-size change, keeps T6 at `{Service: 1, Commerce: 1}`, keeps cs-tier count ≥ 6, and a shelter is thematically a neighbourhood amenity) **or** add a new Service card at T3 (cost 4) — implementer choice, documented with a balance rationale in the work item and updated Help Panel/description text as needed.
3. Update `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` (Arcade expectation; snapshots for any moved tier) and any other tests asserting card tiers/synergies.
4. Update `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Arcade synergy/description; T3 second card (relocated or new).
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — Arcade assertion (`['Entertainment']`); T3/T6 snapshots if composition changes.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — cs-shelter tier assertion (if Shelter is moved).
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — uses Arcade in market/synergy scenarios (verify no assumption of Service pairing).
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — catalog rows, synergy-coverage tables, bridge lists.
- `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — only if a new card is added.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB** (completed) — synergy-type rebalance that *introduced* the Arcade Entertainment|Service bridge; origin of the current design and the `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` rule.
- **CG-0MSQJ1XIB0004QVN** (completed) — Group A business cards including bridge design contract (implementers tune numbers only with documented rationale).
- **CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ** (completed) — Group B community spaces incl. Community Shelter (its tier/rep are asserted in tests).
- **CG-0MT3C744B009DS84** (completed) — 12-tier expansion; T3 = "Neighborhood" (rep 8).
- **CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143** (completed) — family-axis rebalance; `tier-family-balance.test.ts` (community-space tiers count ≥ 6 must hold).
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — seeded determinism precedent for pool-size changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption — option (b) scope:** moving an existing card into T3 is preferred over a new card (no SVG/pool change, no seeded-RNG shift, no cost-ladder expansion). Community Shelter is the candidate; if the implementer finds its T3 placement unbalanced, a new Service card at cost 4 is the fallback — flagged as an Open Question only if neither works.
- **Assumption — T3 composition target:** {Entertainment: 2, Service: 1} (via Arcade + Playground + Service) mirrors today's snapshot so the min change is a single relocated card; any deviation must keep the ≤2× rule.
- **Scope-creep guard:** tuning Service counts in other tiers, adding cards beyond the single T3 slot, or re-running a full synergy rebalance are NOT in scope — record as separate work items.
- **Risk — Disjoint CSV edits:** CG-0MT2WTN0L004JA53 (staff market removal) touches the same CSV; coordinate via worktrees/rebasing (same risk noted in CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB).
- **Risk — seeded RNG:** if a new card is added, deck composition changes shift seeded draws; accepted and documented per precedent CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The Arcade is the sole card in T3; its Entertainment|Service bridge is what gives T3 two synergy types (test-asserted {Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}). If the Arcade becomes Entertainment-only, T3 would be single-type and violate the ≤2× balance rule. Intended resolution? (a) Accept single-type T3 / (b) Add or retag another card into T3 / (c) Move a different card to T3 / (d) Other" — Answer (producer, interactive reply to `/skill:intake`): **(b) Add or retag another card into T3 to provide a second synergy type.** Research: T3 currently holds only Arcade + Playground (both Entertainment); a second card carrying Service (moved Community Shelter or a new Service card) restores `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}` without disturbing other tiers.

# Events in Main Street should be paid for when executed

**Status: Feature already implemented.** This work item was auto-completed during intake because the requested feature was already implemented by CG-0MM8U3SVW1SD1E9P on 2026-03-01.

## Original Request

In Main Street, businesses are taken to the hand for free and paid for when executed. Events should be treated the same way on both counts:
1. Taken to hand for free (already the case)
2. Paid for when executed (already implemented)

## Finding: Already Done

**CG-0MM8U3SVW1SD1E9P** ("Fix incident queue alignment, add investment costs, and remove auto-play of held investments") — completed 2026-03-01 — already implemented cost-at-play for Investment event cards:

- `playEventFromHand()` in `MainStreetMarket.ts` (line 597) deducts `event.cost` from `state.resourceBank.coins` before resolving effects.
- `EventCard` interface includes a `cost: number` field used at play time.
- Test `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` ("charges an event card when played from hand (cost-at-play)") confirms coin deduction.
- Incident events have `cost: 0` by design (auto-drawn, not purchased).

## Per-Turn Holding Cost

The description mentions an "open work item will add a per turn cost to holding a card in the hand." This was handled by **CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY** ("Don't charge for businesses held in the hand") which **reversed** the ongoing-cost deduction for hand-held businesses. By consistent treatment, events also do not incur per-turn costs while in hand.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT5W4V98000EDOO** "Executing an event in Main Street consumes an action" — open, idea stage. Complementary: events cost coins but currently do NOT consume an action. This is the remaining gap in event economics.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Intake Brief: In main street log should show total effects

**Work item:** CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ · type `feature` · priority `high`

**Headline:** The Main Street Activity Log will show the complete effective
(post-mitigation) coin and reputation effects of every action — not just
costs — and a per-turn net summary row, so players can see the total impact
of what they did.

## Problem statement

The Main Street Activity Log records only partial information per action — for
example, playing an event card from hand logs how much it cost but not the
revenue/reputation impact it caused, and there is no aggregate of a turn's net
resource change. Players cannot see the complete (total) effect of their actions
from the log.

## Users

- **Player** — wants to understand, from the activity log, the full effect of
  each action (cost, coin delta, reputation delta) and the net resource change
  per turn, without cross-checking the resource bank themselves.

User stories:

- "As a player, when I play an event card, I want the log to show both its cost
  and its effective coin/reputation impact so I can see what it did."
- "As a player, at the end of each turn I want a summary line showing the net
  coin and reputation change for that turn."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Full effects on all resource-mutating entries.** Every action that
  changes coins and/or reputation produces a log entry showing its effective
  (post-mitigation) coin and/or reputation deltas alongside the existing
  action-specific text (cost, name, slot, etc.). Coverage: play event from hand,
  business purchase, community-space purchase, buy-and-place (incl. premium),
  upgrade purchase, sell (hand & slot), community favour exchange, re-roll
  market, staff hire/layoff, staff & ongoing costs, income phase, incident
  resolution, and any other resource-mutating action currently logged with
  partial information. Deltas are computed as the actual change applied to the
  resource bank (post staff buffs, Brand Ambassador multiplier, reputation
  multiplier — consistent with the existing `describeEventEffects` pattern).
- **AC2 — Played-from-hand event entries.** `playEventFromHand` logs cost plus
  effective deltas (e.g. `Played event X from hand (-€5 cost, +3 coins, +2 rep)`),
  matching the format incidents already produce; classification uses the net
  coin+rep effect (not raw cost).
- **AC3 — Per-turn net summary row.** A single aggregate entry such as
  `Turn N net: +12 coins, +1 rep` is appended at the end of each turn's
  end-of-turn processing, summarizing that day's net coin/reputation change
  (day-start snapshot vs. end-of-turn values). Emitted even when the net is
  zero; defined behaviour when the game ends prematurely (e.g. emitted before
  the game-over entry, or suppressed — chosen by the implementer and covered by
  tests).
- **AC4 — No regression in log readability/mechanics.** Entries remain one line
  where possible (word-wrap already supported); gain/loss/neutral colouring
  remains sensible; scroll/auto-scroll behaviour in `refreshLog` is unchanged
  for the existing entry count handling.
- **AC5 — Tests and docs.** `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` extended
  to assert the enriched entries and the per-turn net row; any existing tests
  asserting old entry text are updated; browser log-rendering tests still pass.
  "All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries."
  "Full project test suite must pass with the new changes."

## Constraints

- Effective (post-mitigation) values only — never raw card values — so the log
  matches what the player actually gained/lost.
- Reuse/extract the existing effect description helpers
  (`describeEventEffects`, `classifyEffect` in `MainStreetEngine.ts`, currently
  private) rather than duplicating formatting logic.
- Log lines stay compact (panel ~300px wide, scrollable); no unbounded text.
- The day-start snapshot needed for the net row must survive save/load and
  replay (include in `MainStreetState` clone/restore/serialization or be
  recomputable from logged data).
- Undo (command snapshots in `MainStreetCommands.ts`) already capture
  `activityLog` wholesale — new entry shapes must remain cloneable there.

## Existing state

- `LogEntry { turn, text, type }` appended via `addLog()`; rendered by
  `MainStreetRenderer.refreshLog()`.
- `playEventFromHand` (MainStreetMarket.ts ≈L603-619) logs
  `Played event X from hand (-€X)` and always classifies 'loss'.
- Incidents (`resolveIncident`), `playHeldEvent`, and `resolveHeldInvestment`
  already log effective deltas via `describeEventEffects` (e.g.
  `Incident: X (+3 coins, +2 rep)`).
- Partial entries elsewhere: purchases log cost only; sells log +coins only;
  income phase logs +coins (+rep as separate lines); duration events log their
  multiplier text.

## Desired change

Each resource-mutating action logs its effective coin/reputation deltas (in
addition to existing text), event cards played from hand are brought in line
with incidents, and a per-turn net summary row is appended at end of turn.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — enrich `playEventFromHand`,
  `purchaseBusiness`, `purchaseUpgrade`, buy-and-place, sellFromHand/SellFromSlot,
  move-to-hand, re-roll log entries.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — expose/reuse
  `describeEventEffects` + `classifyEffect` helpers; enrich community favour,
  layoff, staff/ongoing-cost, incident entries; add per-turn net row in
  `processEndOfTurn`; day-start snapshot in `executeDayStart`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — income/rep/from-cards
  entries (already mostly complete; verify coverage of negative-income cases).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — possibly shared helper
  exports and/or net-row snapshot fields (clone/restore).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — sell-dialog log
  entry enrichment.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` — extend for new formats + net row;
  update tests asserting old text.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** entry classification continues to use the existing
  `classifyEffect` net coin+rep heuristic (gain/loss/neutral), per Q2.
- **Assumption:** the structured transcript recording
  (`recordMainStreetEvent`) is unchanged — this item only alters the
  human-readable log text and adds the net row.
- **Risk (readability):** richer entries could make lines long in a ~300px
  panel. Mitigation: compact formatting (reuse `describeEventEffects` style),
  keep existing substrings (name, slot, €cost), word-wrap already supported.
- **Risk (test churn):** many existing tests assert old entry text. Mitigation:
  additive formatting where possible and update assertions in the same change;
  full suite must pass (AC5).
- **Risk (net row edges):** early game-over/early-return paths in
  `processEndOfTurn` and save/load/replay must handle the snapshot
  (serialization or recomputation) — covered by AC3/Constraints.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "all actions" is bounded by the explicit coverage
  list in AC1; any action type found to need richer logging during
  implementation becomes a follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `CG-0MT5VXSSQ003O5ZC` — "Remove 'Market cycled...' activity log" (open) —
  adjacent log-content change; keep separate.
- **CG-0MM8RCXD511MYXZU** (completed) — reorganised the investments row /
  incident queue / player hand; defines where event-play logging lives.
- **CG-0MM8PGEIK14423LQ** (completed) — updated tests for the
  Investment/Incident rename and held event mechanics; migrated the interactive
  event path to `playEventFromHand`, whose log entry this item enriches.
  (CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X 'Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility' also surfaced by
  automation — unrelated; ignored.)
- Completed log-mechanics items: `CG-0MQK4H9180049050` (scroll off top),
  `CG-0MQQHBHHV0000UNG` (container overflow), `CG-0MMLDBB070D8LO7T` (second
  game blank log), `CG-0MQQHBY72007PZPC` (reduce height) — content is
  unchanged by this item.
- In-repo precedent for effective-delta logging: incident/held-event entries
  via `describeEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngine.ts`).
- Docs touched by related automation: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`,
  `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` (check for log-format
  specs when updating docs per AC5).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Scope:** "The description says the log should show 'the total effects of
all actions', with the event card as the example. Should this item (a) enrich
the whole log (every action type), or (b) focus on event entries first, leaving
other action types as follow-up work items?"
**Answer** — "all" (user). Final scope: enrich the whole log (option a).
Source: interactive reply. Research: all resource-mutating entries were
audited; incidents already log effects, making event-play the most visible gap,
but purchases/sells/favour etc. are also partial.

**Q2 — Event entry format:** "For a played event, should the entry show cost
plus the effective (post-mitigation) deltas, e.g.
`Played event X from hand (-€5 cost, +3 coins, +2 rep)` — consistent with the
existing incident format? Should the 'loss' classification consider the net
coin+rep effect rather than the raw cost?"
**Answer** — "post-mitigation deltas" (user). Final decision: show cost plus
effective post-mitigation deltas; classification follows the existing
`classifyEffect` net coin+rep heuristic (assumption documented in this brief).
Source: interactive reply. Research: `describeEventEffects`/`classifyEffect`
(MainStreetEngine.ts:347-364) already implement both behaviours for incidents.

**Q3 — Turn totals row:** "Does 'total effects' also mean a per-turn aggregate
row (e.g. `Turn 3 net: +12 coins, +1 rep`) summarizing all resource changes
that turn, or strictly per-action entries only?"
**Answer** — "yes" (user). Final decision: add the per-turn net summary row
(AC3). Source: interactive reply. Research: `processEndOfTurn`
(MainStreetEngine.ts:962) is the natural emission point; a day-start snapshot in
`executeDayStart` (L917) provides the baseline; `MainStreetState` clone/restore
must carry any new snapshot fields.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM8PGEIK14423LQ** – Update all tests for Investment/Incident rename and held event mechanics (completed)
- **CG-0MSRKN325004ELH2** – Review optimal pass values for avgCoinsPerTurn, winRate, medianScore (completed)
- **CG-0MLSW8TKZ0YHXJR2** – Investigate and fix broken Golf UI interactions (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: action, actions, actual, actually, add (+304 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actual, actually (+240 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: action, actions, actual, actually, add (+235 more)

# Illegal Move FX on Rejected Actions in Main Street

## Problem statement

In Main Street, when a player attempts an action that is rejected (e.g., insufficient coins, tutorial gating, hand full, no actions remaining), the game displays an instruction text message but does NOT play the 'illegal move' sound effect or visual shake feedback. This is inconsistent with the game feel expectations established in AGENTS.md best practice #8 and the existing `playIllegalFeedback()` helper.

## Users

- **Players** — want immediate, multi-sensory feedback when an action is blocked, so they understand *why* the action failed without having to read text.

User stories:

- As a player, when I try to buy a card I can't afford, I want to hear a挫败 sound and see the card shake, so I instantly know the action failed.
- As a player, when I try to click a card during the tutorial when I shouldn't, I want clear feedback so I understand the constraint.
- As a player, when I try to refresh the market but can't, I want the same feedback as other failed actions, not silence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`onBusinessCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) no actions remaining, (b) tutorial gating denies the action, (c) tutorial wrong card selected.
2. **`onPlayHeldEvent`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) try/catch catches errors in `playEventCommand` beyond "not enough coins" (currently only handles insufficient coins).
3. **`onEventCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) `canPurchaseEvent` legality check fails (hand full, incident event).
4. **`onRefreshMarketClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when `canRefreshMarket` legality check fails.
5. **`onUpgradeCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) `canPurchaseUpgrade` legality check fails (any reason, not just insufficient coins — the current code only plays FX for "not enough coins").
6. **`onStaffCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) `canPurchaseStaff` legality check fails (any reason, not just insufficient coins).
7. **`onHandBusinessCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when tutorial gating denies the action.
8. **`onSlotClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial synergy adjacency check fails, (b) tutorial step gating denies the action.
9. **`onSellCard`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when `canSellBusiness` legality check fails.
10. **`endTurn`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when tutorial gating denies the action (line ~192). The `processEndOfTurn` catch block (line ~223) is a system-level error recovery and does not need FX.
11. **`onDragDropBusiness` try/catch** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for non-coin errors (currently only handles "not enough coins").
12. **`onSlotClick` try/catch** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for non-coin errors in `playBusinessFromHandCommand` (currently only handles "not enough coins").
13. **`onBusinessCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `moveToHandCommand` (currently silent).
14. **`onEventCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `moveEventToHandCommand` (currently silent).
15. **`onUpgradeCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `buyUpgradeCommand` (currently silent).
16. **`onStaffCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `hireStaffCardCommand` (currently silent).
17. **`onDragDropBusiness` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand` beyond "not enough coins" (currently only handles that one case).
18. All existing compliant code paths (e.g., `onPeekClick`, `onCommunityFavourClick`, insufficient-coins cases in drag-drop and click handlers) remain unchanged.
19. Reduced-motion and mute settings are respected via `playIllegalFeedback`.
20. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

## Constraints

- Only modify Main Street code (`example-games/main-street/`).
- Use the existing `playIllegalFeedback()` helper — no new functions or SFX.
- The helper is already imported in `MainStreetTurnController.ts`.
- Each rejection path must pass the card or container reference to `playIllegalFeedback`; where no card is available, use `s.actionContainer` (as done in `onPeekClick` and `onCommunityFavourClick`).
- No changes to engine core, dragDrop, or other example games.

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: adding `playIllegalFeedback` to tutorial gating paths may feel frustrating to tutorial players who are expected to make certain mistakes. Mitigation: the feedback is brief (0.15s reduced-motion, 0.1s normal shake + short SFX) and the text instruction remains; it provides clarity, not punishment.
- Risk: catching all try/catch errors with illegal feedback could mask genuine bugs (e.g., null-reference exceptions). Mitigation: console.error is already logged; the FX is the user-facing layer only. If an error message starts with "Error:" (as all current handlers do), the text remains as the primary signal.
- Assumption: `playIllegalFeedback` is always available in the context (it's a module-local function in the same file). No new imports needed.
- Scope-creep guard: this item only covers Main Street. Other example games that may have the same pattern are recorded as linked follow-up items, not expanded into this one.

## Existing state

- `playIllegalFeedback()` in `MainStreetTurnController.ts:34-82` — wraps `shakeIllegalMove` with container-safe fallback, plays `COMMON_SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE` via `safePlaySound`, respects reduced-motion.
- Several handlers already use it correctly: `onPeekClick` (line ~1275), `onCommunityFavourClick` (line ~1331), insufficient-coins catch blocks in `onDragDropBusiness` (line ~830), `onSlotClick` (line ~1003, 1014), `onUpgradeCardClick` legality (line ~1514), `onStaffCardClick` legality (line ~1611).
- Other handlers have only `s.instructionText.setText()` with no FX.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Add `playIllegalFeedback` calls to all rejection paths identified above.

## Related work

- **Add best practices for animations and sounds on player/AI actions (CG-0MSHFOSGV007W8UC)** — completed; established the mandatory rule that all player and AI actions using core engine helpers must be animated and audible.
- **Main Street Game Feel: animation, audio & VFX enhancement proposals (CG-0MSRGTAA9001F2ST)** — completed; broader game feel improvements for Main Street.

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play a competitive mode against an AI opponent who builds businesses on the **same street**, so that turns give me more to do and the game has a rival to race against.

## Design scope (from feasibility analysis, 2025-07 session)

- **Shared street grid** (10 slots); each placed business is owned by one player; income from a business accrues to its **owner**.
- **Events affect the whole street**: investment events and incidents keep the existing street-wide resolution semantics, but income/damage must be routed per-owner.
- **Staff are player-only**: the AI does not hire staff, and its competitive decision space excludes staff actions (hire-staff, peek).
- **Single shared market row**: buying a card denies it to the opponent (market competition is a first-class feature).
- **Alternating turn structure** — design decision to confirm at intake: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day vs. alternating full days.

## Reusability findings (basis for this item)

- The decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `enumerateLegalActions`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) transfers ~1:1 — it is UI-free and already shared between the Monte Carlo harness and the hint system.
- The state/engine layers are single-owner: `MainStreetState` has one resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining; `applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions` all assume one owner. These need a per-player split plus owner-tagged grid slots.
- Greedy heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street (`scoreBusinessAction = (income+synergy)*horizon - cost`; `aiPlanningHorizon` reads a single score) — scoring must become ownership-aware.
- PRD M3 (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`) explicitly scoped "AI vs. player (competitive mode)" as N/A — this item is a deliberate scope extension; note it in the PRD.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- AC1: A competitive-mode state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG.
- AC2: The AI opponent plays a legal full turn through the existing strategy layer (`enumerateLegalActions` → scored choice → `executeAction`), with staff actions excluded.
- AC3: Income accrues to the owner of each business; street-wide events/incidents affect both players under the shared-street semantics.
- AC4: A head-to-head Monte Carlo harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) measures the win distribution across >=200 seeds to validate competitive balance.
- AC5 (scene, may be split into a child at planning): competitive mode is selectable from the game selector, renders the shared street with owner colouring, alternates turns, and animates AI turns with SFX per the audio/feedback rule (AGENTS.md best practice 8).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30).

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold.
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Deterministic validation: extend `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (or a sibling harness) to run head-to-head AI-vs-AI and, where feasible, AI-vs-baseline matches across >=200 seeds; document win/score distributions.

## Out of scope (decision to record in item)

Whether to add opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — record an explicit in/out decision with rationale; denial can be a follow-up child if in.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- AC2: Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the shared single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- AC3: A deterministic head-to-head Monte Carlo harness runs the adapted strategy against a baseline over >=200 seeds and produces win/score distribution metrics (extension of `MainStreetMonteCarloMetrics` or equivalent).
- AC4: All existing single-player AI tests (ai-strategy, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

# Intake Brief: Add a close business option to Main Street (CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV)

## Problem statement

In Main Street, a business/community-space card on the street grid can only be **sold**, which refunds 50% of purchase+upgrade cost and leaves the card **permanently on the grid** in an inert "sold" state — the slot stays occupied for the rest of the game (placement requires an empty slot). Players need a **Close** option: an action-consuming, coin-free action that **removes the card from the street entirely**, freeing the slot so a new card can be placed there later.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to replace an underperforming business instead of being stuck with a dead sold card in a key slot.

**Example user stories:**

- "As a player, I want to close a business that is losing money (negative ongoing cost) so I can place a better card in that slot on a later day."
- "As a player, I want to clear a community-space card from the street without keeping it as a permanently occupied slot."
- "As a player, I want a clear, confirmable way to close a street card (costing 1 action, no coins) distinct from selling it (free, refund, stays on the grid)."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope & UI (feature behavior):** During `MarketPhase`, every **non-sold** business and community-space card on the street grid offers a **Close** option; **sold** cards never do. The existing click-a-street-card confirmation dialog (`showSellConfirmation`) is extended into a **Manage card** dialog with **[Sell] [Close] [Cancel]** buttons (reusing `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, HUD-container parenting, depth 199/200/201).
2. **Cost:** Closing consumes **exactly one daily action** via the shared `consumeAction` helper (`actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions` decremented, floor 0 — CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) and grants **no coins**. Selling remains free and unchanged.
3. **Removal:** Closing removes the card from `streetGrid[slotIndex]` (slot → `null`), pushes it to the `discardPile` (not removed from the game), incrementally updates affected neighbors' cached income/synergy values, writes an activity-log entry, and the slot becomes **immediately placeable** by new cards.
4. **Undo & feedback:** Close is a **reversible command** (`closeBusinessCommand` via the undo manager restores the card, slot occupancy, action budget, and neighbor values) and is rendered with an **animation + SFX** consistent with the existing sell demolition (`animateSell`) and the event-driven audio rule (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).
5. **Quality & docs:** Unit tests cover legality (MarketPhase, non-sold, slot occupied, action sufficiency), cost, removal, neighbor recalculation, and undo; a browser test covers the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel); HUD/help tooltips and docs are updated (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` action-economy table: Close added under *action-consuming* operations, explicitly NOT in the "Free operations" list; GDD action-economy section; `ux-visual-audio.md` if the close animation differs); the **full test suite passes** (`npm test`) and the production build succeeds (`npm run build`).

## Constraints

- Action cost must go through the **single shared `consumeAction`** enforcement point (CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) — same path as `buyBusinessCommand`/`buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`; no double-decrement, no divergence.
- Follow the engine's existing patterns: `LegalityResult` discriminated union (`canCloseBusiness`), reversible `toCommand`/`snapshotAction` command, and `MainStreetMarket` action module structure mirroring `sellBusiness`/`canSellBusiness`.
- Modal dialog must follow the project's UI best practices (backdrop 199, box 200, interactive 201; parent all text/buttons into `hudContainer`; `dismissOverlay` cleanup) and SLL for positioning.
- Event-driven audio rule (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N-context rule in AGENTS.md): the close action must be animated and sounded via the shared helpers/SoundManager; `shakeIllegalMove`/illegal feedback for rejected closes; reduced-motion and mute/volume settings respected.
- i18n: dialog/label strings should follow the game's i18n pattern if the existing sell dialog strings are localized.
- Doc-update policy: this is a rules/mechanic change — `docs/main-street/*` must be updated in the same change; create a doc-update child work item if it can't land in the same commit.

## Existing state

- **Sell from street:** `sellBusiness` (`MainStreetMarket.ts`) marks `soldSlots[slotIndex] = true`, refunds `Math.ceil((purchasePrice + upgradeCosts) / 2)`, card stays on grid (inert — no income/synergy), **free** (no action consumed). Legality gate `canSellBusiness` (MarketPhase only, unsold only). `updateNeighborsOnSale` recalcs neighbors.
- **UI entry:** clicking a non-sold street card in `MarketPhase` → `MainStreetTurnController.onSellCard` → `MainStreetOverlayContent.showSellConfirmation` (Sell/Cancel, refund text) → `sellBusinessCommand` (free).
- **Placement:** `canPlaceFromHand` requires `streetGrid[slotIndex] === null` — so a sold card permanently occupies its slot today.
- **Engine legacy helper:** `sellFromTableau` already models "remove card entirely + to discard pile", but is unused by the street UI and prices at 75% (old PRD semantics) — NOT to be reused for Close (Close pays nothing).
- **AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` does not enumerate street sells (player-initiated); no AI changes expected, but verify — costs/empty-slot should not break AI budget tests (`ai-action-budget.test.ts`).
- **Docs:** `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` lists "Selling a business" under **Free operations**; Close must be added as an action-consuming op.

# Intake Brief — Main Street sold businesses still provide synergy (CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ)

## Headline

When the player sells a business in Main Street, the sold card must stop producing income (unchanged) but **continue providing its synergy contributions to adjacent non-sold businesses** — selling a shop should not break the street's synergy chain.

## Problem statement

Today, selling a business halts **both** its own income and the synergy effects it provides to neighbouring businesses: the adjacency engine (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) skips sold slots as neighbours in every synergy computation, and the visual synergy link between a sold card and its neighbours disappears. A sale should only stop the sold card's own income/reputation — the sold business stays on the street as a "type anchor" whose presence keeps granting synergy bonuses (coins and reputation) to its non-sold neighbours.

## Users

Main Street players. Example user stories:

- As a player, when I sell a business to raise coins, I expect the businesses next door to keep the synergy income they had before — selling one shop shouldn't degrade the rest of my street.
- As a player, I expect the synergy link lines on the street to reflect the income I actually receive, so if a sold neighbour still contributes synergy, the line should still be drawn.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Sold-card income halt preserved:** a sold business continues to produce 0 income and 0 reputation for itself (`computeBusinessIncome`/per-slot paths unchanged for the sold slot itself).
2. **Coin synergy retained for neighbours:** non-sold businesses adjacent to a sold business keep the exact coin synergy bonus they had before the sale (the sold card still counts toward the matching-neighbour count N in `computeSynergyBonus`).
3. **Reputation synergy retained for neighbours:** non-sold businesses adjacent to a sold business keep their reputation synergy (`computeSynergyRepBonus` counts sold neighbours) under the same rule.
4. **Same-type penalty persists (Q1 = Remains):** a sold same-type business still counts in `hasAdjacentSameType()`, so a non-sold neighbour's 0.6 same-type base-income penalty is unchanged by the sale — selling changes nothing for neighbours.
5. **Visual link retained (Q2 = yes for sold):** `computeSynergyPairs()` continues to produce the synergy pair between a sold business and its non-sold neighbours so the drawn synergy link line remains visible; no stray re-animation of pre-existing pairs on sale.
6. **Testing/validation:** update `tests/main-street/MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` (flip the "should not include sold cards in synergy calculations" case to assert synergy retention) and add coverage in `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts` for: sold card contributes coin synergy + reputation synergy to neighbours, income stays 0 for the sold card itself, same-type penalty persists through sale, and synergy pairs include sold/active endpoints. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. **Documentation:** all related documentation updated to reflect the new sold semantics — `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md`, the `soldSlots` field comment in `MainStreetState.ts` (currently "non-functional, no income/synergy" → "no income, still provides synergy"), Main Street README/help text where it describes sold behaviour, and code comments in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` ("Skip sold neighbour slots" → sold neighbours still count).

## Constraints

- Sold cards stay on the grid dimmed ("SOLD" overlay) and cannot be re-sold, upgraded, or interacted with — unchanged.
- Sold cards never earn income or reputation themselves — unchanged.
- Percentage-based synergy formula, difficulty multipliers (`synergyBonusPerNeighbor`), same-type 0.6 rule, and hand-card synergy math are unchanged — only the sold-slot exclusions change.
- Overall income totals (`computeIncome`) continue to skip sold slots (their contribution is 0) — unchanged.
- The sell refund formula (`Math.ceil((cost + upgradeCosts) / 2)`) is out of scope.

## Existing state

- `sellBusiness()` (`MainStreetMarket.ts`) marks the slot sold, credits the refund, and calls `updateNeighborsOnSale()` which recalculates every non-sold neighbour "as if synergy was lost".
- `computeSynergyBonus()` / `computeSynergyRepBonus()` / `hasAdjacentSameType()` / `computeSynergyPairs()` (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) all `continue`/`return 0` on sold slots — sold cards contribute nothing to neighbours and no synergy line is drawn.
- `MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` contains a test asserting the current (undesired) behaviour: sold cards are excluded from synergy calculations.
- The motion/sale animation and SOLD dimmed rendering (`MainStreetRenderer.ts`) are unaffected by this change.

## Desired change

- In `MainStreetAdjacency.ts`, remove the `if (soldSlots[ni]) continue;` skips in the **neighbour loops** of `computeSynergyBonus`, `computeSynergyRepBonus`, `hasAdjacentSameType`, and `computeSynergyPairs`, while **keeping** the `if (soldSlots[index]) return 0;` source-slot guards so a sold card's own income/reputation stays 0.
- Update `updateNeighborsOnSale()` docs/comments (its recalculation path is retained; with the fix, neighbours' cached values simply stay stable — the sale no longer changes them).
- Update the `soldSlots` semantics comment in `MainStreetState.ts`.
- Flip/extend the tests and update docs per AC 6/7.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — core fix: stop skipping sold neighbours in `computeSynergyBonus`, `computeSynergyRepBonus`, `hasAdjacentSameType`, `computeSynergyPairs`; keep sold-source 0-guards; update comments.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — update `soldSlots` doc comment to the new semantics ("no income, still provides synergy").
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `sellBusiness()`/`updateNeighborsOnSale` comments only (behavioural change lives in the adjacency module).
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` — flip the sold-synergy exclusion test; assert retention.
- `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts` — new coverage for sold-neighbour synergy (coins + rep), same-type penalty persistence, synergy-pair inclusion.
- `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` — document sold-business synergy semantics.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` / scene help text — clarify sold behaviour if described.

## Related work

- CG-0MQOA5U4H000J37N — original sell-cards implementation (introduced `soldSlots` + `updateNeighborsOnSale`).
- CG-0MRVCWNEQ009H52Z — percentage-based synergy formula (current formula this fix preserves).
- CG-0MQK55JM0000KU1T — "Synergies in Main Street are not working" (precedent for synergy bugs).
- CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR — synergy link formation animation (visual pairs path).
- CG-0MSKS963N000ZSTU — "Library next to Bookshop should trigger synergy bonus (line not drawn)" (precedent for line/pair correctness).
- CG-0MQQT9X45002WM4H — same-type rule ("Synergy only works for different businesses").
- CG-0MQQHBHHU001T6D9 / CG-0MQK45ACM0042YMG — Pawn Shop exclusion from synergy (card-level exclusion precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** the fix applies to both coin and reputation synergy; Q1 (same-type penalty) = remains; Q2 (visual link) = visible for sold cards. Recorded in the audit Appendix below.
- **Balance risk:** selling a card no longer weakens its neighbours — the sold card keeps acting as a synergy anchor. This is the explicitly requested behaviour but changes player economics; flag for difficulty/balance review after implementation if noticeable.
- **Edge case:** `computeSynergyPairs` will also emit pairs between two sold cards once skips are removed (both are inert but same-type/type-presence still applies). Decide visually — default: keep symmetric (line drawn between two sold cards is harmless and consistent); if undesired, suppress pairs where both endpoints are sold (small change, visual only).
- **Scope-creep guard:** tooltip copy for sold cards ("still provides synergy"), extra animation polish, and any sell-refund or difficulty changes are out of scope — record as new work items if wanted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (Map → operator): "Q1 (same-type penalty): the 0.6 same-type base-income penalty currently vanishes when a same-type neighbour is sold. Should a sold same-type business still count for `hasAdjacentSameType()` so the sale changes nothing for the survivor, or should the penalty genuinely clear when the competitor is sold?"
  - Answer (operator): "Remains" — the same-type penalty stays in effect; a sold same-type business still counts. Source: operator reply 2026-08-30 to the intake question comment on CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ.
  - Research: `hasAdjacentSameType()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` skips sold neighbours; keeping the sold card in the check makes the sale neutral for the survivor's effective base.
- Q (Map → operator): "Q2 (visual link): should the drawn synergy link line between a sold business and its non-sold neighbours remain visible, or be suppressed for sold cards (income synergy persists but the line is removed)?"
  - Answer (operator): "yes for sold" — the line remains visible for sold cards. Source: operator reply 2026-08-30 to the intake question comment on CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ.
  - Research: `computeSynergyPairs()` skips sold slots entirely (source and neighbour); removing only the neighbour skip keeps pairs between sold and non-sold cards while leaving both-sold pairs as a documented edge case.
## Related work (automated report)

# Intake Brief: Enable Main Street Expansion of Playing Area

## Problem Statement

Main Street currently has a single fixed 2×5 street (10 slots) with no ability to expand the playing field. The player should be able to zoom out at any time to reveal a larger 2D grid of streets, where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots between streets are shared — one card serves all four adjacent streets, with normal adjacency rules.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want to zoom out and explore neighbouring streets so that I can place more businesses and grow my empire beyond the initial 10-slot grid.
- **As a player**, I want shared corner plots between streets so that strategically placed businesses create cross-street synergy bonuses.
- **As a player**, I want the zoom to work like a map — smooth camera movement that reveals streets organically without gating or milestones.
- **As a game engine developer**, I want the grid system to be unbounded (or at least large enough to support extended play) so the game doesn't end prematurely when all streets are full.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Camera system**: A zoom/pan camera system is implemented for Main Street, allowing the player to zoom out to reveal neighbouring streets. The zoom is controlled by the player (e.g. scroll wheel or button), not gated by milestones.
2. **Grid topology**: The street grid is represented as a 2D lattice where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots (where streets meet at the corners of adjacent 2×5 grids) are shared — one card slot serves the shared position, and the card is adjacent to neighbours in all four streets per normal adjacency rules.
3. **Adjacency & synergy**: The adjacency resolver (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) is updated to compute correct 8-way Chebyshev adjacency across street cells, including shared corner slots. Synergy bonuses and income calculations work correctly for cards on expanded streets and shared corners.
4. **Rendering**: All street cells within the current camera viewport are rendered. Cards placed on expanded or shared slots display and interact correctly. Unrevealed streets outside the current zoom level are not rendered.
5. **Save/Load**: The expanded grid state (all placed cards, including shared corner cards, and current zoom/camera position) serializes and deserializes correctly.

## Constraints

- The zoom is **always available** — no gating by milestones, turns, or resources.
- The grid is **conceptually unbounded** (at minimum, support at least a 3×3 or 5×5 grid of streets). Practically, the grid could grow dynamically as the player zooms out further.
- Corner plots are **shared between streets**: one card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules (8-way Chebyshev) apply — the card counts as a neighbour to all adjacent slots across all streets it touches.
- The existing `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` constants and the flat 10-slot array must be refactored to support multi-street topology.
- Must preserve deterministic seed-based gameplay and save/load compatibility.
- Existing adjacency/synergy/Income systems must continue working without modification to core logic — only the coordinate/adjacency mapping layer changes.

## Existing State

- **Single street**: `GRID_SIZE = 10`, `STREET_COLS = 5`, `STREET_ROWS = 2` (from `MainStreetConstants.ts` and `MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Flat array**: `streetGrid` is `(BusinessCard | CommunitySpaceCard | null)[]` with row-major indexing.
- **Adjacency**: `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `toGridPosition()` maps flat index → {x, y} using `STREET_COLS = 5`; `neighbors()` computes 8-way Chebyshev distance within the 10-slot boundary.
- **Rendering**: `MainStreetRenderer.ts` and `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` position 10 slots in two rows, hardcoded layout.
- **No camera system**: Phaser camera is not used for street navigation; the game uses a fixed viewport.
- **SpatialRules**: Core engine provides `Grid<T>`, `neighbors()`, `shortestPath()` (`@core-engine/SpatialRules`) — reusable for multi-street topology.

## Desired Change

- Introduce a 2D street-cell grid where each cell is a 2×5 street (10 slots).
- Add a camera/zoom system to navigate the grid.
- Refactor the adjacency resolver to work with the 2D grid, computing correct neighbours across street cells and shared corners.
- Update rendering to draw all visible street cells within the viewport.
- Update state serialization to include the full grid and camera position.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — Refactor `STREET_COLS/ROWS` into per-street-cell dimensions; add grid dimension constants.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Update `GRID_SIZE` to a dynamic value; remove hard-coded 10-slot assumption.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Change `streetGrid` from flat array to 2D grid structure; add camera/zoom state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Refactor `toGridPosition()`, `neighbors()` to compute positions on the 2D street-cell grid; handle shared corner slots.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Update rendering loop to iterate over visible street cells; add camera transform.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — Update layout calculations for multi-street grid.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Integrate camera control (zoom/pan input), wire up rendering and adjacency changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Update drop-zone and click-target logic for expanded grid.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MM4RDIMT1HLP2DE**: Main Street GDD Review and Consolidation (parent epic)
- **CG-0MM5ZG7071KO7PVG**: Adjacency & Spatial Rules (core engine spatial system)
- **CG-0MQKA533D003P55Y**: Gym: SpatialRules demo scene (Grid + pathfinding)
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC**: Main Street PRD Milestone 6 — Engine Component Extraction
- **CG-0MM4R9UJF1DGI0ZF**: Main Street (parent epic)
- **CG-0MPENWRBO0051ZQT**: Port Main Street to SLL (UI layout modernisation)
- **CG-0MT5Y1X5T001M4S6**: This item — Enable Main Street expansion of playing area

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1**: What triggers the grid expansion? — **A**: No gating — player can zoom out at any time. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2**: How does "zoom" work visually and mechanically? — **A**: Like a map — camera zoom reveals pre-defined streets on a larger 2D grid. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3**: What does "corner plots shared with each edge" mean for gameplay? — **A**: Yes, shared corner slot counts as adjacent to neighbours in both streets. One card slot, one card, normal adjacency rules apply. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief — Tooltips on businesses are confusing (CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ)

## Problem Statement

Event-card tooltips in the market show two effect lines that contradict each other. The first line (card `effect`, e.g. Street Performer "+2 coins to each Entertainment business") describes the per-match rule, while the second line (`Coins: +5.000`) shows the raw `coinDelta` template value regardless of board state. With a single non-Entertainment business (Pawn Shop) on the street, the tooltip still promises `+5` even though the effective gain would be `0`, confusing players.

## Users & User Stories

- **Main Street player browsing the market** — As a player, I want the Street Performer tooltip to tell me what I will actually gain given my current street, so I can judge whether the purchase is worth 5 coins.
- **New player learning synergies** — As a new player, I want one clear effect description, not two numbers that disagree, so I do not have to guess which one is authoritative.
- **Developer / QA verifying card data** — As a developer, I want the tooltip source of truth to align with `resolveEvent` logic, so card-data drift is surfaced rather than masked.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **RCA documented** — Work-item comment or brief appendix records root cause of the mismatch (which fields render which line, why `+5.000` appears for a `+2 per business` SpecificSynergy event, why formatting uses `toFixed(3)`, and any card-data vs effect-text drift for `evt-street-performer`).
2. **Tooltip is no longer confusing** — For market Investment events (and any other event tooltip path with `includeEventDetail`), the tooltip shows a single, non-contradictory effect. For `SpecificSynergy` targets the raw `Coins: +N` line is either removed or replaced with a contextualised line that reflects matching-business count / effective gain (e.g. `Potential: +0 (0 Entertainment businesses)` or `+2 per Entertainment business × N matches`). Raw template deltas must not be shown as if they were the final payout.
3. **Formatting is consistent** — Coin/reputation values in tooltips do not show spurious decimals (`5.000`) and follow the same `formatCurrency` / integer conventions used elsewhere in HUD and logs.
4. **Regression coverage** — Unit tests cover `buildCardTooltipInfo` for `SpecificSynergy` vs `All` events with 0 and N matches, and a regression test for the Street Performer + Pawn Shop scenario; existing suites `business-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`, `card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `staff-market-row-ui.test.ts` remain green.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not change `resolveEvent` / game balance unless the RCA proves the `coinDelta` value itself is wrong; prefer fixing presentation. If `card-data.csv` must change, checksum / save-compat (`loadTemplatesFromCsv`, `CSV_CHECKSUM`) must be considered.
- Keep changes surgical: `MainStreetFormatting.ts` owns tooltip text; `MainStreetRenderer.ts` owns when `includeEventDetail` is passed.
- No new dependencies; reuse `formatCurrency` / existing synergy helpers.
- Locale-aware currency formatting must be preserved.

## Existing State

- `buildCardTooltipInfo()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts:139-141` appends `
Coins: ${e.coinDelta.toFixed(3)}, Rep: ${...}` when `includeEventDetail` is true. Market investment cards pass `includeEventDetail: true` (`MainStreetRenderer.ts:1312,1332,1364`), so every market Investment tooltip shows the raw `coinDelta`.
- `evt-street-performer` in `card-data.csv:61` has `effect` "+2 coins to each Entertainment business…" but `coinDelta` 5.0 — the two numbers disagree and the tooltip renders both. With 0 Entertainment businesses, the effective gain is 0, but the detail line still claims +5.
- `resolveEvent()` in `MainStreetEngine.ts:552-560` applies `coinDelta * matchCount` for `SpecificSynergy`, so the effective value is board-dependent.
- Tooltip formatting uses `toFixed(3)` unlike HUD/log currency rendering.

## Desired Change

- Perform RCA (code + data) and record findings on the work item.
- Update `buildCardTooltipInfo` (and call sites if needed) so event tooltips show one coherent effect: either suppress the redundant raw detail line or render a contextualised line (matches + effective gain) that matches engine logic. Fix decimal formatting to match game conventions.
- If `card-data.csv` drift is confirmed (e.g. Street Performer `coinDelta` should be 2 not 5), correct the data and note the save-compat implication.
- Add/adjust unit + browser tests to lock the new behaviour.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Owns `buildCardTooltipInfo()` and the `includeEventDetail` detail line; primary fix site.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Source of `effect` vs `coinDelta` mismatch for `evt-street-performer` and other SpecificSynergy events; verify/fix if needed.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveEvent()` `SpecificSynergy` handling (`coinDelta * matchCount`); reference for correct effective value.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Call sites passing `includeEventDetail: true` for market/hand tooltips.
- `tests/main-street/business-card-tooltip-info.test.ts` — Existing tooltip tests to extend.
- `tests/main-street/card-currency-formatting.test.ts` — Currency/tooltip formatting tests.
- `tests/main-street/card-manifest.test.ts` / `tests/main-street/card-schema-validation.test.ts` — Card-data validation if CSV changes.

## Related Work

- CG-0MT24RFIV007NQMP — Tooltips for business cards do not work reliably (completed) — prior tooltip reliability fix; same rendering path.
- CG-0MQK4ADJ2007EV1S — Main Street Park tooltip is not working (completed) — prior per-card tooltip content issue.
- CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8 — Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — tooltip content correctness precedent.
